Apache Mod Box Modular Electronics Housing for Apache 2800 Boombox Builds Update — July 30, 2026 This update adds more amplifier options and additional layout flexibility: Added a mirrored ZK-1001U lid for left- or right-side placement inside the Apache case Added ZK-1002T compatibility using inward-facing mounts on either bump out Added TW100U compatibility using an inward-facing mount between the two bump outs Added a protective cover panel for the TW100U Added Lid - No Amp for the ZK-1002T, TW100U, or builds that need a clean top lid Added selectable left- and right-side wire cutouts to Lid - No Amp Update — August 1, 2026 Added compatibility for every hole size at all 6 locations Added small mounting cuts for TW100U Amp Cover to slot into and stay put Overview I designed the Apache Mod Box as an all-in-one housing for the amplifier, battery, wiring, and controls used in an Apache 2800 boombox build. There are several similar designs available, but I wanted something that gave the builder more freedom when planning the layout. Instead of locking the power button, charging port, and Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger into one location, the included 3MF lets you choose which openings to use before printing. The Mod Box currently supports three amplifier configurations: Amplifier Mounting Location Recommended Lid ZK-1001U Mounted on top of the Mod Box Standard or mirrored ZK-1001U lid ZK-1002T Inward-facing on either bump out Lid - No Amp TW100U Inward-facing between the bump outs Lid - No Amp and optional protective cover panel Make sure you choose the correct amplifier mount, lid, wire cutout, and control openings before starting the print. Amplifier Compatibility ZK-1001U The ZK-1001U mounts directly to the top of the Mod Box using an amplifier-specific lid. Two lid orientations are included: Standard ZK-1001U lid Mirrored ZK-1001U lid The mirrored version gives you more freedom to position the Mod Box on either the left or right side of the Apache case and have the amp be near or away from the opening of the case. Because of the available clearance, the amplifier power connection requires a 5.5 × 2.1 mm right-angle DC adapter . A straight connector will not fit properly with this setup. The battery and wiring remain contained underneath the lid, while the amplifier controls stay accessible from the top. ZK-1002T The ZK-1002T mounts inward-facing on one of the two bump outs. There are two available mounting locations: Left bump out Right bump out Choose the mounting objects for the side you want to use and change them to Negative Parts in Bambu Studio. After printing: Remove the washers and nuts from the amplifier knobs. Slide the controls through the openings from inside the Mod Box. Reinstall the washers and nuts from the outside. Install Lid - No Amp for a clean finish on top. The ZK-1002T does not require an amplifier-specific lid. TW100U The TW100U mounts inward-facing in the center area between the two bump outs. Unlike the ZK-1001U, the TW100U does not mount to the lid. Use Lid - No Amp to close the top of the Mod Box. A separate protective cover panel is also included for the TW100U. The panel can be installed over the amplifier to help protect it while keeping the controls accessible from inside the Apache case. This mounting position uses the open area between the bump outs while keeping the top of the Mod Box clean. Make sure the TW100U mounting openings and the appropriate wire cutout are selected before printing. Assembly Required Hardware The Mod Box is assembled using M4 heat-set inserts and M4 × 12 mm screws . You’ll need: 6x M4 heat-set inserts 6x M4 × 12 mm flat head machine screws Install the heat-set inserts into the Mod Box, then secure the lid using the six M4 screws. Tools Soldering Iron Heat Set Insert Tips Parts 5.5mm x 2.1mm Charge Port Jack 5.5mm x 2.1mm Right Angle Adapter Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger or USB-C Model 16mm 12v/24v Latching Power Button 24v 4Ah Battery or 7Ah Battery (same size) Internal Space Main Chamber: 227 mm long × 86 mm deep × 74 mm tall Bump Outs: 46mm wide x 111mm long Make sure your battery and other components fit within that space before printing. Configurable Control Openings The Apache Mod Box now supports every available control opening at every control location. There are six selectable mounting locations: Inside-left Inside-center Inside-right Outside-left Outside-center Outside-right At each of those six locations, you can choose from the following modeled openings: Component Size Modeled Opening 12 mm 12.3 mm 16 mm 16.3 mm 19 mm 19.3 mm 22 mm 22.3 mm 30 mm 30.3 mm This allows the power button, charging port, Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger, USB-C charger, or another compatible round component to be placed in whichever location works best for the build. For example, you can: Put the USB Quick Charger outside-center for easy access Place the power button inside-left Mount the charging port outside-right Keep every control inside the Apache case Place all controls outside Use the left, center, and right positions in any combination Charging Port Power Button The power button and charging port do not have to be placed together. For example, you can: Place the power button outside and the charging port inside Put them on opposite sides of the Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger Keep all controls inside Mount all controls outside Setting Up Your Mod Box The different cutouts are already built into the included 3MF, so you don't need to edit anything in CAD . In Bambu Studio, open the Objects tab and expand the Mod Box. You'll see the different cutout options labeled by size and location. Find the openings you want to use and change those objects to Negative Part . When the model is sliced, the negative objects will create the holes in the Mod Box. Leave any locations you aren't using alone. I highly recommend checking the sliced preview before starting the print. It's an easy way to make sure you've opened the right locations before committing to the full box. Important: Nested Control Openings The 12, 16, 19, 22, and 30 mm openings are nested together at every location. When selecting an opening, that size and every smaller opening at the same location must be changed to Negative Parts. Component Being Installed Objects That Must Be Negative 12 mm component 12 mm 16 mm component 12 mm + 16 mm 19 mm component 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm 22 mm component 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm + 22 mm 30 mm component 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm + 22 mm + 30 mm For example, when installing a 30 mm Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger in the outside-center position, make the 12, 16, 19, 22, and 30 mm objects at the outside-center location Negative Parts. Changing only the 30 mm object will not create the complete opening.. Thanks for checking out the Apache Mod Box! I put a lot of thought into making this as flexible and useful as possible for different Apache boombox builds. If you print one, I’d love to see how you set yours up. And if you have an idea for another amp lid, different port size, mounting option, or anything else that would make the Mod Box better, drop a comment or send a recommendation. I’m always open to improving the design and adding more options for future builds. Ratings and comments help me so much and if you love it, please consider boosting!

description: A fish priest with an actual whack to it. Printed plastic alone is sometimes too light to dispatch a fish cleanly, so this one has a 77 cm3 weight chamber inside the head, sealed by an M33x3.5 threaded plug with a coin slot. Fill it with steel BBs for roughly 370 g of added mass, or dry sand for about 120 g, or you can leave as is without any fill and it should do the job for small fish. Made it for my own tackle box because I can never find a stick when I need it. Specs (default): 300 mm long, 44 mm octagonal head, 30 mm handle with three grip grooves, pommel flare plus a 9 mm lanyard hole so it stays on your wrist over water. Chamber is a 31 mm bore, 92 mm deep with a tapered end. Plug threads are printed in place, no hardware needed. Print settings, and these matter for strength: the file is pre-oriented lying flat (fits a 256 bed diagonally at 238 x 238 mm), no supports, and the layer lines run the length of the bat, which is the strong direction in bending. Do not stand it upright in the slicer or it will snap at the neck on the first hit. PETG or ABS, not PLA (PLA gets brittle in the cold and can shatter on impact). 6 walls minimum, 30% gyroid infill. The plug prints cap-down next to the bat. Wrap the plug threads with PTFE tape, or a drop of CA glue for permanent, so fine sand stays put. Honest note: this is a fish priest, not a demolition tool. Filled with BBs it lands around 550 g total, plenty for trout through salmon. I have not torture-tested it against rocks. Printed one and bonked something? description: SPA Expert - Backpack Carabine Kit Target shooting is a great way to unwind and clear the mind and the UX SPA Expert is a cool little CO2 pistol as entry point into the hobby. It's affordable, semi-automatic, and works easily with CO2 capsules for endless fun plinking. Its low power makes it safe and the design allows for great modularity with add-on parts and customisation. It's the ideal option to anyone looking for outdoor fun. I'm a big fan of Umarex their products because they provide precision and fun at great value, and a great base for upgrading and tinkering. Products » Product universe » Classic » CO₂-powered » 2.4392 » SPA Expert » www.umarex.com This Carabine kit transforms this cool little pistol into a rigid compact takedown carabine. Having a stock improves accuracy and shootability significantly and gives it a nice touch of cyberpunk design. The forend integrates a silencer elevating the little pistol into a complete compact rifle that can be taken down and stashed everywhere. The entire kit is 3D printed and solid as a rock. It comes together with simple dowel parts and a snug fit providing a solid little rifle that can be printed for a fraction of the cost of the pistol. The foregrip has in integrated silencer that reduces noise considerably and the stock really reduces the jerk of the double action trigger. This is a great upgrade for any serious shooter that likes a compact plinking toy or a cool gift for a friend or kid getting into the hobby. With the options 3D printing provides you can customise color and options to your hearts content. Besides the stock and overall look the kit has a few subtle upgrades integrated in the design: Extended foregrip with integrated silencer Textured grips and cheekweld Open window for better CO2 heat transfer during shooting Compact package with the stock removed Grip only version: UX SPA Expert - Custom Grip - Free 3D Print Model - MakerWorld Pictured Red dot Sight: VictOptics SRD 1x18x20 Red Dot Assembly Slide the foregrip part over the picantinny rail and push it all the way to the back. Insert the two grip parts making sure the forend is all the way back, these engage in the botton picantinny rail securing it with the silencer against the barrel port. The hand parts are press fit, but you can use a drop of CA for extra security. Now combine the two stock parts with the printed dowels, use a drop of CA to fix the dowels in place. Alternate the layer orrientation of the dowels for optimal strength and rigidity. Now apply some CA on the dowels and surface, not too much, and pres on the other part to fit tightly. Apply some CA and place the cheekpiece over the stock using the integrated guide dowels and press to fit seamless. This whole three part construction is made to fit tight and have high rigidity when assembled correctly. You can now place the stock like the original grip and you have your own unique little CO2 carabine! Airguns are not toys, use with care and supervision!

description: Log July 29, 2026 The .ino format file cannot be uploaded as an attachment, so the code has been uploaded to GitHub. Please visit https://github.com/tipflowmaker/8-bit-Animated-emojis/tree/main to download it. Explanation This is a new 8-bit model. Compared with the previous version, it eliminates the step of sampling and customizing PCBs, and an independent battery power supply system is added. The hardware assembly can be completed simply by soldering commonly available development board modules and batteries on the market. In addition, the structure and assembly scheme have been optimized, enabling the assembly of hardware components and the enclosure without screws. I have uploaded the Arduino code for displaying animated facial expressions on the exterior. If you have specific requirements, you can also program and develop customized new firmware on your own. My 3D printed model has been verified with the A1 Mini. Given the variations between different 3D printers, I have also uploaded the STP files of the 3D model. You can adjust the tolerance gaps of the model to achieve a better assembly fit. Bill of Materials 1 × ESP32C3 Super Mini Development Board 1 × 0.96-inch SSD1306 I2C OLED Display Module 1 × TP4056 Charging Module 1 × TTP223 Touch Sensor Module 1 × 702025 Specification Battery Assorted Connecting Wires Wiring Reference ESP32C3 Super Mini OLED Moudle TP 4056 TTP 223 Bater 5V OUT+ GND GND OUT- GND 3V3 VCC VCC GPIO 4 I/O GPIO 8 SDA GPIO 9 SCL B + + B- _ Notes The welding direction of the TTP 223 touch sensor is shown in the figure. The touch surface on the other side must be flat so that it can be assembled into the housing. In addition, since no external mechanical switch is equipped for the hardware section, the switching function is implemented via the software of the ESP32-C3. After flashing the Arduino program I uploaded, power-off can be achieved by pressing and holding the TTP223 touch panel for 5 seconds, putting the ESP32 into deep sleep mode. After powering off, pressing and holding the panel for 2 seconds turns the device back on. The sleep mode drastically cuts down battery power consumption. However, the LED power indicator on the ESP32-C3 Mini development board generates substantial leakage current that drains the battery. Therefore, this LED can be damaged using a soldering iron or tweezers to reduce standby power loss. Finally After you finish the hardware soldering work, refer to the attached document for the detailed assembly steps of the casing. Finally, if you like this project, feel free to leave your comments and likes, or give me a free boost.

model_name: Parametric PCB Mounting Tray Generator - OpenSCAD
description: Parametric PCB Mounting Tray Generator Create fully customizable mounting trays for PCBs and electronics modules directly in MakerWorld’s Parametric Model Maker. The generator supports different PCB sizes, mounting-hole patterns, support heights, tray styles and retention methods. It is designed for electronics enclosures, control panels, test equipment, workshop projects, prototypes and custom installations. Custom PCB dimensions The tray can be adjusted to match the required board size. Available PCB settings include: PCB width PCB height PCB thickness edge clearance support height tray border corner radius The model is centered and generated with a flat underside for easy printing. Three PCB mounting styles Screw Standoffs Creates cylindrical supports for PCBs with mounting holes. The standoff system includes adjustable: outer diameter screw-hole diameter support height optional locating collar locating clearance screw-hole lead-in chamfer The locating collar can enter the PCB mounting hole and help position the board accurately before installation. Snap Clips Creates flexible side clips for boards without mounting holes. Clip width, thickness, overhang, clearance and the number of clips per side can be adjusted. The PCB rests on integrated supports and is retained by the clips without additional screws. Sliding Rails Creates two side rails with grooves for inserting the PCB from one end. Rail height, wall thickness, groove depth and groove clearance can be customized. One end is lowered to provide an insertion opening, while the opposite end can act as a stop. This style is useful when the PCB should remain removable without accessing mounting screws. Rectangular or individual mounting-hole layouts The screw-standoff version supports two different hole-layout modes. Rectangular Pattern Creates a regular two-hole or four-hole arrangement using horizontal and vertical spacing values. This is suitable for boards with symmetrical corner mounting holes. Individual Positions Up to eight mounting holes can be positioned independently. Each hole receives its own X and Y coordinate measured from the PCB center. This makes it possible to reproduce asymmetric or irregular mounting patterns found on many real circuit boards. The complete hole layout can also be rotated around the PCB center. Solid Tray or Open Frame Solid Tray Creates a continuous protective base below the PCB. This version provides maximum stiffness and separates the PCB from the mounting surface. Open Frame Creates a lightweight frame with internal support beams. Every active screw standoff is automatically connected to the nearest frame edge, including individually positioned mounting holes. This prevents unsupported standoffs and keeps the structure printable and stable. External mounting options The tray can be attached to an enclosure, wall or machine using optional external mounting tabs. Available configurations include: no external mounting corner tabs side tabs The mounting tabs include configurable hole diameter, tab diameter, neck width, anchor depth and optional countersinks. Their broad connection to the tray improves strength compared with a narrow teardrop-style attachment. Cable access An optional cable opening can be added to one side of the tray. Available positions include: left right front back The width and depth of the opening can be adjusted for wires, connectors or cable bundles. Typical applications The generator is suitable for: Arduino and ESP32 projects Raspberry Pi accessories relay and sensor modules custom control systems test equipment robotics power-supply modules workshop electronics enclosure inserts prototype installations custom PCB mounting solutions Printing The tray is designed for FDM printing with its flat underside placed directly on the build plate. In most configurations: no supports are required screw standoffs print vertically external mounting tabs remain flat on the build plate open-frame supports are generated automatically the model can be printed as one piece Use sufficient wall thickness and a suitable material when the tray will be exposed to mechanical load or elevated temperatures. Important note PCB dimensions and mounting-hole positions vary between manufacturers and board revisions. Always measure the actual PCB and verify: outside dimensions board thickness mounting-hole diameter mounting-hole coordinates required clearance around components connector and cable access screw and standoff dimensions

Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould (2 sides and a small insert for the base) to cast round tumblers/mugs with a smooth sided design. You need to cast plaster in the larger mould two times for the sides, for every one cast of the small insert. This gives a complete plaster mould. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, with most casting slips this should give a final tumbler size of 9cm diameter and 9.5cm height, or a capacity of around 400ml. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 1350ml of plaster for the side pieces and around 180ml for the base insert, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast.

description: Opel Astra H – Dedykowany Uchwyt na Napoje (Cup Holder) 250ml / 500ml Cześć! 👋 Jako wieloletni właściciel Opla Astry H doskonale wiem, jak w tym modelu brakuje porządnego, stabilnego miejsca na kubek czy puszkę. P1S). 🛠️ Instrukcja montażu i parametry druku: Zalecane ustawienia: Wypełnienie (Infill): 50% (dla maksymalnej sztywności i trwałości) Liczba obrysów (Walls): min. 3-4 Podpory: Warto ustawić kąt zwisu (threshold) na 90 stopni , aby podpory generowały się tylko tam, gdzie to absolutnie konieczne. Dodatkowa opcja: Polecam włączyć prasowanie (Ironing) dla miejsc krytycznych, co zapewni idealnie gładką powierzchnię. Montaż: Film instrukcyjny pokazujący montaż znajdziesz tutaj: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LRc1gRT7iXU&feature=youtu.be (wkrótce wrzucę też własne video z pełnego montażu!) . 📌 Zasady udostępniania (Licencja): Projekt udostępniam całkowicie za darmo do użytku prywatnego. After spending hours designing and tweaking, I created this cup holder completely from scratch in Fusion 360, perfectly tailored to fit the Astra H center dashboard. I used to sell this design commercially, but due to the massive wave of copycats and clones popping up everywhere, I decided to release it completely for free to the 3D printing community! Enjoy. 🚗 About the Project: Custom Design: 100% originally modeled in Fusion 360. Perfect Fit: Designed specifically for the Opel Astra H center console – fits snugly and looks clean, almost like OEM. Versatile Size: Engineered to securely hold both 250 ml cans and standard 500 ml cans. Material Choice: Due to high temperatures inside a parked car (especially in summer), I strongly recommend printing in ASA or PETG (the version in the photos is printed in black ASA). Standard PLA might warp in direct sunlight! Printer: Tested and optimized for Bambu Lab printers (such as the P1S). 🛠️ Print Settings & Assembly: Recommended Settings: Infill: 50% (for maximum rigidity and durability) Walls/Perimeters: min. 3-4 Supports: Set the support overhang threshold to 90 degrees to ensure supports only generate where strictly necessary. Extra tip: I highly recommend enabling Ironing for critical top surfaces for a super smooth finish. Assembly: A reference video showing the installation process can be found here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LRc1gRT7iXU&feature=youtu.be (I will also upload my own dedicated assembly video soon!) . 📌 Terms of Use: This project is shared for free for personal use. Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould (2 sides and a small insert for the base) to cast round tumblers/mugs with a Twist design. You need to cast plaster in the larger mould two times for the sides, for every one cast of the small insert. This gives a complete plaster mould. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, with most casting slips this should give a final tumbler size of 9cm diameter and 9.5cm height, or a capacity of around 400ml. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 1350ml of plaster for the side pieces and around 180ml for the base insert, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast.

tags: sand anchor|beach anchor|snow anchor|deadman anchor|camping beac|tent stake|ground anchor|sand stake|outdoor|van life|picnic|pack and deploy|portable|desert|snow campin|basecamp|basecamp anywhere|compression anchor|confinement anchor|dual disc|petg|BAMBU LAB|A1 MINI|no supports|flat pack|fdm printable
description: Why this anchor exists: Every traveler knows the frustration: you arrive at the beach, set up your tent or lay down your towel, and the wind turns your stakes into useless plastic sticks. Sand, loose soil, and snow laugh at conventional stakes. They bend. They slip. They fail. I designed this anchor because I was tired of chasing my gear across the sand. The solution came from studying a classic mountaineering technique called a "deadman anchor" — a buried plate that uses the weight and friction of the ground itself to resist extraction. I engineered that principle into a compact, printable design that fits flat in your bag and deploys in under a minute. How it works (the physics): This is not a stake. This is a compression confinement anchor. Two discs (109.2 mm diameter) are separated by 115 mm along a cross-shaped central shaft. When buried and subjected to an upward pull, the lower disc compresses the sand between itself and the upper disc. The sand, trapped and compacted, generates lateral pressure against the surrounding ground, mobilizing its internal friction angle (φ). The result: the anchor must lift an entire confined cylinder of sand — over 1 liter in volume (1.08 L) — to be extracted. Standard stakes rely on surface friction along their shaft. In loose sand, that friction is nearly zero. This anchor converts a weak material into a solid block of resistance. Measured and calculated performance: Loose dry sand (children's sandbox): extraction force of 8–10 kg-f — already 5 to 15 times higher than a plastic beach stake in the same conditions. Compacted beach sand or moist earth: estimated extraction force of 20–30 kg-f, based on load capacity models with friction angles of 30–35°. Visual proof: when extracted from loose sand, the anchor pulls out a massive sand cylinder, demonstrating the confinement mechanism in action. A conventional stake in the same sandbox? Pulls out clean with almost zero resistance. Key features: Pack-and-deploy: assembles from flat-packed plates into a rigid cross-anchor structure. No tools required. 100% printable: no supports, no external hardware. Designed for consumer FDM printers (tested on Bambu Lab A1 Mini). Dual-disc bayonet lock: discs slide over the shaft, rotate 45°, and lock into teeth — secure, fast, and sand-tolerant. PETG recommended: for outdoor durability, UV resistance, and the flexibility needed during assembly. Scenarios: 🏖️ Beach: secure towels, sunshades, beach tents. ❄️ Snow camping: deadman anchor for tent guylines in powder. ⛺ Loose soil: anywhere conventional stakes fail. INSTRUCTIONS FOR USE Standard Setup: Dig: Make a vertical hole about 15 cm deep (remember: greater depth means greater pull-out resistance). Assemble the cross: Slide the two shafts together to form the cross-shaped structure. Place the lower confinement disc: Slide one disc over the shafts, pushing it down until it rests on the lower locking tabs . Rotate it 45° so the bayonet teeth lock it firmly in place. Bury and compact the base: Place the device into the hole and fill it with sand or snow up to the upper crossbars . Compact the material firmly with your hands to ensure proper confinement. Secure the upper disc: Place the second disc with the locking notches facing up, and rotate it 45° onto the upper crossbars to lock it. Finish filling: Cover the entire anchor, leaving only the tie-down holes visible on the surface for passing ropes through. Advanced Method (Deep Anchoring): For extreme wind conditions or deep snow, use the total burial method: Follow steps 1 through 5, but dig significantly deeper. Before finishing the fill, secure your ropes to the tie-down holes. Then cover the anchor completely and compact. The anchor will work at depth, providing maximum resistance. Usage tip: For tents, use 1 anchor per corner or tension point .

description: I wanted a companion cube cover for the Steam Machine that didn't require a bunch of magnets, screws and other BOM parts to put together. Here is a simple model sliced and designed for printing multi-color with an AMS! If you don't have a printer, I sell these on Etsy for just a little over material cost! https://www.etsy.com/listing/4546580736/3d-printed-companion-cube-case-for-steam?ref=listings_manager_grid Designed with airflow in mind! I designed this to line up with the existing Steam Machine vents and air intake as best as possible given that we are putting a cover over-top of the entire device. The cover does not completely seal the device to the surface it is placed on, there are cutouts on the front and sides to aid in airflow to the bottom of the device (it sits on it's standoffs as designed) Back of the Steam Machine is left completely open for optimal airflow, cable routing, etc. I haven't noticed any issues with temps after installing mine, but you can also remove the faceplate to the steam machine before installing the cover to increase airflow Print Settings and Instructions: Either print it by the plate and assemble with 3D printed dowels (recommend some CA glue or similar) or as a single large print. There is a “Test Fitting” plate so you can make sure everything will fit before committing to the whole build. Supports are needed for at least the front faceplate, I'd recommend using them throughout for the dowel holes. Recommend 3 walls, 10% infill (gyroid or w/e you prefer) If the dowels don't fit you can size them down slightly A couple extra snap dowels are added, in case of breakage during install. Print extra's if you need. Test print should fit flush with the surface and around the Steam Machine, there should be no force required. USB and Power buttons, light bar should be lined up. Assembly Instructions: (if you did not print the All-In-One) You can use the snap dowel pins for glue-less assembly. Front face installs last. Otherwise Tools recommended - clamps wide enough to accommodate the cube, Super glue (CA Glue). If you do not have clamps you can do each side 1 at a time, just make sure it sets as square as possible. Install all faces in one session: Glue dowels into top face Apply glue to left and right faces and attach to top Install and glue any remaining dowels for the front face Glue and place front face Clamp together and let everything set Future Work: Button insert - right now you can use your pinky finger or lift the cover if you need to use the power button. SD Card slot, I had this in during the design phase, but I doubt people are hot-swapping SD cards in this thing, and it was more aesthetically pleasing to have one without the extra hole. (I'm not sure you could easily get it out anyway even if there was a hole, but if folks want it I can certainly add it back!) Snap Dowels for glue-less assembly - COMPLETE Changelog: Revision 1 (R1): 7/27/26 Shrunk dowel size by 0.2mm in length - if dowels are too long for a flush fit, you can shrink them more if needed. description: The Ultimate Ball Generator Create fully customizable decorative, sensory, toy, or hanging balls directly in MakerWorld. Adjust the ball dimensions, surface pattern, hole spacing, wall thickness, colors, custom text, and hanging ring without using external CAD software. One generator. Endless possibilities. Create personalized balls with names or logos, Christmas ornaments, keychains, sensory and fidget toys, bouncing balls, decorative spheres, party favors, and unique gifts. Mix patterns, colors, text styles and accessories to generate thousands of completely different designs — all in just a few clicks. Main Features Ball diameter from 20 to 150 mm (larger also possible per request) Adjustable wall thickness from 1 to 5 mm Airless or solid spheres Multiple pattern styles: Circle Hexagon Diamond Rectangle Triangle Teardrop Heart Flower Star Four pattern effects: None – smooth ball Hole – openings through the shell Emboss – recessed pattern Raised – pattern raised above the surface Adjustable pattern size, spacing, rotation and marking depth Optional rounded pattern edges Optional Seam decorations (basketball, tennis ball, soccer ball, …) Custom text with multiple fonts Two text background styles: Text Outline – background follows the actual letter shapes Plaque – rounded rectangular nameplate Flat, embossed or raised text Adjustable text margin and nameplate curvature Optional reinforced hanging ring Custom colors for the ball, text background and lettering Adjustable sphere resolution for better quality or prototyping How to Customize Ball Dimensions Use Diameter to select the overall size of the ball. Wall Thickness determines the shell thickness when the Hole effect is selected. A value of 2–3 mm is a good starting point for most prints. Sphere Resolution controls surface smoothness: Draft – fastest preview Standard – quick testing Smooth – good balance Fine – recommended default Great or Ultra – smoother result, but longer generation time Pattern Choose the desired shape using Pattern Type . Use: Pattern Size to control the size of each element Pattern Spacing to control the visible gap between elements Pattern Angle to rotate the pattern on the ball Pattern Marking to control emboss depth or raised height Add Fillet on Pattern to round the pattern edges Small patterns combined with very small spacing can create a large number of elements and significantly increase generation and slicing time. Seams (decoration) Use this predefined seam decorations that adds a final touch to your ball. Available now: Basketball Basketball retro Tennis Baseball Soccer ball (football) Custom Text Set Custom Text to On , then enter your message. Choose between: Text Outline for a compact background following the letters Plaque for a traditional rounded rectangular label Text Margin controls the space or outline around the lettering. Plaque Curve Correction allows fine adjustment of how tightly the background follows the ball: Negative values create a flatter curve Positive values wrap the background more tightly The default value is tuned for most ball and text sizes Text effects: Flat – flush multicolor lettering Emboss – recessed lettering Raised – lettering above the surface For multicolor models, download the generated 3MF to preserve the separate ball, background and text colors. Hanging Ring Enable Hanging Ring to add a reinforced loop at the top. Adjust: Ring Hole Size for the string or ribbon opening Ring Thickness for the strength of the loop This option is useful for ornaments, decorations and hanging sensory toys. The color of the ring can be customized in Color section. Best Practices / Tips At first lower Ball resolution to Draft. When done designing try making it higher (only if needed). Please note that dense patterns actually are very good at Draft and there is no need to set higher resolution. Pattern Fillet can be quite heavy to process on the servers but in most of the cases is not needed. If you expirience server timeouts or errors consider turning it off. When you expirience server timeout or errors it most likely means that your set-up is to heavy to process on MakerWorld's servers. Try larger patter or higher spacing, lower resolution. Everything that will make it less complicated will work and try again. Consider the position of the ball when you will be printing it. For example when using heart pattern - the middle part of heart can not face down as you will need to support every patter like this. Thy setting an angle and face it up. The larger the ball is the more render power it requires on MM servers. If you plan going large try less details. Printing Tips Printing spheres is quite challenging and it is important to choose the right options in the slicer. Here are some tips to achieve the best results: Use the generated 3MF when printing in multiple colors. A layer height of 0.16–0.20 mm works well. Enable option “Don't support bridges” Add “Support Blocker” modifier to block supporting areas inside the ball. Rise the blocker a little bit so the base can be supported Tune your “Top Z distance” value for supports Use at least three wall loops for hollow balls. Enable supports when required by the selected pattern and orientation. Build-plate-only supports are usually easier to remove. For small holes, verify the preview before printing. Reduce print speed on the outer wall for a smoother spherical surface. Larger balls, dense patterns and Ultra resolution require more processing time. To achieve optimal bounce, use a suitable filament (TPU, PEBA, other flexible filaments). Important Notes Hole produces a hollow ball using the selected wall thickness. None , Emboss and Raised produce a solid ball. Very thin walls or extremely small gaps may not print reliably with every nozzle size. This generator creates geometry dynamically, so complex configurations can take longer to generate in MakerWorld. Make sure to follow my profile on Maker World for updates and ready to use examples. Have fun printing!

description: 🥤 Universal Clamp-On Camping Chair Cup Holder Never spill your drink at the campsite again! This Universal Clamp-On Cup Holder attaches securely to a wide variety of camping chairs, lawn chairs, and outdoor equipment frames. Designed with flexibility and convenience in mind: the cup holder detaches from the clamp for easy transport, and the flexible cage walls fit standard 85mm cans/mugs while flexing outward to accommodate larger tumblers. Note: An optional print profile featuring TPU anti-slip pads is included to give the clamp maximum grip on smooth metal frames and protect painted legs from scratches! ✨ Key Features Front Handle Opening: Features a vertical cutout along the front, allowing camp mugs and cups with handles to fit effortlessly. Smart Drink Gripping System: Multiple flexible vertical fingers wrap around smaller cans and mugs to hold them securely without rattling, while built-in bottom support ledges keep drinks stable. Advanced Mechanical Clamp: Features a print-in-place rotating nut and guided slot holes in the jaw, allowing the clamp mechanism to adjust smoothly against various rod diameters without binding. Flexible 85mm+ Capacity: Designed for standard drinks while allowing the outer cage walls to expand slightly for larger travel mugs and tumblers. Universal Compatibility: Smooth-threaded clamp easily adjusts to securely grip round metal tubes of various diameters. Modular Two-Part System: Cup holder slides and locks into place on the clamp body, making it easy to disassemble and pack flat. 100% 3D Printed: No hardware required! Every screw, pin, and structural component is fully 3D printed. Optional TPU Anti-Slip Grips: Print profile includes flexible TPU pads that snap into the clamp jaws to prevent rotation on slick aluminum tubes. Outdoor-Ready & Drainage Friendly: Lightweight open slotted design allows condensation and rain to drain freely. 🛠️ Assembly Instructions 🔩 Step 1: Assembling the Main Screw The threaded clamp screw is designed in two halves for maximum strength along the layer lines and support-free printing. Insert Alignment Keys: Take the two rectangular alignment pins/keys and press them into the rectangular sockets on one half of the screw. Join the Halves: Align the matching sockets on the second screw half with the protruding keys, then press the two halves firmly together. (Optional / Recommended) Glue for Permanence: Add a small drop of superglue (CA glue) into the alignment sockets or along the flat mating face before pressing the halves together to ensure the screw never separates during tightening. 🔩 Step 2: Clamp Assembly Prepare the Hinge Jaws: Lay out the movable clamp jaw, the main clamp body, and the hinge pin. Align the Components: Bring the two main clamp bodies together. Align the pivot loop on the movable jaw so it is centered between the upper and lower pivot loops of the main body. The holes in all three loops must be perfectly concentric. Insert the Hinge Pin: Take the hinge pin and insert it from the top down through the aligned upper loop, the middle loop, and the lower loop. 🔩 Step 3: Threading the Clamp Screw Insert Screw: Take your fully assembled main screw from Step 1 and align it with the threaded socket on the back of the clamp body. Hand-thread the screw directly into the print-in-place rotary nut embedded inside the clamp housing. Continue threading by hand until the tip passes through and interfaces cleanly with the guided slot holes in the movable jaw. 🔩 Step 4: Chair Mounting & Final Setup Mount to Chair: Open the hinged clamp jaws and position them around the desired frame tube or rod on your camping chair. Tighten Securely: Turn the knob by hand until the jaws firmly grip the chair leg. (Hand-tighten only—no external tools needed!) Attach Cup Holder: Slide the cup holder's mounting slot down over the mating tab on the clamp body until it locks into place. Ready to Use: Drop in your favorite can, bottle, or tumbler and enjoy your trip! 🔩 Step 5: Optional TPU Anti-Slip Pad Installation If you have printed the TPU anti-slip pads to provide maximum grip and protect your chair’s finish, install them now. Orient the Pads: Examine the two printed TPU pieces. Note that one of the TPU pieces features a distinctive cut or notch along its edge. Install the Cut Pad: Press the TPU piece with the cut firmly into the recess of the larger, static jaw of the clamp body. The cut is designed to clear the internal screw mechanism. Install the Standard Pad: Take the second, standard TPU pad (without the cut) and press it firmly into the recess of the smaller, movable clamp jaw. Confirm Secure Fit: Ensure both pads are seated flush and securely within the clamp jaws before mounting the clamp to your chair. 💬 Feedback & Support: If you enjoyed printing this model, please leave a rating, post a picture of your setup, or drop a Boost ! Happy printing and happy camping! 🏕️

description: I have ADHD, and it sounds dumb, but keeping track of what shot I'm on feels like the worst kind of mental math. description: Storage for small stacking bins. Pick your bin, pick how you want to mount it, pick a grid, and the model builds itself. Bought your bins? The Costco GreenMade Mini Bin and the Lowe's Project Source Teeny Tote are both 4.81 × 3.31 × 2.44 in — the same bin — and the first preset covers both. It's measured off real bins and print-tested. Printed your bins? There are separate presets for the 3D-printed Teeny Tote and HDX Mini Tote replicas , measured off their STLs. These are not the same size as the real tote: the printed Teeny replica is 118 × 78 against the real tote's 122 × 84. Pick the preset that matches what you actually have. Bins hang by the rim of their lid on a pair of ledges. No shelves, no drawers, open bottom — so it uses a fraction of the filament a boxed organizer does, and you can see straight through it. Cells are sized for bins stored with their lids on. The lid is wider than the bin it snaps over, so a rack sized to the bin won't take a lidded one. Turn Store Bins With Lids On off and you get the other rack instead — narrower cells, bare bins. Which bins does a lids-on rack also hold bare? The real store bin (catches by 3.0 mm per side) and the HDX replica (0.8 mm). Not the Teeny Tote replica — its lid is the only part wider than the opening, so a bare bin drops through. Pick the mode you'll actually use on that one. Replicas vary by designer. The two HDX replica sources I compared differ by 10 mm on the lid. Each replica preset is measured off one specific box-and-lid pair. If yours came from somewhere else, measure your lid and use the Custom Bin option — six numbers. Three ways to mount it Freestanding rack — sits on a bench or shelf. Optional solid top, so it becomes a surface you can stack on. Racks sit flush side by side, so you can run a long wall out of a couple of prints. Undershelf — screws up into the underside of a shelf or bench. Bins hang below, every row of them. Screw slots run front-to-back so you can slide to find a joist, and they sit out over the open cells so a driver can actually reach them. Wall mount — screws to a wall through solid strips at each lid level. A single-row unit gets a gusset under every upright to take the tipping load; taller units don't need them. Optional solid top gives you a small shelf above the bins. Customizer Bin — Bin Type (real store bin / printed Teeny replica / printed HDX replica / Custom) · Store Bins With Lids On Storage type — Storage Type (rack / undershelf / wall) · Bin Orientation (long face out = wide and shallow, short face out = narrow and deep) · Columns 1–6 · Rows 1–6 · Solid Top Fit tuning — bin clearance and minimum clear height above the ledge, if your bins end up tight or loose Custom bin — six measurements if your bin isn't on the list. Ignore this section otherwise. Fifteen parameters. Everything else is fixed at a value that works. Print a fit gauge first. There's one per bin in the downloads — 14–20 g, about 15 minutes. Hang a bin in it and confirm the fit before committing to a full rack. Print settings Lay it flat on its back — rear face on the build plate. The plate footprint is the unit's width × height; the print height is only its depth. Every profile in the downloads is already oriented this way. Nozzle 0.4 or 0.6 mm Layer height 0.24 mm , or 0.3 mm with a 0.6 nozzle Walls 4 with a 0.4 nozzle, 3 with a 0.6 nozzle Supports Tree (Slim) , on build plate only Support top Z distance 0.25 mm Material PLA or PETG These are the settings the photos were printed with — 0.6 nozzle, 0.3 mm layers. A big nozzle and thick layers suit this part: it's nearly all walls, so it prints much faster than its size suggests. Print height (the depth of the unit) is 87 mm for a store-bin rack long-face-out and 127 mm short-face-out; 87 / 127 mm for the Teeny replica; 56 / 81 mm for the HDX replica. Supports are only needed under the front brace of the freestanding rack. That brace spans between the uprights with nothing under it — no face angle changes that, so it's squared off rather than pretending otherwise. It's a thin fin at the bottom edge, open to the front, and snaps off. Undershelf and wall units need no support at all. Setting supports to build plate only also keeps them out of the oval windows, which don't need any — they're arches and close over about 7 mm. There's a NO_SUPPORTS rack in the downloads with the brace removed: 41 g lighter, prints with supports fully off. What fits your plate Width, in millimetres, by columns. * is over a 350 plate. 1 2 3 4 5 6 Real store bin, long face 130 258 386* Real store bin, short face 90 179 267 356* Teeny replica, long face 129 257 385* Teeny replica, short face 89 177 265 353* HDX replica, long face 84 166 248 330 413* HDX replica, short face 59 116 174 231 288 345 Real-store-bin rack heights are 77 / 142.5 / 208 / 273.5 / 339 mm for 1–5 rows. Six rows is 404 mm and won't fit a 350 plate. On a 256 plate: the real store bin is one column long-face-out, two short-face-out. A 4-wide short-face undershelf for the store bin is 356 mm — it still fits a 350 plate rotated about 45° , which is how the one in the photos was printed. Filament, at a glance Store-bin rack 2×3 long face 218 g Store-bin rack 2×3 long face, no brace 177 g Store-bin rack 2×2 long face, solid top 220 g Store-bin rack 3×3 short face 378 g Store-bin undershelf 2×2 long face 162 g Store-bin wall 2×2 long face, solid top 217 g Teeny replica rack 2×3 long face 207 g HDX replica rack 3×4 short face 241 g Fit gauge 14–20 g Mounting Undershelf — four screws minimum, #8 or M4, up into the shelf. Slots run front-to-back so you can slide to find a joist. Pull the bins and reach up through the empty cells to drive them. Wall — countersunk holes in the top and bottom strips, at the first and last column. Hit studs where you can. Single-row units carry a gusset under every upright. Design notes A few things this gets right that are easy to get wrong: Real ledges. The uprights neck down to a thin web through each lid band so the lid has somewhere to sit, with a ledge stepping out just below it. On the real store bin that's 5.5 mm per side and 835 mm² of bearing under every bin; 2.4 mm / 315 mm² on the Teeny replica, 2.9 mm / 251 mm² on the HDX replica. Every bin is captive either way — the webs limit sideways play to 0.5 mm, well under the engagement. Measured, not guessed. All three presets come from measuring the actual box and lid. With lids on the fit depends on three things only: the lid's outer size, how wide the bin is just below the lid rim, and how far it hangs below it. Clear height follows the lid. Every ledge gets at least 10 mm above it — including the top row and under a solid top, which is exactly where a bin stops fitting if you get it wrong. A taller lid automatically gets more. Screws you can reach. Nothing sits over a web, where the 5 mm gap between two bins leaves no room for a driver. Oval windows, not rectangles. Printed on its back the windows are horizontal tunnels — an ellipse is an arch and bridges; a rectangle would put 1300 mm² of flat ceiling in the part and genuinely need support. Every published configuration is checked by boolean intersection: bins and lids against the frame, and a clear zone on every ledge. Both must come back at exactly zero. All watertight, all correctly oriented. Inspired by the Teeny Tote and HDX racks already on MakerWorld — this is an independent design, built parametrically and sized for lidded storage.

With this model, you can turn a simple PVC clothesline into a fully functional DIY jump rope. In the video, you can see the rope in action, as well as the complete process from choosing the material and designing the parts to the final assembly Required Materials PVC clothesline with a diameter of approximately 5 mm Ideally with a reinforced nylon core Assembly Normally, I place a lot of importance on using a proper PVC jump rope with a reinforced nylon core. Since my usual favorites have recently been difficult or impossible to get, I wanted to find out whether an inexpensive clothesline could work as an alternative. The clothesline I used is approximately 5 mm thick, also has a reinforced nylon core, and is roughly the same thickness as my weighted rope from Dope Ropes. However, the price is in a completely different league…. 30 meters cost only around 4€ As you can see in the video, the clothesline works surprisingly well as a jump rope. It does not twist, its relatively high weight provides good feedback while jumping, and it works well for regular jumping, fast footwork, Boxer Steps, Double Unders, and tricks such as Mic Releases. Especially for people who simply want to try rope skipping, this DIY rope offers an affordable way to get started. Comparable high quality PVC jump ropes can easily cost between 30€ and 40€, while the clothesline and the printed handles for this DIY rope cost only around 2€ in total. So far, the DIY rope performs just as well as a purchased jump rope. The only remaining question is how long the clothesline will last with regular use. But even if it eventually needs to be replaced, the cost is low enough that replacing it will not really hurt.

description: Its a (semi-overengineered?) guitar pedal replica / pick holder / fidget / desk toy thing. The compartment has slots for 9 guitar picks. The 3 knobs turn from 7 o'clock to 5 o'clock. The pedal has a printed spring so you can push it like a real one. (Though not super far, I'm still trying to figure out how to make springs. If someone wants to remix it with a better spring, cool.) Everything prints in pieces so you don't need an AMS. (There are two knob plates, one is solid black if you don't have an AMS and the other one does have flush down gray on it, so there is almost no AMS wastage if you want dual color knobs.) Zero supports. You will want super glue for most of the features. Prints in only a few hours. Some assembly notes: The six little dots fit in super easy. I used a dot of glue on each of them. The hardest part was getting them off the plate without losing them. The three knobs snap in and then free rotate while captive. You are going to want to push them rather hard straight down. You will probably use more force than you might be comfortable with, but it will work without breaking. I designed this to have dual color knobs. They only rotate the same distance as the real thing, therefore you want to make sure the knob is at somewhere between 7 and 5 before you snap them down. It's easy to tell if you are using two colors, if you are using only single colors, look inside the knobs and you will see where the cutout is and is not. You have a pretty wide margin of error. The two little black bolts are the hinges for the lid. They fit snug through the lid and looser into the base. Still I recommend a bit of glue near the head, so it firmly attaches to the lid while letting the deeper part rotate freely. The spring is asymmetrical. It matches the contour of the rim of the base.

More than 1,200 Mark IV tanks were built, making it the most widely produced British tank of the war. There were two main versions: the Male, armed with two 6-pounder guns and machine guns, and the Female, armed only with machine guns. The Mark IV played a major role in battles such as Messines Ridge and Cambrai, where large numbers of tanks helped break through enemy trench systems. model_name: Midea PortaSplit Condensate Cleaning Tablet Holder
description: For cleaning the condensate tray at the bottom of the Midea PortaSplit. Earlier manuals recommend cleaning the condensate tray with AC cleaning tabs. However the PortaSplit doesn't really come with an ideal location to put these tabs - one might be able to squeeze them in behind the plastic to the left and right of the slot where you can reach the condensate tray from, but I was worried that vibrations might carry the tab out of there. Putting the tabs directly into the reservoir makes them dissolve far too quickly. The purpose of this model is to try to keep the tab above the standing water level, so the tab is never fully submerged. Instead the condensate can drip onto the tablet, and (ideally) drain from the holder immediately. I generated this model for the StayClean Cleaning Tablets, and it will likely not fit tabs that are larger. Ideally print with a water resistant filament like ASA or PETG. If you use PLA, it might degrade quicker, so a reprint every year might be needed. Probably good to inspect it for bacterial growth, and ideally clean monthly. Use at your own risk, I take no warranty whatsoever that this works as intended. It might break your device, kill you, or summon Cthulhu. I also haven't properly tested this model really myself yet since there was currently no need for the AC at this time. I might update this post when I do test it, but I just wanted to get it uploaded in case people might want to try it and so I don't forget.

As a big fan of the Interstellar movie, I wanted to make the black hole (Gargantua) into a lamp. Perfect as a night light or as a reminder of how great this movie is. I really wanted to capture the blackness of the hole, aswell as the gravitational pull from the movie. I accentuated some lines above and under the black hole and used the linear infill method. This created 3d printed lines on the horizontal brim of the accretion disk very similar to the movie (and perhaps real life). I used Sunlu transparant PETG fot the outer spheres. I recommend you test your specific transparant filament with the test plate and my settings included in this project. Tweak as you wish. Assembly: Very precise glueing is needed. 1.Glue the black hole to one of the outer spheres. Make sure the ‘horizontal split’ in the black hole alligns perfectly with the horizontal brim of the outer sphere. (I recommend test fitting the 2 outer spheres with the black hole to see that there is no gap visible anywhere, do not glue 2nd sphere just yet!) 2. Fit your lamp and manage the cables. (Also test your lamp, because you'll need to glue the 2 spheres together. and have no access unless you dismantle it again.) 3. Glue the 2nd sphere onto the first sphere and align it perfectly so there are no gaps. 4. Place it on the foot, light your lamp and try to resist it's gravitational pull! For the light inside, I fit the smallest G9 lamp I could find. My size lamp is added as a negative part to the bottom sphere. This is ofcourse very specific to the size lamp I used, you should measure the size lamp you will use and adjust it accordingly. I drilled 2 holes in the bottom piece for the wires to escape from the black hole. I recommend a warm light. A 5mm negative part is added to the bottom sphere so you can place it on the foot included in this project. If you wish to scale the black hole, keep in mind that you will also need to scale the foot if you wish to use it. You can give this lamp a little extra by downloading other interstellar models (like the endurance I used for photo purposes) from makerworld.

description: Fully printed system to make plaster moulds. This produces a 3-part mould (2 sides and a small insert for the base) to cast round tumblers/mugs with a design based on the future MP for Clacton. You need to cast plaster in the larger mould two times for the sides, for every one cast of the small insert. This gives a complete plaster mould. This print has been scaled to 112% to account for clay shrinkage, with most casting slips this should give a final tumbler size of 9cm diameter and 9.5cm height, or a capacity of around 400ml. With any fully 3D printed mould, you’ll benefit from using a release agent on the base plate surface. I use a generic mouldmaker’s soap, but any product designed for plaster release should be fine. It needs around 1350ml of plaster for the side pieces and around 180ml for the base insert, and you can calculate the weight of water and plaster needed with this tool: Plaster Calculator You can get a much better cast surface, even if your plaster mix is full of air bubbles, by using a paintbrush to dislodge any trapped air from the surface. I would suggest that you pour plaster until the ornament surface is covered but it isn’t completely full, then get a relatively small paintbrush and move it around in the plaster so that you’re brushing all of the details on the base plate surface. This will dislodge air bubbles, and once dislodged they’ll float upwards. Once you’ve finished this, pour in the rest of the plaster. If you manage to avoid adding more air as you do it (just brush gently), you’ll eventually remove all the bubbles from the surface and get a perfect cast. VOTE BINFACE!

description: The BIG WIND is an extreme firefighting vehicle. It was built by mounting two MiG-21 jet engines onto a soviet T-34 tank chassis. The purpose of this machine is to extinguish oil well fires and was designed during the Kuwait fires crisis. This is a 1:35 scale model and is a remix based on the T‑34 Tank Magnetic Modular Platform designed by Bavaria_3D Tanks that is available here: https://makerworld.com/models/2637402?appSharePlatform=copy From this model all the parts from the turret are not needed, also the machine gun barrel Some parts of the model may require some scale model building skills in order to achieve a good result. The model in the images was painted with an airbrush and was printed with a 0.2mm nozzle at 0.08mm layer height which provides a good quality without obvious layer lines. Materials extra needed are some transparent plastic, i took mine from the blister packaging of die cast cars, used for the windows of the cabin. And black electrical wire of about 3.5mm outside diameter that you can use for the water hoses. On the plate with the wire mesh parts no brim was used and the only modification done was to put 0.2mm extrusion diameter, also for the long thin legs of the window shield the fan was manually set to 100% during printing. All the pegs need to be reshaped with an exacto knife afterwards in order to achieve a good fitting on the model The plate with the railing was printed without brim, on the rest of the parts from the other plates a 7mm brim with 0 distance to the part was used. Tree supports on base plate only were used on all the parts The pegs and ball joints were printed in PETG for better resistance For attaching the jet engine to the chassis first the ball joint need to be assembled, then glued onto the jet engine, then you need to tilt the joint at a certain angle and the whole assembly will get into position, first dry fit it, then add super glue on the outside of the socket and do the final assembly. For the wire cage I recommend to assemble it as a separate object and after the model is done it should just clip onto the model, I used no glue for the final attachment, only the pegs in the structure Instructions for assembly are provided below

description: Active Spring-Damped Isolation Rig A Mechanical Z-Axis Stabilization Platform for Insta360 The Active Spring-Damped Isolation Rig is a compact, scientifically designed mechanical stabilization system developed specifically around the Insta360 Luna Ultra . It reduces vertical impacts, vibration, and sudden motion before those disturbances reach the camera’s gimbal and imaging system. Unlike rigid mounts, which transfer nearly all movement directly into the camera, this design places the Luna Ultra on a suspended carriage supported by an adjustable spring and oil-damped shock absorber. The mechanical suspension manages larger physical disturbances, while the Luna Ultra’s internal gimbal and electronic stabilization correct the remaining fine motion. The rig is designed primarily around the Luna Ultra’s geometry, controls, gimbal clearance, and remote-operation capabilities. Its modular mounting interface can also be adapted for other compatible Insta360 cameras. Design Objective The project was developed to create a practical, 3D-printable Z-axis isolation system that could be used across multiple filming environments without restricting the operation of the Luna Ultra. The main design requirements were: Reduce vertically transmitted shock and vibration Preserve unrestricted gimbal movement Maintain access to controls, ports, screen, microphones, and cooling areas Support handheld, tripod, bicycle, pole, suction-cup, and vehicle-mounted use Use readily available hardware Remain easy to print, assemble, maintain, and customise Avoid specialised machining The result is a lightweight mechanical isolation platform that works with the Luna Ultra rather than replacing its existing stabilization system. How the System Works? The Luna Ultra is mounted on a vertically suspended carriage rather than being rigidly connected to the lower mounting structure. The carriage is guided by a bearing-supported linkage and controlled by an adjustable spring and hydraulic oil damper. When the lower mount experiences a vertical disturbance, such as a footstep, road impact, bicycle vibration, or sudden vehicle movement, the lower structure moves first. The suspended camera carriage is allowed to move relative to the frame, reducing the acceleration transmitted directly to the camera. The suspension behaves approximately as a spring–mass–damper system: where: m is the suspended mass of the Luna Ultra and camera carriage k is the effective spring stiffness c is the hydraulic damping coefficient F(t) is the disturbance entering through the handle or mount x is the relative displacement of the suspended carriage The coil spring supports the camera mass and absorbs impact energy during compression. The oil damper controls the velocity of the motion and dissipates energy during compression and rebound. This prevents the repeated bouncing commonly associated with spring-only stabilizers. The mechanical suspension therefore removes a portion of the larger vertical disturbance before it reaches the Luna Ultra. The camera’s gimbal and electronic stabilization then correct the lower-amplitude residual motion. Testing & Validation A preliminary performance assessment was conducted using the Insta360 Luna Ultra payload, approximately 233–235 g, together with the adjustable piggyback oil-damped suspension used in the design. The assessment compares the expected vibration transmitted through a conventional rigid mount with the Active Spring-Damped Isolation Rig during walking, running, cycling, vehicle mounting, and rough-terrain use. The values below are simulated engineering estimates intended to represent realistic prototype performance rather than instrumented physical test results. The suspension was tuned to keep the camera near the centre of its available travel, preserving compression and rebound capacity while reducing vertical shock transmission. The bearing-guided linkage and hydraulic damping provide the greatest improvement during higher-frequency vibration, such as gravel cycling and vehicle use, while still reducing the repetitive vertical motion associated with walking and running. The design also maintains clearance around the Luna Ultra’s gimbal, ports, controls, detachable display, and camera body throughout the simulated motion range. * Future physical validation should compare the rig against a rigid mount using accelerometers, suspension-displacement tracking, high-speed video, and frame-by-frame footage analysis. Testing should also verify fastener retention, bearing wear, structural fatigue, gimbal clearance, and material performance. The current prototype uses PLA with TPU grip components, while PETG or ABS is recommended for functional real-world testing and repeated dynamic use. Test Scenario Rigid Mount RMS Acceleration Active Isolation Rig Estimated Improvement Walking 0.42g 0.27g 36% Running 0.91g 0.54g 41% Ashpalt biking 0.68g 0.29g 57% Gravel Biking 1.18g 0.43g 64% Vehicle Mount 0.82g 0.27g 67% Rough Terrain 1.46g 0.42g 71% Suspension System The central suspension component is an adjustable piggyback oil shock absorber paired with a coil spring. The shock absorber provides three primary functions: Supporting the suspended camera mass Controlling compression under impact Controlling rebound as the carriage returns to its neutral position The threaded adjustment collar allows the spring preload to be changed according to the installed camera mass and the desired suspension response. A softer setup can improve sensitivity to walking and smaller vibrations, while a firmer setup may be more appropriate for bicycle, off-road, or vehicle-mounted use. The suspension should be adjusted so the Luna Ultra carriage rests near the middle of its available travel. This provides sufficient movement in both compression and rebound and reduces the risk of bottoming out or reaching full extension. The shock absorber is connected to the printed suspension structure using two M2 × 16 mm screws , one at each mounting point. Hybrid Manufacturing Approach The rig employs a hybrid manufacturing approach , combining custom 3D-printed structural components with commercially available precision mechanical hardware. Rather than attempting to manufacture every component through additive manufacturing, each element is produced using the process best suited to its mechanical function. The primary structural components, including the main frame, suspension carriage, linkage arms, camera interface, bearing housings, and universal mounting platform, are 3D printed. Precision motion and high-load interfaces are achieved using commercially available metal hardware, including an adjustable oil-damped shock absorber, sealed ball bearings, steel fasteners, and standard mechanical hardware. This combination provides the flexibility of additive manufacturing while maintaining the durability, precision, and reliability of conventional mechanical components. For the prototype presented in this project, the majority of the structural components are printed in PLA , while the handle grip and contact surfaces are printed in TPU to improve ergonomics, provide a more secure grip, and reduce high-frequency vibrations transmitted to the user. For long-term functional use, however, PETG, ABS, or ASA are strongly recommended for the structural components due to their superior impact resistance, fatigue performance, temperature stability, and outdoor durability. These materials are better suited for repeated dynamic loading and demanding environments such as automotive, cycling, and outdoor filming. TPU should continue to be used for the grip sections where flexibility, comfort, and vibration damping are beneficial. This hybrid approach offers several engineering advantages: Lightweight yet rigid printed structure Precision, low-friction motion through sealed ball bearings Proven hydraulic damping using an adjustable oil-filled shock absorber Readily available off-the-shelf hardware Easy maintenance and replacement of wear components Modular construction for future upgrades and customization Compared with a fully printed mechanism, this approach significantly improves durability, dimensional accuracy, wear resistance, and long-term reliability at the moving joints. At the same time, it preserves the affordability, accessibility, and rapid iteration made possible by desktop 3D printing, resulting in a practical, serviceable, and high-performance stabilization platform. Attribution: I was inspired by this model to make this design - Action Camera Anti-Vibration Arm Dual Camera Mounting Options As shown in Figure below , the rig supports two interchangeable camera mounting options that attach to the suspension assembly using the same pair of mounting screws, allowing the interface to be swapped without modifying the rest of the mechanism. The left mount is a standard ¼″-20 UNC threaded interface , where the camera is secured using a ¼″ × ½″ hex-head screw. This option provides broad compatibility with cameras and accessories that use the industry-standard tripod thread, making it well suited for general handheld filming, vlogging, and everyday operation. The right mount is a dedicated slide-lock mounting interface that engages directly with the Luna Ultra camera cover. Once inserted, the camera is mechanically retained within the mount, providing a significantly more secure connection than a threaded attachment alone. This configuration is recommended for high-dynamic applications such as running, mountain biking, vehicle mounting, and other environments with sustained vibration or repeated impacts, where it virtually eliminates the possibility of the camera loosening or separating from the rig during operation. Assembly Instructions (All hardware used is listed in BOM) Step1: Press-fit the bearings into their designated pockets on both side mounting brackets. Ensure each bearing is fully seated and rotates freely without excessive force or deformation of the printed part. Use superglue and mallet if required. Step2: Insert the ¼″-20 UNC × ½″ hex-head screw into the hand grip and secure it in its dedicated recess. Verify that the screw is properly aligned and firmly retained before continuing. Step3: Heat-press four M3 × 4 mm threaded inserts into the screw cover plate using a soldering iron or heat-set insert tool. Ensure all inserts sit flush with the surface and remain perpendicular to the mounting face. Step4: Position the cover plate over the handle assembly and fasten it using four M3 × 8 mm socket head screws . Tighten each screw evenly in a cross pattern to obtain uniform clamping without overtightening. Step5: Assemble the left and right suspension beams onto the common center mount using the M4 pivot hardware . Confirm that both beams rotate smoothly with minimal play while maintaining free movement through the installed bearings. Step6: Mount the piggyback spring-damper between the upper and lower mounting points using two M2 × 16 mm screws and nuts . Verify that the shock articulates freely throughout the suspension travel without binding or interference. Step7: Repeat the bearing installation procedure for the camera-side mounting bracket, then install the selected camera mounting interface (threaded or slide-lock) using the appropriate ¼″-20 UNC screw . Ensure the mount pivots freely while remaining securely fastened. Step8: Apply a thin, even layer of cyanoacrylate (super glue) to the mating surfaces and bond the TPU grip to the handle. And the TPU pad to the surface shown here. Maintain uniform pressure until the adhesive has fully cured before placing the rig into service. Some More Pics……. 😊😊😊 VOILÀ! description: A fully parametric desk cable grommet designed for clean, secure and customizable cable routing through desks, worktops, cabinets and workshop furniture from 16 to 120mm. The grommet uses a threaded sleeve that is inserted from above and secured underneath the desk with a separate hand-tightened locking nut. This allows the model to fit different desk thicknesses without glue, screws or permanent modifications. The recessed removable lid includes an open cable slot, allowing cables to remain connected while the lid is installed or removed. Individual curved snap-fit noses engage with a continuous groove inside the sleeve and help prevent the lid from falling out during normal use. The model is designed for the MakerWorld Customizer and uses BOSL2 to generate reliable matching external and internal threads. MAIN FEATURES - Fully parametric OpenSCAD model - Designed for the MakerWorld Customizer - Adjustable desk hole diameter - Adjustable desk thickness - Adjustable cable-slot width and depth - BOSL2-generated external and internal threads - Separate threaded sleeve and locking nut - Compact hand-tightened nut with grip recesses - Recessed removable lid - Individual curved snap-fit noses - Rounded snap-nose ends - Continuous internal locking groove - Adjustable thread clearance - Adjustable lid clearance - Adjustable snap-fit strength - Adjustable number and length of snap noses - Dedicated thread test - Dedicated snap-fit test - Assembly preview - Support-free or low-support design HOW IT WORKS The threaded sleeve is inserted into the desk hole from above. The separate locking nut is screwed onto the sleeve from underneath the desk, securing the grommet in place. The lid fits into a recessed opening in the upper flange. Its centering step enters the sleeve while the curved snap noses engage with the continuous internal groove. Because the groove extends around the full inner circumference, the lid can engage in different rotational positions. The open cable slot allows cables to pass through the lid without disconnecting plugs or devices.

description: 缩小到一米四尺寸的大疆EV50航模。 大疆EV50是大疆近期（2026年七月）发布的一款垂起固定翼无人机，采用了8+3动力布局，我这款是尺寸缩小到1.4米的缩比航模简化为4+1动力配置，空机大约1.1kg(PETG)建议起飞重量≤2.5kg. 说是缩比EV50但其实翼型用的NACA4412并没有和实机一样用那种超厚的看起来像超临界翼型的方案，并且稍微加大了一些机翼弦长以确保刚好的飞行性能。得益于参考机型巨大的机身尺寸，座头鲸同样也获得了巨大的机身空间，即便是6S2P电池放进去也显得非常宽敞，尽管并不建议用难么大的电池。而为什么要做一米四这个尺寸，很大的原因是为了给打印一整架飞机的耗材量刚好能控制在一卷以内或者多出来也不会太多，另外就是考虑到P1S大打印行程，这个巨大的机身确实是太巨大了。 由于参考资料仅仅是DJI官网的几个图片和一段视频所以也有少量额外的比例失真。 这次我开源了整机基础版的STP实体文件，大家可以根据自己的喜好二次编辑，并且可以直接使用Bambu Studio右上角的整体试图参考装配 490*10的碳管一根，主翼梁 500*8的碳管两根 460*2 400*2 120*2 320*1 140*2 这是3毫米碳棒 机臂是两根12*450的碳管 升力电机座可以直接用这种CNC的 如图 尾推电机座孔位和朗宇2814或者2810是一样的 当然其他电机的孔位也是这个，比如我手头刚好有一个兴耀华2820 当然我建议是2814电机就足够了 升力电机建议使用2801或者3110之类能带9到10寸桨的电机，不建议使用四合一电调，散热不好容易宕机，虽然丑一点我还是推荐用4个分体电调。 舵机需要六个，银燕ES08或者PTK7452的尺寸都是可以的 区域的电设诸如飞控之类看自己预算和喜好了，后舱盖的GPS舱可以容纳280尺寸的GPS模块。 因为现在的飞行报备流程太麻烦，所以暂时我也没打算装机试飞，先打出来看看，也只能期待条件比较方便的模友尝试一下了。

Here is my speaker design, modeled after the Klipsch The Nines, featuring a 200mm woofer.
