Apache Mod Panels Modular Control Panels for Boomboxes, Battery Boxes, and Custom Enclosures The Apache Mod Panels are a set of configurable mounting plates for installing common boombox controls and charging components on Apache cases or other flat enclosure surfaces. I designed these to give builders a cleaner, more finished way to mount a Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger, power button, and charging port without being locked into one panel size or layout. Four panel sizes are included, with selectable component openings already built into the models. Versions with and without mounting-screw holes are also provided. Although these panels were designed to pair with the Apache Mod Box, they can be used independently on any Apache case, speaker enclosure, battery box, control box, or other reasonably flat mounting surface. Included Panel Sizes Triple Panel The Triple Panel includes: 1 × 30 mm component position 2 × selectable 12–22 mm component positions Overall dimensions: 112 × 50 × 5 mm This version can hold a Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger along with two smaller components, such as a power button and charging port. Double Panel The Double Panel includes: 1 × 30 mm component position 1 × selectable 12–22 mm component position Overall dimensions: 90 × 50 × 5 mm This version works well for a Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger paired with either a power button or charging port. Single 30 mm Panel The Single 30 mm Panel includes: 1 × 30 mm component position Overall dimensions: 60 × 50 × 5 mm This version is intended for a standard round Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger or another compatible 30 mm component. Single 12–22 mm Panel The Single 12–22 mm Panel includes: 1 × selectable small-component position Overall dimensions: 46 × 50 × 5 mm This version supports a 12 mm charging port or a 16, 19, or 22 mm power button. Component Openings Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger The 30 mm positions are designed around a standard round Voltmeter/USB Quick Charger. Nominal component size: 30 mm Modeled opening: 30.3 mm A compatible USB-C charger may also work, provided it uses the same mounting dimensions. Charging Port The charging-port option is designed around a standard round charging jack. Nominal component size: 12 mm Modeled opening: 12.3 mm Power Button The selectable small-component positions support three common power-button sizes: Button Size Modeled Opening 16 mm 16.3 mm 19 mm 19.3 mm 22 mm 22.3 mm Always confirm the dimensions of your specific components before printing or cutting the enclosure. Screw-Hole and No-Screw Versions Each panel size is included in two versions: With mounting-screw holes Without mounting-screw holes The screw holes measure 5.4 mm and include a countersunk chamfer so a flat-head screw can sit flush with the front of the panel. M4 flat-head machine screws with washers and nuts are recommended for the screw-hole versions. The required screw length will depend on the panel thickness, enclosure-wall thickness, washer, and nut being used. Component-Clamped Installation Separate mounting screws are not required in many installations. The panel and enclosure wall can be sandwiched between the front of the installed component and its locking nut. Once tightened, the component helps secure the panel to the enclosure. The recessed side of the panel always faces the enclosure. These recessed areas provide clearance for the component locking nuts and help the back of the panel sit properly against the mounting surface. The no-screw version is intended for this installation method. The screw-hole version can also be component-clamped while using additional screws for extra support. Selecting an Opening Open the 3MF in Bambu Studio. Select the build plate containing the panel size you want. Open the Objects tab. Expand the panel object. Locate the opening size you want to use. Change that object to Negative Part . Leave any unused opening objects unchanged. Slice the plate. Check the sliced preview before printing. The selected Negative Parts will remove the material and create the component openings. Important: Nested Small-Component Openings The 12, 16, 19, and 22 mm openings are nested together. When selecting a larger opening, all smaller opening objects at that same location must also be changed to Negative Parts. Component Being Installed Objects That Must Be Negative 12 mm charging port 12 mm 16 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm 19 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm 22 mm power button 12 mm + 16 mm + 19 mm + 22 mm For example, when using a 22 mm power button, make the 12, 16, 19, and 22 mm objects at that position Negative Parts. Changing only the 22 mm object will not create the complete opening. The 30 mm component position uses its own individual 30 mm Negative Part. Final Notes Thanks for checking out the Apache Mod Panels. I designed these to make custom boombox and electronics builds look cleaner while still giving the builder control over the panel size, component layout, opening sizes, and mounting method. These panels pair well with the Apache Mod Box, but they can also be used independently on nearly any suitable enclosure. If you print one, I’d love to see how you use it. Suggestions for additional panel sizes, component openings, layouts, or mounting options are always welcome.

description: 迷你鱼缸背滤，约1.2L水体。鱼缸尺寸11*15*13cm，玻璃厚度4mm。 我想做一个小的过滤缸，因为担心外置过滤漏水的问题，所以我选择了背滤的方式，一体化安装，简单美观。 这可能是你能找到的最小背滤，整合了1cm羊绒棉物理过滤仓>2cm生化棉>100g石英球>珊瑚骨出水口过滤仓，四个舱体。 出水口过滤仓也可以放下一个小型加热棒。 过滤功能齐全，盖板预留了两侧出线孔。出水口有不同款式可以替换。 鱼缸尺寸11*15*13cm，玻璃厚度4mm。这是一个非常容易买到的小鱼缸型号。 水泵我是用的是北极星底吸潜水泵。连接口使用了水泵自带的硅胶管，可以减震。 实测没有噪音。 **注意水位要高于物理过滤仓，且低于溢水口 **注意要先放水，水位平衡后再打开水泵，潜水泵如果没有完全沉水低会有气流噪音。 你也可以缩小到10缸的尺寸，但是水体过小可能过滤意义不大。 水泵是这款，注意需要剪1cm的硅胶管，先套在水泵出水口上，再插入出水过滤盒。 关键词“北极冰 底滤”。你也可以选尺寸相似或者更小的过滤。 **一定注意要先把水加到上进入口至少一半高度的位置，再打开水泵。不然水泵会有进气声。我实测了两周，运行稳定，几乎无噪音。

Parallax - A Modular 3D Printed Putter with Everything You Need Looking for a customizable putter without the price tag of today's premium designs? This project combines the flexibility of 3D printing with design features inspired by modern high-performance putters. The putter head is designed to incorporate removable weights, allowing the player to change the balance of the putter to their liking. These removable weights also increase the mass and MOI of the putter head, providing for a much more forgiving and comfortable feel. One of the key features of this design is its modular construction. The shaft insert is a separate component that bolts into the main putter head, allowing different putter head designs to be swapped without needing to remove or reinstall the shaft. Simply remove a few screws, install a new head, and you're ready to go. The shaft insert has a lie angle of 74 degrees and a static loft angle of 3 degrees to match the feel of many center-shafted putters. The design of the head of the putter has been carefully made to ensure that the center of mass is aligned with the center of the face. Therefore, the design of this putter naturally eliminates the majority of the torque that can open or close the face while putting. This can make it significantly easier to keep the face square at impact. To improve feel, the striking face is printed from TPU, providing a soft but responsive impact that closely resembles the insert faces found on many premium putters. Including the printed parts, added weights, screws, and epoxy, the total mass of the head of the putter is right around 350g. Features Large integrated putting alignment aids High-MOI perimeter-weighted design Center of Mass positioned to produce Low Torque when swinging Modular construction with interchangeable putter heads TPU face insert for a soft, responsive feel Removable shaft adapter secured with screws Designed for commonly available hardware and weights Inexpensive and creative alternative to traditional putters Ability to scoop and retrieve golf ball easily Hope you can have as much fun with this project as I did and get to give it a try out on course! Face Insert - TPU provides a soft yet confident feel when striking the ball. Assembly Be sure to read all the following steps before beginning assembly of your putter! The order in which some of these steps are taken is very important! Print all required components in your favorite colors. Be sure to print each component in its recommended material. Support removal. This step can be rather difficult due to the way the model must be printed, so my recommendation is to work from the outside inwards. I've used normal supports for the flat-bottomed sections to allow for each of the gaps for the weights to be cleared in a singular piece. Press the TPU face into the putter body. Secure it by using super glue or epoxy. Install the weights. All weights should sit flat within the head of the putter when installed correctly. A total of 30 individual 0.25oz weights are to be inserted, with 4 stacked near the face and 2 stacked in all other locations. While removing the film on the weights (making them stick) is recommended, it is not required for the putter to work great. Doing so may reduce noises heard when making contact with the ball slightly but will make it more difficult to remove the weights if interchanging putter heads. Prior to installing the bottom plate, it can be helpful to lay a layer of tape over the bottom plate and cut to size. This will reduce some noise made when putting. Install the bottom plate to the putter head at the 5 holes around the perimeter. Ensure that the side which features cutouts matching the position of the weights is facing the inserted weights. Use 5x M3 x 3/8" wood screws (link provided below for the ones used). Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Cut down the putter shaft to your desired length (I cut mine down to 36in for my height). For a great step-by-step process to complete this, check out this YouTube video: How to Shorten a Putter with a Steel Shaft . Install the grip to your putter shaft. I recommend completing this step before installing the shaft adapter and putter head as there is less time to work and straighten out the grip in comparison. For a great guide to doing this, check out this other YouTube tutorial: How to Install a Putter Grip (jump to 3:00 in the video). Bolt the shaft adapter/insert into the putter head after sliding the shaft adapter into place from the top. Using 3x M3 x 3/8" wood screws, secure the bottom plate, main body, and adapter together through the bottom in the three central holes. Then, complete the installation by using one more screw in the hole near the top of the putter towards the back. Screws should only be hand tight, and do not over-tighten them! Epoxy the shaft into the adapter by applying epoxy to the shaft and sliding it in from the top. The epoxy which is suggested has a long working time which allows you to rotate the putter shaft so the the grip precisely lines up with its correct orientation. My recommendation for alignment of the grip is as follows: look down the shaft and line up the flat part of the grip with the line on top of the putter which is parallel to the direction of your stroke. Once aligned properly, wipe away any excess epoxy from the top of the putter. Let the putter sit overnight so that the epoxy can fully cure. Next step, rolling putts! Calibrate your flow. The gap is 0.15 mm. Over extrusion of 5 percent closes it and the bearing comes out as a solid disc. 2. Set elephant foot compensation. Everything from 6804 upwards is comfortable. The sizes are real These are ISO 15:2017 standard dimensions, so anything designed around a real 6002 will accept the printed one. description: 2 Aug 26 - The ground mount base was accidently included, replaced with pole mount base. Removed “Bird Defender” from level. Update: Added a reinforcement on Level C to allow an for intermediate tension on the 40m element. I've been using flavors of this design for about 6 months and have been very happy with its performance. The SWR on 40, 30, 20, 17, 15 and 12m are between 1.02 and 1.9 across the band. 10m tunes under 2.0 for a portion of the band. V4 of the antenna incorporates a number of changes (V3 not released on MakerWorld): Plates B, C, D and E were reinforced to address creep over time due to tension A new style guy rope attachment was added that is circular and has a small rotating ring (it won't hit wires like the original) Holes for filament ("Bird Defender") were removed because they weren't really working NOTE: If printed in PETG, this design will warp within weeks under high temperature. This is the first version I have printed in ASA. I like building antennas. This is an ongoing project and there have been 3 major version, with V1, V2 and now V4 uploaded to MakerWorld. It makes use of a 12m Spider Pole. There may be more changes to come based on how it works since I post the designs as I implement them. If you want a “sure-thing” and support - I'd recommend a DX Commander. V2 seems to have addressed the deformation of the base, so far. However, over time the upper plates that had tension on them started to deform (B, C, D and E). This release addresses that. It also adds a new style of guy rope connector. The plate style had extensions that can hit the driven elements. It is still in the file, but a 3 piece rotating collar has been added. The hub is in two parts. The collar should be placed on the lower hub (thicker base) and glue applied to the groves on the inside diameter, then insert the upper hub (with "fingers"). The base is designed to use ¼" by 1" stainless steel bolts. You'll also need washers, lock washers and nuts (11) ¼" x 1" stainless bolts (11) ¼" stainless lock washers (22) ¼" stainless washers (11) ¼" stainless wing nuts This uses a 12m Heavy Duty Spider Pole with the top two sections removed. You will need the “stay up” kit. You will also need stainless/marine grade ¼" ring terminals for wiring the driven elements, driven element linking, base ground element linking and radials. (See photo for wiring.) A panel mount SO-239 is used. Note: when wiring it, have the wire make a complete loop (feed the driven elements in both directions). When installing the plates, they can be above or below the “stay-up” clamps. (I found slight tolerance differences in fit on my Spider Poles.) If the plate fits snuggly against the lower section, place the stay-up clamp above it. If it fits loose, place the stay-up clamp below it, and you can put electrical tape on the inside collar of the plate, if needed, for a tighter fit. The Spider Pole mounts on a pipe in the ground. For guy ropes, Kevlar line is recommended. The lines don't need to be tight, they are just there to provide support in the wind. To hold tension on the driven elements, marine-grade shock cord is recommended. For tuning, start with 40 meters. Disconnect the driven elements for all other bands while leaving them installed. Once 40m is tune, go higher in frequency band by band. NOTE: I initially couldn't get 10m to tune. The issue is that with harmonics/parasitic coupling interactions its hard to tell which low is for the 10m element and which is just a harmonic. With all other elements tuned, disconnect the 10m element and use your NanoVNA to do a sweep from 1 MHz to 30 MHz using NanoVNASaver. Save that sweep as a reference. Connect the 10m element and do another sweep. The new now it identifies is the one you would use for tuning 10m. (The 10m element only covers a section of the 10m band due to it's large size.) Related models: I also have a version for temporary use (i.e. POTA). With practice, you can have it up in 30 to 45 minutes. description: This model is the fourth in a series of “Thinline Scale Model" structure kits for Z-scale and N-scale model railroading. The Small Town Station (TSM#04) - This structure is for a small town station that would have likely existed from the late-19th through mid-20th century around the central region of the United States. To see other kits in this series, including HO-scale versions, please visit my collection page: https://makerworld.com/en/collections/15297762-model-train-projects . I designed this model in SolidWorks inspired by a discontinued, but relatively well-known, HO-scale kit that was available throughout the 60's and 70's of the last century. Originally released in 1957 by Revell , the kit was only produced for roughly four years before Revell stopped making model railroad-related model kits. Subsequently, a couple of other manufacturers obtained the product tooling from Revell and I understand that they continued to sell the model up until as late as 1980. While I never had the HO-scale kit, I was able to find numerous photos of the original kit, both unbuilt and in build-up form, and was then able to at least view the general characteristics of that model. While my model bears a strong resemblance to the original HO-scale kit, I created this design from scratch and added my own spin on how this typical small town station might look. Important Note: Before proceeding to print and build these kits, please note the following special requirements needed to produce good results. Also, please read through the entire description to understand all of the assembly steps required. For printing, a 0.2mm nozzle and a clean smooth build plate is required - this model is specifically designed for using a 0.08mm layer layer height and a 0.22mm line width for the Z-scale model. The N-scale model uses a 0.11mm layer height and a 0.22mm line width . This kit includes both single-color and two-color prints - for a single-nozzle printer, an AMS is required . Supplied needed: fast setting (5-10 seconds) CA adhesive with a toothpick or tool for spreading along mating edges; and a selection of acrylic paints / brushes for painting the model (if desired). Tools needed: a good bed scraper tool for removing some of parts from the smooth build plate - I found the bed scraping blade supplied with the printers by Bambu Lab to work well for this purpose (most beneficial was its thin sharp blade for lifting very thin prints) ; and tweezers may be useful during some steps in the assembly. The Print Profiles - Two profiles each are available for each model train scale ( Z or N ) of this structure kit, the profiles differ by single ( P1S , A1 , H2S , A1 Mini , etc.) and dual-nozzle ( H2D and H2C ) printers. Please note that all of the profiles include a number of parameter changes from the standard print profiles that probably should not be tampered with if you want good results. One of the more important profile variances is that I've significantly slowed down the nozzle speed, travel speed and acceleration to help assure the best result printing the detail features of these models - I 've specifically supplied separate profiles based on direct-drive nozzle count because changing the printer of a single-nozzle profile to a dual-nozzle printer (and vice versa) may cause the speed settings to be lost in the profile . I highly recommend that you use the appropriate single or dual-nozzle profile matching your printer capability, and I include the X2D with the single-nozzle printers since its auxiliary nozzle is not recommended for use with a 0.2mm nozzle . Important note regarding the station name: I've included a station name ( SMALLTOWN ) on both the left and right walls of the station. You can choose to keep this name or you can use the text tool within Bambu Studio to change it. If you do choose to change the name, please look for the “ Station Name Left Wall ” and “ Station Name Right Wall ” items in the objects list for the Walls build plate. You should be able to separately select each of those and using the text shape tool, edit the name. I recommend that you only change the size or font of the text if you find that your name doesn't fit within the flat portion of the wall where the name is positioned. After editing the name, you might need to manually recenter the text within the flat portion of the wall. Please note that on these models, the text is quite small and might not print clearly if you reduce the text size or use complicated fonts. Choosing filaments - In my profiles, I've chosen to use Bambu Lab PLA Matte filaments as I prefer the surface finish over PLA Basic . With the model based on four colors as set in the profiles, all of the major elements of the model could be left as printed but there are a small number of details that I recommend be painted to help finish the model (see below for painting recommendations). I've tried to minimize the number of color changes needed on each build plate in the profiles to keep purge waste as low as possible. === ASSEMBLY INSTRUCTIONS === This diagram provides a general overview of the kit parts. The Z-scale and N-scale kits have the same set of parts. While these instructions are illustrated with pictures of the N-scale kit, the instructions are the same for the Z-scale kit. === Painting and Window Glazing Recommendations === At a minimum, I would suggest adding some diluted color washes to give a more weathered look to the structure. Before assembling the kits in the photos, I choose to paint a number of individual details. For this model, I painted the separate benches, the chimney, and the storage box parts.; and you may want to consider also painting the gutters and downspouts (while I chose to leave them unpainted on my N-scale build). Additionally, I chose to paint a portion of the platform base, specifically the fireplace brick and also a number of the walls that might be visible through either the left or right-side windows. For those interested, here is an Amazon link to the Micro-Mark Acrylic paints I've used on my models: https://a.co/d/0fMC2PB2. Note: If you choose to change the filament colors to either reduce the number of filaments or simply to picking more neutral colors with a plan of painting the model, you should consider painting individual parts prior to assembly although adding weathering detail is often done with the overall model built up. Using some paint color washes can help enhance the details while also making the building not appear as it was just build yesterday :-). If you want to add window glazing (simulated window glass), I would suggest that being done either before attaching the walls to the base, or at least right after attaching the walls to the base - going beyond those steps in the assembly process will make it difficult to adding glazing. You also need to consider that if you are painting the model, care must be taken to not get paint on your window glazing so the painting versus glazing order becomes important. I'm still messing around with different techniques for glazing 3d-printed models … either using a clear film/plastic material or something like this clear adhesive by Microscale Industries ( https://a.co/d/0gy3e33L ) that can also be used to form small windows on models (this stuff can be a bit tricky to get it to work right but I've successfully used similar, unfortunately discontinued by Micro-Mark , products in the past. ____ A note regarding these instructions: For this kit, I'm attempting to rely more on photos and illustrations rather than a detailed description of each step. If you have any questions regarding the assembly instructions, feel free to reach out to me for assistance - hopefully the images will be adequate to understand how everything is intended to fit together and you won't have any issues successfully building up the model . The Front Walls The front walls consists of seven (7) parts to be assembled in the order indicated below. Please take care to assure that the orientation of each part matches what is shown in the illustrations. Throughout these instructions, a small yellow glue bottle indicates use of CA adhesive. For the five walls that are used to create the station agent's bay (the center octal-shaped protruding room), start with gluing only the lower portion of each wall onto the supporting features of the base. For walls 1 and 2, there are slots on each side for the walls to be inserted. The front middle wall (3) has an alignment feature. Note: if you find that the bump is possibly sticking out a bit too far, feel free to file it down some. At these model scales, the glue tends to fill any gap that might be created by the bump … I've generally been successful with just holding the wall parallel to the base support long enough for the glue to set up a bit. These two walls (4 and 5) should readily fit flush between the already installed walls. After the station agent's bay walls are in place, I used a glue applicator to apply additional adhesive and made sure that the top portions of the bay is all aligned to create the desired shape. A toothpick can be used instead of my fancy tool for this purpose. The two remaining walls (6 and 7) come next. Take care to use the correct wall for each side - the doors should line up with the gaps of the base supports, this will be important later since the side walls have to align with the beveled edges of these walls. The Back Wall The Front Benches The two narrower benches are placed against the front walls using the bench supports on the platform base. Attaching the Awning Support Posts to the Awning Underside After flipping over the awning underside support structure, locate the awning support posts part along the edge of the underside as shown. Set this assembly aside to thoroughly dry. Adding the Gutters to the Awning Roof and Back Roof Note that each of the two gutters have a different shape with the thinner gutter being for the awning roof. Review these images carefully to help select the right gutter for each roof, and to familiarize yourself with the orientation of each gutter to each roof before applying glue. Starting with the front awning roof … my approach was to apply some glue at one end only, position the gutter and allow it to initially set before proceeding to apply glue further along the roof line to attach the rest of the gutter. Some views of a successfully attached gutter. The gutter for the back roof aligns at a somewhat more angular position relative to the roof, this is because this roof section sits more steeply when attached to the station. The Chimney At this point, you might as well also attach the chimney. Take care to orient it correctly as shown. The Awning Underside installation No glue is needed for this step. The objective is to get this assembly, with the already attached awning support posts, fitted onto the base assembly and ultimately get each of the posts sitting within their respective post bases that are integral to the platform. A bit of gentle persuation will be needed to get the back side of the awning underside assembly past the back edge of the inside wall, and have everything sitting flush across the tops of the existing walls. Take care not to overstress or break any of the posts. The Side Walls Note that each side wall sits partially over edges of the awning underside assembly … you may want to test fit each before proceeding to glue each in place. Take care to make sure that the wall is properly seating onto those edges and also nicely aligned along the edges of the front and back walls, and down flush with the base platform. The Right Side Bench The Roof sections Start with the front awning roof. Make sure that the roof remains flush to the flat surfaces while positioning it as close to the station agent's bay walls as it can get. Insert the center beam into the open slots at the top of the side walls. No glue is used for this step. Make sure that the extending ends of the beam are fully inserted down into the side wall slots. Next is the front roof section with its square cutout fitting over the station agent's bay walls. Take care to get the lower edge of this section fitting evenly aligned with the awning roof section, and the upper edge aligned along the side of the center beam's top surface. Add the back roof. There is no side alignment feature so take care to visually position the roof so that it aligns well with the left and right edges of the front roof. Finally, add the middle roof that sits on top of the station agent's bay. The Gutter Downspouts These can be a bit finicky to attached given that they are quite small parts to work with. You might find using tweezers to hold the parts during placement to be helpful, or you might not 🙂. The location of the back side downspout between the two back doors is left up to you. I note that this downspout tends to want to spring away from the underside of the awning and back wall so I found having the building placed on the table while positioning it to be helpful for alignment while I held it in place long enough for the glue to settle up enough to hold. At this point, hopefully all is well and your station can start to serve passengers. I hope that copies of this model find good homes on model train layouts around the world … if you are careful and patient, you should be able to produce a nice looking structure … have fun with it!

description: Description AuxArc presents the IWB Holster designed for the Springfield Hellcat. This is an IWB Holster for the Springfield Hellcat, one of the more popular requests over the last few months. I've been building holsters for 15 years, and transitioned to 3D Printing them in the last year and have been carrying in a 3d printed design of mine for that time. As long as they're printed in PETG, these holsters have no issues and weather heat well. The Belt Clips are the only part that I expect you may have to print every few months. There's not many printable options for a high wear part requiring the constant flexing of a belt clip, so when I started this I really debated even including them. However, I do use them personally and enjoy them, I just usually crack one after 3-4 months and have to replace it when I get home. That said, any standard IWB type belt clip should work fine. I just hated not to have a turnkey solution for the holsters. So, they work, but if you want a more robust option, they are out there. There are 10 plates, 8 holster options. It's right and left handed versions of the 3 and 4in barrels, with or without the bump for appendix carry. The remaining two plates are the accessories. Belt clips, the holster wing, and a magazine carrier specific to the Hellcat mag, unless you want to customize it further as we're about to discuss. All of these options are also parametric and you can customize them specifically to your needs. Have a wierd comp for your hellcat? Adjust the barrel length, download and print. This holster is also designed to work with the attached parametric magazine carrier, specifically set up to link directly to the holster for appendix carry. It can also work on it's own with the wing if desired. The carrier should already be set up for the dimensions, you simply need to change the angle if desired. Or all of it. Whatever floats your boat. This will allow for a backup magazine, specifically in an appendix arrangement, for those who wish to have a few more rounds. For the purposes of Appendix Carrying, I've added a parametric bump to the backside of both the Right and Left handed versions of this holster, plus a Belt Clip option that can function as a spacer, can be longer or shorter for depth below the pantline, and can be angled to further force the butt of the handgun farther back from printing. The holster is designed to use #8-32 hardware. You'll need 3 button head hex screws 1" long and 3 nylock nuts. When assembling your holster, imagine the belt line running across the front of the holster and the angle you want it to have. If you're appendix carrying, that line should be level, and your belt clips should be level to reflect that. If carrying in the 4 or 5 o'clock position, you'll likely want to angle the holster, and the wing and it's belt clip should be higher than the other clip to tip the holster towards the front of your body. I've also attached new spacers. I'm personally only using one on the right side to help tuck the butt of the grip in, but you could use it on both sides instead of a nut or some other spacer. If you use them, you'll need 1 ¼" or 1 ½" screws. To assemble the wing to the holster, align the hinges and insert a piece of PETG filament from top to bottom, the length of the holster and cut it flush. To install the hardware, start by pressing a nylock nut into the recess on the front of the holster under the trigger area. Insert your handgun and slot a screw from the back of the holster into that nut at the front. Use a 3/32 hex wrench to tension to your desired tightness. Install the belt clips onto the holster and the wing the same way. Press the nylock nut into the belt clip, screw a button head from the back into the nut to hold the clip in place. model_name: Parametric Exhaust Merge Collector Fabrication Kit
description: A free and fully parametric generator for creating custom collectors. Design accurate cutting and marking sleeves for custom exhaust merge collectors directly on MakerWorld. The generator supports 3-to-1 through 8-to-1 collectors , with adjustable tube diameter, merge angle, sleeve fit and extra gripping length. The finished sleeve slides over the tube and provides the required cutting contour, making it easy to mark each primary before cutting and finishing. Choose between two collector layouts: Circular places the primary tubes evenly around the collector centre. All tubes use the same sleeve profile. Rectangular arranges the tubes in two centred rows. Since outer and centre tubes can require different cuts, the generator automatically creates the unique sleeve profiles needed for the selected layout. You can generate either one of each unique type or a complete sleeve set for every tube position. Features 3-1, 4-1, 5-1, 6-1, 7-1 and 8-1 collectors Circular and rectangular layouts Adjustable tube outside diameter Adjustable merge angle from 5° to 55° Adjustable sleeve wall thickness and fit clearance Optional installation slit Automatic sleeve length with a guaranteed straight gripping section Unique rectangular sleeve profiles generated automatically Optional reference pipe for checking fit Optional printable test collector for mock-up and test fitting T3 and T4 turbine flange options Round tube outlet in 2.5", 3", 3.5", 4" or custom diameter Generic V-band outlet for packaging and fit checks Automatic collector trimming for the selected outlet Optional solid, printable transition between the collector and flange Automatic spacing between generated parts Example for a 6-1 collector which will use 2 different cutting profiles. How to use the sleeve Enter the measured outside diameter of your tube, select the number of primaries, choose the collector layout and set the required merge angle. Print the generated sleeve, slide it over the tube and rotate it into the correct position. Trace around the shaped edge with a fine marker or scribe, remove the sleeve and cut slightly outside the line. Finish the profile with a grinder or file until the tubes meet cleanly. For consistent results, use the same reference length, insertion depth and rotational reference on every primary tube. Rectangular sleeve sets Rectangular collectors may require several different sleeve profiles because centre tubes meet more neighbouring tubes than outer tubes. The generator can produce: UniqueTypes, one sleeve for each unique cutting profile FullSet, one sleeve for every physical tube position For example, a rectangular 6-1 collector uses two sleeve types: one for the four outer tubes and one for the two centre tubes. Printable test collector Enable the collector preview to generate a complete hollow test collector using the same parameters as the sleeves. This is useful for checking: overall collector size merge angle turbo position engine bay clearance flange orientation tube and V-band outlet size The collector can also be joined solidly to the selected flange, allowing the complete mock-up to be printed as one connected model. Printing recommendations PETG is a good general-purpose choice because the flex slit benefits from some elasticity. PLA works well for light marking and test fitting, while ASA, ABS or nylon are better suited to repeated workshop use. Print the sleeves upright with the full circular end on the build plate. Supports are normally not required. For best performance in MakerWorld, keep Show collector disabled while adjusting the main parameters, then enable it for final inspection. Important The sleeves and printable collector are fabrication aids and mock-up tools. Always verify dimensions against the actual tube, turbocharger, flange and V-band hardware before cutting expensive material. V-band dimensions vary between manufacturers, so the generated V-band should be treated as a general test-fit profile rather than a guaranteed production match. This generator relies on a substantial amount of geometry, trigonometry and conditional programming to support many different tube counts, diameters, merge angles, layouts and outlet combinations. I have spent many hours developing and testing it, but unusual parameter combinations may still produce geometry that is not perfectly practical or requires some additional fitting and finishing. Always inspect the generated sleeve and collector carefully, test the setup on inexpensive material or matching PVC first, and verify all dimensions against your actual tubing, flange and available space before cutting expensive stainless steel. Feedback is very welcome and will help me continue improving the generator. If you find an error, please send me a direct message rather than only leaving a general comment. Include the exact parameters you used, along with a screenshot if possible, so I can reproduce the issue and test the same configuration myself.

Auto-Lock Paracord Tensioner PIP | Camping Edition ⛺️ Forget complicated knots. This paracord tensioner is designed to offer a quick, secure, and fully auto-locking solution for your camping setup. Optimizing your gear allows you to evolve your outdoor experience infinitely. After all, knowledge is power when it comes to leveraging mechanics to your advantage in nature, letting you fully enjoy the light of the outdoors rather than the darkness of nighttime uncertainties. This 100% original design was built from scratch to maximize structural strength and field usability, ensuring your tent or tarp remains firmly anchored in all conditions. ⚙️ How to Use (The Auto-Lock Mechanism) Anchor: Attach the tensioner to a rigid support (like a tent peg or ring). Feed & Tension: Feed the paracord you want to tension through the outer guide slots, passing under the central toothed roller. Pull the rope outwards to the desired length. During this phase, the roller slides back into the wider space of the frame, allowing the paracord to move freely and without friction. Instant Lock: As soon as you release your grip, the tension generated by the tent (or wind) pulls the paracord in the opposite direction. The friction will instantly make the little roller turn and drag it towards the narrow part of the frame, locking the rope firmly in place. You might give it a little push with your finger for extra security. Release: To release the tension, simply pull the tensioner slightly towards you or push the roller back with your finger to free the rope. 💡 Pro-Tip for the Outdoors (Recommended Orientation) Even though this works in every orientation, for camping purposes, you should orient the tensioner so that the part locking the rope (the roller) faces downwards . By doing this, gravity will assist in locking the rope again if something (or someone) accidentally bumps the tent guy line. If you are using it merely as a "rope break block," this orientation doesn't matter, of course. 🏕️ Key Features Zero Knots: Adjust tension in seconds. The intuitive system allows one-handed operation—a vital feature when setting up camp in the rain or dark. Structural Geometry: Reinforced frame with strategic weight-reduction cutouts. It offers maximum tensile strength while maintaining a feather-light weight, perfect for hiking and backpacking.

description: OctaJoint is a modular, configurable ball-and-socket arm system that allows you to create extension arms with ball ends of any specified diameter, including preconfigured models for the common 17 mm, 20 mm, and 25.4 mm (1") sizes. The ball ends have octagonal sockets and are pressed onto the ends of a fully configurable extension arm that has a matching octagonal cross section. This design offers three significant advantages over other printable ball-and-socket arm systems: Maximum strength: Arms are printed horizontally, orienting the layer lines for maximum bending strength. Unlimited customization: Arms can be configured to virtually any length and in a wide variety of shapes without requiring supports. Independent ball selection: Ball Ends of virtually any diameter can be used on either end of any configured arm, allowing you to mix ball sizes and create adapters between different mounting systems. To create an extension arm, print one OctaJoint Extension Arm and two OctaJoint Ball Ends . Using the provided print profile, either delete the parts you don't need or move only the desired parts to a new build plate. After printing, press the ball ends onto the ends of the arm. The fit is intentionally tight, so it may be helpful to place each ball end on a hard surface and press the arm firmly into it. Adding a couple of drops of CA (cyanoacrylate) adhesive is advised, despite the interference fit. If the fit is too tight or too loose, you can fine-tune the socket size of the ball ends using your slicer's X-Y Hole Compensation setting. Adjust the compensation in 0.1 mm increments until you achieve the desired fit. The system is designed around a nominal 10 mm flat-to-flat octagonal interface , but the final fit can vary depending on filament type, printer calibration, and print settings. Important Printing Note: If you notice misshapen or distorted octagonal arm ends , it may be due to warping/lifting during printing. I have added “Brim Ears” to the longer pieces in the supplied print profile to address this. You may need to do the same thing after using the Customize button to generate a custom arm. Also see the OctaJoint AMPS (30.38mm) Base Plate Adapter and the OctaJoint AMPS Accessory Mounting Plate that can be used with these extension arms. Depending on your application, you may be able to use two of these plates, at opposite ends of an OctaJoint arm, for mounting a component without ball and socket connections. The included print profile contains 17 mm , 20 mm , and 25.4 mm (1") ball sizes, along with several preconfigured extension arms. Using the Customize feature, you can generate additional ball diameters as well as extension arms with virtually any combination of length, offset, and bend angle. Extension arms may use the same ball size on both ends or different sizes to create adapters between mounting systems—for example: 17 mm ↔ 20 mm 17 mm ↔ 25.4 mm 20 mm ↔ 25.4 mm For the arms, this model lets you customize more than just the overall length. You can create: Straight extension arms (any length) Offset arms (any offset and length) Curved arms (any length and any end-to-end angle between 0 and 90 degrees) Custom ball-size combinations Arms tailored to your exact mounting requirements Future compatible components will include adapters for additional mounting systems and accessories beyond ball and socket systems. See my Vehicle Mounting Parts Collection for additional components such as compression sockets that will work with these extensions. Customization Arm Customization Imagine a straight arm along the X-axis of the print plate. The left end will always be aligned along the X axis. The X-Length parameter specifies the horizontal distance between the left and right ends. The Y-Offset parameter specifies a Y-axis offset (rearward relative to the print plate) of the right end relative to the left end. The Angle parameter specifies a counter-clockwise angle (0-90 degrees) for the alignment of the right end relative to the left end (or relative to the X axis). Note that some combinations of parameters might break the model and give you some odd results. If that happens, you probably need to increase the value of one or both of the X and Y parameters. Ball Customization Specify any desired diameter. The model adds about 1% to account for shrinkage. You should be able to use X-Y hole compensation in the slicer to adjust the octagonal opening in the ball if you find you need a tighter or looser fit. Introduction The GoPro Helmet Visor Mount is a no-hardware, no-adhesive solution for capturing point-of-view footage from your helmet. It press-fits directly onto a 3mm helmet visor by sliding over the top edge, keeping the camera close to eye level without drilling, taping, or permanently modifying your helmet. Designed and tested on track, it holds position through hard cornering and vibration while staying easy to remove between sessions. Key Features Press-Fit Installation: Slides over the top of the visor and grips by friction alone — no screws, straps, or adhesive pads required. Universal Visor Compatibility: Fits any standard-shape visor with a 3mm thickness and at least a 3mm gap between the visor and helmet shell. Eye-Level Perspective: Mount the GoPro upside down to drop the camera closer to your natural sightline. The camera body sits just at the top edge of your vision — visible, but not obstructive. Track-Proven: Survived real-world use under sustained G-loading at a local track cross event without shifting or loosening. Standard GoPro Interface: Uses the conventional two-prong GoPro mounting fingers, so it works with any GoPro or GoPro-compatible action camera and standard thumbscrew. Removable: Comes off as easily as it goes on, leaving no residue or marks on the visor. Specifications Overall Dimensions: 70mm × 45mm × 31mm Visor Thickness: 3mm (press-fit tolerance tuned to this dimension) Required Clearance: Minimum 3mm gap between the top of the visor and the helmet shell Mount Type: Standard GoPro two-prong finger interface Hardware Required: One standard GoPro thumbscrew Print Settings Material: ASA-CF strongly recommended. ASA and carbon-fiber-filled variants resist UV degradation and hold their shape under heat and load — critical for a part living on the outside of a helmet in direct sun. PETG-CF or nylon are acceptable alternatives. Avoid PLA, which will soften in a hot vehicle or in sunlight and can fail under load. Supports: Required for the mounting fingers and the underside of the visor channel. Infill Density: 60% - 100%. This is a load-bearing part with a small cross-section — do not skimp here. Wall Loops: 4+ recommended for wall strength around the press-fit channel. Layer Height: 0.16mm - 0.20mm Orientation: Print so layer lines run perpendicular to the primary load direction on the mounting fingers. Requirements Verify your visor is 3mm thick and has at least 3mm of clearance behind it before printing. Fit is intentionally snug. If the fit is too tight, light sanding of the inner channel will dial it in. If it is loose, a strip of thin tape inside the channel adds grip. Test the fit and give the mount a firm tug before every session. Confirm your camera is secure before going out on track. Use of old GoPro Mount for the Nut. It should press fit fine. description: Code and instructions for the calendar are available at my github page: https://github.com/sneakyjoeru/eink-calendar-1872x1404 I wanted to replace my old invisible computers calendar for a long time, because I don't like how it renders things, and that it's resolution is so low. ROSI – Rundlauf-Optimierungs- und Schleif-Instrument für Slotcar-Reifen **ROSI** ist ein kompaktes, überwiegend 3D-gedrucktes Werkzeug zum Optimieren des Rundlaufs und zum kontrollierten Schleifen von Slotcar-Reifen. Das System wurde speziell dafür entwickelt, Reifen möglichst gleichmäßig und reproduzierbar zu bearbeiten. Der Schleifer wird während des Betriebs seitlich nach links und rechts bewegt, sodass der Reifen über seine gesamte Breite gleichmäßig geschliffen werden kann. --- Funktionen Optimierung des Rundlaufs von Slotcar-Reifen Gleichmäßiges Schleifen über die gesamte Reifenbreite Austauschbare Schleifer für unterschiedliche Körnungen Einstellbare Position des Schleifers Geführte Schwinge zur Reduzierung von Vibrationen Riemenantrieb für verschiedene Achsen und Anwendungen Optionale Riemenrollen für Carrera Digital 132 Anpassungen an andere Motoren grundsätzlich möglich --- Benötigte 3D-Druckteile - 1× Basis - 1× Brücke - 2× Gleitlager_oben_rechts_unten_links - 2× Gleitlager_unten_rechts_oben_links - 1× Knob - 1× Knob_Welle_Schwinge - 1× Pressbrücke - 1× Riemen_rolle_RS550 - 1× Riemenrolle_div_1 - 1× Riemenrolle_div_2 - 1× Säule Links - 1× Säule Rechts - 1× Schwinge - 1× Schleifer Der Schleifer kann je nach gewünschter Körnung mehrfach gedruckt werden. Dadurch lassen sich vorbereitete Schleifer mit unterschiedlichen Schleifpapieren schnell wechseln. Optional für Carrera-132-Modelle - 1× Riemenrolle_132_Achse_hinten_1 - 1× Riemenrolle_132_Achse_hinten_2 --- Motor und Antrieb Die aktuelle Ausführung ist für einen RS550-Motor ausgelegt. Das benötigte Zahnrad ist standardmäßig bereits auf dem über die Materialliste (Materialliste ist Teil der pdf Handbücher) verlinkten Motor montiert. Anpassungen der Basis und der Riemenrollen für andere Motoren können grundsätzlich umgesetzt werden. Kontaktiere mich dafür einfach über MakerWorld. --- Schleifpapier Das Schleifpapier wird auf den beiden Erhebungen rechts und links auf der Oberseite des Schleifers befestigt. Je nach gewünschtem Ergebnis können unterschiedliche Körnungen verwendet werden. Für einen schnellen Wechsel empfiehlt es sich, mehrere Schleifer zu drucken und jeweils dauerhaft mit einer bestimmten Körnung zu bestücken. --- Montage und Einstellung Eine ausführliche Montageanleitung mit Bildern ist als separate PDF-Datei verfügbar. Besonders wichtig ist die korrekte Anpassung der Schwinge: - Die Schwinge darf weder seitlich noch nach oben oder unten wackeln. - Spiel in der Führung kann Vibrationen verursachen und das Schleifergebnis verschlechtern. - Für eine möglichst spielfreie Bohrung kann der Federstahl erwärmt und anschließend Stück für Stück durch die Schwinge geschoben werden. - Das Erwärmen muss gegebenenfalls mehrfach wiederholt werden. - Optional können Federn montiert werden, um die Mechanik zusätzlich zu unterstützen. --- Website Weitere Informationen, findest du unter: Link --- Sicherheitshinweise ROSI enthält bewegliche und rotierende Bauteile. - Nicht in laufende Riemen, Rollen oder Achsen greifen. - Lange Haare, Kabel und lose Kleidung von rotierenden Teilen fernhalten. - Die Maschine während des Betriebs nicht unbeaufsichtigt lassen. - Vor Einstell- oder Wartungsarbeiten immer die Stromversorgung trennen. - Erwärmten Federstahl nur mit geeignetem Werkzeug und ausreichendem Hitzeschutz bearbeiten. --- Version **ROSI V1.0**

Made this case for my GMKtec K10 to maximize cooling after adding the extra copper heatsinks to the stock heat pipe and repasting with a PTM7950 phase change pad. It hasn't thermal throttled since. It idles in the 30's and peaks in the 70's. Huge improvement from before when it'd reach the 90's and thermal throttle from basic tasks. PLA is fine, it's not making contact with anything producing heat, the airflow won't let it pick up any heat. I've had it on for a couple weeks now to make sure. I started making this a few weeks ago when I added an external GPU to it, I needed it raised off the table more for the M.2 to occulink adapter, then I decided I was sick of the high temps and set out to fix that issue. I do believe it being raised off the table also helps with the cooling situation, along with leaving the bottom panel off for the occulink adapter, allowing the RAM and NVME to breath. No hardware is needed, though I do have an M3 nut and bolt in the tab on the back as seen in the pictures to hold it together, it's not necessarily required. All you need to take off is the top of the stock case, you dont have to take it all apart. I used a USB to 4 pin adapter to power the 120MM fan, a fan grill as seen in the pictures, and a thin filter for the fan. I'm still working on a solution for the power button, felt that a printed one on the case would be too stiff and not look great, may buy a basic clicker type button online to add to it. I don't really ever turn it off anyway so hasn't been a huge priority, only ever put it to sleep, rarely shutdown. Nice easy print, very little support only for the tab on the back, relatively small amount of filament.

model_name: Kicker KM8 Apache 2800 Spacer & Reinforcemnt Plate
description: This project contains an inner reinforcement plate and outer speaker spacer ring for attaching a Kicker KM8 speaker to an Apache 2800 rugged box. These parts are each 10mm thick to provide a rigid foundation for the speaker on the flexible face of the box. While polypropylene, as an LSE plastic, is very difficult bond to, successful use of these parts has been performed by using Lexel gel adhesive between the speaker and spacer and between the backing plate and the case lid and finally butyl tape between the spacer and the case face. Add the speaker gill to the outside of the speaker and bind this “sandwich” with 4 M4 hex cap screws (approx 50mm long), an M4 washer on the inside and a nylon lock M4 nut. Gradually tightening all screws evenly in small increments, while crossing over X wise to provide an even compression of the speaker gasket and the butyl tape. Clean excess Lexel with mineral spirits before it cures. Scrap off excess butyl tap with a plastic tool to avoid scratching the face of the case or spacer and then clean the remaining residue with an adhessive remover such as “Goo-Gone”. Slightly pre-heating the butyl with a heat gun before cleaning is helpful. There is no rush to do the butyl as it remains pliable through its life. The mechanical binding provided by the mounting screw/nut passed through the 4 screw holes along with these adhesives, provides a reasonable air-tight, water-resistant seal. This has not been tested long-term. There is also the option to add additional binding of the backing plate to the lid using heat set brass nuts in the stock screw bosses at the corners of the lid and fabricate a bracket to connect the backing plate to the screw boss. This has not proven to be necessary in my testing so far. Recommended print settings PETG filament 6 wall loops for strength, particularly the screw holes 45% Cubic infill for rigidness
A1 Mini compatible. Inner dimensions: ~170×140×40. 5 mm thick walls.

description: What It Is The ReSpool Bag Tower is a modular storage and dispensing system for reusable plastic bags. Its structure incorporates the cardboard cores found inside filament refill spools, parts that would normally be discarded after the filament has been used. Instead of printing an unnecessarily large container, the design gives these cardboard cores a practical second life. Each core becomes part of the body of the dispenser, reducing the amount of filament required while increasing storage capacity. The system is modular: add or remove sections according to the number of bags you want to store and the space available. A vertical configuration uses very little floor space, while the weighted base keeps the tower stable during everyday use. Upcycling by Design This project was developed around a simple principle: sustainability should be integrated into the design process, not added as an afterthought. By identifying a common piece of waste, the cardboard core from a filament refill spool—and turning it into a structural component, the ReSpool Bag Tower transforms discarded material into a useful resource. The project balances sustainability with: Practical everyday functionality Comfortable and safe interaction Reduced filament consumption Modular capacity Very Simple assembly An experimental approach that can evolve into new configurations The objective was not simply to make something new, but to create an object with a clear purpose while encouraging makers to reconsider the materials they normally throw away. Feel free to experiment with as many colors as you like, it will look fantastic! Embrace the upcycling spirit and use your leftover filament to create a truly unique combination. Key Features Upcycled structure: reuses cardboard cores from filament refill spools. Modular capacity: add as many sections as needed. Space-saving vertical design: provides generous storage without occupying much kitchen floor space. Weighted base: designed with additional mass for improved stability. Soft dispensing outlet: the flexible TPU nozzle protects both your hand and the plastic bags. Non-slip feet: TPU feet improve grip and help protect the supporting surface. Material-efficient construction: the reused cardboard sections replace a large amount of printed material. Easy loading: bags are inserted through the opening at the top and removed from the outlet near the base. Materials Rigid Parts The base, connectors and remaining structural parts can be printed in PLA, PETG or another rigid material of your choice. For the example shown, I used carbon-fibre-filled PLA. Both PLA-CF and PETG-CF can provide an especially clean surface finish, but standard PLA or PETG will also work well. Flexible Parts The feet and dispensing nozzle are designed to be printed in TPU. I used TPU with a Shore hardness of 95A, although another suitable flexible filament may also work, the softer the better. TPU was selected for the outlet because this is the area that comes into contact with your hand and with the bags. I f you don't like TPU or don't have it, drop me a message and I will provide a special part for the outer ring. The flexible surface: Feels more comfortable when reaching for a bag, does not scratch your hand Avoids sharp rigid edges Helps prevent thin plastic bags from tearing during removal Important TPU Preparation Dry the TPU for at least 12 hours before printing, even if the spool is new. TPU can absorb moisture during manufacturing, storage and transport. Printing wet TPU may cause stringing, bubbles, rough surfaces and weak or inconsistent areas. Proper drying makes a significant difference to the quality of the finished part. Printing the TPU outer ring The outer ring is printed in TPU with PLA support material. This combination works particularly well because TPU does not bond strongly to PLA. The PLA supports the flexible part during printing but can be separated afterwards without permanently attaching to it. After printing, flex and twist the TPU part firmly . The rigid PLA support will normally crack and break into smaller sections, while the TPU bends without damage. Remove the broken support material gradually. Be careful: some broken PLA sections may have sharp edges. Wear gloves if necessary and do not direct the part or fragments towards your face while twisting it. Assembly Print the base, modular connectors, TPU feet and TPU outlet nozzle. Remove the PLA supports, be patient... Glue the TPU feet in the base. Fit the flexible outer ring in its position. Place the first cardboard spool core on the base. Use the printed connecting sections to stack additional cardboard cores. Finish the tower with the upper loading section. Add only as many modules as you need. From a practical point of view, approximately six sections already create a tall dispenser with substantial storage capacity. When building a particularly tall configuration, place the dispenser on a level surface and check its stability before filling it completely. How to Use Insert folded or loose plastic bags (works best with folded bags) through the opening at the top. Folded bags should normally fall through the central channel under their own weight. Looser bags may need to be pushed down gently until they reach the lower section. If a bag becomes trapped inside the channel, use a smooth, blunt tool to guide it down. Avoid sharp tools that could puncture or tear the plastic.Remember tat you can alway detach any ring Remove the bags individually through the flexible TPU outlet near the base. As the dispenser fills, you can either add another modular section to increase its capacity, or print another ReSpool Bag Tower Design Notes The vertical configuration was selected because it offers a good balance between capacity and occupied space. The base is intentionally more substantial than the upper components, lowering the centre of gravity and improving stability. The contrast between the reused cardboard cores, rigid printed components and soft TPU interaction points is an important part of the design. Each material is used where its characteristics provide a functional advantage. This project also reflects an experimental design mindset: test an idea, observe how it behaves in everyday use and allow the system to evolve. Feel free to experiment with as many colors as you like, it will look fantastic! Embrace the upcycling spirit and use your leftover filament to create a truly unique combination. Future Plans A horizontal version may be explored in the future. While the current vertical arrangement makes better use of limited floor space, a horizontal configuration could work well inside cabinets, under shelves or in other locations where vertical clearance is limited. Other possible developments include: Alternative base configurations Wall-mounted versions Modules for other cardboard-core dimensions Additional heights and decorative finishes If you have a particular configuration in mind, leave a comment. Community feedback is often the starting point for the next version. Changelog 2026-07-29 — Initial Release Initial modular vertical configuration Upcycled filament-refill cardboard core structure Weighted printed base Flexible TPU dispensing nozzle TPU non-slip feet

Are you ready to see the world from a little higher through the eyes of a giraffe? The Giraffe Bookshelf is more than just a cute decorative piece. It is an innovative hybrid project that combines 3D printing with Cricut (or similar cutting plotter) technology to create a truly unique bookshelf. Its integrated Shadow Box transforms the piece into a warm and immersive display when illuminated with a simple LED light, bringing depth and atmosphere to your space after dark. The heart of this design hides a meaningful quote between the layers of the Shadow Box: "Reading books puts you ahead of others." These inspiring words came from the imagination of a 10-year-old child and became the inspiration behind this project. I hope this bookshelf holds not only your books, but also your dreams. ✨ Features 🦒 Unique giraffe-shaped bookshelf 🌟 Integrated Shadow Box for beautiful light and shadow effects 🖨️ Hybrid project combining 3D printing and Cricut cutting technology 📚 Spacious shelves for books, plants, toys, and decorative items 💡 Compatible with Bambu Lab LED or standard LED strip lights ❤️ Hidden typography celebrating the power of reading ⚠️ Important Note The layered artwork used inside the Shadow Box is based on a commercial design created by another designer , therefore the original SVG/DXF cutting files are not included with this project. Instead, this project includes: A ready-to-print panel that can be produced entirely with your 3D printer. Customizable cover files so you can create your own unique design. This allows you to enjoy the bookshelf using only a 3D printer or personalize it by designing your own insert. 🛠️ Print Settings 3D Printed Parts Layer Height: 0.20 mm Infill: 15–20% (Gyroid or Grid recommended) Walls: 3 Shadow Box Layers Instead of paper, you can create durable plastic layers that diffuse light beautifully. Simply: Print a flat 0.20 mm single-layer PLA sheet directly on your print bed. Carefully remove the flexible sheet. Place it onto your Cricut (or compatible cutting machine). Cut your SVG/DXF design. This method produces durable translucent plastic layers that look fantastic when illuminated. 📦 Required Materials 3D Printer (optimized for Bambu Lab printers) Cricut or similar cutting plotter (optional) Bambu Lab LED or standard LED Strip CA Glue (Super Glue) 🔧 Assembly The model has been divided into sections that fit standard 256 × 256 mm print beds. Once all parts are printed, simply assemble the joints and secure them with a small amount of CA glue. I'd love to see your finished build! 📸 Share your print and tag me so I can feature your creation. You can also follow me on Instagram (link in bio) to see the design process, Cricut cutting techniques, and behind-the-scenes videos of the Shadow Box coming to life. See you in the next project that expands your horizons and don't forget to design your own! 💛

description: 萌系黑龙/夜煞桌面摆件与屏幕挂件（3D 打印款）完整说明 一、项目主要特点 双形态互动设计： 巧妙的重心与姿态设计，使其既能像趴在屏幕边缘的“监工”一样稳稳挂在显示器上，也能作为独立的立体公仔稳固地站立在平坦的桌面上，兼顾实用与趣味。 超精细仿生鳞片： 尽管是 Q 版造型，但模型体表布满了极其精细的微缩龙鳞与皮革般的肌理纹路，极大地提升了手办的精致度与高级感。 分件灵动大眼： 标志性的超大眼睛极其适合分件打印（或多色 AMS 打印）。黑白分明的灵动大眼不仅是整个模型的灵魂，也大大降低了手残党的涂装门槛。 萌系治愈比例： 采用大头小身子、短手短脚的经典 Q 版拟人化比例，配合充满好奇的无辜神态，能瞬间融化打工人的心。 二、适用场景 & 适配人群 适用场景 电脑桌面 Setup： 绝佳的显示器屏幕挂件或机箱内部装饰，为冰冷的数码办公空间增添一丝奇幻与温馨。 车载治愈萌物： 配合无痕胶固定在车载中控台或屏幕上方，陪伴你的每一次出行。 潮玩盲盒展示： 独立站立姿态极其适合摆放在展示柜中，与其他动漫手办或盲盒完美契合。 适配人群 奇幻动画/萌宠爱好者： 对《驯龙高手》等奇幻 IP 中忠诚、可爱的龙形生物毫无抵抗力的玩家。 办公桌“软装”达人： 喜欢用各种治愈系小物件打造个性化工位、缓解工作压力的上班族。 3D 打印手办玩家： 追求高精度皮肤质感表现，喜欢给模型进行眼部点睛涂装的手工爱好者。 三、3D 打印设置（0.4mm 标准喷嘴通用参数） 为了完美还原极其细密的皮肤鳞片，确保这只小黑龙拥有高级的手办质感，建议参考以下切片参数： 层高（Layer Height）： 强烈建议使用 0.12mm - 0.16mm。头顶与背部等平缓的圆弧区域建议开启“动态层高（Adaptive Layers）”，以彻底消除顶部的等高线台阶。 墙数量 / 外轮廓（Walls / Perimeters）： 3 层。多层外墙能让表面的微小鳞片起伏更加立体扎实。 填充率（Infill）： 10% - 15%。推荐使用 聚 Gyroid（陀螺仪） 填充。若打算将其主要作为屏幕挂件，较低的填充率能减轻整体重量，使其挂在屏幕上时重心更稳。 打印速度： 外部可见区域（Outer Wall）建议降速控制在 40-60 mm/s，慢速不仅能大幅提升哑光耗材的表面光泽一致性，还能确保每一片微小的鳞片细节不糊、不拉丝。 四、补充打印 & 组装建议 尺寸缩放参考： 屏幕挂件款（80–100mm）： 专门为显示器定制的最佳尺寸，不挡视线，小巧灵动。 (注：缩放前请先使用卡尺测量您显示器边框的厚度，确保缩放后龙爪与身体的间隙能够刚好卡住您的屏幕边缘) 。 桌面标准款（120–150mm）： 适合作为独立的手办摆件放在鼠标垫旁或书架上，体表的鳞片细节表现力最强。 超大镇宅款（180mm以上）： 适合拥有大尺寸打印机的玩家，极致放大后的鳞片犹如真实的爬行动物皮肤般震撼。 耗材与色彩推荐： 强烈建议使用哑光黑（Matte Black） 或带有极细微闪粉的 星空黑（Galaxy Black）耗材打印主体，能完美过滤掉廉价的塑料反光，复刻出深邃的高级皮革质感。 眼睛涂装/点睛小贴士： 如果是单色打印，眼睛部分可以用丙烯马克笔（白色打底，黑色画瞳孔）轻松涂装。强烈建议在纯黑的瞳孔边缘点上一抹白色的“高光”，这能让整只小龙瞬间注入灵魂，眼神变得极其清澈灵动。 屏幕安全固定技巧： 虽然模型设计有卡住屏幕的物理结构，但为了防止不小心触碰导致其掉落摔坏，建议在挂上屏幕时，在龙的腹部或前爪内侧贴一小粒蓝丁胶（Blu-Tack）或透明无痕纳米胶，既稳固又绝对不会损伤显示器屏幕。

description: Why I Made This My cat has a very simple life philosophy: If it isn't edible, it isn't interesting. The only thing that gets him running is chicken freeze-dried treats. Whenever I'm home, I toss treats across the room so he has to chase them. I like to imagine it taps into his little hunter instincts, and judging by his enthusiasm, I'd say it works. That got me thinking… How could I design this so he could keep playing his little “hunt for food” game when I'm not home or can't play with him, and still enjoy it on his own? So I designed this pet interactive treat launcher. No electronics, no batteries - just paws, springs, and determination. What's Included Two Versions Included I've uploaded two versions of the model: Clean version - smooth exterior with no decorations. It prints perfectly without AMS. Mecha version - simple surface details for a little extra personality. Without AMS, some patterns and text may not be fully displayed as intended. Model Components The launcher consists of 9 printable parts , from left to right, they are: Base Left shell Treat tray with integrated paw pedal Spring stop Right shell Spring Spring lock Lid Launch port insert You'll also need 10 round magnets and glue or double-sided tape for fixing the magnets. The magnet pockets are designed as: Diameter: 5.2mm Depth: 2.2mm Refer to this dimension to choose the appropriate size of round magnets. Printing & Assembly Notes For printing, I recommend using PETG for the spring and spring lock , since they need good toughness and durability. The other parts can be printed in PLA. Before installing the magnets, make sure to double-check their polarity so the two shell halves will attract each other after assembly instead of repelling. After the pedal is released, it hits the shell and can make a fairly loud “clack”. To reduce the noise, I recommend adding a small silicone pad or sponge pad where the pedal contacts the shell. I also recommend adding anti-slip feet underneath the base. Otherwise, when the pedal is pressed, the whole launcher may slide forward. Since I mainly use chicken freeze-dried treats (about 15mm cube size), the default launch port insert I designed has a 20mm(W) × 40mm(L) opening, which works well for larger treats. I also designed an alternative version with a 15mm(W) × 40 mm(L) opening, which is better suited for smaller treats around 10mm. You can simply choose the version that best matches your treats when printing. In addition, depending on the size and weight of the treats, as well as how difficult you want the game to be for your pet (whether treats should be launched easily every time or require more patience and effort), you can fine-tune the behavior by rotating the launch port insert to adjust the launch position. If you want even more customization later, you can also easily redesign or modify the launch port geometry directly in Bambu Studio. Real-World Testing (AKA: Pets Are Creative) Now for the honest part… This isn't one of those toys that every pet instantly understands. Expect a little teaching and encouragement at first. And once they do figure it out… they'll probably invent ways to completely ignore your intended design… So here's one piece of wisdom from experience: Secure the launcher to the floor if you can. I'm still observing whether, after blocking off every other possible workaround, he will eventually learn to use the pedal to launch treats. If your furry little problem solver spends ten minutes carefully studying this machine, experimenting with different strategies, and plotting increasingly ridiculous ways to steal a treat… I'm really happy that the launcher has already done part of what I hoped for - getting even the laziest furry friends moving, thinking, and hopefully making their alone time a little more fun.

model_name: Letrero de Nombre Cursivo con Corazón
description: ¡Hola! 👋 Este letrero personalizado te permite escribir cualquier nombre (¡o hasta dos nombres juntos! 💑) en una preciosa tipografía cursiva, con la opción de añadir un corazón y unas colas decorativas que le dan un toque súper especial y romántico. Perfecto para regalar, decorar una estantería o sorprender a alguien especial 🎁✨ 🔤 ¿Cómo escribo el nombre? Solo tienes que escribir el texto en el parámetro texto . Puedes usar mayúsculas y minúsculas sin problema para las letras normales 😊 ⚠️ Importante: las colas decorativas (inicio, final y el corazón) solo funcionan con letras en minúscula . Si escribes una letra en mayúscula donde debería ir una cola, esa letra se quedará "normal", sin la colita. Así que, si quieres el efecto completo, ¡escribe el nombre todo en minúscula! (ej: "aurora" en vez de "Aurora") 💕 ¿Cómo pongo el corazón entre dos nombres? ¡Súper fácil! Solo escribe los dos nombres separados por un espacio , por ejemplo: "oscar giu". El sistema detecta automáticamente el espacio y coloca ahí el corazón, uniendo las dos palabras de forma preciosa 🥰 No hace falta escribir ningún símbolo especial, ¡el espacio ya hace toda la magia! 🪢 ¿Qué son las colas de inicio y final? Son dos pequeños adornos decorativos (una especie de rúbrica caligráfica) que se añaden antes de la primera letra y después de la última letra de todo el texto, dándole un acabado mucho más elegante y "hecho a mano" ✍️ activar_adorno_inicio ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva la cola antes de la primera letra activar_adorno_final ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva la cola después de la última letra activar_corazon_espacio ✅/❌ — activa o desactiva el corazón en el espacio entre nombres Recuerda: estas 3 opciones solo se aplican si la letra correspondiente (primera, última, o la de antes del espacio) es minúscula 🔡 ⚙️ Todos los parámetros que puedes personalizar 📏 Tamaño ancho_deseado_letrero — el ancho total del letrero en mm; las letras se ajustan solas para que el texto entero mida justo esto, sea cual sea el nombre 📐 ✏️ Texto texto — el nombre o los nombres que quieres grabar (recuerda: minúsculas para el efecto completo de colas) 🖋️ grosor_texto — el grosor (altura en Z) del relieve de las letras, en mm 🔼 💕 Adornos especiales activar_adorno_inicio — cola decorativa al principio del texto activar_adorno_final — cola decorativa al final del texto activar_corazon_espacio — corazón automático en el espacio entre dos nombres 🧱 Base contorno_base — grosor del borde/marco sólido alrededor de las letras, en mm grosor_base — grosor de la base, en mm (con un valor alto, ej. 50mm, el letrero se sostiene solo de pie sin necesitar agujeros de montaje) 🧍 🕳️ Parches Tapahuecos (por si alguna letra deja huecos sueltos, como en la "o" o la "a") activar_parche_izquierdo / activar_parche_derecho / activar_parche_centro — activa cada parche donde lo necesites parche_izq_x / _y, parche_der_x / _y, parche_cen_x / _y — posición de cada parche (mm) radio_parche_izq / _der / _cen — tamaño (radio) de cada parche, en mm 🎨 Colores color_base — color del cuerpo/base del letrero color_texto — color del relieve de las letras (colores disponibles: Rojo, Amarillo, Rosa, Verde, Azul, Naranja, Morado, Negro, Blanco, Gris) ¡Espero que te encante el resultado! 💖 Si tienes dudas al generar tu nombre personalizado, no dudes en preguntar 😊🖨️ Hi! 👋 This personalized sign lets you write any name (or even two names together! 💑) in a beautiful cursive font, with the option to add a heart and decorative tails for a super special and romantic touch. Perfect for a gift, decorating a shelf, or surprising someone special 🎁✨ 🔤 How do I write the name? Just type the text in the text field. You can use uppercase and lowercase letters without any problem 😊 ⚠️ Important: the decorative tails (start, end, and heart) only work with lowercase letters. If you type a capital letter where a tail should be, that letter will remain "normal," without the tail. So, if you want the full effect, write the name all in lowercase! (e.g., "aurora" instead of "Aurora") 💕 How do I add the heart between two names? Super easy! Just type the two names separated by a space, for example: "oscar giu". The system automatically detects the space and places the heart there, beautifully joining the two words 🥰 No need to type any special symbols, the space does all the magic! 🪢 What are the start and end tails? These are two small decorative flourishes (a kind of calligraphic signature) that are added before the first and last letters of the text, giving it a much more elegant and "handmade" finish ✍️ activate_flourish_beginning ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the flourish before the first letter activate_flourish_end ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the flourish after the last letter activate_heart_space ✅/❌ — activates or deactivates the heart in the space between names Remember: these 3 options only apply if the corresponding letter (first, last, or the one before the space) is lowercase 🔡 ⚙️ All the parameters you can customize 📏 Size desired_flag_width — the total width of the flag in mm; The letters automatically adjust so the entire text measures exactly this, whatever the name 📐 ✏️ Text text — the name or names you want engraved (remember: lowercase for the full tail effect) 🖋️ text_thickness — the thickness (Z-height) of the letter relief, in mm 🔼 💕 Special Embellishments activate_embellishment_start — decorative tail at the beginning of the text activate_embellishment_end — decorative tail at the end of the text activate_heart_space — automatic heart in the space between two names 🧱 Base base_outline — thickness of the solid border/frame around the letters, in mm base_thickness — thickness of the base, in mm (with a high value, e.g., 50mm, the sign stands on its own without needing mounting holes) 🧍 🕳️ Patches Filler letters (in case any letters leave gaps, like in the "o" or the "a") activate_left_patch / activate_right_patch / activate_center_patch — activate each patch where you need it left_patch_x / _y, right_patch_x / _y, center_patch_x / _y — position of each patch (mm) left_patch_radius / right_patch_radius / _center_patch — size (radius) of each patch, in mm 🎨 Colors base_color — color of the body/base of the sign text_color — color of the letter relief (Available colors: Red, Yellow, Pink, Green, Blue, Orange, Purple, Black, White, Gray) I hope you love the result! 💖 If you have any questions while creating your personalized name, don't hesitate to ask 😊🖨️

Easy Plug Puller for EU Type E/F A simple two-part lever designed to make tight electrical plugs easier to remove. Instead of pulling hard on the cable or repeatedly rocking the plug, press the large rounded lever to help release the plug with less effort. The mechanism can remain permanently fitted to the plug and is particularly useful for low wall outlets, tight sockets and plugs that are difficult to grip. For low outlets, the large lever can also be pressed with a socked foot in a dry environment. This accessory may be particularly helpful for older adults and for people with arthritis, reduced grip strength, limited hand mobility or other difficulties handling tight electrical plugs. By using a large lever, it reduces the need for a strong pinch grip and can make everyday unplugging more comfortable. Main features Makes tight plugs easier to remove Helps avoid pulling directly on the electrical cable Helps reduce the pulling effort applied to the wall outlet May help users with reduced grip strength or limited hand dexterity Large lever designed for easier hand or foot operation Remains fitted to the plug after use Works with straight and angled plug bodies Two fully 3D-printed parts Clip-together assembly No glue, screws or additional hardware Printable in PETG or PLA Only approximately 12 g of filament Approximately 32 minutes of model printing time Compatibility Tested with European: Type E plugs Type F plugs CEE 7/7 plugs Straight plug bodies Angled plug bodies It has been tested with plugs used on extension leads, power strips, kettles and other household appliances.
