description: # 🌿 Plumeria Frangipani Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Wer schon einmal dekorative Pflanzentöpfe mit aufwendigen Blattmotiven skaliert hat, kennt das Problem: Wandstärken verändern sich, Details werden unsauber und das Design verliert an Wirkung. Deshalb erhältst du hier vier separat angepasste Größen, die jeweils speziell für ihre Größe optimiert wurden. Jeder Topf trägt ein plastisch ausgearbeitetes **Frangipania**, das besonders bei einfarbigen Drucken hervorragend zur Geltung kommt und den Töpfen ihren charakteristischen Look verleiht. --- # 💧 Selbstbewässerungssystem Alle Größen wurden für die Nutzung als Selbstbewässerungstopf ausgelegt. Der eigentliche Pflanztopf sitzt im oberen Bereich. Darunter befindet sich ein separates Wasserreservoir. Über einen Kapillardocht, der durch die Bodenöffnungen des Orchideen- oder Aroid-Topfes geführt wird, kann die Pflanze selbstständig Wasser aus dem Reservoir aufnehmen. Dadurch wird eine gleichmäßige Wasserversorgung ermöglicht und die Gießintervalle können deutlich verlängert werden. Bei allen Größen wurde darauf geachtet, dass die Innentöpfe bequem von oben entnommen werden können, ohne im Topfinneren hantieren zu müssen. --- # 👀 Sichtfenster (optional) Auf der Rückseite befindet sich ein Sichtfenster, durch das sich Wasserstand und Wurzelentwicklung bequem kontrollieren lassen, ohne den Innentopf herausnehmen zu müssen. Das Sichtfenster ist als optionales Negativ ausgeführt und kann im Bambu Studio bei Bedarf aktiviert oder deaktiviert werden. ### Mit Sichtfenster ✅ Kontrolle des Wasserstands ✅ Kontrolle der Wurzelentwicklung ✅ Ideal für Orchideen, Alocasien und andere Aroid-Pflanzen ### Ohne Sichtfenster ✅ Geschlossene Außenwand ✅ Nutzung als Dekoration ✅ Nutzung als Vase ✅ Nutzung als Stiftehalter ✅ Nutzung als allgemeines Aufbewahrungsgefäß --- # 📏 Größen ## Größe S * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **100 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe M * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **7,6 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **200 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Einfaches Einsetzen und Herausnehmen des Innentopfes --- ## Größe L * Passend für einen klaren Orchideentopf mit **9 cm Durchmesser** * Wasserreservoir: **400 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Orchideentopf geführt werden * Ideal für größere Pflanzen mit höherem Wasserbedarf --- ## Größe XL * Passend für einen **10 cm Aroid-Topf** * Der Aroid-Topf ist tiefer und ragt bewusst leicht über den oberen Rand hinaus * Dadurch lässt sich der Innentopf besonders komfortabel entnehmen * Wasserreservoir: **500 ml Kunststoffbecher** * Kapillardocht kann problemlos durch den Aroid-Topf geführt werden zum Beispiel: Becher: https://amzn.eu/d/01GtIsBM https://www.variegata.de/produkt/toepfchen-der-toepfe/ AROID TÖPFE https://www.sybotanica.com/de-de/products/dursichtiger-plfanzentopf S und m 9 cm Klarsicht-Orchideentopf https://www.obi.de/p/2807519/ --- # ⚠️ Wichtiger Hinweis Die Druckdateien enthalten ausschließlich die dekorativen Außentöpfe. description: Bring a warm Halloween glow into your home with the GlowPaws LED Tealight Holder Collection ! Each design features an adorable animal peeking over a classic jack-o’-lantern while the light shines beautifully through the carved pumpkin face. This allows you to switch the light on and off directly from underneath without removing it from the holder. An additional print profile is also included with a Twist-Lock Bottom featuring an integrated Light Tube . This version uses the same Twist-Lock system but adds a Light Tube that helps keep non-Bambu LED tea lights centered, hides the light from direct view, and creates a softer, warmer, and more atmospheric glow. Both Twist-Lock Bottom versions are fully compatible with the Bambu Lab LED Tea Light . If your LED tea light is operated by a remote control or built-in timer , there is no need to access the switch manually. If you want to slice the files yourself, make sure to print all threaded parts (tealight version) with 0.16mm layer height. The solid shade was designed to be printed with vase mode. If you use translucent filament, you can also use the thicker shade for a frosted glass effect. If you print the shade in vase mode on an open printer (A1 series), the shade can slightly deform. This depends heavily on the ambient temperature and the filament being used. model_name: Türstopper - Hält die Tür, bis du ihn trittst!
description: It’s not uncommon for a stiff breeze to blow through an open patio door, causing doors to slam shut. Meanwhile, a little one might be crawling on the floor, finding the door fascinating—only to quickly get their fingers caught in the hinge or the gap at the bottom. Or perhaps you just want the door to stay open while carrying dishes back and forth between the kitchen and dining room. The stopper is 3 millimeters high, so you need at least that much clearance—plus the thickness of the adhesive—under your door. That’s why I designed this great door stopper. It attaches at the spot where you want the door to stay open (using double-sided tape, hot glue, etc., or two screws; both versions are pre-sliced). When you move the door over the stopper, the raised section prevents it from swinging back. The door can only be closed or moved again once you press that raised part down—either by hand or with your foot. In our case, this ensures safety, as our baby can't simply move the door and get their fingers trapped while exploring the house. While similar solutions exist, I focused on keeping this design simple, ensuring the curves are just right, and making it durable enough not to break—provided it’s used properly and not handled roughly. Please make sure to print the door stopper using PETG so it functions optimally and doesn't break. PLA is too rigid to withstand the constant up-and-down movement or the stress of a door being pulled shut with a bit of force. Enjoy the product—feel free to leave a boost and give me some feedback!

description: Bring a warm Halloween glow into your home with the GlowPaws LED Tealight Holder Collection ! Each design features an adorable animal peeking over a classic jack-o’-lantern while the light shines beautifully through the carved pumpkin face. Because the LED tealight is inserted from underneath, the light is contained inside the pumpkin, creating a much brighter and more dramatic glow through the eyes, nose and mouth—even when the room isn’t completely dark. Every model includes a Twist-Lock Bottom , making the collection both practical and highly versatile. The design can be used with all kinds of tea lights, with max. dimensions of around 1.89inch diameter and 1.57inch height. 🔥 Twist-Lock Bottom System Every model includes the Standard Twist-Lock Bottom , specifically designed for the Bambu Lab LED Tea Light (Ø 37.2 mm / 1.46 in) . The LED tea light clicks securely into the bottom piece. The complete bottom is then inserted into the holder and twisted into place. This allows you to switch the light on and off directly from underneath without removing it from the holder. An additional print profile is also included with a Twist-Lock Bottom featuring an integrated Light Tube . This version uses the same Twist-Lock system but adds a Light Tube that helps keep non-Bambu LED tea lights centered, hides the light from direct view, and creates a softer, warmer, and more atmospheric glow. Both Twist-Lock Bottom versions are fully compatible with the Bambu Lab LED Tea Light . If your LED tea light is operated by a remote control or built-in timer , there is no need to access the switch manually. In that case, both bottoms can also be used with LED tea lights up to 48 mm (1.89 in) in diameter. For other LED tea lights, simply leave the Twist-Lock Bottom off and place the tealight holder directly over the light. ✨ Features Cute animal-themed Halloween LED tealight holder Fully enclosed pumpkin for a brighter lighting effect Jack-o’-lantern face glows beautifully from within Compatible with many LED tea lights Easy to print with clean FDM-friendly geometry Perfect seasonal home decoration ⚠️ Important Note LED tea lights only. description: LumaForge – Customizable LED Lamp Generator Version: 1.2.0 LumaForge is a MakerWorld customizer for creating complete layered LED lamps for desks, bedside tables, shelves, ambient room lighting, or pendant installations. Choose a style, dimensions, and light source, then generate matching printable parts with a glowing diffuser between decorative upper and lower shells. Every lamp includes four core parts: lower decorative base removable light-source insert translucent diffuser upper decorative cap Optional configurations can also add a captured reflector and a separate press-fit light window in the upper cap. 🎛️ What You Can Customize 17 ready-made visual presets or fully manual settings rectangular, round, hexagonal, and octagonal bodies table or pendant installation body width, depth, diameter, height, shell thickness, and illuminated gap connected pixel, skyline, equalizer, peak, and stepped shell profiles smooth or ribbed diffuser texture 16 diffuser pattern families, including stars, waves, city skylines, hexagons, neon cracks, constellations, circuits, Aurora ribbons, mixed bats, and spider webs bright recessed or dark raised diffuser effects optional captured reflector optional sharp, rounded, or oval top light window cable routing, ventilation, clearances, screw mounting, and M3 heat-set inserts separate colors for the housing, diffuser, insert, reflector, and upper window assembled, exploded, print-layout, and individual-part output Generated 3MF files retain the assigned part colors, making it easier to prepare multi-color or multi-material projects. The diffuser should still be printed from a suitable transparent, translucent, natural, or white filament. 💡 Supported Light Sources LumaForge includes removable inserts for: Bambu Lab LED Lamp Kit 001 (MH001) Bambu Lab RGBW Puck Light (KC007) commercial E14 lampholders commercial E27 lampholders custom round LED modules Universal interchangeable fit creates one shared housing interface for compatible inserts. Export the housing once, then change only the light source and export the required inserts. Compact source-specific fit produces a smaller lamp intended for one selected light source. For E14 and E27, measure the real holder neck diameter, body diameter, and height before printing. E14/E27 describe the bulb thread, not the outside dimensions of the holder. Measure the actual holder before generating the insert. 🎨 Presets and Light Patterns The 17 presets cover bright architectural lamps, dark neon designs, round columns, polygonal beacons, skyline patterns, stars, circuits, constellations, flowing Aurora-style light bands, and two Halloween themes. Haunted Bats combines a black round housing, orange diffuser, mixed bat silhouettes, and a matching upper window. Spider Web uses a dark rectangular housing with a violet diffuser, large webs, and occasional spiders. Every affected section starts with its own preset override switch. You can keep a preset's colors while changing its body, replace only the diffuser pattern, adjust the shell profile independently, disable its upper window, or manually change the lamp dimensions. Patterns are generated within one continuous illuminated band, so the diffuser can be rotated to present a different section without changing its fit. Recessed effects preserve a configurable minimum wall thickness to avoid cutting through the diffuser. 🚀 Quick Start Choose a style preset. Select the light source. Keep Universal interchangeable fit or choose the compact interface. Select table or pendant installation. Check the assembled or exploded preview. Select All printable parts for the final export. Test the insert and diffuser fit before printing a full-height lamp. 🖨️ Print Notes The default diffuser wall is 2.8 mm. For illuminated patterns, use enough wall loops to fill the diffuser wall and disable sparse infill for that object. Six or seven walls with Arachne are a practical starting point. Print the diffuser upright. The generated lower base, insert, upper cap, reflector, and window insert use support-friendly orientations in Print layout. Use a small positive clearance if your printer produces overly tight press fits. Print a short fit test before committing to a tall lamp or expensive translucent filament. The MakerWorld preview may not show translucent filament exactly as it will look when printed and illuminated. 🧩 Assembly Install the selected light source in its removable insert. Fasten the insert to the lower body using four M3 screws. Select their length for the configured plate and mounting thickness; use the configured M3 heat-set inserts when that mounting mode is enabled. Place the diffuser on its lower support seat. Add the optional reflector or upper-window insert. Fit the upper cap over the diffuser. Removing the insert screws releases the complete light-source assembly for servicing. Removing the insert screws releases the complete light-source assembly for servicing. ⚠️ Electrical Safety Use only low-temperature LED light sources. For E14 or E27 configurations, use a certified commercial lampholder, insulated wiring, proper strain relief, and an LED bulb. Printed plastic must not replace electrical contacts, insulation, or certified mounting hardware. Pendant lamps require a certified cord grip so the electrical conductors do not carry the lamp's weight. Follow the electrical and fire-safety rules applicable in your country. Visible red 3D warnings identify unsafe or conflicting settings. The assembled and exploded modes also warn that they are previews only. description: The first publicly released 3D-printable customizable window screen repair patch! Customizable Window Screen Repair Patch Generate a window screen repair patch in nearly any size using MakerWorld’s Customize feature. This model is designed to closely match common 18 × 16 fiberglass window screen mesh . After printing, the patch can be heat-bonded to compatible synthetic screen material for a more permanent repair. Customization Click Customize , then enter the desired width and height of the repair patch. Default Dimensions Overall patch size: 3 × 3 inches Metric dimensions: 76.2 × 76.2 mm Strand width: approximately 0.28 mm / 0.011 inch Default Mesh Spacing 18 strands per inch in one direction 16 strands per inch in the other direction X-axis pitch: 1.411 mm Y-axis pitch: 1.588 mm Approximate opening size: 1.13 × 1.31 mm These dimensions are intended to resemble common household fiberglass insect screen. Recommended Slicer Settings Layer height: 0.08 mm Wall generator: Arachne Print flat on the build plate Smooth build plate is recommended Installation Trim away any loose or damaged strands around the hole. Clean the repair area and allow it to dry. Place the printed patch over the damaged section. Hold the patch in position so it remains flat against the existing screen. Set a heat gun to its lowest practical temperature and airflow setting. Warm the patch gradually using constant movement. The patch may shrink slightly during heating. This is normal . After approximately 30–45 seconds of gradual heating, stop and allow the patch to cool completely. Gently test the corners and edges for adhesion. Apply a small amount of additional heat only where needed.

description: # 🌿 Alocasia Nebula Selbstbewässerungs-Topfset – S, M, L & XL Dieses Set wurde speziell entwickelt, damit die Töpfe **nicht skaliert werden müssen**. Über einen Kapillardocht, der durch die Bodenöffnungen des Orchideen- oder Aroid-Topfes geführt wird, kann die Pflanze selbstständig Wasser aus dem Reservoir aufnehmen. description: Modular kit for securely adapting your portable AC to an open tilt-window and adding an intake hose for better cooling efficiency. Holds the window firmly in place while sealing off the opening and providing excellent airflow for both the intake & exhaust vents. For complete sealing, I recommend cutting foam pieces to fill the open space above and below the opened window. The kit includes a 255x230mm to 150mm intake hose adapter for portable AC units, a modular plate with two 150mm vents and adjustable brackets to fit the majority of tilt-windows as shown in the cover image. Printing : Print this in PETG or ABS . The exhaust vent will get too hot for PLA. The file is structured as follows: The kit is made up of multiple 250mm segments and a smaller 105mm segment. In my case, the window was 85.5cm in height, so I needed both adapter segments ( plates 3 and 4 ), as well as the top segment with mounts ( plate 5 ) and the short 105mm fill plate ( plate 7 ), which adds up to 855mm. Perfect fit, almost like I designed it specifically for that window or something :) In your case, measure the height of your window. Then print the plates according to your needs. You can add a blank 250mm segment by printing plate 6, or a blank 105mm segment by printing plate 7. It is likely that you'll need to modify at least one piece to achieve a perfect fit, if you wish to have zero gap. Whether you do that with a hacksaw or by simply shortening the piece in the slicer is up to you. Assembly: Assembly is fairly simple, refer to this image. The only supplies required are some M8x20 Screws, nuts and washers to secure the mounting brackets . The locking pieces to secure the segments together are meant to fit tightly, don't hesitate to tap them into place lightly with a hammer. You can assemble the segments in different orders than shown here, just be sure to have a set of mounting brackets somewhere near the top and another somewhere near the bottom. Test fit everything and then tighten the screws. The brackets can be both slid back and forth within their mounting slots, as well as tilted to fit as tightly as possible. Make sure to place the exhaust vent ABOVE the intake vent! The intake will otherwise ingest hot air directly from the exhaust! While this design should fit most european-style tilt windows as shown in the cover image, there is no way I can guarantee it will fit yours exactly. The modular design and seperate brackets should however make it easy to adapt with minimal effort. Happy printing and enjoy!

model_name: HEXAGON TESSERA - Modular Parametric Wall Tiles
description: HEXAGON TESSERA Modular parametric wall tiles on a hexagonal grid — 28 pattern engines, seamless across every joint. The idea Most tiled wall models give you one tile and repeat it. The pattern restarts at every joint, and from two metres away you see a grid of identical squares. HEXAGON TESSERA works the other way round. There is one infinite pattern field , and each tile is a hexagonal window cut out of it . The design does not restart at the joints — it flows straight through them. Truchet loops wander across four tiles. A labyrinth's corridors run from one side of the wall to the other. A sunflower spiral can span the entire installation. Pick a pattern, pick a size, generate one tile per position. The wall assembles itself. This is the hexagonal sibling of TESSERA , my square-grid tile system. Same philosophy, different tessellation — and hexagons pack with a rhythm that squares simply cannot give you. What you get 28 pattern engines — geometric, woven, organic, sculpted surfaces and true 3D reliefs Two orientations — flat top for aligned rows, pointy top for the classic honeycomb Seamless by construction — same seed, same field, and every joint matches Six-edge bowtie connectors — no handedness, no left/right tiles: any tile fits any neighbour on any edge Hidden keyhole mounting — nothing visible from the front Shelf and hook tiles — functional add-ons as separate, colourable meshes Backlight mode — pierced tiles plus a printable LED spacer frame Multi-colour ready — each mesh exports as its own object in the 3MF Fully parametric in MakerWorld's Customizer, or in OpenSCAD if you prefer Quick start 1 · Calibrate the joint first. Set part = calibration, print it, test the fit, adjust conn_clearance. Higher = looser. A connector weighs about 1.5 g; a tile does not. Do this once per filament and forget about it. 2 · Choose the look. Set part = preview, preview_layout = block. Try patterns, sizes and hex_orient. What you see is what you print. 3 · Read the addresses off the preview. Keep preview_labels = true and every tile is embossed with its own col,row. That is your wall plan — no counting, no working out hexagonal coordinates by hand. 4 · Export tile by tile. Set part = tile, type the pair into tile_col and tile_row, export. Repeat for each position. 5 · Print the hardware. part = connectors_plate gives you twelve connectors at a time. One per shared edge. ⚠️ Use the same seed for every tile of a wall. The seed is what makes adjacent windows agree. Changing it mid-way gives you a wall that does not line up. Change it freely before you start exporting — every seed is a different wall. The pattern engines Flat 2D reliefs — extruded, and the only ones that accept chamfer, height modulation and backlight: Truchet arcs · Diagonal maze · True labyrinth · Voronoi web · Hexagon honeycomb · Tri-weave · Isometric cubes · Diamond plate · Flowing waves · Concentric ripples · Sunflower (Fibonacci phyllotaxis) · Fish scales · Basket weave · Star lattice · Girih strapwork · Celtic plait · Bubbles · S-wave flames · Scallop interlace True 3D reliefs — these build their own mesh: Hicks hexagon — open hexagonal rings chaining into continuous ribbons, in three colours Vertex cubes — cubes stood on a vertex, three faces showing, in compressed staggered rows Hex height field — a honeycomb where every cell rises to one of several heights Overlapping hexagons — interpenetrating hexagons of random radius across several passes Scallop interlace (domed) — the scallop ribbon as a revolved, filleted section Sculpted height fields — here the tile is the surface, a single continuous solid: Ridges / silk — parallel ridges meandering along a sine path Dunes — three interfering plane waves, soft and never repeating Interfering waves — alternating domes and saddles Radial splash — concentric swells fading from a point you place anywhere on the wall Stepped topography — terrain quantised into flat terraces, with optional raised contour lines Each engine has its own parameter group in the Customizer. Only the group belonging to the selected pattern does anything. Sizing tile_size is the distance across the flats — the short diameter, the one you measure with a caliper. The corner-to-corner diameter is 1.1547 × larger. A 100 mm tile needs 115.5 mm of bed. Check that against your printer before you commit to a size. Print settings Setting Suggestion Orientation Flat on the bed, relief facing up Supports None — every overhang is shaped to avoid them Layer height 0.2 mm; 0.12 mm for the sculpted engines Walls 3 or more Infill 10–15 % Connector clearance Start at 0.15–0.2 mm, then calibrate Assembly: lay the tiles face down, slide a connector into each shared edge, press the neighbour on. Work outwards from a single tile rather than building clusters and joining them — tolerances add up. Then hang from the keyholes. For shelf and hook tiles, set keyholes = 2 and drive at least one screw into a stud or a rated wall anchor. Multi-colour Enable Preferences → Features → lazy-union in OpenSCAD so every mesh exports as a separate object. Most tiles: 2 objects — base and relief Hicks hexagon: 3 objects — base, bands, centre hexagons Shelf / hook tiles: 3 objects — base, relief, add-on Sculpted engines: 1 object — base and surface are genuinely one solid Backlight mode Set render_style = cutout and the tile is pierced right through, so an LED strip behind it lights the pattern from within. Any pattern produces islands — the inside of a Truchet ring, the centre of a star. The support web is what stops them falling out: a grid of thin lines running in world coordinates, so it aligns across tiles like window muntins. web_style = tri runs three families at 60°, which sits more naturally on a hexagon than an orthogonal grid. part = backlight_spacer prints the box behind the tile: wall mounting, LED chamber, wire pass-through, and a rebate the tile drops into. One thing to know before you start There are no edge pieces. A hexagonal wall ends on a ragged, staggered edge. That is the intended look, not something missing — hexagons do not close onto a rectangle without a whole family of half and wedge pieces, and adding them would change the character of the thing entirely. If you want a wall that ends flush on all four sides, use TESSERA instead. If you want the honeycomb rhythm, this is the one. Notes Designed in OpenSCAD, compatible with 2021.01 and later. No external libraries. A full printable guide (PDF) is attached, covering addressing, joints, every engine group, and troubleshooting. Made a wall with it? description: A more compact version created from user feedback A user of the original Easy Plug Puller asked whether I could create a more compact version for European outlets installed side by side. This V2 is the result of that feedback. It keeps the same simple two-part mechanism as the original version while introducing several important improvements: More compact design for adjacent outlets with 45 mm centre spacing Offset pivot to increase the effective lever arm Easier plug extraction with less hand effort Improved pivot locking to help prevent the parts from disengaging during use Reduced overall width No screws, glue, magnets or additional hardware What is new in V2? Compact 45 mm design The overall width has been reduced so that two plug pullers can be used on adjacent European outlets with approximately 45 mm between their centres . This makes the V2 better suited to double wall outlets, power strips and other closely spaced sockets. Increased leverage The pivot position has been moved to increase the effective lever arm. This improved geometry makes it easier to begin extracting the plug, especially when the plug is tight or difficult to grip. Improved pivot locking The pivot and retaining geometry have been redesigned to reduce the risk of the two printed parts disengaging while force is being applied. The mechanism remains simple to assemble while providing better retention during use. How does it work? The mechanism is fitted around the body of the electrical plug. When the large rounded lever is pressed toward the wall, it bears against the outlet faceplate and helps push the plug outward. Once the plug begins to move, simply hold the plug body and complete the extraction. This helps: Reduce the amount of grip strength required Avoid pulling directly on the electrical cable Make tight plugs easier to remove Improve accessibility for people with reduced hand mobility or grip strength Main features Designed for European Type E and Type F plugs Compatible with many CEE 7/7 plug bodies Compact design for adjacent outlets Designed for approximately 45 mm outlet spacing Offset pivot for improved leverage Improved anti-release pivot geometry Two fully 3D-printed parts Quick clip-together assembly No screws No glue No magnets No metal parts No AMS required Small amount of filament Fast and simple print Can remain fitted around a compatible plug Compatibility The V2 is designed for many common European plugs, including: Type E plugs Type F plugs CEE 7/7 plugs Straight plug bodies Angled plug bodies Adjacent outlets with approximately 45 mm centre spacing Electrical plugs and outlets can vary in shape and dimensions depending on the manufacturer. Before printing, compare your plug with the photographs shown on this page. The mechanism must never prevent the plug from being inserted completely into the electrical outlet. The 45 mm measurement refers to the centre-to-centre distance between two adjacent outlets. Assembly instructions Print both parts using the supplied orientation. Remove the small support areas carefully. Check that the pivot surfaces are clean. Gently spread the two arms of the lever. Position the circular plug collar between the arms. Align the arrow marks on both pivots. Press both sides together until the pivots are completely engaged. Check that the lever rotates freely. Check that both pivots remain correctly locked in position. Fit the assembled mechanism around the plug body. Do not spread the arms more than necessary. If one of the pivots does not engage correctly, do not force it. Remove the collar, realign the parts and try again. How to use Check that the printed mechanism is not cracked, loose or deformed. Fit it correctly around the plug body. Insert the plug completely into the electrical outlet. Press the large lever toward the wall. Allow the lever to begin extracting the plug. Hold the plug body and complete the removal. Never finish the extraction by pulling on the electrical cable. Safety information This model is a convenience and accessibility accessory. It is not a certified electrical safety device and it is not a medical device . Never use it if it prevents the plug from being inserted completely. Never touch the metal pins of the plug. Never operate or adjust the mechanism while touching exposed electrical contacts. Do not use it with a damaged plug. Do not use it with a damaged or loose electrical outlet. Do not use it if the plug or outlet is cracked, wet, deformed or unusually hot. Do not use it on a damaged or loose outlet faceplate. Stop using the printed part if it becomes cracked, loose or deformed. Inspect the mechanism regularly. Always complete the extraction by holding the plug body. Never pull directly on the electrical cable. The user is responsible for checking compatibility with their plug and electrical outlet. Created from community feedback This V2 was created following an improvement request from a user of the original model. Community feedback directly led to: The more compact 45 mm design The offset pivot The increased lever arm The improved locking system Thank you to everyone who comments, tests the model and shares suggestions. If you print the V2, please publish a Make and mention the type of plug and outlet you tested. Your photos and feedback will help me verify compatibility with more European plug designs and improve future versions. model_name: CIRCULAR TESSERA - Modular Parametric Wall Tiles
description: CIRCULAR TESSERA A modular decorative disc that splits itself to fit your build plate — and carries one continuous pattern across every joint. Pick a diameter. Pick a pattern. The model works out how to cut the disc into printable pieces, hides the joints behind bowtie connectors, and flows the design across every seam so the finished piece reads as one object, not a mosaic of tiles. 28 pattern engines. Any size. Multi-colour out of the box. The idea Most large wall pieces are built from tiles, and you can always tell — the grid shows. CIRCULAR TESSERA works the other way round. The pattern is defined once, across the whole disc , as a single continuous field. Each piece simply shows its own window onto that field. Two neighbouring segments aren't drawing their own pattern and hoping it lines up; they're computing the same pattern in different places, so it has to match. The cuts exist for one reason only: build plate size. Everything else in the model is there to make them disappear. What you get Centre disc + concentric rings. Set the centre radius, the ring thickness and how many rings. That's the whole geometry. It cuts itself to fit. Tell it the longest piece your printer can handle and every ring is split accordingly — outer rings automatically get more segments. Seams that don't line up. Radial cuts are staggered on alternate rings, so no cut ever runs straight through the disc. Hidden joinery. Bowtie connectors sit in pockets recessed into the back. Nothing is visible from the front. Two-mesh pieces. Every piece exports as a base and a relief, ready for a colour change with no post-processing. Wall mounting built in. Keyhole hangers recessed into the back, with the exact drill coordinates printed to the console. 28 pattern engines , from geometric tilings to sculpted surfaces. Default settings give a 210 mm disc in 21 pieces. Scale it to a coaster or to something that fills a wall — the model doesn't care. The patterns Polar-grid — built on the disc's own circular grid Truchet arcs · Diagonal maze · True labyrinth Flat geometric — one field across the whole disc Voronoi web · Hexagon honeycomb · Tri-weave · Isometric cubes · Diamond plate · Flowing waves · Concentric ripples · Sunflower (Fibonacci phyllotaxis) · Fish scales · Basket weave · Star lattice · Girih strapwork · Celtic plait · Bubbles · S-wave flames · Scallop interlace · Hicks hexagon Sculpted — the whole surface becomes one continuous curve Radial waves · Silk ridges · Dunes · Interfering waves · Stepped topography True 3D relief — engines that build their own solid geometry Vertex cubes · Hex height field · Overlapping hexagons Each has its own parameter group, so you can tune density, scale and character. seed re-rolls anything random — every seed is a different disc. A few worth trying first: Concentric ripples for something classical, Sunflower to make the most of the circular format, Radial waves for a sculpted splash that peaks at the centre, and Hicks hexagon if you want three colours. Make it yours Everything runs through the Customizer. The order of the panel follows the order you'd actually make decisions in: Pattern — pick the engine, set stroke_width and seed Centre — solid hub, pattern all the way in, or a clean central hole Geometry — center_radius, ring_thickness, ring_count Segmentation — set max_arc to your plate size and let it do the maths Base / Edges — thickness, relief height, optional chamfer on the pattern edges Joints / Wall mounting — connector fit and keyholes Then set part to what you want: assembly for the full preview, exploded to inspect the joints, or the individual parts for printing. Tip: design on part = segment or ring_here. Rendering the full assembly on every change gets slow, especially with Voronoi or the sculpted engines. Printing Print the calibration piece first. Set part = calibration. You get two test plates sharing a socket, plus one connector. Check the fit — snug, but you can push it home by hand. Adjust conn_clearance in 0.05 mm steps until it's right. Five minutes here saves reprinting real pieces later. All tolerance lives on the connector. The sockets in the pieces stay at nominal size, on purpose: if the fit is off you reprint a connector that costs a quarter of a gram, never a whole piece. Everything else: No supports , anywhere, on any piece or any pattern. The sockets are recesses in the underside, so they print against the plate as clean pockets. Print flat, face up , exactly as generated. 0.2 mm layers are fine. Drop to 0.12–0.16 mm for the sculpted patterns — their whole surface is a curve. 3+ walls , 15–20% infill. Print a few spare connectors . They're tiny, and a contrasting colour makes assembly easier to keep track of. Multi-colour Each piece is generated as separate meshes — a base and a relief, plus a third mesh of solid cores on the Hicks hexagon engine. That's what lets you assign a different filament to the pattern without splitting anything by hand. Assembly Work outward from the middle : centre disc first, then ring 1, then ring 2. Building inward from the outside means fighting the last ring into place. Complete each ring before moving on — join its segments to each other and close the circle, then connect that finished ring to the one inside it. Push each connector fully home into one piece, then slide the neighbour on. If a connector needs real force, stop and adjust conn_clearance rather than risk splitting a piece. Hanging it Set mount_mode and the model recesses keyhole hangers into the back, then prints the exact screw positions in millimetres from the disc centre. Mark, drill, leave the heads a couple of millimetres proud, slide the disc down onto them. Use two screws, not one. A disc is rotationally symmetric — its weight is the same all the way round — so a single screw leaves nothing to stop it turning. The pattern settles crooked and stays that way. Two keyholes on a horizontal line fix the orientation completely. This is the one thing that's genuinely different from hanging a square tile. Mount in the centre disc for small and medium sizes, or spread the keyholes around a ring for something large or heavy. With a 3 mm base the chamber suits thin and countersunk heads; raise base_thickness to 4 mm for standard pan-head screws. Good to know Why do some ring-to-ring connectors go missing? They're placed only where there's genuinely clear space between the radial cuts of both neighbouring rings, so a socket never lands on a cut. circ_n is a target, not a guarantee — rings with many segments simply offer fewer safe gaps. The disc is still held: nested rings can't fall apart, and the connectors are there to stop them rotating out of pattern alignment. Why does the centre look different on some patterns? The three polar-grid engines have cells that get narrower toward the middle, so they keep a small solid hub by default. Set center_mode = fill to run them all the way in anyway, or empty for a clean central hole. Every other engine reaches the centre on its own. edge_chamfer seems to do nothing. It shapes the top rim of the relief on the flat 2D engines. The sculpted and 3D-relief engines already shape their own surface, so they ignore it. Rendering is slow. Voronoi is by far the heaviest engine, and the sculpted ones scale with sculpt_res. Design on a single segment and render the full assembly only at the end. Included circular_tessera_v1_0.scad — the full parametric model, OpenSCAD 2021.01 compatible User guide (PDF) — 17 pages covering the joint system, every parameter, the pattern catalogue, printing, multi-colour export and troubleshooting Xeyos Design See also the other projects by the TESSERA family

description: Bring a warm Halloween glow into your home with the GlowPaws LED Tealight Holder Collection ! If your LED tea light is operated by a remote control or built-in timer , there is no need to access the switch manually. In that case, both bottoms can also be used with LED tea lights up to 48 mm (1.89 in) in diameter. For other LED tea lights, simply leave the Twist-Lock Bottom off and place the tealight holder directly over the light. ✨ Features Cute animal-themed Halloween LED tealight holder Fully enclosed pumpkin for a brighter lighting effect Jack-o’-lantern face glows beautifully from within Compatible with many LED tea lights Easy to print with clean FDM-friendly geometry Perfect seasonal home decoration ⚠️ Important Note LED tea lights only. Make sure they sit completely below the current printing surface. Resume the print. Make sure the washers do not protrude from the cavities, as they could collide with the nozzle. The washers are optional, but they are highly recommended for a more stable and professional display. Arm Assembly The vertical arms are printed separately and must be glued into the sockets in the base. A thick, gap-filling adhesive is recommended because the assembly has a small amount of clearance between the parts. Recommended adhesives: Two-part epoxy, such as Poxipol 5-minute epoxy Another thick structural adhesive suitable for plastics Gel cyanoacrylate Standard liquid cyanoacrylate is not recommended because it is very thin and may not properly fill the small gaps between the arms and the base. Apply a small amount of adhesive inside each socket and onto the bottom of the arm. Insert the arm completely, check that it is straight, and allow the adhesive to fully cure before hanging the keychains. Avoid using too much adhesive, as excess material may come out around the joint. Important Information The World Cup trophy keychains shown in the photos are only an example of use. This download includes the keychain display stand only. Keychains, metal rings, chains, washers, and adhesive are not included. description: 📻 AMPER - Retro Radio Toddler Lock Socket Cover Tired of ugly wall outlets, messy power strips, and loose cables spoiling your interior? AMPER transforms exposed wall sockets into a functional piece of mid-century modern decor. Styled after classic vintage tabletop radios, it seamlessly blends into your home while keeping live outlets safely out of reach. Designed for easy single-color or multi-color printing with zero external hardware required for the body assembly . 📸 Overview & Features Covers 23.5x19.5x8.5 cm socket box. Toddler-Proof Cable Protection: Completely covers exposed wall outlets. The front mesh panel uses a tight friction fit to prevent toddlers from pulling it open, while functional, rotatable knobs give little hands a safe, satisfying element to play with. Smart Cable Access: To plug or unplug devices, simply slide the mesh panel up, route your cable through the top groove, adjust through the mesh opening, and slide the panel back down into its tracks. Authentic Vintage Aesthetic: Dual-knob layout, detailed frequency dial face, and a sliding speaker grille pattern. 🖨️ Print Settings & Assembly Tips Setting Recommendation Supports Required on Main Body & Mesh Grooves Mesh Scale 99.6% (Default friction fit) Material PLA / PETG 💡 Support & Finish Notes: Mesh Panel Grooves: Supports inside the sliding grooves require careful removal and light filing/sanding. Do not skip these supports—the printing orientation is essential for structural integrity. Middle Horizontal Bar (Wood Texture Artifact): Depending on your support interface distance, the support interface under the middle bar may leave slight layer-line separation. This is a deliberate feature! It creates an authentic, subtle wood-grain texture that enhances the vintage radio look. Prefer a completely clean line? Simply tune your top support distance / interface layers tighter in your slicer. Friction Fit Tuning: The mesh panel is pre-scaled to 99.6% . Position the shell against the wall over your outlet/cables and mark the four leg peg locations on your shelf. Drill pilot holes into the shelf at the marked points. Drive 4 screws down through the internal leg peg guides into the shelf. Plug in your devices, pass the cables through the top groove, and slide the mesh panel down to lock everything securely.

description: 🧊 The first thermos for 250ml cans with active cooling! Enjoy your favorite drink always perfectly iced, wherever you are. Introducing a revolutionary thermos that not only keeps your drink cold, but can also actively cool it itself! Main advantages: ⏱️ Active cooling for up to 6 hours: Enjoy maximum refreshment even during long summer days, on the beach or on the go. ❄️ Cools even a warm drink: Forgot to put the can in the fridge? No problem, our unique cooling system will handle it easily and cool your drink. 🔄 Replaceable freezing cartridge: An ingeniously simple solution for continuous operation. While you are using one cartridge, you can have the other ready in the freezer. 📏 Perfect fit for 250ml: Designed exactly to fit narrow cans - ideal for your favorite energy drinks, iced coffees or lemonades. Design and practicality in one: The stylish matte finish in a refreshing lime color is complemented by a reliable snap-on closure and a practical folding handle. The thermos is easy to carry, fits perfectly in your hand and does not get in the way anywhere. 👉 Don't let a hot drink ruin your day. Equip yourself with a smart thermos that changes the rules of the game! INSTRUCTIONS Place the freezer cartridge with the thread facing up and fill it with water up to the MAX mark, place the cartridge on a plate and place it in the freezer, with the thread facing up, do not close the cartridge, freeze without a cap. When the water in the cartridge freezes, clean the frost from the outside of the cartridge with a sponge soaked in warm water, clean the thread and close the cartridge. The cartridge prepared in this way, cleaned of external frost, dried, closed can be placed back in the freezer. A cartridge prepared in this way can be frozen repeatedly, I recommend upside down, I recommend two cartridges for quick replacement. The freezer cartridge is inserted into the thermos packaging, it has 3 small locks that lock when inserted into the packaging and turned according to the arrows on the cartridge. The model is printed from PLA MATE, it is possible that other materials will need corrections, especially on the pins (hinge, closure) the pins should be functional, they can be secured with a small amount of glue to anchor them (I did not use glue). The pin on the hinge is inserted into the upper part of the package after the lock is assembled and finally pressed with an Allen key, for example, you should feel a slight click. The hinge pin is also pressed using an Allen key, the pin must not protrude beyond the hinge profile. I recommend testing the pins before assembling to see if they are passable, especially in the hinge part. The cartridge and cap have printed backings, which can be removed easily. The pins can be cleaned with a knife.

Introducing Duna, a small desk clock built around a face that behaves like a landscape. The dial is a soft sculpted ripple in sand tone, held inside a rounded square case, and two bare hands sweep across it without a single numeral to interrupt the surface. The frame in the photos is walnut cut on my CNC, and the files ship the same frame as a fully 3D printable part, so the piece is yours either way. Design & Concept I designed Dune around the idea that a clock does not need to announce itself. Taking the numerals away leaves the hands and the surface, and the surface is where the piece lives: a gentle dune relief that catches light differently through the day, flat and warm at midday, deeply shadowed by evening. The case sits the dial slightly recessed, which frames it the way a vitrine frames an object. Wood and filament are both first-class here, because a dark printed frame lands the same contrast against the sand-toned body that walnut does, with nothing but the plate. Key Features: Sculpted Dial: A soft dune relief replaces the printed face, so the hands read against a landscape instead of against numbers. No Numerals: Two hands and nothing else. The hour is legible at a glance without a mark on the surface. Wood or Filament: The walnut frame in the photos is my CNC build. The uploaded files include the same outer frame as a printable part, no workshop required. Two-Tone Build: A dark frame around a sand-toned body, straight off the plate with no painting. Clean Assembly: Outer frame, inner body, hour hand, minute hand, and a rear cover that closes the case and hides the movement. Desk Scale: Compact enough for a nightstand or a shelf, solid enough to hold its own beside a stack of books. Hardware Required: MakerWorld Clock Kit: Required. The kit supplies the movement that drives the hour and minute hands. Assembly Print the outer frame, the inner body, the two hands, and the rear cover. The outer frame can also be machined in wood if you have a CNC. Seat the inner body inside the outer frame. Install the movement from the MakerWorld Clock Kit through the back of the inner body. Fit the hour hand and then the minute hand onto the shaft. Close the case with the rear cover. Commercial License The downloaded files are for personal use only. If you are interested in selling physical prints of this design, please visit www.collecticraft.co to find details about my commercial license and subscription plans. Download Dune today and let the hours drift across it. I'd love to see whether you build yours in wood or in filament.

description: Parametric Ribbed Box Design I couldn't find a fully parametric ribbed box that allowed me to easily customize every important dimension while keeping the ribbed design adjustable. So I decided to create one myself. This model is fully parametric , allowing you to customize the width, length, height, corner radii, and rib pattern to create a box that perfectly fits your needs. Whether you're making a desk organizer, storage box, planter, or simply experimenting with different designs, this model gives you complete control over the final result. Because the ribs wrap around the entire model, the order in which you adjust the parameters is important . Following the steps below will give you the best results. How to Customize Step 1 — Width Start by adjusting Width . This changes the overall width of the box. Since the rib pattern is distributed around the entire perimeter, changing the width may cause the ribs to no longer line up perfectly where the pattern starts and ends. Don't worry about that yet—we'll fix it later. Step 2 — Length Next, adjust Length . This changes the overall length of the box and, just like the width, affects the total perimeter. After changing the length, you may notice that the rib pattern no longer connects perfectly at the seam. This is completely normal. Ignore it for now. Step 3 — Height Adjust Height to the size you want. This only changes the height of the box and normally does not affect the rib alignment around the perimeter. Step 4 — Ribbed End Distance (Most Important) This is the most important parameter. Ribbed End Distance determines where the rib pattern finishes. After changing the width or length, the ribs may no longer meet perfectly. Increase or decrease the Ribbed End Distance until: the first and last rib line up correctly; there is no visible gap at the seam; the rib pattern wraps smoothly around the entire box. Take your time with this step—it only takes a few seconds and ensures a perfect result. Step 5 — Ribbed Quantity Only adjust Ribbed Quantity after the Ribbed End Distance has been corrected. This parameter controls how many ribs are distributed around the box. Lower values create fewer, wider ribs. Higher values create more, finer ribs. Choose the amount that looks best for your design. If you make a very large change to the rib count, you may need to make a small adjustment to Ribbed End Distance afterwards. Step 6 — Inside Radius The Inside Radius controls the roundness of the inside corners. Smaller values create sharper corners. Larger values create smoother, more rounded inside corners. Step 7 — Top Radius The Top Radius controls how rounded the upper edge of the box is. Small values create a sharper edge. Larger values create a softer, more premium-looking finish. Recommended Workflow For the best results, adjust the parameters in this order: Width Length Height Ribbed End Distance Ribbed Quantity Inside Radius Top Radius Following this workflow ensures the rib pattern stays clean and perfectly aligned. Printing Tips Always check the preview after making changes. Pay special attention to the seam where the rib pattern starts and ends. This model is designed to print upright and generally does not require supports . A 0.20 mm layer height works great for most prints, but feel free to adjust your print settings to suit your printer and material. Overview This kinetic sculpture has linkages that cause the ball to be always centered in the exact same position. Due to each hinge axis passing through the center, no matter how each link is moved, it will cause the entire structure to articulate around a stationary center. It features a print-in-place and thread-together design that requires no glue or additional hardware. It requires no supports and is extremely fascinating and satisfying. The base can also be filled with sand or other materials to provide a more premium feel. I have also created other versions that are completely compatible with all of these parts. You can find the collection here: https://makerworld.com/en/collections/29606948-fixed-center-kinetic-sculptures For printing Standard setting can be used for printing. No AMS is required and no supports are needed. For the print profiles, there is one with all parts on separate plates for different colors for each part and two that have all the parts on a single plate (one includes the funnel and the other does not). All materials should work; however, for the ball to stay more centered, avoid flexible materials like TPU. Features The model prints in three pieces: the ball, the base, and the print-in-place linkages. Additionally, a funnel can be printed to more easily fill the base with sand or another material. The hole for filling the base is the same hole that the linkage structure threads into. The entire structure is about 95 mm in diameter and about 105 mm tall. All parts are compatible with the other versions. Assembly Assembling this model is very simple. Optionally, the funnel can be threaded into the hole in the base and the base filled. After the funnel is removed, the linkage structure can be threaded into that same hole until it stops. The location of where the threads stop should position the linkage structure properly. Lastly, the ball can be threaded onto the rod at the center of the ring. The links may be slightly stiff and not want to move after printing, but with some slight pressure, the links can be broken free. Interactive 2D map view - Resize, rotate, or drag your choice of shape on a 2D map view. Selective water body removal - You may or may not want to print some of the fetched water bodies. You can extend the tiles by adding new tiles in the Interactive 2D Map View. Jigsaw puzzle - Generate up to a 20×20 jigsaw terrain puzzle with full control over the jigsaw shape parameters and randomness. What Lies Within? While traditionally understood as a grand tomb for Pharaoh Khufu, the Great Pyramid remains an enigma. Beyond the famous King’s Chamber —home to the enigmatic red granite sarcophagus—and the Queen’s Chamber , the pyramid contains the breathtaking, corbelled-roof Grand Gallery . Hidden shafts, mysterious voids discovered via muon tomography, and an unfinished Subterranean Chamber carved deep into the bedrock all point to a level of engineering sophistication that continues to challenge our understanding of the Old Kingdom. Are these voids hidden burial sites, or part of a larger, lost architectural plan? Reports indicate potential anomalies, including vertical shafts and structured, geometric patterns reaching deep into the bedrock beneath the major pyramids. While these findings have sparked intense debate among archaeologists regarding their nature and origin, they offer a tantalizing glimpse into what may still be hidden beneath our feet. Este proyecto convierte cualquier persiana en una persiana motorizada inteligente controlable desde botones físicos o desde tu celular con la app Blynk IoT . Un ESP32 recibe las órdenes (subir, bajar, stop, auto) y las manda a un motor DC a través de un driver TB6612FNG que protege el microcontrolador de la corriente del motor. El sistema recuerda cuánto tiempo tarda en abrir o cerrar del todo, respeta un límite máximo de apertura para que la persiana no se enrede, y guarda toda esa configuración en la memoria del ESP32 aunque se apague la luz. description: Hold a medically accurate piece of human anatomy right in your hands! (Read the last sentence for a curiosity question!) 🩻 Overview 🩻 This advanced 3D model is a highly detailed representation of the human shoulder (glenohumeral) joint, developed through a hybrid medical and digital workflow. The skeletal framework was extracted directly from real CT scans to ensure an anatomically correct bone morphology. The surrounding soft tissues were subsequently hand-modeled in Blender, carefully crafted based on anatomical studies and medical literature. To ensure the best possible 3D printing experience and educational clarity, this model focuses on the primary structures. Some minor or overlapping anatomical elements were intentionally omitted, providing a clean, understandable, and highly printable display piece without overwhelming the slicer or the viewer. 🦴 Included Anatomical Structures The model highlights the key bony landmarks and major soft tissues crucial for understanding shoulder biomechanics: Skeletal Framework (CT Extracted): Scapula (Shoulder Blade), Clavicle (Collarbone), and Humerus (Upper arm bone), featuring accurate articular surfaces and bone topography. 💪 Muscular System (Blender Modeled): Key musculature, including major components of the rotator cuff and biceps, which are essential for shoulder stability and movement. 🔗 Ligaments & Connective Tissue (Blender Modeled): Essential stabilizing ligaments and capsular elements highlighting the articulation points. 🎯 Intended Use Education & Study: A brilliant hands-on visual aid for medical students, anatomy classes, and healthcare professionals. Clinical Communication: Perfect for physical therapists and orthopedic specialists to easily explain shoulder mechanics, impingements, or rotator cuff injuries to their patients. Advanced 3D Printing Showcase: A fantastic display piece that highlights the precision of your printer on complex organic shapes. 💡 Print Settings & Recommendations Material: This model has been fully designed and optimized for standard PLA . No flexible or exotic filaments are required. Versatile Print Profiles: To make this model accessible to everyone, I will be uploading dedicated print profiles for both AMS and non-AMS setups . The multicolor profile is organized to maximize visual contrast and educational value. Based on the provided images, the recommended color mapping is: Bone White: Skeletal structures (Scapula, Clavicle, Humerus) and tendons. Red: Musculature (Rotator cuff and supporting muscles). Blue: Ligaments, and capsular structures. Different colors are presented in the non-AMS setup for printing reasons. SIMPLY INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE NO-AMS PROFILE ⚠️ Disclaimer: This model is intended strictly for educational, illustrative, and hobbyist purposes. It is not a clinical tool and does not replace professional medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. For the most interested ones, a bit of anatomy! 🤓🫀🔬 The shoulder, or shoulder girdle, is a complex system designed to give the upper limb a very wide range of motion, with bones, muscles, tendons, and ligaments working together. In my model, the labeled parts show both the supporting framework and the soft tissues that stabilize movement. Bones 🦴 The scapula is a flat triangular bone at the back of the thorax, and it provides attachment for many shoulder muscles. The humerus is the upper arm bone, and its rounded head articulates with the scapula to form the glenohumeral joint, which is the main shoulder joint. The clavicle acts like a strut between the sternum and the scapula, helping keep the shoulder positioned away from the chest wall so the arm can move freely. Soft tissues 💪 The rotator cuff is made of four muscles and their tendons, and its main job is to keep the head of the humerus centered while the arm moves and rotates. The tendons connect muscle to bone, and the long head of the biceps tendon also contributes to shoulder stability as it passes near the joint. The ligaments connect bone to bone and reinforce the joint capsule, helping prevent excessive movement and instability. The subacromial bursa is a small fluid-filled sac that reduces friction between the acromion and the rotator cuff tendons during arm elevation. A question for the more curious viewer: Why does the biceps tendon anchor to the scapula instead of attaching directly to the humerus? Let me know in the comments!

description: A fully 3D-printable Push-to-Open mechanism with 4 tactile click stages and a completely new rotating locking wheel concept. Snap-fit assembly No supports required No additional hardware No tools required 4 parts 1 printing plate Approx. 3 hours print time Approx. 110 g filament Tested with PLA, standard print settings and the printer X1E and X1C I designed a completely new Push-to-Open (Push-to-Lock / Push-Push) mechanism. This model is intended as a functional demonstration of the working principle and can be assembled quickly using snap-fit connections. I plan to use this Push-to-Open principle in future projects. Unlike other 3D-printed Push-to-Open mechanisms, this new concept is based on a wheel with movable print-in-place contact pins. To make the mechanism easier to understand, I added viewing windows to the model so every movement step can be observed clearly. The mechanism creates 4 distinct click sounds that provide both tactile and audible feedback during every cycle🔔: The first click indicates that the button can be released The second click confirms that the mechanism is locked Pressing again creates the third click, indicating that the button can be released. The fourth click confirms that the mechanism is open and the cycle can start again Additionally, the spring elements inside the mechanism are not permanently loaded in the locked or unlocked position, which increases durability (This does not apply to the spring that retracts the sliding latch). The locking wheel rotates 90° during each open-close cycle. Suitable Applications This functional model is suitable for: Educational and demonstration purposes Mechanical concept studies DIY projects Prototype development for Push-to-Open systems Just to have fun with the mechanism 😉 I believe this mechanism has potential for many different applications and further development. For example: Different spring forces for opening and closing could be implemented Different actions could be triggered after each 90° rotation The mechanism could be activated from all four sides I am open to application ideas, improvement suggestions, and remixes.👐 Print Settings and Material The mechanism can be printed without any special print settings. I tested the mechanism using PLA for all parts. Other materials may require adjustments and were not tested. In my tests, the spring elements of the locking wheel were stiffer when printed in standard PLA, which made the click sounds more noticeable. PLA Tough+ for the locking wheel was more flexible and allowed the mechanism to run slightly smoother, but the click sounds were less pronounced. Assembly The functional model consists of four parts: Housing ① Base plate ② Locking wheel ③ Spring-loaded sliding latch ④ Do not heavily load the spring elements immediately after printing. Allow the parts to cool down completely first. Check if the spring elements inside the locking wheel can move freely. Sometimes a small amount of plastic may fuse inside the gap during printing. This can usually be separated easily. Press each pin toward the center as shown in the image. 2. Insert the spring-loaded sliding latch into the housing as shown in the image. Make sure the guide rails are aligned correctly. 3. Place the locking wheel into the housing. The locking wheel must sit flush inside the housing as shown in the image. 4. Slightly press down the spring-loaded sliding latch at the push point while inserting the base plate from the top until the snap-fits lock into place. 5. Finished!🥳 Do not store the spring of the sliding latch in a permanently preloaded position, as this may reduce the spring force over time. From my experience, the mechanism runs smoother after several cycles. It is important that the locking wheel can rotate freely. Too much friction may cause the mechanism to malfunction. This was a problem in my first prototypes, but the newer versions worked reliably. If you experience any issues, feel free to leave feedback.🤔 Detailed Function Description (Now things start getting a bit more technical😉) I marked the most important elements with colors: The housing contains: First locking position (pink) Second locking position (purple) The locking wheel contains: First contact pin (red) Second contact pin (yellow) These pins can move toward the center and spring back afterward. The locking wheel also contains: Spring-loaded locking sliders (blue) Rotation stops (green) The following section explains the closing and opening sequence of the mechanism. The circled numbers correspond to the images shown below. Closing Process During closing, the spring-loaded sliding latch is inserted from the top by hand and presses against the first contact pin, causing the locking wheel to rotate clockwise ①. At the same time, the second contact pin is pushed toward the center by the side wall of the sliding latch and becomes preloaded, creating enough space for the sliding latch to move to the end position②. As soon as the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the first locking position ③. This prevents the locking wheel from rotating backward. The spring-loaded sliding latch can now move backward slightly using the spring force (spring not shown). Due to the previous rotation of the locking wheel, the return path of the sliding latch is blocked by the rotation stop ④. Because of this, the sliding latch can only move back to the rotation stop position and the mechanism is now locked ⑤. In this position, the preloaded second contact pin can move back into the matching recess of the sliding latch ⑥. Once this happens, the Push-to-Open mechanism can be opened again. Opening Process Opening is performed by pressing the sliding latch a second time by hand. The sliding latch pushes the second contact pin downward until the end stop is reached ⑦. The required travel distance is only 5 mm. During this movement, the first contact pin is preloaded against the side wall of the sliding latch ⑧. When the sliding latch reaches the end position, the locking slider snaps into the second locking position to again prevent the locking wheel from rotating backward ⑨. The sliding latch can now be fully pulled out of the mechanism by the spring force (spring not shown) ⑩. Since the first contact pin is no longer pressed against the side wall of the sliding latch, it can spring back into its original position ⑪. The system is now back in its starting position and the cycle can begin again. Thanks for checking out the project! 😁

CYBERHAND 🤖✋ Five fingers. Four servo channels. One printed differential to reconcile them. The CyberBrick receiver gives you four servo channels. A hand has five fingers. CyberHand closes that gap with a printed differential rocker shared by the ring and the pinky: when one finger touches the object first, the rocker keeps feeding travel to the other until both are loaded with the same force. The grip self-equalises on shapes it has never seen — exactly like your own ring and little fingers, which share a tendon path and never move fully independently. Thumb, index and middle each keep their own channel. Works with any CyberBrick transmitter, and pairs natively with the CyberGauntlet — close your fist and the printed hand closes with you, very satisfying! HOW IT WORKS ⚙️ Tendons, not gears. Four 9 g servos wind 0.6 mm nylon cord on printed R11 winch horns; the pull runs through the finger channels like a flexor tendon. It is quiet, it is compliant, and when a finger is blocked the clutch slips instead of a gear train stripping. TPU flexure knuckles — zero pins, zero bearings. Every joint is a printed TPU hinge that also acts as the return spring. No axles, no fasteners, nothing to fall out of a finger mid-build. The joint is the part. Thermoformed palm mesh. The palm shell prints flat, then a few seconds of heat let you curve it into a real anatomical shape over your hand — the technique Steve Wood pioneered on the Flexy-Hand 2. Servo bay in the chassis. The four servos, their leads and the CyberBrick receiver all live inside the palm and wrist bracket. No dangling electronics, no external servo brackets. Built on the CyberBrick kit. The Hardware Kit covers the receiver, the wiring and most of the hardware. You add 7× M3 self-tapping screws and three extra 9 g angular servos to reach the four channels. Ready-made controller config. The listing includes CYBERGAUNTLET-CYBERHAND.json — import it in the CyberBrick app, flash both boards, and all four channels are already mapped. No manual channel setup. Display stand included. Rod + base, so the hand stands on your desk instead of lying on it. ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS 🙏 The finger architecture, the TPU flexure hinge principle and the thermoform palm technique come from the outstanding Flexy-Hand 2 by Steve Wood (Gyrobot) — an open-source prosthetic hand built for the e-NABLE community. CyberHand is a heavy mechanical redesign on that foundation: new palm chassis with an internal servo bay, winch-horn tendon drive, CyberBrick receiver mount, wrist bracket, differential connector and reworked fingertips. If you like this model, go look at the original first. It was built to give people hands. 👉 https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:380665 BILL OF MATERIALS 🔩 Printed — everything is already sliced and plated in the included Bambu Studio project, TPU parts included. Nothing to source or slice separately. Hardware CyberBrick Hardware Kit (receiver + 1× 9 g servo + wiring) 3× additional angular servos — 4 servos total 7× M3 self-tapping screws (3× M3×10 of them hold the servo fixer) 0.6 mm black nylon cord for the tendons (the tendon-end screws come in the servo accessory bags) A heat gun for thermoforming the palm mesh Files — CYBERGAUNTLET-CYBERHAND.json, the CyberBrick app config with all four channels pre-mapped. Tools — flush cutters, needle-nose pliers, tweezers, small Phillips driver, heat gun. ASSEMBLY 🛠️ 15 min, one chapter per step, and deliberately slow on the fiddly parts. A printable PDF guide is attached to this listing. Print the parts and gather the hardware first, then follow along: Upload the CyberBrick firmware — import the included CYBERGAUNTLET-CYBERHAND.json, connect & flash both boards (1:19) Connect the servos — any receiver port order works at this point (1:35) Assemble all the TPU joints — start by sorting the finger bones (1:38) Assemble each finger — same technique, five times (3:00) Get your controller & connect power to both — the CyberGauntlet, or any four-joystick transmitter for testing (3:41) Install the servos in the palm chassis as shown (4:14) Mount the wrist bracket and the receiver (6:03) Mount the servo fixer — 3× M3×10 self-tapping (6:41) Cut the nylon threads to length — measured against the model (6:59) String and tension the tendons — anchor each thread with a screw from the servo accessory bag, then cap the fingertips (7:12) Testing time! — close your fist, the hand closes with you (11:30) Thermoform the palm mesh (12:42) Then the final assembly — palm mesh on, battery cover closed — and the hand goes on its stand (14:25) . THE FIVE THINGS THAT DECIDE WHETHER IT WORKS 💡 Centre the servos before mounting the horns. A horn fitted off-centre costs that finger half its travel, and the only fix is pulling the servo back out. Check the hinge direction. The TPU knuckles are asymmetric. Mounted backwards, the finger fights you instead of returning on its own. Tendon tension is the build. Too loose and the servo spends its travel taking up slack, so the finger lags behind; too tight and the finger sits pre-curled at rest and never fully closes. Tune it one finger at a time. Balance the differential last, and as a pair. With the servo centred, the rocker should sit level. If it starts tilted, one finger hits its limit before the other and you lose the self-equalising grip. Heat the mesh, don't cook it. Sweep the heat gun in short passes from a distance until the sheet goes rubbery, then press it between the two mold halves. Held too close, PLA blisters and goes glossy before the whole sheet is pliable.

My Educational Mechanical Examples Series This model is one of my educational mechanical mechanism examples on 80mm x 80mm base plates. You can find all models of the series in this collection => [Mechanical Mechanism Examples] The present model This is an educational model of a spherical gear system, which is also called as ABENICS named after the inventor's name Abe. Brief Description A spherical gear system consists of one spherical gear and two cylindrical gears. Each cylindrical gear can rotate around its central axis, and that axis itself can swing around a second axis pointing toward the center of the sphere. By driving these two axes independently for each cylindrical gear — four axes in total — the system can control the orientation of the spherical gear across the full range of pitch, roll, and yaw. In a real application, the only limits on the motion range come from mechanical interference between the output coupler on the sphere and the surrounding structure, not from the gear geometry itself. The spherical gear is constructed by engraving a spur gear tooth profile around one axis of a sphere, then repeating the process around a perpendicular axis. The gif animation below illustrates this two-step process: first one rotation, then a second rotation about an axis 90 degrees away, yielding the characteristic cross-hatched spherical surface. The cylindrical gear is designed by rolling a basic spherical gear — engraved around only one axis — against a cylindrical blank. This process leaves one distinctive eye-shaped feature on the cylinder surface. Because of this, the cylindrical gear is also called a monopole gear. When you handle the printed model, you may notice that the spherical gear tends to stall at certain orientations. This happens when the monopole of the cylindrical gear aligns with a pole of the spherical gear. At this position, the spherical gear can not rotate in the direction of the cylindrical gear's central axis. To rotate the sphere in any intended direction, the secondary axis of the cylindrical gear must first be driven to make the main axis perpendicular to that direction. Only when the control software does this intelligently, the spherical gear can achieve motion in any arbitrary direction. To convince yourself that the spherical gear can indeed be moved in any direction from any orientation, try the following when it locks up: put your finger on the sphere and move it in small circles. Since the lock only resists one specific rotation at a time, pushing in various directions will gradually swing the cylindrical gear into an orientation where it can drive the sphere the way you want. Try this at different orientations of the sphere and you will find that free motion in any direction is always recoverable. The spherical gear system is a relatively new concept, first published in 2021, and is intended for robotic joints that achieve the same three rotational degrees of freedom as human joints. Reference Kazuki Abe; Kenjiro Tadakuma; Riichiro Tadakuma (October 2021). "ABENICS: Active Ball Joint Mechanism With Three-DoF Based on Spherical Gear Meshings" . IEEE Transactions on Robotics . 37 (5). Case This model is compatible with the case included in my first set . Printing Use the models named ???-printable.stl for printing . The models named ???-assembled.stl are provided just to show how they should be assembled. Use well-dried PETG to have better dimensional accuracy. Use 0.1 mm or 0.08 mm layer height to have smoother surfaces. Use slow printing speed for overhangs. Select “Random” seam position to have smoother rotation. Randomly distributed seam should be easily worn out after some wearing.Printing Sanding and Filing Note that, in this model, the rotation of the bases for bearings is intentionally made not too smooth. Sometimes, the gears suffer from the stringing effect and/or elephant foot effect, resulting in a too tight fit to the shafts (they are designed with a 0.15 mm radial clearance). If you see rough surface on the shafts due to stringing, sand off the roughness with a small piece of sand paper. If you feel the gears do not rotate smoothly due to an elephant effect, widen the hole slightly by using a thin round bar file. Without those issues, the parts should rotate very smoothly with minimal friction. Assembly (1) The spherical gear is printed in two pieces to have easy and precision printing. Combine them with two dedicated pins. (2) The cylindrical gear is also printed in two pieces. Combine them with two dedicated pins. (3) Push the shaft into the cylindrical gear and secure the other knob with the retaining ring. (The gears are simplified in these pictures to make it easy to handle in the CAD.) (4) Mount the assembled cylindrical gear with shaft onto the bearing. (5) Put the sphere on the plate. (6) Put the cylindrical gear on the bearing. (7) Push the secondary shaft of the cylindrical gear into the bearing on the plate. It should snap fixed in the square hole on the bottom plate of the smaller bearing. Other examples You may also be interested in the models in my educational mechanical mechanism examples. Find them in this collection: https://makerworld.com/collections/15048577-my-educational-mechanism-models Happy printing! He also makes excellent gear models himself. This series wouldn’t have existed without his inspiration. I learned a lot about technical detail of designing gear tooth profiles from Haguruma-No-Hanashi website . I’m truly grateful for that.
