Manchmal entstehen die besonderen Dinge nicht aus einem Auftrag, sondern aus dem Herzen. Vor einiger Zeit wurde ich gefragt, ob ich ein kleines Bärchen mit einer Schleife gestalten könnte – als Symbol für Menschen, die gegen Brustkrebs kämpfen. Die Idee dahinter war so einfach wie berührend: Ein kleines Bärchen, das Hoffnung schenkt und vielleicht genau in einem schwierigen Moment ein Lächeln ins Gesicht zaubert. Normalerweise nehme ich keine individuellen Aufträge an. Doch dieses Mal war es anders. Krebs hat auch in meinem Leben Spuren hinterlassen und mir Menschen genommen, die mir sehr am Herzen lagen. Deshalb war dieses Projekt für mich keine Arbeit, sondern eine Herzensangelegenheit. So entstand das Solidaritäts-Bärchen . Es soll ein kleines Zeichen sein, das etwas Großes ausdrückt: Du bist nicht allein. Manchmal braucht es keine großen Worte – manchmal genügt eine kleine Geste, um Mut zu schenken, Kraft zu geben oder einfach daran zu erinnern, dass irgendwo jemand an einen denkt. Das Bärchen ist 150 mm hoch und wurde mit einer 0,4-mm-Düse bei 0,16 mm Schichthöhe gedruckt. Wer möchte kann bei der Schleife auch variable Schichten verwenden damit die Oberfläche schöner wird .Die Oberfläche entstand mit Fuzzy Skin (Einstellungen nur in der 3MF-Datei). Bis auf den Bauch wird kein AMS benötigt, und bei der Farbwahl könnt ihr eurer Kreativität freien Lauf lassen. Ob klassisch in Rosa oder in euren ganz persönlichen Farben – jedes Bärchen trägt dieselbe Botschaft. Ich wünsche allen Menschen, die gegen Krebs kämpfen, von ganzem Herzen viel Kraft, Hoffnung, Liebe und Menschen an ihrer Seite, die sie durch schwere Zeiten tragen. Und allen Angehörigen wünsche ich den Mut, weiter Licht zu schenken, auch wenn der Weg manchmal dunkel erscheint. Euer Fred aka Lemmy3Dprint

description: This BONBON capsule introduces you to the colourful world of Hoardlings , a race of tiny treasure-seeking dragons . Inside is a complete miniature experience , including an easy-to-build kit card , a gold coin , a coin-purse lair , and a full-colour illustrated field guide . Everything fits neatly inside a 2.7" BONBON with plenty of room to add extra coins if desired. Finally, the scroll rounds out the entire package with easy assembly instructions and an inside look into the world of Hoardlings. No BONBON? No problem! Print as much or as little of the Hoardling experience as you want. Ready to Print* Your Own Hoardling? Let's begin! Just a few common sense things to be aware of: Small parts, choking hazard , keep away from babies/pets/cranky adults This is a miniature and not suitable for everyone Clean build plate is a MUST Textured build plate recommended (high tack plates may break cards upon removal) Fit differs between printers and filaments ; always do a test print before gifting or batch printing. Parts can break off prematurely while removing the card from the build plate unless you take a few simple and easy steps first. Use a freshly cleaned textured build plate . Let it cool completely first , then slowly and carefully flex the plate. The card should pop off easily if it hasn't already self-released. Easy peasy, I promise! Troubles? Please see any of my other kit card models for tips and tricks. Why not here? Because I'm working on a universal resource guide so I don't keep repeating myself :) *berri3D makes no guarantees about the law-abiding nature of your new Hoardling friend. Hoardlings can, will, and do (with joyful impunity) steal anything vaguely shiny, valuable, and/or structurally important to modesty/world peace. 📜 Paper Scroll 📜 For best results, download and print the PDF version of the guide ( not the image above). The PDF is a high quality vector file and can be found in the “Documentation” section below ⬇️ Print the guide double-sided on regular-weight paper. Cut out along dotted lines . If this will be put in a BONBON, trim paper close to the border edges so that overall width is ~50 mm (2"). This is to ensure a hassle-free fit inside the capsule. Print the scroll band from the print profile. Roll the field guide into a tight tube then slip the scroll band over to secure. 🪙 Coins 🪙 Coins can be printed in two ways: whole or notched. Coins with notches can be “held” by one or more dragons. Multi-notched coins can be found in the RAW file (click “Download STL/CAD Files”) beneath the Print Profile pane up above. They're either performing a cash summoning ritual or engaged in a 6-way tug-of-war for dominance. 👛 Coin Purse 👛 CREDIT: Although I'm not required to say so, it's only fair that I give a shout-out to one of the tools I used to create the purse. I modelled the base mesh in Fusion (as shown below) and then put it through Bumpmesh (a free, open-source browser-based app) to add the texture. Assembly should be done before placing into the BONBON or giving as a gift . The clasp will be a tight fit and may require using a hard surface to press it in. Once it clips in, it will be quite secure and will hold on its own. However, since it's technically possible to remove it with a bit of determination, a bit of glue is recommended as discouragement. Print Details This model has been optimized specifically for 0.4mm nozzles and the following settings: Part Layer Height Wall Generator Tested With Kit Card 0.2mm (Standard) Classic Basic PLA Silk PLA+ Silk PLA Coin Purse 0.28mm (Extra Draft) Classic Matte PLA Galaxy PLA “Gold” Accents (coin, clasp, and band) 0.12 (Fine) Classic Silk PLA+ Silk PLA All my 3mfs include these values in addition to other settings I've developed over the years to ensure the best possible result. Changing these values may result in parts not fitting or small details printing incorrectly. Test prints were made using the filaments listed in the Build of Materials using default profiles on a Bambu X1C. All parts were found to have a good fit. Your results may differ due to filament colour/type/brand, and printer. About I started this project as a “quick” (ha) kit card. Done and submitted within a few days. But then I made the mistake of wondering how much I could stuff into one capsule. The dragon wanted some treasure. So I added a coin. Then I thought it should be able to hold the coin. Then I thought if there's a coin, there should be a coin purse. And if there's a coin purse, why does a tiny dragon need one? And so on and so forth until all of a sudden I found myself having written a back story, made bonus accessories, and printed so many tiny thieving draconian reprobates that no matter where I go in the house, I'm three feet away from one at any given time. … If anyone wonders why I'm not a fast modeler, I present Exhibit A (this whole project) 😅

The Peacock Bass is not a peacock or a bass. It's actually the largest member of the cichlid family, not related to largemouth or smallmouth bass at all. It gets its name from the eye-like circle on it's tail that, like the markings on peacock feathers are used to deter predators. This vibrant fish is native to the Amazon and Orinoco river basins but has been transplanted to other tropical environments like southeast Asia and Florida. They are sought after by anglers for their violent fights, they have a reputation for damaging or destroying fishing equipment when they strike. These fish can reach up to about 1 m (3.3 ft) and weigh 13 kg (29 lbs). During the rainy season, males will develop a large fatty pump on their foreheads. The fish comes in a variety of subspecies, each with their unique patterns. The print profile I've uploaded includes 3 different color variations (same model, just different painting); spotted PB, Butterfly PB, and a blank for you to paint your own pattern on either in BambuStudio or with acrylics after printing. Like my other fish models, this Peacock bass uses interlocking scale units to swim. After printing, the two halves can be aligned with the registration pin and glued together by their head, tail, and perimeter scales. Happy printing (and fishing)!!

description: Lemure Swarm Miniature – Tide of Damned Souls This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lemure Swarm represents one of the most horrifying manifestations of infernal corruption—a heaving mass of countless damned souls fused together into a single crawling nightmare. Closely inspired by the uploaded reference and the Monster Manual 2024 depiction, this miniature emphasizes overwhelming organic horror rather than speed or aggression. The miniature is designed on a Large (50 mm) round tabletop base , allowing the sprawling mass of bodies to nearly fill the entire footprint. Instead of depicting individual Lemures standing separately, dozens of infernal bodies have merged into one towering mound of living flesh. The broad contact area gives the model exceptional structural stability while creating an unmistakable silhouette unlike any other fiend in the collection. The lower portion forms a thick pool of liquefied infernal flesh that spreads naturally across the base. From this grotesque foundation, countless humanoid forms emerge as though attempting to free themselves from eternal imprisonment. Bodies are only partially formed before dissolving back into the surrounding mass, creating a seamless transition between individual Lemures and the larger swarm. No figure appears completely separate; every soul remains permanently fused to the collective. Dominating the composition are numerous screaming faces positioned at different heights throughout the mound. Some stretch upward with mouths opened impossibly wide in silent agony, while others twist sideways or emerge only halfway from the flesh. Every expression conveys suffering rather than rage, reinforcing the tragic nature of these damned beings. The faces vary subtly in size and angle, preventing visual repetition while maintaining the impression of an endless sea of tortured souls. Multiple malformed arms reach outward from every direction. Some extend fully toward unseen victims with clawed fingers spread wide, while others appear only halfway formed before disappearing back into the flesh. Thick strands of melting tissue connect every limb directly to the central body, ensuring there are no fragile unsupported parts while enhancing the impression that the swarm itself is continuously shifting and reforming. The surface of the miniature is densely textured with stretched skin, flowing muscle fibers, sagging folds, puckered scars, exposed veins, and merging anatomical forms. Faces dissolve into shoulders, arms vanish into torsos, and bodies blend seamlessly together without clear boundaries. This continuous sculpt creates remarkable visual depth while remaining strong enough for reliable resin printing. Rather than standing upright, the swarm advances slowly as a creeping wall of flesh. The front of the miniature pushes forward with numerous crawling limbs dragging the mass across the ground, while the rear rises into a mound of intertwined bodies that gives the model impressive height despite having no fragile vertical structures. This low center of gravity makes the miniature exceptionally durable for gaming. The scenic base depicts corrupted infernal ground partially submerged beneath pools of viscous flesh. Weathered skulls, broken bones, scattered debris, and patches of cracked earth emerge from beneath the advancing tide, suggesting countless previous victims consumed by the swarm. Every scenic element is sculpted directly into the base to maximize durability and simplify printing. The recommended paint scheme closely follows the uploaded reference. The flesh should be painted using pale ivory, unhealthy pinks, bruised purples, raw crimson, and desaturated flesh tones blended together across the numerous bodies. Deep burgundy washes settle into every fold while lighter ivory highlights emphasize the stretched skin. The mouths benefit from dark crimson interiors with yellowed teeth and pale tongues, creating striking focal points across the model. Thin layers of gloss varnish on selected areas can simulate wet, freshly formed flesh without overwhelming the entire miniature. The infernal ground beneath is best painted using dark earth browns, blackened stone, scattered bone colors, and pools of coagulated crimson. No soul escapes. Every scream becomes another voice. Hell remembers everyone. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Large swarm composed of countless fused Lemures. Numerous screaming faces emerging organically from the mass. Multiple grasping arms integrated directly into the body. Rich sculpted textures featuring flowing flesh, scars, folds, and merging anatomy. Low, stable composition with exceptional structural integrity. Scenic infernal base with skulls, bones, and corrupted ground. No floating elements or unsupported anatomy. Outstanding centerpiece for infernal encounters, Lower Plane adventures, and complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime in grey or black before layering pale flesh tones across the entire swarm. Build variation using ivory, bruised pinks, muted purples, crimson glazes, and sepia washes to distinguish individual bodies without separating them visually. Highlight raised folds using pale ivory while keeping deep recesses saturated with burgundy and violet washes. Paint mouths with dark reds, gums in fleshy pinks, and teeth using aged bone colors. Finish selected areas with controlled gloss varnish to create the appearance of wet infernal flesh. The base works beautifully with blackened stone, dusty earth pigments, scattered skulls, and dark blood effects. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Large Recommended Base: 50 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Perfect for infernal invasions, abyssal battlefields, Lower Plane encounters, fiend-themed campaigns, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: The Court of the Vampire Queen Illya'Dra, Former Matron of House 'Dra All models in this series are set in a .2mm Nozzle Profile. These are long prints . To ensure success: Clean the build plate before you start the print. A clean build plate is essential before starting a long print. Nothing worse than a support coming off the plate ¾ of the way through. The supports are designed to be thin and easy to remove. With that stated, some of the points of connection are on or around small details. They will come away cleanly, just go slow and use the proper tool. Flusher Cutter, Razor, etc. The models are designed and positioned for success, so be patient when removing the supports particularly around the Axe , the Sword , and the Cane . If you have not tried my print profile, just use it. It is a high detail, slowed, increased wall and thinned out support profile designed to work well with these models. I post many .4mm profiles models on makerworld as people tend to like the speed over the detail but for home use I print every model in this .2mm profile. For an example see the .2mm Profile Beholder in my models. It takes longer, but it is worth it. The Beholder shown here is cleaned up and thats it. No primer and no paint. For the Vampire with the sword, there is a point on the base with a very tiny hole that the tip of the sword will slip into. If you do not line it up with the hole in the base, the sword point will actually be a fraction of a mm longer than his legs and make it challenging to glue him to the base. For the most part the bases are interchangable, but slightly different per model. If you see one you like more than the rest, resize it to the correct size and print it again. The bases are quick and use very little filament. So use what you like. The Queen is a much larger size model. I did this because I like it. That doesn't mean you need to love it. Resize any or all of these to fit your needs. They are scaled to work with a 32mm TTRPG of your choice, with the Queen being much large and daunting. The others hover right near there, give or take a few mm. if you run into any issues printing these, let me know! I have printed each of them two times. Once for my personal use and once as a followup test print. That doesn't mean all machines and filament are the same. I printed these using Sunlu HS PLA+ 2.0, which is currently a bit of a meta filament in the FDM miniature community as it prints with clean, high detail and cleans up easily. I have also taken the steps to calibrate that filament on my machine. If you find issues during your print, leave a comment and I wil see what I can do to address the comments and help. Aside from some stringing my filament is very dialed in. The stringing i have intentionally left in the pictures so that you can see what it looks like before being cleaned up and primed or painted or whatever else people do to these things to make them seem impossibly clean. These are thinner models with higher level, smaller details. IMO that leads to higher stringing when using a .2 on HS filament even when dried, dialed in retraction and calibrated. So my pictures of the printed models can and will look better after clean up and paint. I have a terrain build that I created spefically to with this Vampire Encounter, my first larger terrain piece. Here is what it looks like but I still on the fence about releasing it. It takes about 1kg of filament to print the entire thing, it has verticality to it as it is supposed to be a fallen temple that has begun to sink into an ever expanding swamp lands. Many might not like the verticality of it as it gently slopes. I have a couryard and a few other areas that would fill an entire table. But they are unique pieces that probably don't see much play, take a ton of filament even on 4% infill, and take up a great deal of space when not in use. I don't know that I want to go down this road. I will let people see it though to help me decide if it's worth releasing or not. I have several projects like this I created over the last couple years that are original and specific to the story I was running at the time. I just don't know how well they fit into anyone elses worlds. Anyway, happy printing all! ***UPDATE NOTE*** I will be adding some .4mm nozzle profiles for the model that I can. If they are just going to fail on people at .4 I won't put the profile up. There are some thin points that will prove challenging in .4

🏖️ Kurz zurück aus der Sommerpause… 🏖️ Ich melde mich für einen kurzen Boxenstopp aus meiner Sommerpause zurück und werde die nächsten 2–3 Tage noch einige Modelle hochladen, die entweder kurz vor der Pause oder gerade währenddessen entstanden sind. Ich sage nur: 💖 Love is in the Air! 💖 Hier kommt das More Love Bärchen – randvoll mit Liebe, einer ordentlichen Portion Charme und hoffentlich auch dem ein oder anderen Lächeln. 😊 Das Bärchen hat eine Höhe von ca. 150 mm . Skalieren sollte grundsätzlich kein Problem sein – aber wie immer gilt: ohne Gewähr . 😉 Gedruckt wurde alles mit Bambu Lab PLA Matte/Basic . Der Zusammenbau ist ebenfalls unkompliziert… vorausgesetzt, ihr habt nicht gerade zwei linke Hände. 😄 Hier und da etwas Kleber, ein wenig sanfter Druck und schon findet alles seinen Platz. 📦 Es stehen drei verschiedene Profile zur Verfügung: 🟢 Profil 1 – Druck nach Objekt Alles befindet sich auf einer Platte. Kompatibel ab Bambu Lab A1 . 🔵 Profil 2 – Druck nach Ebene Mehrere Platten, dafür könnt ihr problemlos Teile überspringen oder einzelnen Bereichen andere Farben zuweisen. 🟠 Profil 3 – Für alle H2C-Besitzer Wer möglichst wenig Filamentmüll produzieren und alles in einem Stück drucken möchte, ist hier genau richtig. 🛠️ Druckdetails 0,4 mm Düse 0,16 mm Schichthöhe Natürlich könnt ihr auch andere Einstellungen verwenden. Aber bitte denkt daran: Wenn ihr mit einer 0,6er Düse , 0,3 mm Schichthöhe , drei Tage altem Filament und halb gereinigter Druckplatte druckt und das Ergebnis nicht perfekt wird… dann ist nicht automatisch der Designer schuld. 😅 Apropos Druckplatte: Die sollte sauber sein und der Drucker ordentlich kalibriert. Mit meinen Profilen lassen sich die Stützen problemlos entfernen. Alle Bärchen besitzen außerdem eine Fuzzy Skin Oberfläche (in der 3MF-Datei ), die für eine richtig schöne, weiche Optik sorgt. ❗ Das obligatorische Kleingedruckte Bitte spart euch Anfragen nach anderen Modellen. Ich drucke und konstruiere das, worauf ich gerade Lust habe . Es ist und bleibt ein Hobby – und genau so soll es auch bleiben. Ebenso biete ich keinen 3D-Druck-Support und keine Nachhilfe an. Ein bisschen Eigeninitiative gehört schließlich auch zum Hobby dazu. 😉 🤖 Für die KI-Schwabbler Ja… auch dieses Modell wurde neben Nomad Sculpt und Blender mit Unterstützung von KI entwickelt. Wer damit ein Problem hat, darf ganz entspannt weiter scrollen. Das spart euch Zeit und mir Kommentare. Win-win. 😄 Wenn euch meine Arbeit gefällt, freue ich mich wie immer über ein Like, Feedback oder einen Boost . Das motiviert ungemein und zeigt mir, dass sich die viele Arbeit gelohnt hat. In diesem Sinne: Viel Spaß beim Drucken und lasst etwas Liebe durch eure Drucker fliegen! ❤️🐻 Information : Da immer wieder Anfragen kommen, warum meine Bärchen nicht exakt wie das Original aussehen: Ja, das ist mir bewusst. Ich betrachte diese Modelle als Fanart . Da sich das Ganze in einer rechtlichen Grauzone bewegt – wie viele ähnliche Modelle auf MakerWorld – habe ich bewusst darauf geachtet, keine 1:1-Kopie zu erstellen. Diese Figuren sind nicht Bestandteil meiner kommerziellen Lizenz . Sollten sie dennoch von Dritten verkauft werden, geschieht dies auf eigene Verantwortung. description: Kenku Miniature – Cunning Crowfolk Scout and Master Mimic This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Kenku is one of the most recognizable avian humanoids in the Monster Manual 2024, combining the appearance of a clever crow with the posture and equipment of an experienced rogue, scout, or thief. Renowned for their uncanny mimicry, stealth, and resourcefulness, Kenku survive through intelligence rather than brute strength. This miniature faithfully follows the uploaded reference, capturing a wary infiltrator caught in the middle of a burglary or reconnaissance mission. The miniature stands on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a low stalking pose. The Kenku balances with one foot planted firmly on uneven cobblestones while the opposite foot rests atop a weathered wooden crate, giving the impression that it is silently navigating rooftops, alleyways, or forgotten ruins. The crouched posture lowers its center of gravity and immediately communicates stealth, agility, and constant awareness. Every point of contact remains securely connected to the base for excellent print stability. Its anatomy reflects the lean proportions described in Monster Manual 2024. The body is slender and athletic rather than muscular, built for climbing, running, and quiet movement. Narrow shoulders transition into long arms ending in dexterous clawed hands capable of manipulating tools and weapons with remarkable precision. The digitigrade bird-like legs terminate in powerful talons that grip both the ground and the crate naturally, reinforcing the dynamic balance of the pose. The head is unmistakably raven-like, featuring dense layered feathers that create a textured crown across the skull and neck. A long black beak curves gently downward with realistic proportions rather than exaggerated length. Sharp amber eyes peer cautiously toward unseen danger, conveying intelligence and suspicion rather than aggression. The head tilts slightly forward, reinforcing the feeling that the Kenku is constantly evaluating its surroundings before making its next move. The left arm reaches forward with spread talons as though preparing to steady itself or silently grab a nearby object. The opposite arm remains pulled back, gripping a simple steel dagger in a reverse grip suitable for ambushes or close-quarters combat. The blade is intentionally broad and sturdy enough for reliable printing while retaining a realistic profile. Unlike many fantasy birdfolk, the Kenku possesses no functional wings. Instead, its body is covered in layered black feathers that transition naturally into feathered arms and a short fan-shaped tail. The feathers are sculpted in overlapping layers that produce excellent depth when painted while remaining thick enough for clean printing. The tail extends naturally behind the miniature, providing visual balance without creating unsupported elements. Its clothing reflects the practical lifestyle of an experienced infiltrator. A hooded travel cloak drapes across the shoulders before falling behind the body in thick layered folds. Beneath the cloak, multiple leather straps cross the torso to secure pouches, satchels, and equipment. A weathered belt carries additional supplies including small utility bags, bottles, and tools appropriate for scouting or lockpicking. Layered cloth panels protect the hips while maintaining complete freedom of movement. The wrapped forearms and lower legs reinforce the impression of an adventurer accustomed to dangerous environments. The scenic base follows the uploaded reference closely. Uneven cobblestones form the primary terrain while a sturdy wooden crate elevates one foot, creating vertical variation without distracting from the figure itself. Beside the crate lie a small sack, a discarded cup, and scattered debris, suggesting a back alley, marketplace, or smuggler's hideout. These scenic details remain fully integrated into the base and are designed for straightforward printing. The recommended paint scheme matches the reference miniature. Feathers should be painted deep charcoal black with subtle blue-grey highlights applied through careful drybrushing to reveal individual feather layers. The beak and talons use satin black highlighted with cool greys. Leather equipment ranges from warm browns to dark chestnut with lighter edge highlights, while the cloak combines muted olive, brown, and weathered grey fabrics. Metallic buckles and the dagger receive aged steel finishes with selective silver highlights. The amber eyes provide a bright focal point that immediately draws attention to the miniature's expressive face. Every shadow hides opportunity. Every voice can become its own. The silent watcher has already memorized your final words. ✨ Key Features Faithful Kenku based on the Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Dynamic stealth pose with one foot resting on a wooden crate. Distinctive raven-like head with layered feather detail. Reverse-grip dagger ready for ambushes. Practical adventuring gear including belts, pouches, bottles, and satchels. Fully feathered body without functional wings, true to the classic Kenku appearance. Scenic cobblestone base with integrated crate and urban clutter. Strong silhouette designed for tabletop visibility. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, or unsupported scenery. Optimized for resin printing and suitable for carefully tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature black before building the feathers using successive layers of charcoal, dark blue-grey, and subtle light grey drybrushing across the raised feather texture. Paint the beak and talons in satin black with cool grey edge highlights to create natural contrast. The cloak works well in muted olive-brown or weathered grey, shaded with dark brown washes before lighter edge highlights. Leather belts and pouches should be painted using varying shades of brown to break up the equipment visually, while metallic buckles and the dagger benefit from dark steel tones highlighted with silver. Finish the eyes with vivid amber or golden yellow to emphasize the Kenku's alert and calculating expression. The base combines layered stone greys for the cobblestones, weathered brown wood for the crate, dusty earth pigments between the stones, and small touches of muted green on the scattered bottles to create subtle visual interest without overwhelming the figure. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, urban adventures, thieves' guild encounters, wilderness scouting parties, rogue-themed campaigns, and Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: Lich Miniature – Undying Master of Forbidden Magic This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lich stands among the most feared spellcasters in all of fantasy—a skeletal archmage who willingly embraced undeath to achieve eternal mastery of arcane power. The miniature stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base , where the flowing robes occupy much of the footprint while leaving the model perfectly balanced. Unlike dynamic melee creatures, the Lich stands with calm confidence, radiating complete control. The pose is static yet commanding, emphasizing centuries of accumulated knowledge rather than physical strength. The skeletal body is tall and unnaturally thin. Bare ribs and vertebrae remain visible beneath the open robes, while elongated bony arms stretch confidently outward. The exposed skeleton is anatomically clean and sharply sculpted, with every rib, finger bone, and joint clearly defined without becoming overly fragile. The feet emerge from beneath the robes as exposed skeletal bones planted firmly upon cracked stone flooring. The skull serves as the unmistakable focal point of the miniature. Empty eye sockets glow with unnatural magical power, while the permanent skeletal grin creates an expression that is simultaneously calm and terrifying. Long strands of ancient black hair still cling to the skull, hanging behind the shoulders in weathered locks that hint at the Lich's once-living appearance. Resting upon the brow is an elegant crown of dark metal adorned with sharp golden points, symbolizing forgotten kingdoms and immortal authority. Flowing around the skeletal body are magnificent layered robes that create the majority of the miniature's silhouette. Thick overlapping folds sweep naturally toward the base, producing dramatic movement without relying on unsupported fabric. The outer robes feature ancient embroidered borders and ornate trim inspired by long-lost arcane empires, while the inner garments remain darker and heavier to create visual depth. Small tears and worn edges reveal centuries of decay without compromising structural integrity. Across the chest hangs a collection of ancient necklaces, talismans, and arcane ornaments. Suspended from the waist are elaborate ceremonial decorations featuring sculpted skulls, infernal masks, carved bone icons, and hanging charms that remain thick enough for dependable printing. These decorative elements reinforce the Lich's role as an immortal master of necromancy without creating delicate unsupported pieces. The left arm extends outward with claw-like skeletal fingers partially curled as though directing unseen magical servants or issuing a silent command. Rather than depicting visible spell effects, the pose alone communicates overwhelming magical authority while keeping the model completely free of floating magical energy, smoke, or visual effects. In the opposite hand the Lich firmly grips an ancient wizard's staff that reaches from the base nearly to the height of the skull. The twisted wooden shaft appears weathered by centuries of use, while its upper section is crowned by a polished humanoid skull that serves as both arcane focus and symbol of mastery over death. The staff remains fully connected to the base through the Lich's hand, ensuring excellent stability during printing. The scenic base depicts cracked stone flooring from a forgotten crypt or ruined throne room. Scattered skulls, broken bones, loose flagstones, and fragments of ancient masonry surround the Lich's feet, subtly reinforcing the atmosphere without distracting from the central figure. Every scenic element is sculpted directly into the base to maximize durability. The recommended paint scheme follows the uploaded reference closely. The skeletal anatomy should be painted with aged bone colors shaded using sepia and brown washes before being highlighted with warm ivory. The robes combine deep black, charcoal, dark violet, and rich burgundy layered together with subtle edge highlights. Ornamental trim, the crown, and jewelry should be painted using antique gold with selective weathering. The staff is best rendered in aged wood with bone-colored highlights on the skull, while the stone base benefits from layered greys and dusty brown pigments to create the feeling of an ancient tomb. Death became a doorway. Knowledge became eternity. The king of undeath still waits. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Layered ceremonial robes with rich sculpted folds. Ancient necromantic jewelry, skull ornaments, and arcane decorations. Twisted wizard's staff crowned with a sculpted skull. Scenic crypt base with broken stonework and scattered skulls. No floating magic, smoke, or unsupported spell effects. Ideal centerpiece villain for undead armies, ancient tombs, legendary campaigns, and complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before painting the skeleton with layered bone colors shaded using sepia and dark brown washes. Highlight the skull and ribs using warm ivory to emphasize the sculpted anatomy. Paint the robes with rich blacks, charcoal greys, deep purples, and burgundy highlights to create luxurious yet ancient fabrics. Use antique gold for the crown, jewelry, embroidered trim, and ceremonial ornaments. description: American Bison Highly detailed multipart bison designed for glueless snap-fit assembly and multicolor printing. The model captures the powerful muscular build, thick shaggy fur, and aggressive stance of the American bison with clean interlocking parts that assemble without glue. Color Handling : Multipart design → no AMS required. Print plates separately in desired filaments. You can also rearrange the parts onto different plates if you want to mix the colors in a more unique way. Options: Print plates 1-4 for multipart assembly or use available options. Note: I printed mine at 100% scale but decided to enlarge the multipart model before release to match the other bovine figures . At 126.67% scale, the bison should look realistic next to my bull model . Use glue if needed and please, let me know if the snaps aren't perfect at this scale! Plates front part back, head and front legs hooves and horns nose and eyes [option] bison AMS [option] bison single color Scaling Advice Scaling Up : Larger sizes should work well but not extensively tested yet. The peg connectors are robust, but connections may need minor tolerance tweaks (e.g., slight peg sanding or scaling adjustment) if fit feels off after upsizing. Scaling Down: Smaller sizes should also be possible, but connections might not be as clicky or secure → use glue if needed. Best Practice : Always scale all parts uniformly with the exact same percentage in Bambu Studio before slicing. Apply scaling globally to the entire project to keep peg/socket alignments perfect. Verification : After scaling, check the sliced preview in Bambu Studio to make sure supports are properly generated for overhangs and that small features don’t have thin walls. Keep in mind, some parts may not be printable if they’re too small. Assembly instruction This multipart model is designed for effortless, glueless assembly! Snap everything together using the peg connectors. No glue required for a secure, satisfying fit. Preparation Carefully remove tree supports before assembly. Tree supports release most cleanly when cut between branches… snap them away without stressing surfaces. Peg Connections Almost all parts use the same snap-fit peg system Pegs are intentionally tight for rock-solid hold → align and then push firmly until you feel/hear the snap. If too tight → lightly trim peg domes (green) with a knife. If slightly loose → a tiny drop of superglue fixes it instantly. Smaller pegs may feel less "clicky" than larger ones but still provide reliable strength. Orientation Note : Left (L) and Right (R) are labeled based on the character’s own perspective, not the viewer’s. Rather than rushing into combat, he has paused at the critical moment to direct his troops, embodying leadership through action rather than spectacle. His physique is broader and more muscular than that of a standard Hobgoblin Warrior. Thick shoulders, a powerful chest, and strong forearms suggest years of campaigning while maintaining realistic proportions suitable for a disciplined military officer. The head follows the uploaded reference closely. The skin is a warm bronze-brown with subtle olive undertones characteristic of Hobgoblins in the Monster Manual 2024. A deeply furrowed brow, sharp cheekbones, and pronounced jawline give the face a hardened, uncompromising expression. His eyes remain intensely focused on the battlefield ahead, conveying tactical calculation rather than uncontrolled fury. Long pointed ears project outward from the sides of the head while remaining thick enough for reliable printing. His dark hair is gathered into a tightly bound warrior's topknot positioned high on the crown, reinforcing the clean military appearance expected of a commanding officer. The torso is enclosed within heavy layered plate armor worn over chainmail. Large angular pauldrons protect the shoulders while a reinforced breastplate dominates the chest with broad overlapping steel plates. The armor features restrained rivets and practical construction instead of elaborate ornamentation, emphasizing the Hobgoblin philosophy of military efficiency. A deep crimson officer's tabard hangs from beneath the breastplate, extending to mid-thigh in broad layered folds. The cloth provides a striking visual contrast against the dark steel armor while clearly distinguishing the Captain from ordinary soldiers. Behind him, a heavy crimson cloak flows naturally from the shoulders, draping behind the legs in broad supported folds. The cloak remains connected to both the shoulders and lower body to ensure durability without sacrificing movement. The Captain's left arm extends dramatically forward with the index finger pointing directly toward the enemy. This commanding gesture defines the entire miniature. Rather than appearing delicate, the fingers remain slightly thickened and naturally supported by the forearm's angle, ensuring excellent printability while preserving the unmistakable impression of issuing battlefield orders. His right hand firmly grips a practical longsword held low beside the body. The blade is broad, straight, and reinforced with a thick spine, ideal for tabletop durability. The sword hangs in a ready position rather than an exaggerated attack pose, reinforcing the Captain's role as a leader who fights only when necessary. At his waist hangs a second sheathed weapon secured by broad leather belts crossing the hips. Multiple pouches, buckles, and utility straps provide additional military realism while remaining closely integrated into the armor. Layered chainmail skirts emerge beneath the plate armor around the hips before transitioning into heavily armored greaves protecting the legs. Thick leather boots stand securely upon uneven rocky terrain, with both feet making full contact with the base. The round base depicts a rugged battlefield strewn with loose stones, compact earth, and scattered debris. A damaged crimson shield bearing the Hobgoblin legion's insignia lies discarded near the Captain's feet, exactly as shown in the uploaded reference. This broken shield subtly reinforces the ongoing battle while remaining fully integrated into the terrain without creating fragile elements. The recommended colour palette closely follows the uploaded miniature. The skin is painted warm bronze-brown with olive shading and lighter flesh highlights across the face and hands. The armor uses dark weathered steel shaded with black washes before receiving restrained silver edge highlights. The tabard and cloak are painted rich crimson fading into deep burgundy shadows. Leather belts and boots use dark walnut tones with lighter brown highlights. The discarded shield matches the tabard with a dark crimson face and black legion emblem. The rocky terrain combines muted earth browns, weathered greys, and sparse dry grass. Advance. Hold the line. Cable Buddy - Panda Hey everyone, I want to share the latest addition to my CripWorks designs: The Cable Buddies. I was looking for a way to stop my charging cables from bending and breaking at the connector, and I decided to make a cute and functional solution. The concept is simple. The Cable Buddy essentially "bites" onto the end of your cable. This not only protects the weak spot of the cord from wearing out, but it also gives you a much better grip when you are unplugging your devices. It is designed to fit standard USB-C cables comfortably. As you can see from the pictures, the print requires some support material under the belly and inside the mouth area. This is honestly somewhat fiddly to remove - a small flat screwdriver did the trick for me. Just be careful not to break off the teeth. It took quite a while to design and color them. I redesigned the USB cable to make it more suitable for different USB-C cable types. As a workaround for not repainting them after the redesign, I simply added the new cable as a negative → This should not be removed in the slicer. Print Recommendations: Material: PLA or PETG works perfectly fine. PETG is my favorite as it is a little more sturdy. Layer Height: Variable layer height for more details. Infill: 15% Fuzzy Skin: Enabled Supports: Skinny tree This Panda is part of a larger Cable Buddy series I am working on, so keep an eye out for more animals coming soon. I hope you enjoy printing this little guy as much as I enjoyed designing it. Happy printing! description: Guard Miniature – Vigilant Defender of the Realm This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Guard represents the disciplined soldiers that protect towns, castles, temples, and trade routes throughout countless fantasy settings. While individually less powerful than seasoned adventurers, Guards form the backbone of every civilized realm. Their equipment is practical, standardized, and built for reliability rather than heroics. The Guard stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a disciplined defensive stance. Both feet are planted firmly on uneven cobblestones, with the weight distributed evenly to create a stable and believable pose. Rather than charging forward or posing dramatically, the Guard stands ready to receive an approaching threat, conveying professionalism and restraint. The body is realistically proportioned beneath practical clothing and armor. The figure wears a quilted red gambeson that extends to mid-thigh, providing protection while allowing freedom of movement. Heavy folds in the fabric create strong sculptural depth, making the miniature rewarding to paint without introducing unnecessary complexity. A simple steel helmet protects the head. It features a rounded dome with a reinforced brow and subtle rivet detailing, remaining thick enough for reliable printing. Beneath the helmet, the Guard's face is stern and focused, with a determined expression suited to a veteran soldier accustomed to long watches and dangerous patrols. Around the neck rests a wrapped cloth scarf or padded collar that softens the transition between helmet and torso while adding visual interest. The clothing beneath the gambeson remains practical, with loose sleeves gathered beneath simple leather cuffs. The Guard's right hand firmly grips a long spear held vertically beside the body. The shaft is thick enough for durability while remaining visually straight and elegant. The spearhead is broad and leaf-shaped with reinforced proportions that preserve its appearance without creating fragile edges. The spear's butt rests naturally against the base, creating an additional structural anchor. The left arm carries a sturdy kite shield positioned slightly forward in a defensive posture. The shield closely matches the uploaded reference, featuring a wooden construction reinforced by metal edging and a pronounced central boss. Broad panel divisions create excellent painting opportunities while maintaining a robust printable design. The shield is securely attached to the forearm rather than floating independently. A leather belt secures the gambeson at the waist, supporting several practical pouches and a simple utility knife. These accessories remain integrated into the sculpt, adding realism without cluttering the miniature. The trousers are practical and loose-fitting, tucked securely into rugged leather boots suitable for long marches. The boots stand firmly upon the terrain with both feet making complete contact with the base, maximizing stability. The round base depicts a weathered cobblestone street or castle courtyard. Uneven paving stones, shallow cracks, scattered dirt, and sparse patches of dry grass provide subtle environmental storytelling while keeping the Guard as the clear focal point. The terrain remains intentionally low-profile, making the miniature suitable for use in nearly any settlement or fortress encounter. The recommended colour palette follows the uploaded reference. The gambeson is painted in muted crimson or dark red with brown shading and lighter red highlights. The helmet, spearhead, shield rim, and shield boss use worn steel with restrained edge highlights. Leather belts, boots, and pouches work well in dark brown, while the wooden spear shaft and shield face are painted in weathered oak. The shield itself features deep red panels bordered by dark metal, matching the classic town guard appearance. Steadfast at the gate. Watchful through the night. Hallo PokePopper Fans, ich bin ein absoluter Fan von den Meisterwerken vom Designer galledgoose. Um genau zu sein meine ich seine quetschbaren Pokébälle die ihr hier findet: https://makerworld.com/de/models/3012876-pokepoppers?from=search#profileId-3384044 Ich wertschätze den Designer sehr für seine Arbeit. Es sind wahnsinng tolle Quetschbälle die teilweise Print-in-Place gedruckt werden und deshalb im Vergleich zu anderen Quetschbällen recht gut zusammenbaubar sind und auch stabil halten. Schaut also unbedingt bei Ihm vorbei wenn ihr Quetschbälle sucht. Als ich den Standard Pokeball gedruckt habe und mit einem Gummi versehen habe, entand ein sehr spaßiges Spielzeug für mich und meine Kids. Schnell kam aber auch dann der Wunsch, dass es sich ebenso gut auch drehen könnte. Warum nicht Drehen und Quetschen zusammen? Also beschäftige ich mich 2 ganze Tage damit um einen Spinner daraus zu machen. Ich habe gleich 2 verschiedene Kugellager ausprobiert, um möglichst vielen von Euch die Wahl zu geben, je nachdem was ihr gerade zu Hause habt. Es waren 608er Kugellager und R188 Mini Kugellager (beides Open Hybrid aus dem Bambu Shop) am Start. Viele Versuche und Druckstunden später hatte ich den ersten drehbaren Pokéball in der Hand. Übrigens hier gehts zu meiner PokéPoppers Spinner Kollektion: https://makerworld.com/de/collections/32299850-spinning-pokepoppers-with-box (Boostet fleißig, dann gibts auch die anderen Pokébälle als Spinner) Die Collectors Box findet ihr auch dort. Folglich gibt es 2 Versionen: Für kleine R188 Lager und für 608er Standard Lager Da die 608er Kugellager recht schwer und klobig sind, und das “Handgefühl” des Spinners verändern empfehle ich Euch eher die R188 Variante. Auch dreht sich der Spinner mit den R188 Kugellagern deutlich leichter, länger und schneller. Aber funktional ist die 608er Version eben auch auf jeden Fall. Bitte beachtet, dass die Spinner bzw. die Kugellager eine gewisse “ Einlaufzeit ” nötig haben, bis sie ihr volles Potenzial ausschöpfen können. Auch ein Tröpfchen Öl am Lager können helfen. Habt also etwas Geduld. Wichtig ist allerdings nach dem Druck zu prüfen ob die Stützen vom Deckel sauber entfernt wurden und die Oberfläche relativ glatt ist. Sonst bremst es durch Reibung. Solltet Ihr wider Erwarten trotzdem Probleme mit Reibung haben, so skalieren Sie den Deckel ein wenig größer, aber nur in der Höhe (Y=). So wird der Stiel länger und der Abstand zum Ball größer. Mir war allerdings das runde Design sehr wichtig, sodass ich es möglichst eng anliegend designed habe. Bei mir war ein nachträgliches skalieren bisher nicht nötig, alle meine vorbereiteten Pokebälle laufen reibungslos. Es gibt zahlreiche Drucker,- Filamenthersteller und Farben. Alles hat unterschiedliche Kalibrierungen, Toleranzen und Schrumpfungen. Ich habe mit dem P1S von Bambu Lab und dem PLA Basic gedruckt. Sollte der kleine Deckel bei Euch wider Erwarten lose sitzen oder abfallen, so könnt ihr ihn einfach nochmal minimal größer skalieren und erneut drucken (die Druckzeit ist ja nicht so lang). Das ist bei mir bei allen Pokeball-Varianten aber nach meiner Bearbeitung nicht mehr der Fall gewesen. Wichtige Druckparameter: Ich habe auch das Druckprofil ein wenig optimiert: So habe ich für die Teile mit Rundung eine adaptive Schichthöhe gewählt, damit keine hässlichen Layerkreise auf der Oberfläche entstehen. Beim Knopf habe ich die vom Designer zusätzlich angebrachte Stütze entfernt, weil sie sich bei mir nicht gut entfernen lies. Ich empfehle überall den automatischen Baum-Support mit der Einstellung: Stützen nur auf Druckplatte ! Besonders wichtig ist diese Einstellung bei den Schwarzen Teilen. Montageanleitung: Der ursprüngliche Designer galledgoose hat ein Youtube Video zum Zusammenbau hochgeladen. Ihr findet das Video und zusätzliche Hinweise zum Zusammenbau auf der Originalseite von galledgoose: https://makerworld.com/de/models/3012876-pokepoppers?from=search#profileId-3384044 Schaut euch vor allem die schwarzen Teile gut an. Es ist wichtig, dass sie alle gleich herum ausgerichtet sind, weil das Gummiband sonst nicht korrekt in der Nut sitzt. Das Gummiband wird dann auf der Seite angebracht wo die entsprechende Vertiefung dafür ist. Über wertschätzende Kommentare, Likes und Bewertungen freue ich mich immer sehr. Ich werde auch alle beantworten.

description: Ghast Gravecaller Miniature – Herald of the Restless Dead This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts . The Ghast Gravecaller is depicted as a more cunning and ritualistic form of undead predator: a corpse-born summoner that does not merely hunt among the graves, but commands the darkness beneath them. Its silhouette combines the gaunt brutality of a Ghast with the visual authority of a necromantic leader, creating a miniature that is immediately distinct from the common Ghast while remaining clearly part of the same undead lineage. The creature has a tall, lean, and heavily emaciated humanoid body with long arms, powerful thighs, and a broad but hollow chest. Its posture is hunched forward, yet more controlled than the feral crouch of an ordinary Ghast. The Gravecaller stands with its legs spread widely across the base, one foot slightly advanced and the other braced behind, giving it a stable ritual stance. The torso twists subtly toward the outstretched arm, creating a strong diagonal line through the body and making the pose feel active without relying on magical effects. Its head is hairless and corpse-like, with a high, angular skull, pointed ears, deeply sunken eyes, and a mouth stretched open in a guttural command. The jaw is filled with irregular teeth and prominent fangs, while the cheeks are gaunt and drawn tightly against the bone. Several long, string-like tendons or decayed strips of flesh hang from the lower jaw and chin, giving the face a grotesque, ceremonial appearance. These strands should be grouped into thick, connected forms rather than sculpted as individual fragile threads. The left hand grips a tall grave-calling staff planted firmly into the base. The shaft is made from dark, weathered wood or bone-bound timber and is reinforced with wrapped cords, metal bands, and crude ritual bindings. At the top sits a large skull framed by smaller bones and curved supports, creating a dramatic focal point. Every decorative element is physically attached to the staff structure, and the lower end connects directly to the ground for added stability. The staff should appear ancient and macabre, but not overly delicate or overloaded with tiny ornaments. The opposite arm reaches forward with the palm open and the fingers curled, as if the Gravecaller is directing nearby undead toward its prey. The hand is oversized and clawed, with long but thickened nails. Its gesture is commanding rather than mindless, separating this creature from the more animalistic Ghast. The arm remains slightly bent at the elbow to reduce overhang and improve printing strength. The Gravecaller wears a collection of decayed ritual garments and scavenged grave ornaments. A torn mantle hangs from one shoulder and falls behind the upper arm in broad, connected folds. Around the waist is a heavy belt decorated with a central skull, bone plates, and several large talismans. Ragged cloth panels descend between and beside the legs, forming a dark ceremonial skirt. The fabric is heavily damaged, with irregular pointed edges, but all hanging pieces connect to one another or to the legs to avoid unsupported sections. Its exposed skin is stretched tightly over the ribs, shoulders, arms, and legs. Scars, open wounds, hardened growths, and areas of rough necrotic tissue cover the body. The chest remains visibly hollow and starved, while the thighs and shoulders retain enough muscle to suggest the unnatural strength of a Ghast. The fingers and toes end in hooked claws, and both feet are planted securely against the base. The color palette is dominated by desaturated green-grey, pale corpse flesh, and bruised blue. Dark purple and blackened red can be used around wounds, eyes, and the mouth. The garments suit faded violet, charcoal, dirty burgundy, or mouldy black, while the bone ornaments provide pale focal points. The staff works well in dark brown wood, aged ivory, tarnished bronze, and old blood tones. The round tabletop base represents a desecrated burial site. Several skulls, large bone fragments, cracked earth, and grave debris are embedded around the creature’s feet. The staff is planted among these remains, visually connecting the Gravecaller to the dead it commands. The terrain stays low and compact, ensuring that the model’s silhouette remains clear and that no scenery becomes fragile or distracting. A voice beneath the soil. A command the dead obey. The grave answers back. ✨ Key Features Distinctive Ghast Gravecaller design based on the Monster Manual 2024 creature. Clearly differentiated from the standard Ghast through ritual gear and commanding posture. Tall, gaunt undead anatomy with long limbs and visible ribs. Wide, stable stance suited to a necromantic battlefield leader. Grotesque head with pointed ears, sunken eyes, fangs, and hanging jaw tendons. Large grave-calling staff planted directly into the base. Staff topped with an integrated skull and securely attached bone decorations. One clawed hand extended in a commanding summoner-like gesture. Heavy ritual belt with skull ornamentation and large bone talismans. Torn shoulder mantle and layered ceremonial cloth panels. All fabric sections attached to the body or neighbouring garments for print safety. Thickened claws, tendons, staff details, and bone elements for dependable printing. Both feet firmly connected to the round base. Desecrated graveyard terrain with skulls, bones, and cracked earth. No floating spirits, magical energy, smoke, aura effects, or separate components. Strong asymmetrical silhouette suitable for encounter leaders and display collections. Designed for resin printing while remaining achievable on finely tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a muted green-grey, pale blue-grey, or dead flesh basecoat. Shade the recesses with dark purple, black-green, or brown washes, concentrating around the ribs, face, joints, and damaged tissue. Rebuild raised areas with pale grey, ivory, or desaturated green highlights. Add bruising with thin purple, burgundy, and blue glazes around the shoulders, knees, wounds, and mouth. Paint the ritual garments in faded violet, dark burgundy, charcoal, or mouldy brown. Apply a black or dark purple wash, followed by dusty grey or muted lavender edge highlights. Bone ornaments and skulls can be based in dark beige, washed with sepia, and highlighted through bone to pale ivory. For the staff, use dark brown or grey-brown wood with lighter streaks along the grain. Metal bands can be painted in tarnished bronze or blackened iron, with small green or orange corrosion accents. The skull topper should receive stronger highlights than the surrounding bones to make it the visual centre of the miniature. Finish the base with dark soil, grey stones, aged bone, and restrained dead grass tones. Selective gloss inside the mouth, around fresh wounds, or on the eyes can contrast effectively with the matte corpse skin and dusty clothing. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games and miniature collections.

description: Guard Captain Miniature – Veteran Commander of the Watch This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Guard Captain represents an experienced military officer entrusted with the defense of city gates, noble estates, fortified settlements, and important public figures. More disciplined, better equipped, and more imposing than an ordinary Guard, the Captain commands through authority earned in battle rather than extravagant ornamentation. The Guard Captain stands on a Medium 25 mm round tabletop base in a confident frontline pose. The feet are placed apart across uneven stone paving, forming a broad and stable foundation. The torso faces forward while the shoulders rotate slightly, creating a natural sense of alertness. The Captain does not appear caught in an exaggerated attack. Instead, the figure looks ready to issue an order, block an advancing enemy, or personally reinforce a vulnerable section of the line. The body is realistically proportioned, with a sturdy build shaped by years of training and active service. Broad shoulders and strong arms remain visible beneath practical layers of military clothing and armor. The silhouette should immediately appear more experienced and authoritative than the standard Guard without becoming oversized or excessively heroic. The head is protected by a reinforced steel helmet with a rounded crown, pronounced brow, and additional cheek or temple protection. Its construction is more elaborate than the ordinary Guard’s helmet while remaining utilitarian. Subtle rivets, layered metal plates, and shallow engraved details add visual richness without creating fragile projections. The Captain’s face is stern and weathered. A strong jaw, furrowed brow, and focused eyes communicate patience, discipline, and battlefield awareness. The expression should remain controlled rather than enraged. This is a professional soldier who understands when to hold a position and when to commit troops. The torso is protected by a combination of chain mail, padded fabric, and reinforced plate sections. A heavy surcoat or gambeson hangs beneath the armor, creating deep folds and layered edges suitable for painting. The armor should appear functional and well maintained, but not ceremonial. Scratches, shallow dents, and worn edges can suggest extensive service without making the equipment look neglected. One arm carries a large reinforced shield positioned forward and slightly outward. The shield forms a major part of the silhouette and clearly establishes the Captain’s defensive role. Its broad wooden or layered construction is protected by a thick metal rim and central boss. Decorative divisions or simple heraldic panels may be sculpted into the face, but they should remain restrained enough that the model can represent guards from many different kingdoms. The opposite hand grips a heavy one-handed sword. The blade should be broad, straight, and practical, with a reinforced crossguard and sturdy grip. It is held diagonally downward beside the body rather than extended in an unsupported horizontal line. The lower section of the blade may rest close to the shield, leg, or terrain to create a naturally reinforced composition. The weapon remains clearly separate and readable while avoiding a fragile floating position. A thick leather belt supports several practical accessories, including a small pouch, scabbard fittings, and perhaps a whistle, key ring, or compact command horn. These items should lie against the body rather than hanging freely. A short cloak or officer’s mantle may drape across one shoulder and flow down the back, helping distinguish the Captain from rank-and-file troops while remaining securely connected to the torso. The legs are protected by sturdy trousers, greaves, or reinforced boots designed for patrol duty and close combat. Both boots remain fully planted on the base, with no narrow ankle balance points. The stance should communicate complete control and readiness. The round base depicts a fortified courtyard or city gate. Cracked cobblestones, fragments of weathered masonry, scattered grit, and small patches of worn earth create an adaptable urban environment. A low broken stone or damaged shield fragment may be included near one foot, but the scenery should remain compact and firmly integrated. The recommended colour palette follows the uploaded miniature. Deep crimson, dark red, or muted burgundy works well for the surcoat and cloth elements. Armor can be painted in worn steel with black washes and restrained silver highlights. The shield may combine dark wood, red-painted panels, and aged iron reinforcement. Leather straps, boots, and pouches suit rich brown tones, while the Captain’s insignia can be picked out in brass, antique gold, or polished steel. The wall may fail. The line may bend. The Captain does neither. ✨ Key Features Faithful Guard Captain inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Commanding veteran pose based on the uploaded visual reference. Clearly distinguished from the standard Guard through superior armor and equipment. Reinforced steel helmet with practical military detailing. Stern, disciplined facial expression suited to an experienced officer. Layered chain mail, gambeson, surcoat, and plate protection. Large defensive shield with durable metal rim and central boss. Broad one-handed sword positioned for reliable printing. Integrated officer’s accessories, belt equipment, and short mantle. Wide grounded stance with both feet securely attached to the base. Walgreens is one of the largest pharmacy store chains in the US. It's one of those places that seems to be, at least here in the Chicagoland area, in every neighborhood, and you can drive 10 minutes in any direction and hit one of the stores. I will always remember going to Walgreens to get photos developed from my film/disposable cameras. Or, picking up new DVD movie rentals from the Redbox outside the store. The building design has changed over the years as the new buildings are more boxy with a clean white, modern look. But there are still so many older-looking buildings with the brown/tan brick, green awnings, and corner entryways. One thing that hasn't changed is the logo which is classic and easy to recognize. This is a large build and some of the pieces take up almost the entire build plate. But I wanted the building to be as accurate as I could get it, and also include the drive-thru and a parking lot. For assembly, I used super glue for the doors and windows. Most of the other pieces, like the logo signs and the logo window frame and awnings have a nice press fit. I included the base connectors in the 3mf for the base. The connectors are a huge help with these larger model sets with a lot of base pieces. The Redbox signage image is included in the attached PDF. I printed the image on sticker paper and cut it out. The assembly guide is included with list of filaments used. Hopefully you enjoy this build as much as I do! Feel free to reach out with any questions. More models are in the works and coming soon!

description: Lemure Miniature – The Lowest Soul of the Nine Hells This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lemure is among the most pitiful yet disturbing fiends found in the Nine Hells—a damned soul stripped of identity and reduced to a quivering mass of tortured flesh. The miniature stands on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base , though its silhouette is unlike that of any humanoid. Rather than walking upright with confidence, the Lemure appears to be slowly pulling itself upward from a melting mound of its own body. One elongated arm stretches desperately toward an unseen victim while the opposite arm hangs limply at its side, giving the creature a tragic yet unsettling posture. The upper torso rises from a thick pool of malformed flesh that spreads across the base, creating a broad, stable foundation ideal for resin printing. Its anatomy deliberately rejects natural proportions. The body appears to have partially liquefied, with muscles, skin, and bone merging into flowing layers of flesh. The head is little more than a swollen skull wrapped in sagging skin, its enormous gaping mouth frozen in an eternal scream. Empty white eyes stare sightlessly into the distance, while broken teeth jut unevenly from twisted gums. The neck barely exists, swallowed by thick folds of distorted tissue that merge directly into the torso. Across the chest and abdomen, countless tormented faces emerge from the creature's flesh. Some scream silently with open mouths, others grimace in agony, while several seem only partially formed, as though trapped forever beneath the skin. Hands, fingers, and malformed limbs protrude randomly from the mass before disappearing back into it, reinforcing the impression that numerous damned souls have fused into a single infernal body. These grotesque details remain sculpted as thick reliefs rather than fragile protrusions, ensuring excellent printability while preserving the horrific visual complexity. The outstretched left arm provides the model's primary sense of motion. Long, bony fingers reach desperately forward, their stretched tendons and wrinkled skin emphasizing eternal suffering rather than aggression. The opposite arm hangs lower with curled claws, suggesting the creature barely possesses the strength to support itself. Both limbs remain proportionally thick and securely attached to the torso for maximum durability. The lower half dissolves entirely into a broad mound of flowing flesh. Instead of separate legs, thick organic folds spill downward across the base like melting wax. Additional screaming faces, grasping hands, and distorted features emerge throughout this mass, creating visual interest from every viewing angle while simultaneously providing exceptional structural stability. There are no unsupported overhangs or delicate contact points, making the model especially suitable for resin printing. The scenic base represents cracked infernal stone partly consumed by the Lemure's corrupted body. The creature appears almost fused to the ground itself, as if slowly crawling across the blasted surface of the Nine Hells. Small fractured paving stones and subtle ground texture provide visual contrast without distracting from the monstrous figure. Everything remains fully integrated into the base with no loose scenery or fragile details. The recommended paint scheme follows the uploaded reference closely. Pale flesh tones mixed with sickly pinks, bruised purples, and raw crimson washes emphasize the creature's diseased appearance. Recesses between folds benefit from deep violet and red shading, while careful ivory highlights pick out stretched skin and protruding faces. Teeth receive aged bone colors with brown washes, while the ground is painted in dark grey stone with subtle dusty brown highlights. A selective gloss varnish inside mouths and between fleshy folds can add an unsettling organic appearance while preserving the overall matte finish of the miniature. No soul remembers its own name. Only endless agony remains. The first step into eternal damnation. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Horrific melting humanoid sculpt with flowing infernal anatomy. Large screaming primary face with distorted proportions. Multiple partially formed faces emerging throughout the body. Organic mound replacing traditional legs for exceptional print stability. Outstretched grasping arm creating dramatic tabletop presence. Thick sculpted folds designed for crisp resin printing. Scenic infernal stone base fully integrated with the creature. No floating parts, magical effects, smoke, or unsupported elements. Perfect for infernal encounters, devil armies, Nine Hells campaigns, or complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in light grey or bone before layering pale flesh tones mixed with desaturated pinks. Apply crimson, burgundy, and violet washes deep into every fold to create the appearance of bruised, tortured tissue. Highlight raised skin with ivory and pale flesh while painting the embedded faces with slightly different flesh variations to make each one distinct. Teeth are best finished with aged bone colors and brown washes. The stone base benefits from layered greys with dusty brown drybrushing, while selective gloss varnish inside the mouths and deepest fleshy recesses enhances the grotesque organic textures. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Perfect as a low-ranking devil, infernal horror, Nine Hells encounter, fiendish warband member, or essential addition to a complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collection.

description: Merfolk Skirmisher Miniature – Swift Spear of the Shallow Seas This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Merfolk Skirmisher serves as the swift frontline hunter of merfolk communities, patrolling reefs, coastal waters, and submerged ruins with speed and precision. Armed with a long hunting spear and relying on agility rather than heavy armor, this sculpt captures the moment a skilled underwater warrior prepares to strike before disappearing back into the currents. Mounted on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base , the Merfolk Skirmisher rises from a natural underwater environment in a dynamic combat stance. Its powerful fish tail coils tightly beneath the torso before sweeping gracefully around the base, providing both visual balance and structural stability. The upper body twists naturally toward its target while both hands firmly grip a long two-handed spear held diagonally across the body, ready to thrust or parry incoming attacks. The pose conveys fluid underwater movement while remaining solid and practical for tabletop use. The humanoid upper body is lean, athletic, and built for speed rather than brute strength. Defined shoulders, chest, and arms emphasize a lifetime spent swimming through powerful ocean currents. Every muscle appears toned without becoming overly exaggerated, preserving the elegant silhouette traditionally associated with merfolk while maintaining the appearance of a capable warrior. Its face carries an alert, focused expression with sharp predatory features that distinguish it from surface-dwelling humanoids. High cheekbones, narrow eyes, and rows of small pointed teeth hint at its aquatic nature without appearing monstrous. Large fin-like crests extend upward and backward from the head, replacing hair with layered aquatic fins that resemble those of a lionfish or reef predator. Smaller fins continue along the jawline and neck, blending seamlessly into the anatomy. Instead of wearing heavy armor that would hinder movement underwater, the Merfolk Skirmisher is equipped with lightweight protective gear. Sculpted shoulder guards, forearm bracers, and simple leather harnesses provide defense while leaving the torso largely unobstructed. Around the waist hangs a layered skirt formed from broad aquatic leaves or flexible fin-like plates that move naturally with the currents. The design remains practical while reinforcing the civilization's close relationship with the sea. The long spear serves as the miniature's defining weapon. Constructed from a sturdy wooden shaft reinforced with carved details, it ends in an elegant double-edged spearhead decorated with small ornamental rivets and flowing aquatic motifs. The weapon appears equally suited for thrusting in close combat or hunting dangerous sea creatures beneath the waves. From the waist downward, the body transitions into a long muscular fish tail covered in finely sculpted overlapping scales. The scale pattern gradually changes in size along the length of the tail, becoming broader toward the powerful tail fin. The tail curves naturally around the scenic base before ending in a wide flowing caudal fin that reinforces the miniature's graceful underwater movement. Every curve has been designed to create a pleasing silhouette while remaining durable during handling. The scenic base depicts a vibrant section of the ocean floor. Small rocks, coral formations, seaweed, and scattered marine vegetation surround the lower tail, creating a believable underwater environment without overwhelming the figure itself. These natural elements frame the miniature beautifully while reinforcing its aquatic habitat. For painters, the Merfolk Skirmisher offers a wide range of opportunities to explore rich marine color palettes. Turquoise, sea green, deep blue, teal, and muted aqua create beautiful transitions across the scales and fins, while the humanoid skin can feature pale green, blue-grey, or lightly turquoise tones. Careful glazing across the tail enhances the appearance of shimmering scales, while selective edge highlights emphasize each sculpted row. The coral, rocks, and aquatic plants provide additional opportunities for colorful accents using warm oranges, reds, purples, and natural greens. Silent currents carry the hunter forward. The spear strikes before the ripples fade. The sea protects its own. ✨ Key Features Faithful Merfolk Skirmisher inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Dynamic underwater combat pose with a two-handed spear. Athletic humanoid upper body with powerful coiled fish tail. Distinctive fin-like head crest and aquatic facial features. Lightweight armor designed for underwater mobility. Ornamental spear featuring elegant aquatic details. Beautifully sculpted layered scales from waist to tail fin. Scenic ocean floor base with coral, rocks, and sea plants. Graceful silhouette full of movement and balance. Rich organic textures across fins, scales, armor, and equipment. Excellent addition to coastal, underwater, and aquatic encounters. Perfect companion to other merfolk and ocean-dwelling creatures from the Monster Manual 2024 Collection. 🎨 Great for Painting Begin with a light grey primer before applying layered blends of turquoise, teal, sea green, and deep blue across the tail and fins. Use subtle glazes to create natural transitions between the scales, finishing with light edge highlights to enhance the sculpted texture. Paint the skin using muted blue-grey or pale green tones with soft shading around the muscles to preserve the elegant anatomy. The coral and marine vegetation offer opportunities for vibrant accent colors including reds, oranges, purples, and bright greens, while the spear combines natural wood tones with polished steel for visual contrast. Finish the rocky seabed using cool greys with patches of algae and weathering to complete the underwater setting. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. An excellent miniature for underwater adventures, coastal campaigns, ocean encounters, submerged ruins, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.
