description: Lizardfolk Geomancer Miniature – Tribal Master of Stone and Earth This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lizardfolk Geomancer represents one of the tribe's ancient spiritual leaders, channeling the enduring strength of stone and the deep power of the earth rather than raw physical dominance alone. The miniature stands on a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base in a commanding, balanced pose. One clawed foot is planted slightly ahead of the other, creating the impression that the geomancer is advancing while simultaneously calling upon the ground beneath its enemies. The torso twists slightly toward the viewer as one muscular arm reaches forward with an open claw, while the opposite hand grips a towering ritual staff planted firmly beside the body. This asymmetrical composition creates an expressive silhouette without sacrificing structural stability. The Lizardfolk possesses the powerful anatomy typical of its kind. Thick reptilian legs, broad shoulders, muscular forearms, and a heavily scaled torso emphasize both strength and resilience. Large overlapping scales cover the limbs and tail, while the chest and abdomen transition into smaller armored belly plates. A thick tail curls naturally behind the legs before resting against the ground, providing both anatomical realism and an additional point of support for the printed model. Its head displays the unmistakable features of an experienced reptilian shaman. A broad crocodilian snout reveals rows of sharp teeth arranged in a confident, almost predatory grin. Narrow reptilian eyes suggest intelligence rather than savagery, while short cranial spines and ridged scales continue across the top of the skull and down the neck. The expression conveys calm authority, as though the geomancer commands the battlefield through patience rather than fury. Unlike the heavily armored Lizardfolk Soldier, the Geomancer wears ceremonial tribal armor suited to a respected elder. Layered shoulder guards carved from wood and reinforced with bronze fittings rest over leather harnesses crossing the chest. Numerous carved skulls, primitive talismans, beads, and bone ornaments decorate the armor, reflecting years of spiritual leadership and ritual significance. Wide leather bracers wrap around both forearms, while engraved hanging cloth panels descend from an ornate belt decorated with carved masks and tribal motifs. Every decorative element remains thick, interconnected, and securely attached to the body for excellent printability. The focal point of the miniature is its imposing ritual staff. Crafted from a thick wooden shaft wrapped with leather bindings, the weapon terminates in a massive cluster of rough-hewn stone crystals secured within primitive bindings. Rather than appearing magical through floating rocks or visual effects, the power is implied entirely through the sculpt itself. The staff stands planted firmly upon the base, providing another strong structural anchor while reinforcing the geomancer's commanding posture. The extended left hand reaches toward unseen enemies with spread claws, suggesting the casting of earth-shaping magic. Because no magical energy, floating stones, or spell effects are included, the model remains fully compatible with practical resin printing while still conveying dynamic action through pose alone. The scenic base depicts cracked earth scattered with broken stones, weathered skulls, fractured rock formations, and sparse desert vegetation. Beside the staff lies a partially collapsed stone shrine with primitive offerings, subtly reinforcing the geomancer's connection to ancient earth spirits. Every scenic component is sculpted directly into the base to maximize strength and eliminate fragile separate pieces. The recommended paint scheme closely follows the uploaded reference. Olive-green scales shaded with darker moss tones contrast beautifully against pale tan belly scales. Wooden armor receives warm brown tones highlighted with lighter drybrushing, while bronze fittings gain depth through verdigris or dark washes. Bone ornaments are painted with aged ivory and sepia shading. The ritual staff combines rich wood grain with layered grey stone, while the base uses dusty browns, muted rocks, scattered bones, and touches of dry vegetation to complete the rugged wilderness appearance. The earth remembers every step. Stone answers only the patient. The oldest wisdom lies beneath your feet. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. Powerful reptilian geomancer with commanding ritual pose. Muscular lizardfolk anatomy with highly detailed overlapping scales. Extended spellcasting hand without fragile magical effects. Massive earth-themed ritual staff topped with bound stone crystals. Ceremonial tribal armor featuring carved wood, bronze fittings, skulls, and bone ornaments. Ground-supported tail providing additional structural stability. Scenic wilderness base with rocks, skulls, primitive shrine, and scattered debris. No floating elements, smoke, spell effects, or unsupported components. Perfect for wilderness encounters, tribal shamans, earth priests, reptilian civilizations, and complete Monster Manual 2024 collections. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before layering olive greens and moss tones across the scales, gradually highlighting raised edges with lighter yellow-green. Paint the belly scales using warm tan and bone colors shaded with brown washes. The ceremonial armor benefits from rich leather browns, weathered wood tones, and bronze metallic accents. Bone ornaments are best painted with ivory, sepia washes, and cream highlights. The ritual staff combines textured wood grain with layered grey stone drybrushing, while the scenic base uses dusty earth, weathered rocks, scattered skulls, and muted vegetation to emphasize the geomancer's connection to the land. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Medium Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. Ideal as a tribal shaman, wilderness spellcaster, reptilian elder, earth priest, encounter leader, or centerpiece for Lizardfolk-themed adventures within a complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collection.

description: Lizardfolk Soldier Miniature – Relentless Tribal Warrior This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Lizardfolk Soldier represents the disciplined frontline warrior of the reptilian tribes, strong, pragmatic, and utterly fearless. Closely inspired by the uploaded reference and faithful to the Monster Manual 2024 depiction, this sculpt emphasizes brute resilience over elegance, combining primitive craftsmanship with practical armor and a powerful hammer. The miniature stands upon a Medium (25 mm) round tabletop base , adopting a broad, stable stance that immediately conveys physical strength. Both clawed feet are planted firmly on uneven ground with the knees slightly bent, creating the impression that the soldier is prepared to absorb an incoming charge or deliver a devastating crushing strike. The pose is symmetrical and balanced, producing an exceptionally sturdy model with an unmistakable battlefield silhouette. The Lizardfolk possesses a heavily muscled reptilian physique covered in overlapping scales. Powerful shoulders, thick forearms, and broad legs emphasize raw physical power rather than speed. The torso remains partially exposed, revealing durable abdominal scales and a lighter armored underbelly that contrasts naturally with the darker scales across the back, arms, and tail. The long muscular tail curls naturally behind the legs before resting against the ground, providing additional structural support while reinforcing the reptilian anatomy. The head is unmistakably that of a predatory reptile. A broad snout lined with numerous sharp teeth forms a permanent intimidating grin, while narrow reptilian eyes project constant vigilance. Short horn-like cranial spines and layered neck frills continue down the back of the skull, adding visual interest without becoming fragile. The expression remains calm and confident rather than feral, portraying a veteran warrior accustomed to battle. Unlike lightly equipped tribal hunters, this soldier wears practical armor assembled from forged metal and scavenged materials. Large layered pauldrons protect the shoulders while reinforced bracers shield both forearms. Heavy greaves wrap around the lower legs without restricting movement, and leather harnesses cross the chest to secure armor plates and battlefield equipment. Bone trophies, carved fangs, and small skull ornaments hang from the harness and belt, displaying victories over dangerous prey while remaining thick enough for dependable printing. The centerpiece of the miniature is its imposing two-handed hammer. The long reinforced haft is grasped firmly with both hands across the front of the body, creating an exceptionally stable composition. At its end rests a massive rectangular stone-and-metal hammerhead, weathered through years of combat. Its broad shape immediately communicates crushing power while remaining easy to print and resistant to damage during gameplay. Because both hands support the weapon, there are no thin unsupported connections anywhere on the sculpt. The clothing remains intentionally simple. A rugged leather loincloth reinforced with stitched hide strips hangs from a heavy belt decorated with carved skulls and primitive ornaments. Small pouches and simple survival equipment are attached around the waist, reflecting the practical lifestyle of the Lizardfolk rather than excessive decoration. Every accessory remains securely attached to either the body or armor to maximize durability. The scenic base depicts dry wilderness terrain scattered with cracked earth, weathered stones, broken bones, and partially buried skulls that hint at previous battles or ancient hunting grounds. Sparse tufts of hardy vegetation emerge between the rocks, providing subtle environmental storytelling without distracting from the central figure. Every scenic detail is sculpted directly into the base for maximum print stability. The recommended paint scheme follows the uploaded reference closely. The scales are best painted in layered olive green, moss green, and muted yellow-green, while the belly scales transition toward pale tan or warm bone. Armor plates should be rendered in worn iron with bronze trim and subtle weathering. Leather straps and cloth are painted in dark browns, while the bone trophies receive aged ivory highlighted with warm cream. The hammer combines weathered stone greys with dark metallic reinforcements, and the base benefits from dusty earth tones accented with scattered bone fragments and muted green vegetation. The swamp forged its body. Battle forged its discipline. Survival forged its purpose. ✨ Key Features Faithfully inspired by Monster Manual 2024 . Closely matches the uploaded reference miniature. description: Hydra Miniature – Five-Headed Apex Predator of the Primeval Marsh This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Hydra is one of the most iconic legendary monsters in the Monster Manual 2024, a colossal reptilian predator whose greatest terror lies in its regenerative ability and its writhing mass of ravenous heads. This miniature faithfully follows the uploaded reference, depicting a powerful five-headed Hydra crouched low as every serpentine neck lashes outward in search of prey. The Hydra occupies a Huge (75 mm) round tabletop base . Its body sits low against the ground, emphasizing tremendous weight and raw power rather than speed. All four limbs are planted firmly upon the terrain with broad reptilian feet gripping the earth, creating an exceptionally stable miniature despite its enormous size. The wide stance immediately conveys that this creature dominates everything around it. The central body is massive and muscular, resembling an enormous crocodilian or monitor lizard. Thick shoulders blend into an immensely powerful chest while broad hindquarters support the creature's tremendous bulk. Dense overlapping muscles remain visible beneath the scales without appearing exaggerated, reinforcing the impression that every movement is driven by incredible strength. The most striking feature is the cluster of five independent serpentine necks , each emerging naturally from the broad shoulder girdle rather than appearing attached as separate pieces. The necks twist around one another in a tightly woven composition that matches the uploaded reference while remaining fully printable. Their curves support one another structurally, eliminating fragile floating sections and producing a cohesive sculpt. Each head possesses its own subtle personality while remaining unmistakably part of the same creature. Every head features an angular crocodilian skull covered with rugged scales and heavy brow ridges. The mouths are opened in deafening roars, exposing rows of long conical teeth and fleshy throats. Slight differences in neck angle and jaw position make every head feel alive without disrupting the balanced composition. Short bony horns and irregular cranial spines decorate each skull. These remain broad and heavily rooted within the head plates rather than becoming thin spikes, preserving both durability and the unmistakable silhouette associated with the Monster Manual Hydra. The necks display layered reptilian scales that gradually transition from larger armored plates near the shoulders into smaller flexible scales toward the heads. Deep folds appear beneath each neck where the creature bends and twists, producing rich sculptural detail ideal for washes and drybrushing. The back is protected by rows of heavy dorsal spines and thick armored scales. Rather than needle-like projections, the spines are short, broad, and integrated directly into the natural armor. These continue along the spine before fading into the muscular tail. The forelegs are immensely powerful, terminating in broad clawed feet equipped with thick curved talons. Matching hind legs anchor the creature solidly to the ground, ensuring the miniature remains exceptionally stable. Every claw presses firmly into the terrain, emphasizing the Hydra's immense weight. A long muscular tail emerges from the rear of the body and sweeps naturally around the back of the base. Following the uploaded reference, the tail remains close to the ground and curves behind the hind legs, improving structural integrity while balancing the overall composition. The round base depicts a devastated marshland or ancient riverside. Broken tree stumps, shattered logs, scattered rocks, compact mud, and weathered debris surround the creature, suggesting a landscape repeatedly destroyed by the Hydra's relentless movements. These scenic elements remain low-profile and fully integrated into the base so they never distract from the monster itself. The recommended colour palette follows the uploaded miniature closely. The scales are painted deep olive green with darker forest-green shadows between each plate. Raised scales receive progressively lighter olive and moss-green highlights. The underside transitions into pale khaki and muted ivory running from the lower jaws across the throats and belly. Horns, claws, and teeth fade from dark brown into aged bone. The mouths use deep crimson and muted pink, while the base combines muddy earth browns, weathered timber, cool grey stone, and scattered marsh vegetation. Five mouths roar as one. Five hunters strike together. The battle has already begun. ✨ Key Features Faithful Hydra inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Closely based on the uploaded reference miniature. Massive five-headed configuration with naturally intertwined necks. Broad crocodilian body emphasizing immense physical power. Individual roaring heads with subtle anatomical variation. Heavy layered reptilian scales across the entire body. Thick integrated dorsal spines optimized for durable printing. Powerful clawed limbs with full contact to the terrain. Long muscular tail positioned close to the base for structural strength. Marshland base featuring broken logs, rocks, and muddy ground. No floating magical effects, smoke, aura, or detached scenery. Exceptionally strong tabletop silhouette visible from every angle. Optimized for high-detail resin printing and suitable for carefully tuned FDM printers. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before applying a deep olive-green basecoat across the scales. Shade the recesses using dark green mixed with brown before layering progressively lighter moss-green highlights across the raised scales and dorsal ridges. Paint the underbelly using khaki blended into warm ivory, carefully glazing the transitions where the belly meets the darker scales. The mouths benefit from deep burgundy and crimson tones highlighted with muted pink along the gums and tongues. Teeth and claws should be painted aged ivory shaded with sepia before receiving sharp bone-white edge highlights. The broken logs work beautifully in weathered brown with subtle grey drybrushing, while the muddy ground combines layered earth browns, olive washes, and patches of dark green vegetation. Finish the miniature with a matte varnish while leaving the mouths and eyes with a slight satin finish to create a lifelike appearance. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Huge Recommended Base: 75 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm, 32 mm, and heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games, swamp encounters, legendary monster battles, high-level adventures, and premium miniature collections.

description: About Models: These models are designed to represent real animals as naturally as possible, with focus on accurate size, shapes, proportions, colors, fine details, and natural movement or pose. Some models include articulated, hinge, or flexi parts for motion and flexibility, while others are non-articulated and focus on realistic appearance. Some parts, such as legs, can be carefully adjusted with gentle heat for a more natural pose, but too much heat can damage or deform the model. Print: All settings are pre-configured and optimized for a balance between detail, print time, strength, functionality, and easy support removal. I recommend printing the models at their original scale. Scaling down may cause issues such as fused moving parts, small hinges not working correctly, or fine details not printing properly. Difficulty Guide: The difficulty icon is a general overall guide and may vary depending on your printer, filament, slicer settings, calibration, and experience. It mainly reflects print complexity, filament changes, possible waste, fine details, support use, and support removal. Multicolor prints may create more waste on single-nozzle AMS or AMS Lite systems, such as A1 with AMS Lite, compared to dual-nozzle or lower-waste systems like X2D or H2C. Level 3 / Supports: For higher difficulty models, especially Level 3, I recommend using Support Material for PLA. It can make support removal much easier, cleaner, and safer for delicate parts. This is especially helpful when the model has many supports, thin details, legs, antennas, or other fragile areas. Note / Handling: Some models may have very small hinge parts or delicate thin areas, such as legs, antennas, tails, or other small details. On some models, these parts may disconnect or break more easily if handled roughly. Please handle the models with care. They are not intended for aggressive play, but rather as educational models, display pieces, or gentle collectible toys. Durability may vary from model to model. Some models are stronger and may be suitable for careful play, while others are more delicate and better suited for display on a shelf. Articulated / Hinge Versions: For models with moving parts, hinges, or flexi sections, please open the included 3MF file, ideally in Bambu Studio. Exporting to another slicer may cause hinge problems. My hinges are created and tested by me, usually designed to print without supports, and are added this way so they can be moved, adjusted, customized, or removed when scaling the model down. STL / 3MF Note: STL files are usually provided without moving parts. The prepared articulated or hinge version is inside the 3MF file. This helps avoid problems with small scaled-down models, where moving parts, gaps, or hinges may fuse or fail. If needed, you can remove the hinges and print the model as a solid version. Safety Notice: Some models may have sharp edges or small parts. Avoid printing them too small and do not leave children unattended with them, as there is a choking risk. If you adjust parts with heat, always proceed carefully and use heat gently. Support / Links: I truly appreciate every comment, rating, or photo of your print it really motivates me to keep creating. description: Steam Mephit Miniature – Scalding Mischief from the Boiling Mists This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. Formed where fire and water collide, the Steam Mephit is an energetic and troublesome elemental that delights in confusion, bursts of scalding vapor, and sudden ambushes. Equal parts playful and dangerous, it appears almost weightless as it darts through clouds of mist before striking with razor claws and boiling breath. This sculpt captures the creature in a low stalking pose, moments before it erupts into motion. Mounted on a Small (25 mm) round tabletop base , the Steam Mephit crouches with both clawed feet firmly planted on uneven stone. Its knees remain deeply bent while the torso leans aggressively forward, creating a compact yet energetic silhouette. Both arms extend outward with long hooked claws poised to slash at nearby prey. The pose conveys agility and constant movement while maintaining excellent tabletop stability and a clean, readable profile from every viewing angle. Unlike the fiery Magma Mephit or the soot-covered Smoke Mephit, the Steam Mephit's body combines smooth mineral plates with softened edges that suggest stone continuously shaped by heat and moisture. Its physique remains lean and athletic, emphasizing speed over strength. Layered scales cover the limbs and torso, while broader armor-like plates protect the chest, shoulders, and hips. The entire anatomy feels streamlined, almost polished by centuries of exposure to boiling vapor. The head immediately commands attention with an impossibly wide grin filled with rows of long needle-like teeth. Large pale eyes dominate the face, giving the creature an unsettling, almost ghostly appearance. Curved horns rise from the crown while numerous jagged fins and layered scales radiate around the cheeks and neck, creating the impression of condensed mineral deposits formed by endless cycles of steam and cooling water. Its chest and abdomen display overlapping plate-like scales that resemble cooled mineral crust rather than rough volcanic rock. Smaller scales continue along the arms and legs before transitioning into large clawed hands and feet capable of gripping slippery stone surfaces. The claws themselves remain long, sharply curved, and elegant, reinforcing the creature's agile hunting style. Large bat-like wings spread high above the shoulders, creating the iconic mephit silhouette while remaining compact enough for practical tabletop use. The supporting wing bones appear sturdy and slightly weathered, while the membranes look thin and worn, featuring subtle tears and stretched folds that suggest countless flights through turbulent clouds of hot vapor. The wings remain broad enough to balance the composition without overwhelming the miniature's compact proportions. A thick reptilian tail extends behind the creature before naturally curling around the base. Covered with layered scales matching the rest of the body, the tail provides both visual balance and structural stability. Toward the tip, the scales become larger and more pronounced, creating an elegant transition that reinforces the elemental's reptilian appearance. The creature wears only a simple layered loincloth formed from thin overlapping mineral plates that blend naturally into the rest of its anatomy. This restrained design keeps the sculpt focused on its elemental form while adding subtle visual variety around the hips. The scenic base depicts weathered stone scattered with cracked paving and uneven rocky textures, suggesting ancient ruins constantly exposed to moisture, heat, and rising vapor. The base remains intentionally understated, allowing the Steam Mephit itself to remain the primary focal point while providing an environment appropriate for volcanic springs, geothermal caverns, or elemental planes. For painters, the Steam Mephit offers wonderful opportunities to explore cool neutral palettes accented by subtle warm undertones. Pale greys, weathered stone colors, soft blue-greens, and muted ivory create convincing mineral surfaces, while careful glazing introduces hints of dampness across the scales. Thin blue-grey washes emphasize the recesses between the layered plates, while gentle edge highlights define the sculpted details. The eyes can be painted with bright white or pale blue to create an eerie supernatural glow, while the wing membranes benefit from delicate gradients between pale grey, dusty pink, and muted blue to suggest thin semi-translucent skin. The air grows strangely warm. Mist gathers across the battlefield. Then the vapor strikes. ✨ Key Features Faithful Steam Mephit inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Dynamic crouching pose full of speed and anticipation. Lean elemental anatomy covered in layered mineral scales. Wicked grinning face with rows of razor-sharp teeth. Large pale eyes creating an eerie supernatural expression. Curved horns with jagged fin-like facial spines. Large bat-like wings with weathered membranes. Thick scaled tail naturally curling around the base. Rich layered stone and mineral textures throughout the sculpt. Scenic rocky base suitable for geothermal and volcanic environments. Distinct silhouette ideal for elemental encounters. Perfect companion to the complete collection of elemental mephits. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature using a light grey primer before building layers of cool stone greys, pale ivory, muted blue-greens, and soft weathered browns across the body. Apply blue-grey washes between the layered scales to create depth before carefully edge-highlighting the raised plates with pale grey or off-white. The eyes provide an excellent focal point when painted with bright white or icy blue, while subtle glazing around the face can create the impression of lingering moisture. Paint the wing membranes with soft transitions between pale grey, dusty pink, and muted blue while highlighting the supporting bones with warm ivory. Complete the base using weathered stone, damp rock effects, and subtle mineral staining to evoke ancient ruins surrounded by hot springs and drifting steam. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Small Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. A perfect addition to elemental encounters, geothermal caverns, volcanic adventures, planar campaigns, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: Winged Kobold Miniature – Dragonkin Aerial Ambusher This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. While ordinary kobolds rely on numbers and cunning traps, Winged Kobolds add an entirely new dimension to the battlefield. Blessed—or perhaps cursed—with leathery draconic wings, they dive from cavern ceilings, ruined towers, and dragon lairs to harass intruders from above before disappearing into darkness. This miniature faithfully follows the uploaded reference, portraying a Winged Kobold poised in a low, aggressive stance with its wings fully extended, spear in hand, ready to launch into combat. The miniature stands on a Small (25 mm) round tabletop base in a broad, crouched pose that immediately communicates speed and agility. Both clawed feet are firmly planted among scattered rocks, with deeply bent knees and a low center of gravity that suggests the creature has only just landed—or is moments away from taking flight. The pose creates an energetic silhouette while maintaining excellent structural integrity for printing. Its anatomy follows the classic draconic proportions of a kobold. The body is compact, lean, and wiry, built for speed rather than brute strength. Long forearms, digitigrade legs, and a flexible tail emphasize the creature's reptilian heritage. The tail emerges naturally from the lower back and curves around the rear of the base in a wide arc, remaining close to the ground to provide additional visual balance without creating unsupported overhangs. The head is unmistakably draconic, featuring an elongated snout filled with sharp triangular teeth displayed in an open snarl. Narrow reptilian eyes glare fiercely beneath ridged brows, while large pointed ears angle backward alongside small horn-like protrusions that rise from the crown. The facial expression conveys equal parts confidence, aggression, and mischievous cunning, perfectly fitting the unpredictable personality of Winged Kobolds. The creature's defining feature is its pair of fully extended dragon-like wings. Rather than feathered wings, these are leathery membranes stretched between sturdy finger bones, closely resembling those of small dragons. Each wing connects naturally to the shoulders with thick musculature before extending outward in a broad, symmetrical display. The membranes feature subtle wrinkles, stretched textures, and reinforced wing fingers that create dramatic visual appeal while remaining thick enough for dependable resin printing. Their wide span gives the miniature an instantly recognizable aerial silhouette without becoming excessively fragile. The right hand grips a crude short spear held low beside the body, ready for quick thrusting attacks during aerial dives or skirmishes. The spear has a thick wooden shaft bound with rope and fitted with a rugged forged metal spearhead that reflects improvised kobold craftsmanship. The left hand remains open with extended claws, reaching toward an approaching enemy as though preparing to grab hold or maintain balance during flight. The Winged Kobold wears only minimal equipment appropriate for its lightweight role. A simple stitched leather chest harness provides modest protection without restricting wing movement. Rough cloth wrappings cover the forearms and portions of the legs, while a worn loincloth hangs from a rope belt. A small pouch attached at the hip hints at tools, sling stones, or scavenged valuables collected during raids. Every accessory is kept compact and securely attached to avoid fragile components while reinforcing the creature's practical survivalist nature. The scales covering the body vary naturally in size. description: Smoke Mephit Miniature – Ashen Trickster of Smoldering Skies This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. Formed where fire and air intertwine, the Smoke Mephit is a cunning and unpredictable elemental that thrives amid volcanic vents, burning ruins, and choking clouds of ash. Rather than overwhelming strength, it relies on speed, deception, and bursts of blinding smoke to harass enemies before disappearing into the haze. This sculpt captures the creature in a tense, predatory stance, ready to dart forward while filling the battlefield with suffocating smoke. Mounted on a Small (25 mm) round tabletop base , the Smoke Mephit crouches low with both clawed feet firmly planted on cracked volcanic stone. Its body leans aggressively forward while both arms extend toward its victim, long talons spread wide in anticipation of a sudden strike. The balanced stance keeps the miniature stable while giving the impression of constant movement, perfectly reflecting the restless and mischievous nature of these elemental beings. Unlike the glowing Magma Mephit or the crystalline Ice Mephit, the Smoke Mephit's body is composed almost entirely of dark soot-black stone and scorched scales. The anatomy remains lean and athletic, emphasizing agility over brute force. Muscles are sharply defined beneath layered rocky scales that resemble cooled volcanic slate, while only the smallest glowing ember cracks peek through the darker surface. The overall silhouette feels lighter and more elusive, like a creature born from drifting ash rather than molten lava. Its head is immediately recognizable thanks to its wicked grin stretching almost ear to ear. Rows of narrow, needle-like teeth fill the mouth, glowing with a faint ember-orange hue deep inside the throat. Bright orange eyes burn beneath sharply angled brows, providing the strongest source of color across the face. Two compact curved horns rise from the crown while layered rocky spines frame the cheeks, neck, and shoulders, giving the head an intimidating crown-like silhouette. Across the torso, overlapping scales form natural armor that transitions seamlessly into muscular arms and powerful digitigrade legs. Unlike polished armor, every plate appears chipped, weathered, and rough from constant exposure to smoke, ash, and volcanic debris. The claws are long, curved, and sharply defined, making the miniature feel dangerous even without wielding manufactured weapons. Large bat-like wings dominate the upper silhouette without overwhelming the compact body. Their skeletal supports resemble blackened volcanic bone while the wing membranes appear dark, weathered, and slightly ragged from endless flights through hot ash clouds. The wings are spread just enough to create an imposing profile while remaining compact enough for practical tabletop use. Fine folds and subtle tears provide visual interest without making the sculpt appear fragile. Behind the creature, a thick reptilian tail sweeps naturally around the base. Covered in overlapping rocky scales, the tail gradually widens into layered ridges that resemble cooling ash deposits. This flowing curve balances the composition beautifully while helping reinforce the mephit's reptilian and elemental origins. The only clothing worn by the creature is a simple layered loincloth fashioned from hardened volcanic plates. It integrates naturally into the sculpt, preserving the lean anatomy while adding subtle variation to the textures across the lower torso. The scenic base depicts fractured volcanic rock dusted with ash and scattered stone fragments. Instead of flowing lava, the environment suggests cooled volcanic terrain where smoke still rises from hidden fissures beneath the surface. The restrained basing supports the miniature while allowing the creature itself to remain the clear focal point. For painters, the Smoke Mephit offers an excellent opportunity to work with dark monochromatic palettes accented by vivid points of glowing heat. Begin with charcoal, black, and cool dark greys before layering lighter grey edge highlights across the rocky scales. The glowing eyes, mouth, and tiny ember fissures can be painted with oranges, reds, and bright yellows to create subtle internal warmth without overpowering the darker body. Thin drybrushing enhances the stone textures, while selective glazing around the glowing details creates the illusion of lingering heat hidden beneath the soot-black exterior. Ash drifts across silent ruins. A wicked grin appears through the haze. Then the smoke comes alive. ✨ Key Features Faithful Smoke Mephit inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Dynamic crouching pose full of speed and menace. Lean elemental anatomy covered in soot-black rocky scales. Wicked grinning face with glowing ember-filled mouth. Bright orange eyes beneath jagged volcanic brows. Curved horns with layered rocky neck spines. Large bat-like wings with dark weathered membranes. Thick scaled tail curling naturally around the base. Rich layered stone textures across the entire body. Scenic volcanic base with cracked stone and ash-covered terrain. Distinct silhouette ideal for elemental encounters. Perfect companion to the complete collection of elemental mephits. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime the miniature in black before building layers of dark charcoal and cool greys across the rocky surfaces. Drybrush progressively lighter greys to emphasize the sculpted textures while maintaining the creature's dark appearance. Paint the glowing eyes, teeth, mouth, and subtle ember cracks using deep reds, bright oranges, and touches of yellow to create restrained internal heat. The wings look particularly striking with gradients of black, dark brown, and smoky grey, finished with slightly lighter highlights along the stretched membranes. Complete the volcanic base using black stone, dusty ash effects, and scattered grey highlights to evoke an ancient landscape still haunted by lingering smoke. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Small Recommended Base: 25 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. description: Marilith Miniature – Six-Bladed General of the Abyss This miniature is part of the Monster Manual 2024 Collection , a series of iconic creatures faithfully reimagined as dynamic, tabletop-ready sculpts. The Marilith is one of the most recognizable demons of the Abyss, a terrifying combination of supernatural elegance, martial perfection, and overwhelming brutality. Towering over lesser fiends, this sculpt captures the creature as a master swordswoman whose every movement is precise, calculated, and impossibly fast. Mounted on a Large (50 mm) round tabletop base , the miniature presents the Marilith in a commanding upright pose. Rather than lunging wildly into battle, she stands with absolute confidence, coiled like a striking serpent that knows victory is inevitable. Her massive serpentine body forms a broad spiral across the base before rising vertically into a powerful humanoid torso. The coiled tail creates an exceptionally stable foundation while naturally guiding the viewer's eye upward toward the six-armed upper body. The lower half is that of an immense constrictor serpent covered in overlapping scales that gradually shift from broad armored belly plates along the front to tightly layered scales wrapping around the back and sides. The tail coils tightly across the base before disappearing naturally beneath the body and continuing seamlessly into the upright torso. This continuous transition emphasizes that the Marilith is a single creature rather than a humanoid standing on a snake body. Above the waist, the physique is athletic, muscular, and perfectly symmetrical. Defined shoulders, powerful arms, and a sculpted abdomen reflect centuries of endless combat. Unlike brutish demons that rely on raw strength alone, the Marilith possesses the physique of an immortal weapon master whose speed rivals her immense power. The six arms are arranged in an elegant radial composition that remains balanced from every viewing angle. Each arm is positioned independently, ensuring every sword has clear visual separation while avoiding unnecessary overlap. Together they create the unmistakable silhouette that has made the Marilith one of the most iconic demons in fantasy gaming. Every hand grips a wickedly curved abyssal blade with unique orientation, suggesting a whirlwind of perfectly coordinated attacks waiting to unfold. The swords themselves feature cruel, forward-curving profiles with sharpened inner edges, engraved guards, and dark infernal craftsmanship. While similar in style, subtle differences in angle and positioning keep the weapon arrangement dynamic without becoming visually chaotic. Her face conveys calm confidence rather than mindless rage. Sharp cheekbones, focused eyes, and a stern expression suggest a calculating battlefield commander who has orchestrated countless massacres. Long flowing black hair falls naturally behind her shoulders while leaving the face fully visible. Two elegant, backward-curving horns emerge from beneath an ornate infernal crown that frames her features without overwhelming them. The armor is decorative yet functional, emphasizing her status among the highest ranks of demonkind. Layered bronze and dark gold armor protects the shoulders, hips, and chest while leaving the muscular torso visible. Intricate engraved details, infernal motifs, and overlapping scale-like plates complement the serpent anatomy without hiding it. Matching arm bracers and jewelry unify all six arms into a coherent design. The scenic base represents broken infernal stone flooring scattered with fractured flagstones and jagged spikes emerging from the ground. These architectural remnants subtly suggest the corrupted fortresses and endless battlefields of the Abyss while remaining low enough that the Marilith remains the undisputed focal point of the miniature. For painting, the Marilith offers an outstanding balance of organic textures and metallic detail. The serpentine scales lend themselves beautifully to gradients of dark brown, charcoal, crimson, or deep purple, while lighter highlights across individual scales create impressive depth. Bronze and antique gold armor contrasts elegantly with darker skin tones, and the six blades provide opportunities for polished steel effects with cold blue highlights. The horns, claws, and teeth complete the infernal appearance using ivory, bone, and subtle weathering. Six blades move as one. An immortal general surveys the battlefield. Every strike is already foreseen. ✨ Key Features Faithful Marilith inspired by the Monster Manual 2024 . Iconic six-armed demon with an elegant serpentine lower body. Massive coiled snake tail seamlessly transitioning into the humanoid torso. Six individually posed arms, each wielding a curved abyssal sword. Powerful athletic anatomy emphasizing speed and martial mastery. Regal infernal crown with backward-curving horns. Flowing long hair framing a calm yet intimidating expression. Ornate bronze and gold infernal armor with layered scale motifs. Detailed serpent scales across the entire lower body. Scenic infernal stone base with fractured masonry and abyssal spikes. Dynamic silhouette that remains balanced from every viewing angle. Excellent centerpiece miniature for demon armies and high-level encounters. 🎨 Great for Painting Prime in black before building the skin using rich crimson, dark mahogany, muted purple, or warm brown tones. Layer progressively lighter highlights across the muscles and serpent scales to emphasize volume while applying darker washes between individual scales for additional depth. Paint the armor using antique bronze or aged gold with selective edge highlights to bring out the intricate engravings. The six swords benefit from polished steel effects with subtle blue reflections along the cutting edges. Finish the horns, claws, and teeth in warm ivory, while weathering the stone base with layered greys and dusty browns to create a stark contrast against the richly colored demon. 📏 Scale & Compatibility Creature Size: Large Recommended Base: 50 mm round tabletop base Compatible with standard 28 mm and 32 mm heroic-scale fantasy tabletop games. An exceptional centerpiece for Abyssal encounters, demon legions, infernal campaigns, planar adventures, and complete Monster Manual 2024 miniature collections.

description: Bring elegant alien architecture and versatile battlefield cover to your tabletop with this detailed Aeldari-inspired ruined wall section. This terrain piece represents the remains of an ancient and highly advanced alien structure. Tall arched openings, flowing ornamental lines, slender supporting pillars, curved details, and damaged upper edges give the model a distinctive and elegant Aeldari-inspired appearance. The wall fits naturally into ancient alien settlements, ruined temples, abandoned outposts, Webway sites, forgotten cities, overgrown battlefields, ceremonial complexes, and countless other science-fiction environments. Its long profile makes it highly versatile during gameplay. The wall can be used as battlefield cover, part of a ruined building, a decorative boundary, the remains of an ancient temple, or as an architectural element within a larger alien settlement. The open arch sections create interesting lines of sight while still providing believable protection and visual separation for infantry models. This makes the terrain useful not only as decoration, but also as a functional and tactical part of the battlefield. The damaged upper edge creates the appearance of an ancient structure that has survived centuries of warfare and decay. Flowing frames, recessed details, elegant pillars, and curved ornamental elements give the wall plenty of visual depth and make it especially suitable for drybrushing, washes, glowing energy effects, weathering, overgrown ruins, and contrasting colour schemes. All my models are based on real test prints — not only digital renders. I always aim for the best possible balance between print time, detail, durability, and filament consumption, ensuring that the terrain looks impressive on the tabletop while remaining reliable and practical to print. The model is specifically designed for FDM printing and prints beautifully in standard grey PLA without requiring filament changes. It can be painted to match your army and battlefield, or used directly from the printer as clean grey science-fiction terrain. description: Ultimate Parametric Pipe & Cable Clip Looking for a pipe or cable clip that fits your exact needs? This fully parametric generator lets you customize almost every important dimension, making it easy to create a clip tailored to your application. Create perfectly sized clips for pipes, cables, hoses, conduits, and many other round objects without having to modify the model manually. Simply adjust the parameters and generate the size you need. Whether you're organizing cables, mounting plumbing, or securing larger pipes, this generator gives you complete control over the most important dimensions. Features Fully parametric design Adjustable pipe/cable diameter Adjustable clip width Adjustable arm thickness Adjustable opening angle Adjustable wall distance Adjustable mounting hole diameter Compatible with multiple mounting methods: Countersunk screw (default) Socket head screw Hex nut By default, the model is generated with a countersunk screw recess. If you prefer a socket head screw or a hex nut , simply adjust the corresponding parameters described in the guide below. For rigid pipes, I recommend using a slightly larger opening angle to make installation easier. For cables, you can even print the clip in TPU . Thanks to the flexibility of the material, the cable can be inserted easily while still being held securely in place. Parameter Guide Gap Angle Controls how far the clip arms are opened. Adjust this value to change how tightly the clip wraps around the pipe or cable. Do not exceed 150° , as larger values may cause the model geometry to become invalid. Wall Distance Controls the minimum distance between the wall and the nearest point of the pipe or cable . A minimum value of 10 mm is recommended, but feel free to experiment. Need to move the pipe farther away from the wall? Simply increase this value and use a longer mounting screw. Arm Thickness Controls the thickness of the clip arms. Thicker arms provide greater stiffness and strength. A value between 3–5 mm is recommended for most applications. Larger pipe diameters may benefit from thicker arms. Pipe Diameter Outside diameter of the pipe or cable. Remember to add a small clearance (for example 0.1 mm ) unless you want a tight press fit. Clamp Width Controls the overall width of the clip. Increase this value for larger or heavier pipes and cables if additional strength is required. Hole Diameter of the mounting hole. Remember to add enough clearance so the screw can pass through freely. Head Nut Depth Used when mounting with a socket head screw or a hex nut instead of the default countersunk screw. Measure the height of the screw head or nut, add a small clearance (approximately 0.2 mm ), and enter the result here. Head Size Controls the diameter of the socket head screw recess. The default value is 1 mm , which disables the recess. If you're using a socket head screw, simply measure the screw head diameter, add a small clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Nut Size set to 1 mm. Nut Size Controls the size of the hex nut pocket. Measure the nut across the flats , add approximately 0.2 mm of clearance, and enter the result here. When using this parameter, keep Head Size set to 1 mm. Printing Recommendations Recommended material: PETG TPU is an excellent choice for cable management applications No supports required Print flat on the build plate I designed this generator to eliminate the need for creating a new model every time you need a different pipe or cable diameter. Fully 3D Printable Pocket Grips After seeing the fantastic all-metal Pocket Grips available from MetMo, I wondered whether it would be possible to create a similar version that could be produced entirely on a standard FDM 3D printer—with no screws, pins or additional hardware. This model is the result of that challenge. Although inspired by the original concept, this isn't simply a copy. Considerable CAD modelling, prototyping and testing went into re-engineering the mechanism so it could be manufactured as a practical, fully 3D printable assembly. Inevitably, some features of the original metal design had to be simplified or omitted in order to achieve that goal. For example, this version does not feature interchangeable jaw inserts or integrated wire-cutting edges, allowing the mechanism to remain printable while still capturing the satisfying functionality of an adjustable pocket-sized grip. One feature I'm particularly pleased with is the pivot for the adjustment screw. Rather than requiring a metal pin or fastener, it simply uses a short piece of standard 1.75 mm filament, making this a genuinely hardware-free print that can be assembled straight off the printer. Assembly Please refer to the included exploded-view assembly video before putting the model together. Important: the adjustment screw and thumbwheel must be installed before the two handle halves are joined together. Once the handles are assembled, these components cannot be fitted without disassembly. Printing PLA is fine, I recommend printing with a generous number of walls/perimeters and for the best strength, a more durable filament such as PETG, ABS, ASA. Even then, remember that this is a plastic tool and should be treated accordingly. A Note on Expectations While these printed grips are surprisingly functional and great fun to build and use, they are not intended to compete with the strength, precision or durability of the original machined metal product . If you're looking for a professional-grade tool that will withstand years of heavy use, the original Pocket Grips are exceptionally well made and well worth a look. This project was created as a personal engineering challenge and as something enjoyable for the 3D printing community to build—not as a replacement for the original product. If you'd like to see (or purchase) the beautifully machined metal version that inspired this project, you can find it here : If you print a set, I'd love to see your makes and any improvements or remixes you come up with. Happy printing!

description: Workshop Dust Filter Blower Bring clogged dust filters back to life with this simple but effective Workshop Dust Filter Blower . Want a cute storage solution for your knick-knacks? Wish you had a quick and easy setup for displaying them at a market or craft fair? Look no further! I combined these concepts into one 3-tiered solution. This is the mini version, meaning each box is ~45mm wide and ~35mm deep (except for the bottom box, which is closer to 40mm deep). (Full-size version is near-complete, but it doesn't stay together as securely as Id like!) I designed them to sit nicely on top of each other when closed, and used the back-brace as a way to secure it all together as well as support it when displayed. When fully open for display, I noticed the middle box sagged backwards a little, so I made a little spacer that wedges into the middle divider and against the topmost box to keep it straight! The back-brace also shifts down to support the full height of the display when open, and back up when it's packed up again. I can hold and shake this thing sideways, frontways, upsidedown, and toss it into a large box with other loose things, and it stays closed quite well! I recommend PETG for the bolts that hold the screws on, but PLA should work too. (Just be sure to sloooow down the first layer of PETG if you use it, I had a fun time working out how to get the thing to stick down with such a small object). Requires: Two (2) 2.5mm x 10 mm screws (to hold the back brace on) and Sixteen (16) 2.5mm x 8mm screws (to attached the levers to the boxes). I used machine screws as that's what I had, but any screw in those sizes should work! The holes for the screws may need a bit of loosening if your filament has sagged down, I found this was easier than dealing with supports for them. Assembly is as simple as attaching the levers and the back-brace to the boxes as shown in the photos. The top lid slides on and off, and has a small lip to secure it in place when closed. I usually just keep the spacer wedge for the middle box inside one of the middle compartments for when I open it up. This is my first proper 3D model! I'm very open to improvements, so please try it out for yourself and let me know what you think!

MODYLO Quiver Same idea as the MODYLO Column rod, but for tubes. Open the Customizer, set the length and the inner diameter you want, hit Generate. It works out how many segments you need, lays them out on the plate, and you screw them together afterwards. I built it to store posters. Then I built a fat one to hold the tablecloth that lives rolled on a Column. If you read one thing, read this Segments print standing on the bed, and tall standing prints topple if adhesion is not right. This is the single thing that goes wrong. The Quiver is much steadier than a Column rod, because a 40 to 90 mm tube has a far wider footprint than a 30 mm stick. I did not need a brim. But if you have had tall prints fail before, here is the order to reach for: Clean plate. Soap, then isopropyl. A Cool Plate SuperTack helps a lot. Lower Max segment height. More segments, shorter ones, far less leverage. This is the most effective dial you have. Add an external brim to the segments (not the caps). Use Quiver Braced. Two versions in this listing Quiver - no internal bracing. Fewer parts, less filament, faster. Use this if you have your process under control. Quiver Braced - generates a sacrificial support tube inside each segment. It has a wide base for bed grip and is held to the inner wall by a few small tabs, so the segment can't pivot on its base and the tabs break away cleanly afterwards. Minimum length 180 mm. Both use the same geometry and the same thread. The braced version just leaves the support features enabled. Pick whichever suits your printer, they assemble together. The bracing costs about 185 g and 3h40 on a 1.4 m tube. If your printer handles tall prints and your plate adhesion is good, skip it. If you have had segments fall, it is worth every gram. MakerWorld's Customizer cannot switch a Fusion feature on and off, which is why this is two entries rather than one checkbox. What you can set Parameter Range What it does Total length 30 to 3000 mm (Quiver) 180 to 3000 mm (Quiver Braced) The usable space inside the finished tube. Inner diameter 40 to 90 mm The narrowest opening inside the tube. Whatever you want to store has to fit through this. Extra wall thickness 0 mm and up Added on top of the 2.8 mm default wall. Max segment height Quiver only The longest a single segment is allowed to be. Lower it for more segments, shorter ones, and less chance of anything toppling mid-print. Length is usable internal length. It does not include the threads or the caps. If your poster is 841 mm, ask for 841 mm. Ask for 850 if you want a little slack. Add roughly 17 mm to the outside length when you are working out shelf space. Inner diameter is the narrowest point, which is the wall inside the top thread, not the middle of the tube. So the number you set is the number that matters: if it says 60, a 60 mm roll goes in. Extra wall thickness does two jobs: a stiffer tube, and a heavier, more stable segment while it prints. At 40 mm diameter and full height, a millimetre or two is cheap insurance. Max segment height is the toppling dial. If your printer struggles with tall prints, bring it down. You get more joints and a slightly longer total print, and much less risk. It is only on the unbraced version, since the braced one solves the same problem a different way. What size do I need? Length, by content: Content Short side Ask for A3 297 mm 300 mm A2 420 mm 425 mm A1 594 mm 600 mm A0 841 mm 850 mm US 24 × 36 in 610 mm 615 mm Inner diameter, by use: Use Suggested ID One or two posters, light stock 40 mm Several posters, or heavy / matte stock that creases 60 mm Rolled around a 30 mm Column rod (tablecloth, fabric, banner) 60 mm Rolled around a Column with a thick fabric, or a big stack 90 mm Tight rolls leave memory creases in heavy paper. If in doubt go one size up, the extra filament is mostly in the length, not the diameter. Printing Segments print standing on the bed, threaded socket down . The caps print flat. The Customizer lays this out for you, but the plate layout is not preserved if you re-slice from a saved profile, so check it. Quick self-check: if your slice is full of supports, the orientation is wrong. Layer height: 0.2 mm Walls: 2 Infill: lightning. This one matters. A gyroid or grid infill sends the toolhead darting back and forth on every layer, and on a tall thin segment that is exactly the force that tips it over. Lightning leaves the head running smooth continuous loops around the wall. Less filament, less time, and much less shaking. Supports: none. All overhangs clear along the vertical axis. Brim: I did not need one. The tube footprint is much wider than a Column rod, so it sits far more solidly. If you see any lifting, or you have had tall prints fail before, add an external brim to the segments and leave it off the caps. Filament: standard PLA Real slice, 1.4 m tube, 60 mm inner diameter, 7 segments of 200 mm on one plate: Version Filament Time Quiver 595 g 12h39 Quiver Braced 780 g 16h19 If you have had segments topple, print fewer per plate. The risk is not really about any single segment, it is about how long they all stand there and how much the toolhead has to travel between them. Seven segments standing for twelve hours is seven chances, and one faller can take out its neighbours. Printing them one at a time costs surprisingly little: about 1h50 each plus a few minutes of prep, so roughly 40 minutes more machine time across the whole tube. You pay for it in plate changes, not in printing. Worth it if the alternative is losing a plate at hour ten. Worth being straight about this: a cardboard poster tube costs a few euros and this does not beat it on price. What it gives you is the exact length you asked for, a screw cap that actually closes, segments you can reconfigure later, and an object that will outlive twenty cardboard tubes. On the wall: the 2.8 mm figure is the wall envelope, not 2.8 mm of solid plastic. Inside it, two printed skins with lightning infill between them. That is deliberate: faster, lighter, and far more stable on a tall segment. Plenty stiff for storage. Do not stand on it. Assembly Screw the segments together. The thread is a 3-start thread with a detent, so it seats firmly and does not back out on its own. Every segment is identical, so: Assemble them in any order A cap screws onto any segment, at either end A 900 mm tube can be taken apart and rebuilt as two shorter ones with a second pair of caps Print one spare segment now and extend the tube later instead of reprinting it Dry-fit keeps it adjustable. A drop of glue on the threads makes it permanent and noticeably stiffer. Your call. Seam tip: set seam position to Back before slicing. Not Aligned. Aligned drifts the seam around from segment to segment and you can never line them up. Back puts it in the same place on every segment. Then, because the thread is 3-start, each joint seats in three positions 120° apart. Dry-fit and try all three at each joint, keep the one that lines up. You end up with a seam running close to straight down the whole tube instead of spiralling. Pairs with MODYLO Column MODYLO Column is the same idea as a solid rod. Roll fabric onto a Column, slide the whole thing into a Quiver, cap both ends. That is the setup I use for the tablecloth, and it is what a 60 mm inner diameter is sized for. Tell me what you put in it I make things because I need them, then share them in case someone else does. So far all I know about this one is that it holds posters and a tablecloth, because that is what I built it for. If you print a Quiver, I would like to know what goes inside it. description: I designed a nature-inspired dock station for the Luna Ultra camera. This design incorporates many features and introduces a new technique developed by myself. The main idea behind this dock is to create a decorative, functional, customizable, and fun device for your desk — one that allows you to support, charge, and organize a set of accessories for your Luna Ultra camera. For this reason, I developed a technique that transforms filament leftovers into small, strong, and flexible springs , allowing you to create unique flexible accessories. This main feature creates a fascinating effect of flying butterflies, which can be attached to your Luna camera cover or used to decorate your dock station. Components This design is complex, and I split it into three main parts: the spring-making device, the camera cover , and the dock station , . The spring-making device This new technique, developed by myself, allows small pieces of filament to be transformed into strong, rigid, and flexible springs . The main idea consists of modifying the geometry of the filament and using a high-temperature heat source to alter the internal stress state of the material through a controlled process of heating and rapid cooling. This device uses a nut and a lock nut , which must be tightened to prevent the spring from elastically recovering to its original shape during the heat treatment process. The camera cover This is a portable and customizable accessory for your Luna Ultra camera. By using self-made springs and butterflies, it creates a unique flying effect. You can customize the colors and spring lengths to create different visual experiences. Assembly Use glue for spring, cover, butterfly connecting The dock station The dock station allows you to incorporate the original USB Type-C cable into the design and connect it directly to your computer. It also features a secret door that provides hidden storage for SD cards and small Luna Ultra accessories. The larger branch includes removable mushrooms that reveal slots for inserting up to three camera covers, each featuring butterflies in different colors. Assembly Use simple filament piece as hinge Use glue for covers and springs connecting

Ecco un progetto semplicissimo per rinfrescarvi nelle estati roventi davanti al pc. Un creativo e funzionale modello di Ice Cooler, a praticamente costo zero. L'idea è piuttosto semplice: sfruttare il ghiaccio per rinfrescare l'aria. Mettete una bottiglia di plastica da 500ml nel vostro freezer (attenzione a lasciare la bottiglia piena solo al 75/80% massimo, altrimenti esploderà!) e lasciatela congelare. Inseritela nell'alloggiamento del mio Ice Cooler e avviate la ventola. Entro pochi secondi, aria freschissima uscirà e vi donerà un gradevolissimo refrigerio. E può funzionare per diverse ore prima che il ghiaccio sia completamente sciolto e perda la sua efficacia!!!! Tutto quello di cui avrete bisogno è: - 1 ventola da PC 120x120mm a 12v - Un alloggiamento Batterie da 9v - 4 viti almeno da 50mm Io ho utilizzato questo hardware perchè il più comodo per me: ciò non toglie che potete valutare un'alimentazione da USB, o da PowerBank, con Regolatori di velocità etc etc. Sta solo a voi: il mio modello esige solo una ventola da 120mm; il cavo della ventola fuoriesce dal posteriore del Case e da lì potete fare quello che preferite. Una volta stampato tutto, testate i contatti della ventola unita al pacco della batteria da 9v, in modo da poter verificare la corretta direzione di rotazione della ventola (deve buttare aria FUORI dal Case, non dentro). Sì, la ventola è un 12v e la batteria un 9v, ma funzionerà benissimo, ad una velocità leggermente inferiore. Una volta verificato questo e segnato i corretti fili, inserite il filo della ventola nel buco in alto a sinistra e fatelo uscire dal posteriore, unendolo poi al pacco batteria. Avvitate la ventola nel case e inserite l'alloggiamento della bottiglia nel Case, prestando attenzione che la parte aperta sia in direzione della ventola. Ora, potete inserire la bottiglia ed accendere! Potete anche utilizzare il tappo per contenere al meglio la temperatura della bottiglia, migliorando la resa grazie anche ad un piccolo effetto “Venturi” causato dai piccoli fori in alto da cui viene aspirata l'aria che, scendendo attraverso la spirale, si raffredda più velocemente. Entro pochi secondi, sentirete una magnifica aria fresca uscire dal vostro nuovo Ice Cooler! Non dimenticate, quando cambiate la bottiglia, di verificare se la vaschetta di raccolta dell'acqua causata dalla condensa è da svuotare (alla base del Case dove va in appoggio la bottiglia). Buona estate a tutti!!!

description: Measure your T-track, customize the runner, print and assemble a full miter gauge that actually fits your saw. No more wobbly stock gauges with sloppy side play. This is a complete, fully 3D-printed miter gauge system with a customizable T-track runner, adjustable fence, two-color angle scale (0 to 60 degrees both sides), ergonomic locking knob and a runner lock for repeatable positioning. The runner uses MakerWorld's built-in customizer, so you can dial in the exact cross-section of your T-track (check the description below) and get a snug, zero-play fit on any table saw, band saw or router table. Designed and tested on an Evolution R255TBL+ table saw. Works with any machine that has a T-slot miter channel, as long as you measure and customize the runner to match. Key features Customizable T-track runner fits any non-standard slot profile 120-degree range (60 degrees each side of zero) Two-color scale, printed separately (no AMS required) Adjustable fence (19.4 cm top, 25 cm bottom), slides along two slots for positioning Runner lock with optional spring for progressive clamping feel Reinforced pivot boss (6 wall loops) for long-term durability under side load Lightening holes reduce weight without sacrificing stiffness All hardware is standard M6, easy to source anywhere Hardware required 1x M6 x 25mm hex head bolt (pivot) 1x M6 x 45mm bolt (main locking knob) 1x M6 x 25mm bolt (runner lock) 2x M6 x 35mm bolt (fence) 5x M6 nut 1x M6 washer, minimum 10mm outer diameter Optional: spring, approximately 25mm long, any type that fits over M6 shaft (recommended for runner lock) CA glue (optional, for extra security when attaching the scale) How to get your parts This listing has two buttons: "Open in Bambu Studio" and "Customize." "Open in Bambu Studio" gives you the full print profile with all 6 plates (base, scale, knob, small parts, fence, example runner). All print settings are pre-configured. "Customize" opens the parametric runner generator. Enter your T-track measurements (top_width, bottom_width, top_height, bottom_height), generate an STL, then either add it as a new plate in Bambu Studio or replace the example runner plate (plate 06) with your custom runner. Important: measure your T-track before printing the runner! The example runner included in the print profiles is sized for the Evolution R255TBL+ table saw with the following default values: bottom_width = 24.30 mm bottom_height = 4.30 mm top_height = 6.00 mm top_width = 19.40 mm Your saw almost certainly has different slot dimensions. Use the Customize button to adjust these four parameters to match your specific T-track. A caliper measurement accurate to 0.1mm will give you the best fit. Printed parts (6 plates) 01 - Scale (two-color, no AMS needed, print in contrasting colors) 02 - Base (main mitre gauge body) 03 - Knob (large locking knob + cap) 04 - Small knobs + pivot cap + scale bolts (all small parts on one plate) 05 - Fence 06 - Example runner (customize before printing) Assembly 1) Measure your T-track slot dimensions and customize the runner model (top_width, bottom_width, top_height, bottom_height). Use the included example runner as a reference for print settings. 2) Insert 3x M6 nuts into the runner slots (from the bottom). 3) Align the scale with the cutout on the base, press the locating tabs in. The scale should hold on its own. Optionally apply CA glue for extra security. 4) Place the base onto the runner. Insert the pivot bolt (M6 x 25mm hex head) through the boss into the runner nut. The hole is intentionally tight to eliminate play, you may need to screw the bolt in rather than push it through. Press the cap onto the bolt head. 5) Insert the M6 x 45mm bolt from the top of the large knob (push through the hex channel, use a screwdriver to press it down). Place the M6 washer (min 10mm diameter) onto the bolt shaft from the bottom. Pass through the arc slot and tighten into the runner nut with moderate force. Press the cap onto the top of the knob. 6) Press 2x M6 x 35mm bolts into the fence holes (press-fit). 7) Insert an M6 nut into each of the two small fence knobs, close with caps. 8) Slide the fence bolts through the slots in the base, thread the small knobs onto the bolts. 9) Insert the M6 x 25mm bolt into the runner lock knob, place the spring (recommended) onto the bolt shaft, screw the assembly into the nut at the end of the runner. Press the cap onto the knob. Using it Loosen the large knob, set your angle using the scale markings, tighten the knob. The runner lock at the end of the bar lets you fix the gauge position along the T-track. For repeatable cuts, tighten the runner lock once you find your position, then only adjust the angle knob between cuts. Print hints Material: PLA works well. PETG is fine if you want extra durability. The base prints flat. The large knob prints vertically with a brim. The scale is a separate print in a contrasting color (white scale on dark base or vice versa). No AMS needed, just filament swap in the middle. The example runner profile is customized for the Evolution R255TBL+. You must customize it for your own saw before printing. If you print it, please leave a rating, it helps a lot. description: 🦷 Dental Tooth & Gum Demonstration Model with Weighted Display Stand This is a realistic dental demonstration model (cartoonish picture with the real dentist for proprotions) designed for dentists to clearly explain treatments and procedures to their patients. It represents a cross-section of a tooth and surrounding gum , allowing patients to better understand tooth anatomy and what their treatment involves. The project was developed in collaboration with a practicing dentist , ensuring it meets the needs of daily clinical use while remaining practical, durable, and visually engaging. The tooth and gum are separate pieces , allowing the tooth to be removed from the gum and shown more closely to patients during consultations. The display stand was designed in Fusion 360 , while the tooth and gum were sculpted in Nomad Sculpt to achieve a realistic organic appearance. The stand includes a hidden cavity that can be filled with weights, such as old screws, nuts, or other metal pieces, giving it excellent stability and preventing it from tipping over during demonstrations. For the model shown in the photos, I used clear UV resin to recreate the enamel, producing a remarkably realistic translucent effect. I also used thin electrical wires to represent the nerves and blood vessels inside the tooth. Once positioned, they were secured with super glue and encapsulated with UV resin for a clean, natural finish. Rather than using an AMS, I chose to hand-paint the entire model using an airbrush and fine brushes. This gave me much greater control over the colours and subtle shading, resulting in a unique, highly realistic finish. Of course, if you have an AMS, you can also download the individual parts and create your own multicolour version. I would recommend printing all the parts in white filament and treating the painting as part of the project. It's incredibly rewarding and allows you to achieve a truly professional-looking result. This model has taken many months of design, sculpting, testing, and refinement , and I'm incredibly happy with how it turned out. My dentist friend was genuinely surprised by how professional and useful it looked, which made all the effort worthwhile. If you decide to print it, I'd be truly grateful if you could share a photo of your make . Seeing other people enjoying and using my designs is the best reward I could ask for. Thank you very much, and I hope you enjoy building and painting it! The display stand looks stunning on Wood PLA, also includes a small name plate at the front, allowing you to personalize the model with a dentist's name, clinic name, or logo from the bambulab text option . This adds a professional touch and makes it ideal for use in dental practices, consultation rooms, or educational displays.
