It builds on V2's aesthetic restyling — rounded body, central anti-wobble guide tongue, fillets at the root of the arms, chamfered mouth — and adds a robustness pass on the latch holes, a true new D-ring attachment, independent bulge controls on X and Y, optional insertion guides, and a reorganized, multilingual Customizer menu. Every dimension stays parametric and protected by automatic safety clamps. What's New in V3 Robustness pass: the minimum wall margin around each drilled attachment has been increased from 1.2 mm to 1.6 mm, for cord/paracord/D-ring tabs that print reliably. Fixed a latent flaw: the window (female cavity) now extends far enough to let the arms fully relax once they have snapped into place. New true D-ring attachment ("d_ring"), for closed/welded D-ring hardware: it is a straight round hole, drilled horizontally through the tab from side wall to side wall (like a hinge-pin hole), not vertically through the top/bottom faces. It is invisible from above and shows only as a hole in the side walls of the tab. The diameter matches the dring_wire parameter, i.e. the diameter of the ring's wire/stock (not its overall size): the ring opens, hooks into the hole and closes again, without having to thread the whole buckle through it. The "loop" attachment has been renamed (sewn eyelet / carabiner opening) to clearly distinguish it from the new d_ring. New independent bulge controls for a more organic, less "boxy" look: bulge_x (barrel bulge on the long side, applied to both male and female) and bulge_y (bulge on the short/head-to-tail edge). The safety rule is kept: the female edge facing the mouth never bulges, because it must stay flush against the base of the male during assembly. New optional insertion guides (guide_rails): two visible funnel-shaped notches, cut into the top/bottom caps at the mouth, on either side of the central guide tongue, to make blind insertion easier (assembly without looking). Disabled by default, with no effect if there is no central guide tongue. Customizer menu reorganized into a more logical order for the average user: Part -> Dimensions -> Attachment -> Snap-fit tuning -> Aesthetics -> Thicknesses -> Advanced. Removed the now-redundant "language" selector: every parameter label already shows all 5 languages (Italian/English/French/German/Chinese) at once. The "guide" mode (parameter legend in the 3D preview) now prints all 5 languages side by side. Every Customizer section (Part, Dimensions, Attachment, Snap-fit, Aesthetics, Thicknesses, Advanced) is now preceded by an emoji icon, so you can scan the panel at a glance. Main Features Side-release snap-fit mechanism: two spring arms with latch teeth click into the female cavity; you press on the exposed side windows to release. Optional central guide tongue (guide_width parameter): eliminates lateral play, guides insertion and acts as an anti-over-flexion end-stop for the arms. Every dimension is parametric and derived with built-in safety clamps: the script automatically limits values that would produce walls that are too thin, latch teeth that are too long, self-intersecting bulges, etc., displaying on-screen NOTES when it intervenes — it is very hard to generate invalid or unprintable geometry. Fully native OpenSCAD: no external libraries, works directly in the MakerWorld/OpenSCAD Customizer. Male and female attachments are chosen completely independently from 8 types, each with its own dedicated sizing parameters. Covers a wide range of strap widths (10–60 mm) and thicknesses (5–14 mm), with wall and cap thickness adjustable separately. 8 Attachment Types sewn_slot : Sewn slot/eyelet for attaching directly to the strap by stitching. belt : Wider pass-through opening, for threading a belt or a band. triglide : Adjustable tri-glide (two slots + central bar) for length-adjustable runs of strap. paracord : 2 or 4 round holes for lacing paracord or thin cord. loop : Large sewn eyelet / carabiner opening. cord : Single round hole for a cord or rope. flat : Solid tab, with no cut-out, for permanent glued or riveted mounting. d_ring : New in V3: a horizontal hole drilled sideways through the tab, sized to the diameter of the ring's wire (dring_wire), for closed/welded D-ring hardware. Print Notes Designed to print flat on the print bed, without supports. FDM print tolerance is adjustable via the clearance parameter (default 0.35 mm). With the d_ring attachment, the hole is drilled sideways through the tab (from side wall to side wall): the tab dimensions must be large enough to keep the hole within solid walls relative to the chosen dring_wire diameter; the script's safety clamps intervene automatically and flag on-screen with a NOTE if an entered value is not compatible. Works across a wide range of FDM printers and materials. In general, if a set parameter would lead to walls that are too thin, latches that are too long or self-intersecting bulges, the script corrects it automatically and flags it on-screen with a NOTE. Ideal For V3 is meant for people who actually need to use the buckle: pick the strap width and thickness, pick the attachment for the male side and for the female side even in combinations that differ from each other, adjust clearance and bulges to taste, print flat without supports, and assemble. description: Hey guys, the new mushroom hole punch you’ve been waiting for is finally here! This is the first in a new series of fully 3D printed mushroom-style punches designed for discbound notebooks and pocket-sized planners. It lets you punch your own paper, photos, dividers and other inserts, so you’re no longer limited to buying pre-punched sheets. The entire punch prints in place in around 1.5 hours , including the smooth hinged mechanism. Small side guides help position paper up to approximately 108 mm wide , making it ideal for smaller notebooks and pocket-sized discbound systems. A lot of testing went into this design. I went through nearly ten different versions of the mushroom cutting profile alone, trying to get the cleanest and most reliable cut possible. I eventually narrowed it down to two profiles: W-Shaped Profile This gave me the best overall results across most of my testing. Curved Profile This performed better with certain paper types and thicknesses. Directions for Use Place the paper right up against the hinge, then move the guide into position so it just touches the edge of the paper. Put both hands on the press and apply equal pressure on both sides. Push down firmly in one clean motion until you hear and feel a solid click. If one side goes down before the other, the cuts may vary. For the cleanest result, press straight down evenly with both hands in one smooth “thoom.” …………………………… Both versions are included, so you can test them and decide which works best for the paper you use. One of my main goals was to make it capable of punching 160 GSM paper , as this is a popular thickness for making sturdy notebook pages. It can also work with thinner or thicker paper, although results may vary depending on the material and cutting profile. Occasionally, some paper may leave a tiny whisk of material that can be removed with almost no effort. Considering this is a fully printed, free alternative to an expensive metal discbound punch, I think that is a pretty fair trade-off! I was tired of "one-size-fits-all" sink caddies that sat loosely in the middle of my divided sink, slid around, and got in my way. I also hated that I couldn't put them at the top or bottom of my sink due to its curves. So, I designed a sink caddy that looks “built in”; it hugs the dimensions of my sink, fits flush with the upper or lower curves, and eliminates wobble. Sweet. I wanted to make some for friends, but their sinks were all shaped differently… Lame. My only viable option was to turn the model into a parametric caddy that could be customized after taking a few measurements of their sink. When that was done, I decided to go ham and make the basket sizes individually customizable, and then added a single basket option as well. 🧮 Customization for everything but the kitchen sink Use the customize button to tweak your dimensions and even print a fit test before committing to the full caddy. Basket sizes and combinations: Adjust the total length of the caddy from front to back. Independently configure how deep each basket sits inside your sink and how far out it extends into the basin. (Height + Width) Toggle either side on/off to generate a single sturdy basket. Generate unlimited combinations sized for various items or needs, while keeping a clean, built-in look. Sink dimensions (measurement guide at the end): Inner Sink Curve Radius: Hugs the exact rounded (or straight) corners of your basin where the divider meets the sink walls. Divider Width and Top Curve Radius: Generates a perfectly snug bridge over your sink divider. The top curve can be 0 (flat), but it looks nicer if there are no gaps. Advanced/Optional Settings: Counter Overhang - My sink has a nasty overhang so I created this setting to automatically notch the back of the baskets so they slide underneath. If you also have an overhang, I'm sorry. But at least it gives us added stability. Sink Taper/Grade - Angles the baskets to match the slope of your sink walls to sit flush. Most people won't have to touch this. Fit test for the filament frugal: Toggle the “Generate Fit Test Cutout” option to remove the baskets and print only the divider bridge to ensure everything sits flush. “Fit test height” allows you to print a taller or shorter segment to test your sink’s taper, or test only the bridge itself. Note: fit tests get printed upside down to minimize support filament. 🖨️ Printing Instructions & Best Practices using Bambu Studio/Handy If you follow the measurement guide below you will be fine printing directly from the Bambu Handy customizer to get a sturdy flush-fit caddy. The only exception being a multi-height basket (see support section). Included Profile to boost customizer print quality in Bambu Studio: Because the parametric model maker only allows limited slicer optimization, I made the “Customizer Profile” to apply all my highly-optimized global slicer settings (walls, seams, speed, overhangs, strength, etc.). The only other thing I might suggest is adding extra cooling to your filament profile. I set my Bambu Matte PLA to 100% Part/Aux fans after the 2nd layer. Here is how to use it: Generate your caddy via the customizer, download STL (optional) Enable “fit test” in customizer, click generate, download .3mf, print to ensure fit Download/Open the “Customizer Profile” in Bambu Studio Import your customizer STL file, replace model on the plate You are ready to roll!! Bridge/Basket Support: Same height baskets will print with slim trees to support the divider bridge via the .3mf. It works great, but of course if you have a dual nozzle you can flip the support interface to PETG. If you are printing a "Multi-Height" variation where one basket floats in mid-air, a 0 Z-gap PETG support interface is strongly recommended to provide a solid floor for the basket corners to print on. Bambu Studio will probably want you to use normal support, but tree [strong] is just fine. 🛠️ Advanced 3D Printing Engineering This model is a bunch of pieces that all sync together with code based on your inputs. The geometry is heavily optimized for customization but a few caveats: I spent an incredible amount of time testing various sink dimensions and basket sizes, tweaking the code to ensure a clean print and that all reasonable dimensions will work without breaking the model. That said, I can't guarantee every single combination of basket size, sink curve, height, etc will work, and there may be small issues and edge cases. If you find one, comment with your dimensions and I’ll take a look. If you aren't sure about your measurements, please use the print test customization option to print a small section to ensure a good fit! 📏 How to Measure Your Sink for a Flush-Fit Caddy These don't have to be exact, but you'll have a sturdier and better looking caddy the closer you get. If you aren't sure about any measurements, print the customizer’s fit test option before printing a full caddy. Measuring will take about 5 minutes once you have what you need. Let’s go! 1. Inner Sink Curve Radius This is the curve of your sink's corners. Because it's hard to measure with a ruler, I suggest printing this awesome tool: If you have a large curve: RadGauge Dual Mega If you have a small curve: RadGauge Dual Quick hack: Find any circular object (I initially used a coaster) that fits nicely in your sink’s upper divider corner, measure the width, divide by two, done. Alternatively, tie some string to a pencil and make some circles on paper. 2. Divider Width & Top Curve Radius Measure the thickness of the bridge between your two sink basins. Make sure to measure the thickness below the top curve (where the walls straighten out) so the caddy doesn't get stuck. If the top edges of your divider are curved, you can use the outer-curve side of the RadGauge Dual to measure it. Quick hack: You can get away with measuring tape on the width (when in doubt round up) and leaving the top curve at low number. 3. Sink Taper / Grade Grab any straight flat object like a ruler or remote and press it flat against the top half of your sink divider. If it looks perfectly vertical, go with 0. If it looks only very slightly off, leave the preset .5mm or bump to 1mm. You can also measure how much the sink wall moves inwards per 100mm with two rulers. When in doubt, use the customizer fit test height option to print a tall test. If anyone wants taper tests let me know, I'll upload a plate. 4. Counter Overhang (if needed) If you have an under-mount sink where the countertop sticks out over the basin, measure how far the counter protrudes past the sink wall. Input this number in mm to generate a custom notch so your baskets slide underneath. 🔥And that's it! 🔥 Thanks for checking out my project. I’m new to 3d printing so if anyone has any advice or suggestions on how to improve the model or profile settings, I’m all ears. If you decide to print a basket, I would love to see it. Cheers, WK Changelog Update 7/24/26: Based on feedback, added adjustable chamfers to all interior and exterior edges that are not hugging the sink (enabled by default). Should be easier to clean and much harder to get scraped by a sharp edge. Update 7/24/26: Fixed chamfer extrusion when generating single basket caddy.

Planetary Gear Screwdriver A compact, dual-mode mechanical screwdriver powered by an internal 4:1 planetary gear system! Key Features: Dual-Mode Operation: Push the front lock back for high-speed driving (4 turns per single rotation of the handle), perfect for quickly running down long threads. Slide the lock forward to engage high-torque mode for final tightening. Two Build Options: Choose between the full-hardware version using standard 604/6702 bearings and 3x20 mm dowel pins, or the 100% printable version that requires only a single standard M3 screw! Complete PDF Assembly Manual: Step-by-step PDF instructions are attached below for both hardware and non-hardware builds, complete with troubleshooting tips. How It Works & How to Use It The screwdriver has two modes. For fast tightening or unscrewing, make sure the lock piece is in the back position. Holding the main body part with one hand and twisting the back piece will cause the front bit holder to rotate fast with a ratio of 4:1 (one turn of the back will cause the front to spin 4 times). This mode is ideal for long threaded screws to tighten them quickly. For final tightening or high-torque mode, engage the lock at the front by pushing the lock piece into the front position. This will lock the bit axle piece to the main handle piece so you can use it like a regular screwdriver. Printing Instructions & Parts Read all about how to print this model and what extra parts you'll need. Parts As mentioned before, there are two variants, and I've provided print profiles for both. For materials, I recommend PLA, PETG, or ABS. I would stay away from fiber-filled or silk filaments: fiber-filled materials can leave rough surfaces, and silk filaments tend to swell, making it harder to reproduce exact dimensions and tight tolerances. Assembly Check out the exploded view to get an idea of how everything goes together. For detailed step-by-step instructions, check the attached PDFs! Once printed, assemble as follows: Main Body & Roller Door: Print the white body and roller shutter door first. Slide the roller door into the internal tracks of the main body, then glue the top cover into place. Glue Application Note: Apply glue only along the outer edge of the top cover . Do NOT apply glue to the main body tracks to prevent accidentally sticking the roller door shut! (During testing, a glue-less snap-fit design was attempted, but due to the large size and leverage of the shutter door, opening it repeatedly caused the cover to pop off. Using glue along the edges provides long-term durability). Glue-Free Snap Parts: The black upper plates and gold clasps do NOT require glue. To resolve this, I designed two gold handles on the shutter so you can comfortably use both hands to operate the door smoothly. The "Go Big" Decision: I debated several times whether to downscale the model for smoother slider mechanics. I love this model because it is easier to push, stronger, and more comfortable to hold than many commercial models I've bought in stores. I've gone through 23 iterations of the fan blade, and I made an Onshape Featurescript for it. It hits 6.525 revolutions per squeeze of the fan blade, so that's about 870-900 rpm. It creates a noticeable breeze even from a more relaxed distance so you don't have to hold it right in front of your face. List of Materials 85g of filament A 6.5x22mm extension spring (the place I bought it from is now unavailable, so any extension spring that's around 20mm long and < 9mm OD will work, but it may be harder to push in or slower to come out) 3 M3x8 self-tapping flat head screws Oil lubricant (Super Lube Multi-Purpose Synthetic Oil) Printing Make sure your filament is dry because if the axles for the gears have too much stringing, then they will turn less smoothly, and the fan blade won't work as efficiently. Also, the fan blade is using a layer height of 0.14mm, so don't mix it with the other objects, which use a layer height of 0.20mm. Assembly Confirm the spring's loops are in the correct position; make sure one of the loops of the spring is perpendicular to the coil and the other side is separated into a single cord, not a closed loop. I had to separate it myself and do some finicking to make the coil sit flat with the loop flat on the bottom. Put the spring in the tiny hole in the pusher part. Oil the big hole (the rotation axle) on the pusher part and then put it in the frame. Put in the gears in the order of the numbers in the picture, oiling the center hole and the teeth as you go. Put on the top cover, then the fan blade. Make sure the blade is pushed down until it is almost touching the frame. Screw it in (self-tapping), and then flip the whole thing over and screw in the bottom-most hole that's farthest from the blade. Screw in the hole on the middle-left, and only screw it in a tiny bit or the handle will be very hard to push in; the screw's top can even be flush with the bottom of the frame. If the model is hard to push in, the most likely reason is that this screw is screwed in too much. Happy printing!

I also created fish shapes to hold necklaces and earrings, similar to those by kelleninprogress , but I drew mine completely from scratch using the Bezier curve tool in Tinkercad. Please note that TuTu's Mini Pocket Slide Box is on Printables with an Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike license , which is why TazMan was able to remix it (and then I was able to remix TazMan's). TuTu's model is also on Makerworld, but here it has a Standard File License, which would disallow remixes, but TazMan created his remix under the previous license. description: For Larger needs - SnapCore Parametric Resizable Vial Holder (Double Hinge / Single Latch) The SnapCore Resizable Vial Holder is a fully parametric storage system that automatically resizes to fit your needs. This version features a double hinge and single latch , making it ideal for medium to larger sized vial holders while maintaining the simple, hardware free SnapCore design. Instead of downloading dozens of different versions, simply change a few parameters and it will generate a custom box sized specifically for your vial layout. To calculate inside height you must add wall thickness for both the lid and base, otherwise the inside height will be off by wall thickness X 2 - important for calculating for vial height For smaller needs see here for single hinge design Features ✔ Fully parametric design ✔ Automatically resizes the length and width of the box ✔ Configure the number of vial positions: Horizontal (Width) Vertical (Length) ✔ Adjustable vial diameter ✔ Adjustable latch width ✔ Adjustable hinge dimensions and clearances ✔ Double printed hinge design ✔ Single SnapCore latch ✔ No hardware required for assembly ✔ Designed for easy printing and assembly Simply enter the number of rows and columns and the model rebuilds automatically. Customizable size The model is fully customizable using the below parameters: When you export the model from the “customize” tab, it will appear as a fully assembled box. In the slicer, you can right click and “split to objects" as shown: once split it will all be in 1 pile on the plate you must drag each piece to position it, and make sure the lid and hinge flat side is on the plate. Adjustable Parameters The model includes parameters for: Number of vial spaces (Width) Number of vial spaces (Length) Vial diameter Vial spacing Box length (automatic) Box width (automatic) Latch width Hinge spacing Hinge insert clearance Wall thickness Base height Lid height Stay within the recommended minimums and maximums for best results, box may not function outside of those parameters. Please ensure you are adjusting the base height and lid height for you vial needs. These do not update as it is difficult to tie those together so must be manually updates Important Notes ⚠ Double Hinge / Single Latch Design This version uses a double hinge and single latch . It performs exceptionally well for medium and larger-sized boxes. ⚠ Box Height Does NOT Automatically Resize The box automatically adjusts its length and width , but it does not automatically adjust the height for different vial sizes. If you change to a taller or shorter vial, you must manually adjust: Base Height Lid Height A good starting point is to make the combined base and lid height approximately 2 mm taller than your vial (also calulating for wall thickness) to provide adequate clearance for printing tolerances and easy removal. Example: 40 mm tall vial → Total inside height ≈ 42 mm To calculate inside height you must add wall thickness for both the lid and base, otherwise the inside height will be off by wall thickness X 2 ⚠ Latch Width The latch width is user adjustable. Larger boxes may benefit from a wider latch for additional strength, while smaller boxes can use a narrower latch. ⚠ Changing Vial Diameter Changing the vial diameter automatically resizes the footprint of the box, but remember to verify and adjust the box height separately if your new vial has a different overall height. Printing Recommendations PETG is highly recommended. This design has been extensively tested in PETG across a wide range of sizes and configurations with excellent results. PLA should also print and function well , although it has not been tested as extensively. No supports required. Print the parts in the supplied orientation. No hardware, screws, magnets, or additional components are required for assembly. description: Lazy River Legends! Next on my list of mini-series is something I've been working and test printing for the last couple of weeks and am VERY Excited to finnaly share - Lazy River Legends! The idea behind this series was to make a fun, modular design of some common masked superheros on vacation… but.. these floaters actually needed to.. well.. float! After a few design iterations and infill tests I landed on a model that achieves everything I set out to achieve! Each character uses the same universal floater body and tube base, while the heads can be printed separately and swapped whenever you feel like changing the crew. Build your favorite lineup, mix and match the masks, or create a completely unexpected crossover for your shelf, desk, bathroom, or summer display. Print one relaxed floater or assemble an entire lazy-river squad. With interchangeable heads and a shared body design, expanding the collection is quick, easy, and perfect for multicolor printing. Because behind every intimidating mask is someone who just wants to sit back, soak up the sun, and float for a while. Choose your mask. Grab a tube. Join the Lazy River Legends! The Print Profiles Each print profile includes a couple of things - A color version of the Tube and Head, as well as a Single Color version of each for those that want to paint themselves or don't care to wait for the long AMS print times (all color models are AMS capable and only have 4 colors, but it is ideal to print on H2C, or at least an h2d or x2d printers to save time/filament). I have included the complete character set/float in each profile so the folks that print from their phone - please note that if you just want to print a single tube and multiple heads you will just need to print the appropriate build plate from each loaded profile. At the time of the upload I am targeting a list of 9 different characters, and depending on interest/requests I will continue expanding the set in the future! User Instructions Please note that even though the model is enclosed, PLA material is water permeable which means that after extended use in water these WILL have seep inside. From fload testing, I did not see any significant water infiltration until the models soaked for about 2 hours (at which time it still continued to float, you could just hear the water inside when shaking the model). Due to this, after use in water I recommend setting the model set out on a towel/drying matt for an hour or two to let the water leave the model. disclaimer* - The main images have clearly been photoshoped to include the fun product photography/water effects. All models in the images are 100% real and have been rigorously test printed and adjusted to ensure they can all be printed with no issues.

description: Description A fully parametric vial storage solution for 10ml crimp-top vials. Unlike 3ml vials, 10ml vials vary noticeably between suppliers — both diameter and height are Customizer settings from the start, so measure your own vials with calipers before printing. A validated alternate preset is included below. Includes optional label windows so you can read vial labels without opening the lid. Two ways to print: Ready-to-print profiles for common quantities — just load the plate you need and hit print Parametric OpenSCAD file for any custom configuration your storage needs require Need a Different Size or Vial? Use the Parametric File The included OpenSCAD file lets you generate any configuration using the built-in Customizer. Layout is controlled by vials_per_row and num_rows, up to 8x8 (64 vials) — the largest grid that fits a 256mm build plate at default vial size. Vial diameter and height are fully adjustable, so this same file works with 10ml vials from any supplier. Validated Vial Presets Default: 22.01mm diameter × 54.0mm tall Alternate (short/wide): 24.02mm diameter × 49.55mm tall Customizer Settings Vial Size vial_od — vial body diameter, measured at the widest point of the straight wall. Measure YOUR vials first — 10ml vials are not standardized across suppliers vial_h — total vial height, from the base to the top of the cap slot_depth_f — how deep the vial sinks into its pocket, as a share of its height. Default 0.65 leaves the cap and neck clear of the pocket Layout vials_per_row — number of vials per row (1–8) num_rows — number of rows (1–8) render_part — set to base , lid , or both Vial Windows show_windows — turns label windows on or off. On by default, so you can read vial labels without opening the lid. Note: the window cutout has a flat top edge that may need supports depending on your slicer/printer — check the slicer preview before printing, or turn this off to avoid the issue entirely Fit Tuning clearance — increases vial pocket diameter. Start at 0.5mm, adjust in 0.05mm steps if vials fit too tightly lid_gap_mode — auto or manual. Auto (default) widens the gap on small prints, which are stiffer and can squeak going on, and tightens it on larger ones. Set to manual to force an exact value lid_gap_manual — the gap used only when lid_gap_mode is set to manual Snap Feel snap_p — snap tab protrusion. 1.2mm is the PETG starting point (0.8mm is too soft for PETG at this scale) snap_z — tab position, affects how easy the lid is to pop off snap_tip_ratio — ramp shape. Lower = gentler on/off feel Recommended Materials PETG — recommended for freezer or long-term cold storage. Handles repeated freeze/thaw cycles without becoming brittle. Use snap_p of 1.2mm or higher. PLA — becomes brittle at freezer temperatures; fine for room-temperature storage or test prints only Printing Tips No supports required for the base or lid geometry itself — but if show_windows is on, check your slicer preview: the flat top edge of each window opening may need light supports depending on your printer and settings 15% infill or higher works fine — these are solid prints that don't need to be dense Print base and lid separately or use both to lay them out side by side automatically Always measure your vials and do a small test print (2x1) first before committing to a large grid — 10ml vial dimensions are not standardized Grids larger than 8x8 are possible in the SCAD file directly, but check your build plate size first Design Notes Designed in OpenSCAD, sharing the same snap-lid mechanism as the 3ml Parametric Peptide Vial Holder — a finger lift tab and chamfered entry for smooth on/off feel. Since 10ml vials vary significantly by supplier, this model was built parametric from the ground up rather than fit to one specific vial.

This parametric generator is the evolution of a previous model that received valuable feedback from the community. Initially, the project was divided into three fixed sizes (you can still find it on my profile), but to answer the many requests for customization, I created this new, completely customisable version. ⚠️ Please note: The Customizer feature is currently only available via Desktop browser (PC) and not from mobile devices (smartphones/tablets). Even with an appropriate frame, some animals might need time to get used to it, or they might never feel completely comfortable. That being said, this project aims to offer practical support, hoping to give your little friends a bit of independence and make their daily lives a little easier! 🚀 Quick Start Enter the measurements of your pet to adapt the frame. Download the file in STL or 3MF format. Import it into your slicer , cut it if necessary, and start printing. Assemble everything by adding the wheels and making the harness. 📏 How to take measurements To get a proper frame, it's essential to take your pet's measurements accurately. Get someone to help you hold them in a standing position. Important: Remember to take into account the height of the wheels you are going to use! Refer to the illustrative image to identify the necessary measurements: ⭐ Features (Customizer Parameters) Here are all the customizable parameters to adapt the frame. 📏 General Dimensions wheel count Choose between 2 wheels (rear support) or 4 wheels (full support). width, length, height Overall dimensions in millimetres. ━ Frame Thickness profile height Height of the frame tube profile (side view) in mm. Modify this value for a lighter or sturdier frame. profile width Width of the frame tube profile (front view) in millimetres. 🦿 Leg Geometry wheel flare out Adjust how much the legs flare outwards in mm to prevent tipping. wheel mount height Height of the lower straight vertical section for wheel attachment in millimetres. 🕳️ Holes & Slots wheel axle hole diameter Diameter of the hole for the wheel axle pin in mm (remember to add a small tolerance). top hole diameter Diameter of the front top holes for passing the harness in millimetres. strap slot count Number of strap slots per side. strap slot length Length of each single strap slot in millimetres. strap slot margin Minimum safety distance of the slots from the edges in millimetres. ✨ Finish Quality fillet radius Increase or decrease the rounding of the edges in mm to make the frame softer and more comfortable. leg samples Technical sampling value for the resolution of the leg curve. 🖨️ Printing Advice Orientation: I recommend printing the wheelchair upside down. This minimizes the use of supports and ensures a better finish on the top part, which is the most visible and in contact with the animal. Settings (Infill & Walls): I don't provide a specific preset because every printer is different. Find the right balance between structural strength (it must support weight while moving) and lightness (it must be easy to pull). Tolerances: Pay close attention to hole tolerances, especially for the wheel axles. Generally, adding an extra 0.1 mm or 0.2 mm margin to the diameter is sufficient, but adjust based on your printer's accuracy. 🛠️ Extra Hardware Required The final assembly requires a few simple extra elements: Harness Pattern: Among the project files, you will find an A3 PDF containing a pattern. Use it as a base to sew the fabric "cradle" (it will obviously need to be adapted to your pet's specific proportions). Velcro or Straps: Soft hook-and-loop tape or webbing to pass through the slots ( Strap slots ) to securely and adjustably attach the harness to the frame. Wheels: You can use salvaged wheels (from rollerblades, old suitcases, etc.) or 3D print them. If you choose to print them, I highly recommend inserting metal bearings for optimal smoothness. Axles/Pins and Nuts: A simple threaded rod or long screws (e.g., M6 or M8) to attach the wheels to the frame. Use self-locking nuts if possible to prevent them from accidentally unscrewing due to vibrations. 🤝 Open Source Project This project is totally Open Source : the underlying code of the generator (OpenSCAD) can be read, modified, and improved by anyone. The true strength of 3D printing is collaboration, so any suggestion is welcome! Feel free to publish Remixes or share constructive ideas in the comments. Together we can make this support increasingly useful. Happy printing! 🐾 🔮 Upcoming implementations: The ability to split/cut the frame directly in the generator by entering your print bed dimensions, instead of having to do it later in the slicer. A 4-wheel version with swivel front wheels to promote 360-degree mobility (I haven't found a 100% OpenSCAD-compatible optimal solution yet, but I'm working on it!).

description: This project was developed as an exploration and research into new features designed to extend the operational capabilities of the human body through 3D-printed mechanisms. The goal is to test how the natural flexion of fingers rarely used for precision tasks (the ring and pinky fingers) can actuate a passive mechanism, leaving the primary fingers (thumb, index, and middle) completely free to manipulate objects or perform tasks. Project & Mechanism Notes Digitally-Actuated Kinematics: The container lid opens through the combined movement of the ring and pinky fingers. It serves as a study on hand biomechanics to reduce the need for using both hands to access small components. Closure Management: To prevent accidental opening during casual hand movements, the closure is assisted by a magnet system: 2x Magnets (8x2mm): Positioned on the lid ( the seats are defined as negative volumes in the model, making them easy to modify directly in your slicer ). 4x Magnets (5x1mm): Provide a light additional resistance, ensuring that the lid opens only through intentional finger flexion. Ergonomics & Mounting: The wrist/hand mount is contoured to fit the shape of the hand and is designed to be secured using a standard garment elastic strap (16mm width, 0.8mm thickness). Print Recommendations Recommended Material: Printing in PETG is strongly recommended , especially for the wrist/hand mount, pins, and locking rings, to ensure the necessary flexibility and structural durability required by the moving parts. Ten swappable texture rollers for play dough, air-dry clay, fondant and salt dough. Each roller is 150mm long and 30mm across with a bold 1.2mm raised pattern that stamps deep, crisp impressions in one easy pass. Every roller shares the same 8.6mm centre bore and spins freely on the included printed axle, held by two press-fit end caps, so you can swap patterns in seconds. Print them upright with no supports, one colour each, and build the whole collection over time. Dots - A field of 130 raised domes in neat staggered rows. The pattern has no direction, so it is the most forgiving roller of the set: roll it any way you like and the polka dots always line up. A great first print. Chevron - Five bands of bold zigzag arrows wrapping the barrel. Roll parallel passes and the chevrons tile into a striking knitted-jumper texture across the whole slab. Rings - Clean pinstripe rings with little dash rows between them, like it came off a lathe. Perfect for banded borders, ruled lines and anywhere you want a tidy, orderly finish. Daisy - Thirty-five little five-petal daisies scattered in offset rows. Rolls a soft floral wallpaper pattern that looks brilliant pressed into fondant or pastel clay. Weave - Classic basketweave with alternating pairs of bars, just like a woven pie crust. Turns any flat slab of clay into an instant wicker texture, and it feels great to roll. Hearts - Rows of chunky hearts marching around the barrel in offset ranks. The go-to roller for Valentine biscuits, love-note clay tags and general cuteness. Stripes - Six candy stripes spiralling the full length of the roller. Because the stripes are helical, they lay down as continuous diagonal lines for as long as you keep rolling, which is oddly satisfying. Night - Crescent moons alternating with sparkle stars in a checkerboard sky. Made for bedtime-themed play dough sessions and space-mad kids. Waves - Rippling zigzag wave bands rolling around the barrel. Reads as water, bunting or mountain ranges depending on which way up your imagination is holding it. Honeycomb - An offset grid of hexagon outlines like a slice of beehive. Pairs perfectly with bee cutters, and makes a great all-over texture for hex-tile fans. Axle kit One 7.9mm rod with a printing flat and two press-fit end caps. Drop any roller on the rod, push the caps on the ends, and the roller spins freely with 0.35mm of running clearance while your hands stay still. The flat face means the rod prints lying down with no supports, and it also reduces bore contact so the spin is even smoother.

description: Just a quick right-angle wrench for use with standard ¼-inch screwdriver bits. The bits will be fairly tight for the first few uses, so I recommend having some pliers or other hand tools ready to remove them. After some use, they will open up more and be easier to put the bits in and remove them. It is 102mm x 21mm x 10mm. To install the magnets, I recommend you do the following: Put the magnet on the end of an allen wrench (as wide of one as possible. This will allow for more even pressure and less likely to flip the magnet out of the hole). Put a dab of super glue on the other side of the magnet Use the allen wrench to carefully push the magnet into the recess in the bit hole. Maximised Visibility: An open-fronted, angled design so you can easily check paint names and colours. High Density: Line them up flush side-by-side or stack them vertically to build a massive, seamless paint wall as your collection expands. Compatibility Be aware that pot holders only interlock and fit together with pot holders of the same size. If you have a relatively small collection, from multiple brands and sizes, it might be best to pick one or two pot holder sizes that fit the majority of paint pots in your collection so you can easily tile the holders on the wall. For example, the 25 mm pot holder is a great pick for all dropper bottle style brands, but if you have a large collection of Games Workshop Citadel paints with only a few of the slightly smaller ProAcryl and Dirty Down paints, there's no need to print holders specifically for the ProAcryl and Dirty Down, the 32 mm Citadel paint holders will fit the ProAcryl and Dirty down just fine, they'll just be a little loose. Customisation To get started, simply press the Customize button at the top of the page bellow the list of print profiles. There are two settings that can be customised: Pot OD: The outer diameter of your paint pot, ideally measured with a pair of callipers. Symmetric: A Boolean (true or false) variable, 0 for false and 1 for true. If set to 1 (true), one pot is removed to make the holder symmetrical. Good for standalone holders, or as the rightmost holder in a row to give a cleaner overall look Clean-up Removal of the organic tree supports may be tricky. It's recommended to use a pair of flush cutters to clip each branch off at the main trunk and remove them one by one working from the outer two pots in toward the middle to allow easier access to the supports for the middle two pots. Installation When it comes to installing multiple holders on a pegboard, because of the interlocking nature of the design, it's important to start from the bottom left, completing one full row at a time before moving on to the next row above. See video example. As mentioned in the compatibility, only group same sized pot holders together in rows and columns. If the pot sizes are different, they will not fit together . Unless you have a very large collection of ProAcryl sized paints, generally most people will benefit from having a wall of 25 mm sized holders for dropper style bottles, and a separate wall of 30 mm sized holders for Games Workshop paint pots and similar, slightly smaller pots from other brands.

Parametrischer DIN-Schienen-Adapter (Hutschiene) — Smart-Home, Relais, Netzteile… d.h. alles was man gerne an diese genormten Schienen befestigen möchte. Fully parametric DIN-rail (top-hat) mounting adapter with a flexible hole pattern — snap-on or slide-on clip, for smart-home modules, relays and power supplies. Everything adjustable in the MakerWorld Customizer. Eine voll parametrische Montageplatte, die auf genormte DIN-/Hutschienen aufgeclipst wird. Damit befestigst du beliebige Komponenten (Smart-Home-Module, Relais, Shelly, ESP, Netzteile, Klemmen, Sensoren …) sauber im Schaltschrank oder Verteiler. Das Lochbild ist bewusst flexibel gehalten, damit fast jedes Bauteil verschraubt oder mit Kabelbindern an einer DIN / Hutschiene fixiert werden kann. Highlights DIN-Normen als Pull-down — die passende Schiene einfach im Customizer wählen (DIN EN 60715): TH 35 × 7.5 (Standard), TH 35 × 15 (schwere Lasten), TH 15 × 5.5 (Miniatur) oder Benutzerdefiniert . Zwei Klemm-Mechanismen Snap-on (Federclip) — auf die Schiene aufrasten, mit Lösehebel wieder abnehmbar. Slide-on (starr) — von der Seite aufschieben, maximal steif für schwere Bauteile. Flexibles Montage-Muster — Lochraster (exakte Anzahl Spalten × Reihen), Langlöcher, beides kombiniert, oder Blankoplatte. Bei beides sitzen die Bohrlöcher in der Mitte , die Langlöcher an den Seiten . Zusätzlich Kabelbinder-Schlitze an den Enden. Senkkopf-kompatibel — optionale Senkung für Bohrlöcher und Langlöcher, wählbar innen oder außen auf der Montageplatte (die Clip-/Schienenseite bleibt flach zum Aufklippsen). Narrensicher — unsinnige Werte werden gar nicht erst umgesetzt: der Customizer begrenzt jeden Regler, und harte Prüfungen (assert) stoppen den Export mit Klartext-Meldung, wenn eine Kombination nicht druck- oder montierbar wäre. Druckfertig ausgerichtet — Montagefläche liegt flach auf dem Bett, Clip zeigt nach oben. Keine Stützen nötig. DIN-Schienen-Normen (recherchiert) Maße nach DIN EN 60715:2018 (löste EN 50022 / 50045 ab): Norm (Auswahl) Gesamtbreite Höhe/Tiefe Hutbreite Blechdicke typische Nutzung TH 35 × 7.5 35 mm 7.5 mm 27 mm 1.0 mm Standard — Relais, Automaten, Smart-Home TH 35 × 15 35 mm 15 mm 27 mm 1.5 mm schwere/größere Geräte TH 15 × 5.5 15 mm 5.5 mm 10.5 mm 1.0 mm Miniatur / Reihenklemmen Benutzerdefiniert frei frei — — Sonderprofile Hinweis: Die G-Schiene (G 32, EN 50035) hat ein grundlegend anderes Clip-Prinzip (Untergriff von innen) und ist bewusst nicht enthalten — dieser Adapter deckt die weit verbreitete Hutschienen-Familie (TH/Top-Hat) ab, die ~95 % aller Smart-Home- und Elektronik-Anwendungen abdeckt. Quellen: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DIN_rail · de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tragschiene Standard-Maße Eigenschaft Wert Platte (B × L × H) 48 × 45 × 3 mm Schiene TH 35 × 7.5 Klemm-Modus Snap-on (Federclip) Lochbild Raster (M3-frei, Ø 3.4 mm) + Kabelbinder-Schlitze Alle Werte sind im Customizer anpassbar. Klemm-Modi im Vergleich Snap-on (Federclip) — eine Wand ist fix, die andere federt über einen dünnen Federhals aus und rastet über die Schienenkante. Ein Lösehebel oben erlaubt das Abnehmen mit dem Finger/Schraubendreher. Ideal für Module, die man wieder abnehmen will. Slide-on (starr) — beide Wände starr; der Adapter wird seitlich auf die Schiene geschoben. Maximale Steifigkeit für schwere Bauteile (z. B. Netzteile), kein Federbruch möglich. Montage — so wird's zusammengebaut Der Adapter macht nicht-DIN-Geräte hutschienentauglich . Aufbau von der Wand nach außen: Wand → DIN-Hutschiene → Clip/Schenkel → Grundplatte → dein Gerät Gerät anschrauben — dein Bauteil auf die Montagefläche (die ebene Seite ohne Clip) legen und mit Senkkopfschrauben festschrauben. Die Senkfasen liegen auf der Montageseite , d. h. die Köpfe sitzen bündig, das Gerät liegt plan auf, und die Clip-/Schienenseite bleibt völlig flach . Auf die Schiene setzen — die Baugruppe auf die Hutschiene aufrasten (Snap-on, mit Lösehebel wieder abnehmbar) oder von der Seite aufschieben (Slide-on). :warning: Schraubenlänge beachten: Die Löcher liegen mittig über dem Schienenkanal. Verwende kurze Schrauben (die im Gerät bzw. in Gewindeeinsätzen/Standoffs greifen), damit die Spitze nicht auf der Clip-Seite herausragt und im eingebauten Zustand an die Schiene stößt. Bei 3 mm Platte genügen Fasentiefe (~1.4 mm) + etwas Gewinde ins Gerät. DIN-Schienen-Norm — rail_norm (Pull-down). Bei Benutzerdefiniert : custom_rail_width, custom_rail_depth. Klemm-Mechanismus — clip_mode (snap/slide), wall_thickness, spring_wall_thickness, hook_catch (Untergriff), hook_height, fit_clearance (Spiel), neck_thickness (Federhals), release_lever + lever_height. Grundplatte — plate_width (quer zur Schiene), plate_length (entlang der Schiene), plate_thickness, corner_radius. Montage-Muster — mount_pattern (none / grid / slots / grid+slots), hole_cols × hole_rows (Anzahl Bohrlöcher), hole_diameter, hole_margin, countersink (Senkung für Senkkopfschrauben, auf der Montageseite), slot_count / slot_width / slot_length (Langlöcher), cable_tie_slots + tie_slot_width / tie_slot_length. Bei beides (grid+slots) liegen die Bohrlöcher in der Mitte , die Langlöcher an den Seiten der Mittelzone — überlappungsfrei. Alle Löcher bleiben zwischen den Klemmwänden (nie unter einem Schenkel → volle Druckstabilität). Tipp Fein-Fit: Klemmt der Clip zu stramm, fit_clearance in 0.1-Schritten erhöhen. Sitzt er zu locker, verringern. Rastet der Snap-Clip schwer ein, neck_thickness reduzieren (dünnerer Hals = leichter federnd). Druck-Empfehlungen Das Modell ist bereits korrekt ausgerichtet — bitte so drucken, wie es geladen wird: Orientierung: Montagefläche unten auf dem Bett, DIN-Clip nach oben. So entsteht eine glatte Sichtfläche, und die Haken haben nur kurze, selbsttragende 45°-Überhänge. Stützen: nicht nötig . Brim: 5–8 mm empfohlen — die schmalen, hohen Klemmwände (v. a. bei TH 35 × 15 und bei ABS/ASA/CF) neigen sonst zum Ablösen/Warping. Brim & Stützen stellst du selbst in Bambu Studio ein. Einstellung Empfehlung Schichthöhe 0.2 mm (0.16 mm für feinere Haken) Wände / Perimeter ≥ 4 (Klemmwände sind tragend) Top / Bottom Layer ≥ 4 Infill 40–60 % (Gyroid), tragende Teile Brim 5–8 mm Stützen keine Filament-Empfehlung (Stabilität & Wärme) DIN-Adapter tragen oft warme Bauteile (Netzteile, Relais) im geschlossenen Schaltschrank . Deshalb zählen Wärmeformbeständigkeit und Steifigkeit/Maßhaltigkeit mehr als bei Deko-Drucken. Richtwerte (Quelle: Simplify3D Materials Guide, Bambu Lab): Filament Wärmeformbest. (ca.) Steifigkeit Zähigkeit Eignung PLA / PLA+ ~50–60 °C hoch spröde nur kühle Umgebung / Testdruck PETG ~70–75 °C mittel hoch guter Allrounder, ideal für Snap-Clip ABS / ASA ~95–100 °C mittel hoch warme Schränke (ASA zusätzlich UV-fest) PC (Polycarbonat) ~110–120 °C hoch sehr hoch Hochlast + Hitze (schwer zu drucken) PA (Nylon) ~80–95 °C mittel sehr hoch zähe, langlebige Federclips PLA-CF ~55–65 °C sehr hoch spröder steife Blankoplatte, aber nur kühl PETG-CF ~75–80 °C sehr hoch mittel Empfehlung: steif + wärmestabil PA-CF / PET-CF ~120–180 °C (HDT) sehr hoch mittel Profi: max. Steifigkeit + Hitze Sind CF-Filamente sinnvoll? — Ja, aber gezielt Carbonfaser (CF) erhöht Steifigkeit und Maßhaltigkeit , reduziert Verzug (Warping) und hebt die Wärmeformbeständigkeit an. Das ist genau richtig für die Trägerplatte , damit sie sich unter Last (z. B. Netzteil) nicht durchbiegt. Aber: CF macht das Material spröder . Der dünne, wiederholt biegende Federclip (Snap-on) hält mit einem zähen Kunststoff länger. Daraus folgt: Slide-on (starr, keine Feder): → CF-Filament ideal (PETG-CF / PA-CF) = maximale Steifigkeit. Snap-on (Federclip): → PETG oder PA / PA-CF = genug Steifigkeit und Federzähigkeit. Reines PLA-CF hier meiden (der Federhals kann brechen). Beste Allround-Wahl: PETG-CF für die Platte + Snap-Clip, oder PETG wenn nur einer. Düse: CF/Glasfaser sind abrasiv → gehärtete Stahldüse nötig. Die Bambu Lab H2C, P2S und P1S haben serienmäßig gehärtete Düsen und sind CF-tauglich. CF-Filamente vor dem Druck trocknen . Lizenz & Autor Autor: Jan Tiedemann · 2026 · Lizenz CC BY 4.0 . description: Ever needed a very specific binding post or Chicago screw size that just doesn't exist in hardware stores, or had 3D-printed threads snap off right at the head? Your door handles is loose and you don't want to go all the way to the hardware store just for one screw ? I designed this fully parametric OpenSCAD generator to create clean, robust, and perfectly fitting Chicago screws in seconds. Whether you're binding leatherwork, making custom album covers, assembling PCB stacks, or fixing door handles , you can generate the exact dimensions you need. ✨ Key Features Full ISO Metric Range: Standard sizes plus all intermediate options (M1.6, M2, M2.5, M3, M3.5, M4, M4.5, M5, M6, M7, M8, M9, M10, and M12) . Anti-Snap Reinforcement: Features a 45° conical fillet right at the neck junction. No more snapped screw heads when tightening! Independent Head Sizes: Adjust the male and female head diameters separately to fit flush into any counterbore. Smart Wall Thickness: Customize the female barrel wall thickness (with automated safety limits so it never prints too thin) . Super Fast & Manifold Mesh: Generated with pure mathematical polyhedrons in OpenSCAD, no CGAL rendering errors, no freezing, and instant STL export! 🎛️ Fully Customizable Parameters Using MakerWorld’s online Parametric Model Maker or OpenSCAD , you can tweak the following settings to get a 100% tailor-made fit: Thread Size (Thread_Size): Pick any standard metric thread from M1.6 to M12 . The script automatically handles ISO pitch calculations and depth for you. Fit Clearance (Clearance): Adjust the tolerance between threads (default 0.15 mm ). Increase slightly if your printer over-extrudes, or tighten it up for a snug precision fit (0.20 is a good compromise if 0.15 fails) . Head Diameters (Male_Head_Diameter & Female_Head_Diameter): Modify each head size independently so they match your project’s counterbore holes or clamping surface area. Lengths (Female_Length & Male_Length): Set the exact barrel depth and threaded rod length to perfectly fit your door backplate or material stack thickness. Barrel Wall Thickness (Female_Wall_Thickness): Reinforce the female post for heavy-duty mechanical strain. The script includes a built-in safety limit so the walls never print dangerously thin. Display Mode (Display): Render both parts side-by-side, or isolate just the female post or male screw if you need to re-print a single replacement part! 🖨️ Recommended Print Settings To ensure the threads turn smoothly right off the build plate without binding, here are my tried-and-tested slicer settings : Orientation: Print both parts vertically, heads flat on the bed. Supports: None needed! The thread angles print cleanly in mid-air. Wall Generator: Arachne (Highly Recommended for crisp thread detail) . Layer Height: 0.12 mm or 0.08 mm (finer layers = smoother threads) . Wall Loops: 4 to 5 walls (This makes the male threaded rod almost 100% solid plastic). Outer Wall Speed: Slow down to 40–50 mm/s for sharp thread profiles. Seam Position: Random (Prevents a single seam line from creating a bump along the threads). 💡 Pro Tip If your printer extrudes slightly heavy, you can adjust the Clearance parameter right in the script (default is 0.15 mm) , or use X-Y Hole Compensation (+0.05 mm) in your slicer. After printing, give the screw a quick run in and out with a screwdriver to smooth out any tiny layer lines! Enjoy the model, and happy printing! If you print a set, please share your make , give a like, save to your collection :) Edit : correction to fit the makerworld generation model ; 0.25 perfect tolerance

description: About the model I wanted to design a portable nice looking, yet simple DIY fan to use at home or at the office. Since it is powerd by USB-C I can use PC, laptop, powerbank or even my phone to enjoy a gentile breeze. This is the model and design I came up with. The fan can be positioned at three different angles. Please let me know what you think (Like/Rate/Comment/Boost). I’d love to see a picture of your build. Also check out my other Models . Used components & tools 140mm Fan: Arctic P14 Pro 400-2500 RPM (a 2500 RMP fan is recommended to generate noticable air-flow). Fan speed controller: Runicci-Yun PWM Fan Speed Controller , DC 0-12V USB power: Zolara USB-C PD trigger Board Module (make sure to set the switches to output 12V) 2 small electrical wires (to connect usb power to fan speed controller) (Beware the design is build around the components I used) 3D printer, obviously Soldering iron + tin (to connect 2 wires to the Fan speed controller) Some glue Tips / warnings Build and use at your own risk. Be carefull not to let fabric, hair, etc. get caught in the fan. It is not a toy. Keep away from children. The cable from the fan is rather long. Consider winding it around the outside (narrow side) of the fan before inserting it into the 3d printed casing. Consider removing additional connectors from the cable of the fan if present. Check if the hardware works before assembly or applying glue. Also make sure to check the dirrection of the air flow. I used some (hot)glue to keep the USB and fan speed controller permanently in place. Print settings General: 0.16 mm layer height, high quality. 4 wall loops (I used Panachroma Matte Fillaments Muted Moss (CA04095) and Wood Brown (CA04041)) Top part / enclosure (plate 1): Use brims (outer brim only), Tree support manual on build plate only, for a small overhang (already painted) (Beware adaptive layer height does not work with tree supports in Bambu Studio) Bottom part (plate 2), connectors and stand (plate 3) No supports, no brims required Fuzzy skin is applied on the outside of the bottom part and part of the stand Variable layer heigth is applied on the components (and therefore devided in 2 plates).

⌨️ Customizable Keyboard Keychain Maker - Design Your Own! Welcome to the ultimate customizer for mechanical keyboard lovers! This parametric model allows you to generate your very own personalized keycaps and a matching keychain base in seconds. Whether you want to print your name, your initials, or a cool word, this tool makes it incredibly easy. ✨ What is this model? This project includes two perfectly matched 3D printed parts: A Custom Keycap: A standard Cherry MX compatible keycap where you can emboss any text you want. A Geometric Display Base & Keychain: A custom-designed base that securely holds your mechanical switch. It features a beautifully integrated keychain loop, angled perfectly at 15 degrees for a smooth, aesthetic look. The generated model is automatically split into two build plates —one for the keycaps and one for the bases—making multi-color printing quick and easy. 🛠️ What do you need to complete this? (Hardware) 1× Mechanical Keyboard Switch: The keycap and base are perfectly designed to fit standard Cherry MX style switches (the switches with the plus-shaped stem, such as Cherry MX, Gateron, Outemu, or Kailh). 1× Keychain Ring (Optional): If you want to use it as a keychain. No glue required! Simply insert the mechanical switch into the base, then attach the keycap by pressing it firmly onto the switch. It may require a little finger strength 💪😉, but once assembled, everything stays securely in place. ⚙️ How to use the Customizer You don't need any 3D modeling skills to make this yours. Just follow these simple steps right here on MakerWorld: Click the "Customize" button at the top of this page. Enter your Text: Type any name, word, or nickname in the "Custom Text" box. Multi-Language Support: If you are typing in Hebrew, Arabic, or any Right-to-Left language, simply toggle the Right_To_Left option. Choose your Font: Thanks to the built-in Google Fonts integration, you have access to thousands of amazing fonts! Just pick your favorite from the dropdown menu. Generate & Print: Click Generate to create two build plates —one for the keycaps and one for the bases. This makes multi-color printing easy. Simply move both plates into one project in Bambu Studio and use Print by Object for automatic color changes. 🔧 Step 4 – Assembly Start with the printed base. Insert the mechanical switch into the base. Attach the keycap by pressing it firmly onto the switch (it may require a little finger strength 💪😉). Assembly complete—no glue required! 🎉 🖨️ Print Settings & Recommendations Supports: NONE! The model is fully optimized to print completely support-free. Layer Height: 0.16mm or 0.12mm is highly recommended for the best text resolution on the keycaps. Infill: 15% is perfect. Orientation: Both build plates are already correctly oriented and ready to print. Happy printing! 🎉 I'd love to see your creations, so don't forget to share your photos in the Makes section!

model_name: Insta360 Luna Ultra MagCage — Magnetic Case+Dock
tags: printforluna|bambulab|insta360lunaultra|insta360|luna ultra|camera case|magnetic mount|tpu|gimbal|camera accessory|vlogging|low angle mount|sd card holder|microsd|ambidextrous|functional|a1 mini
description: A TPU armour case for the Insta360 Luna Ultra, built around a 19-magnet alternating-polarity spine. Stick the camera to steel. Give the detached screen somewhere to live. Carry six microSD cards that tell you at a glance which are full, plus your lav mic and its magnet. A place for everything. Nothing left at home. The problem with a camera that comes apart The Luna Ultra's detachable 2" screen is its best feature and its most annoying one. Pull it off to use as a remote and you're holding a loose part with nowhere to put it — and there are no magnets in it, so it sticks to nothing. Same story with the rest: the card holding your entire shoot is a 15×11mm sliver, the mic is separate, and without the battery handle the body won't stand up on a table. MagCage solves all of it with one idea: build the mounting hardware into the case instead of hanging it off the outside. Camera and screen, mounted separately, no hands. One magnet array, four jobs Five stations up the spine, three stacked magnets in each — 15 in the case, 4 in the Remote Plate. Surface mounting. Any ferrous surface — a car door, a roll cage, a tool chest, a fridge. No clamp, no strap, no adapter to lose. It will hang off the underside of a steel rail with the gimbal running. Inverted under a galvanised gate rail. Magnets only. Screen docking. The Remote Plate cradles the screen and carries four magnets on the same 11.95mm pitch, so a part with no magnets in it mounts anywhere the case does. Four magnets against five stations gives it four valid positions — high or low, either rotation — and it self-selects. Offer it up and it settles where it belongs. You can't get it wrong. Four magnets, recessed behind a retaining lip. Plate parking. When the screen is on the camera instead, the plate snaps flat to the back of the case and rides along. Nothing to stow. Mic docking. The mic snaps on and stays. There's a slot in front of the wind guard for its magnet, too. Six card slots that keep score Moulded into the sleeve edge. Load a fresh card label out ; when it's full, put it back face in . A glance tells you what you've shot — no tape, no marker, nothing to remember. The Luna Ultra shoots 8K; you will fill cards and you will lose track of which ones. All six stay reachable with Insta360's stock cover fitted. About ten pounds The last frame before it let go. Straight pull on a luggage scale, right at the point of release. First run 9.9 lb, best run 10.4 lb / 4.7 kg . I'd rather give you both numbers than pick the flattering one. The camera body weighs 233 g — so the array holds roughly twenty times the weight of what it's carrying . And that's through paint; it was measured on a glossy painted toolbox, and bare steel does better. It doesn't creep , and when you finally overload it sideways it slides rather than letting go. That's the failure mode you want. Magnets that release without warning drop cameras. Surface matters — thick steel beats thin sheet, and every layer of paint or wrap costs you real hold. Keep it off hot surfaces for long periods; neodymium weakens permanently past about 80°C. Does it interfere with the gimbal? Not that I've seen, across roughly thirty prints' worth of shooting. No drift, no hunting, no odd heading behaviour. The array is static relative to the body, so it isn't a changing field the camera has to chase, and it sits low and behind rather than up against the gimbal. That's my experience, not a lab result — if you see different, tell me in the comments and I'll add it here. It doesn't cost you anything Insta360 part Works with the case Wind guard ✅ Untouched — and it helps hold the case on In-box protective cover ✅ Fits over the top, all 6 card slots still reachable Battery handle ✅ Not blocked 1/4"-20 thread handle ✅ Not blocked — you keep your tripod mount Extension modules ✅ Not blocked Detachable touchscreen ✅ Docks natively, or in the Remote Plate Every button, port, vent, USB-C ✅ Open The handle and module fit is snug on purpose, and it works in both directions — the module locks in, and it locks the case down with it. Between that and the wind guard at the other end, the case is clamped by Insta360's own hardware. No latch, no strap, no screw. The best retention feature in this design is one I didn't design. One known limitation: with the screen in the Remote Plate it isn't charging — the plate holds it against the body, not in the contacts. Dock the screen directly and park the plate on the back when you need the charge. Pass-through pogo pins are what the next version is chasing. Printing it ⚠️ Do not enable supports in your slicer. Two hand-drawn support structures are built into the model — less material, cleaner release, better contact face than the slicer's. They break away by hand in seconds. Turning slicer supports on layers auto-generated ones over mine. Bambu TPU for AMS, 68D. No AMS required — that's the filament's name, not a hardware requirement; I print it from a single spool on a bare A1 mini. 47.97 g for both parts. Full print settings, BOM and the assembly sequence are in the Documentation — including the two-pass magnet install, which is the one part worth reading before you start. Design notes This is v4.0 . There was a box of the ones that weren't — around thirty full prints, most five hours apiece. I had the magnets wrong for a long time. The one on the left has twice as many and holds noticeably worse — it's less magnet by volume (500 mm³ against 785), and thin discs are weak for their size on top of that. Fewer, thicker, in one line beat every version of the two-column idea. The rake on the back does four jobs. It's the face the magnet stations sit square to. It lets the whole part lie flat on the bed, so the spine prints without a scaffold. It turned out to be a low-angle camera stand. And because it goes down on the plate, it comes off the printer carrying the textured PEI finish — which is exactly what you want between a magnet array and a steel wall, because friction is what resists sliding. Gimbal clearance at full travel was the last thing I caught — while shooting the photos for this listing. A millimetre of margin on a good day isn't a spec. Two degrees out of the back fixed it. The finished part looks simple. Simple is what's left after you throw away the versions that weren't. The magnet array is an open interface Five stations, 11.95 mm pitch, Ø10 × 2 mm, alternating polarity. That's the whole spec. Which end starts which way round doesn't matter — build against a finished case and let the magnets pick their own orientation. An Arca-Swiss plate, a filter caddy, a cold shoe, a belt clip, a vent mount. One tip if you build one: use single through-magnets, not blind pockets. A magnet seated to attract a station necessarily presents the opposite face outward, so your accessory republishes the case's own alternating pattern on its outer face — and becomes a docking surface for the next thing. Stack them as deep as you like. Remix away, and post it. I'd like to see it. License CC BY-NC-SA. Credit the original, keep your version open under the same terms, don't sell it. I designed this custom 1mm intimate guard to solve this problem. Perfect Fit: Snaps right onto the Philips All-in-One / Multigroom Series 7000 (also compatible with most Series 5000 and 9000 models). The slightly wider gaps catch hair efficiently so you don't have to do as many passes. Extremely safe, just use slight care. 10-Tooth Version (MAXIMUM SAFETY): The gaps are so tight that skin absolutely cannot get between the teeth. It is the safest possible option, but note that it may require a few extra strokes to catch all the hairs. Print Settings & Recommendations Material: PETG is highly recommended - It provides the perfect amount of flex and long-term durability for the snap-on retention tab. PLA works perfectly fine too, but the tab may become brittle and snap over time. Layer Height: 0.08mm (Intentional to ensure the curves touching your skin are buttery smooth). Wall Loops: 3, Wall Generator: Arachne (Best for the thin features like the teeth). Supports: None required! Infill: 15% (but effectively 100% since is low and never gets to the infill step, it's 100% solid). 🛠️ Workflow & Usage Instructions Print: Slice and print using the recommended settings above. Post-Processing (IMPORTANT): Carefully remove any stringing between the teeth. You want the gaps perfectly clear so hair can pass through easily. Use a small steel wire brush, tweezers, or very quickly pass a lighter flame over the teeth to melt away micro-hairs. Attach: Slide the guard down over the metal trimmer head, then press gently on the back end of the guard until the tab goes "click". Check that it is fully secured. Trim: Trim away! For the best results, take a few slow strokes per area and always trim against the direction of hair growth. Aftercare: Remove the guard from the trimmer after use and dry it off completely to keep it sanitary and prolong the life of the plastic tab. ✅ Verified Compatible Philips Models This guard fits the standard metal & intimate trimmer heads of the Philips Multigroom / All-in-One Series 5000, 7000, and 9000 . description: Enhanced Hotel Door Lock - Superior Carpet Grip Security Maximize your hotel room security and gain ultimate peace of mind with this custom-engineered, 3D-printable travel door lock. While most standard door wedges and portable locks struggle on the low-pile carpets frequently found in hotels, this device is designed specifically to utilize that carpet for enhanced leverage and physical resistance. This lock creates a powerful mechanical barrier, making it significantly more difficult for anyone to open the door from the outside, even with a key or card. Key Features & Advantages: Designed for Carpets: Engineered from the ground up to solve the carpet-grip problem. While wedges slip, this lock anchors itself, pressing firmly down into the carpet fibers as you tighten it against the door. Adjustable and Precision-Fit: Features a threaded, screw-down foot that allows for precise height adjustments. Once tightened, the constant pressure creates a rock-solid hold. Gap Adjustment Shim Included: Comes with a specially designed spacer wedge (shim) that can be placed under the lock's base if the door has a high clearance from the floor. Highly Portable and Travel-Ready: The lock disassembles into three simple pieces (the main body, the threaded cylinder foot, and the adjustment shim). They are lightweight, compact, and fit easily into any suitcase or carry-on. Simple, Tool-Free Use: Intuitive design—install and remove in seconds without any tools or damaging the door. Insert the Shim (If necessary): If the gap between the bottom of the door and the floor is too high, insert the included flat shim (wedge) between the floor and the flat base of the lock that goes under the door to fill the empty space and ensure a tight fit. Lower the foot: Rotate the screw-thread cylinder clockwise so it moves downwards towards the floor. Tighten firmly: Continue tightening until the screw foot is pressed deep into the carpet pile, creating a strong, secure tension between the floor and the door. Confirm security: Test the door to ensure it is physically locked and secured from opening. To remove, simply loosen the screw. Disclaimer: This is a secondary security device. Wird er danach einfach wieder in den Korb gestellt, kann er entsprechend wieder umfallen. Kurz gesagt: Cup raus = Halter mit abnehmen. Description Sign up for a Commercial license for this model on my Patreon This modular tray system is designed to maximize the usable space inside the Harbor Freight Apache 2800 case while providing organized storage for up to 46 standard 10-vial kits . With each kit holding ten 3 mL vials, the complete system provides a maximum capacity of: 46 kits 460 individual 3 mL vials The system uses three stacked levels inside the Apache 2800: Level Capacity Bottom level 16 kits Middle level 16 kits Top level 14 kits Total 46 kits / 460 vials Each level is divided into a left and right half tray. The halves may remain separate for easier lifting and access, or they may be joined with the included dovetail connectors to create three full-width trays. Flexible Tray Configuration Each level can be used in either of two ways: Six individual half trays with built-in lifting handles Three connected full-width trays using the included dovetail connectors This allows the user to choose between lighter, independently removable sections or larger unified trays. Features Designed specifically for the Apache 2800 protective case Holds up to 46 ten-vial kits Maximum capacity of 460 individual 3 mL vials Three storage levels maximize the available internal height Bottom and middle levels each hold 16 kits Top level holds 14 kits Left and right tray halves include integrated lifting handles Optional dovetail connectors join each pair into one large tray Bottom and middle trays use standoffs to support the level above Trays do not need to rest directly on the stored kits Case can be used before every compartment is filled Allows room to expand gradually as additional kits are added Open-frame design reduces unnecessary filament while maintaining support No permanent modification to the Apache case is required Supported Stacking Design The bottom and middle tray levels include support posts that carry the weight of the tray above them. This means the upper levels are supported by the printed structure rather than resting directly on the vial kit boxes. The case therefore does not need to be completely full before the stacked system can be used. Kits may be added over time, provided they are distributed appropriately and the support structure is correctly installed. Connector Options The files include dovetail connectors with two fit tolerances: 0.10 mm tolerance 0.15 mm tolerance Printer calibration, material type, filament shrinkage, and extrusion settings can affect connector fit. Print a small connector test first when possible. Use the tolerance that provides a secure connection without requiring excessive force: Start with the 0.10 mm version for a tighter fit. Use the 0.15 mm version if the tighter connector is difficult to install. NOTE: The print profile is designed for printing these successfully. The bridging is slowed down a little bit for the dovetails to help ensure the connectors slide in easily. Supports are intentionally off in the dovetail slots. It's not fun trying to pull supports out of those. Supports are needed on the slots where the handles connect to the bottom of the tray and are set to a sufficient easily removed support design. It would be best to print 1 tray and one connector/riser before printing the whole set so you can ensure that the bridging is ok and that you have the right tolerance connectors. Installation Instructions Option 1: Six Separate Half Trays Use this configuration when you want each side to remain independently removable. Bottom Level Install the smaller risers on the plate labeled "Btm Tray Riser Disconnected Config" into the left and right bottom trays. Confirm that all risers are seated securely. Load up to eight kits into each half for a total of 16 kits on the bottom level. Middle Level Install the middle trays without using any dovetail connectors Load up to eight kits into each half for a total of 16 kits on the middle level. Top Level Install the top trays without using any dovetail connectors Load up to seven kits into each half for a total of 14 kits on the top level. Ensure that there is at least 1 kit on each top tray half to help prevent movement. Confirm that the case closes without interference. This configuration creates six smaller trays that can be removed individually using their side handles. Option 2: Three Connected Full-Width Trays Use this configuration when you prefer each level to function as one large tray. Before Assembly Select either the 0.10 mm or 0.15 mm dovetail connectors. Test the fit before forcing a connector into the tray. Make sure the left and right tray halves are correctly aligned and resting on a flat surface. Bottom Tray Install the Long Risers on the plate labeled “Btm Tray Riser Connected Config” into either the left or right tray. Slide the other tray onto the risers to connect the two sides. Place the assembled full-width bottom tray into the Apache case. The bottom connector also forms part of the support system for the tray above. Middle Tray Install the appropriate tolerance dovetail connector and join the two halves the same way as the bottom trays. Confirm that the two halves are securely joined and level. Place the assembled middle tray onto the bottom-level risers. Top Tray Install the appropriate tolerance dovetail connector and join the two halves the same way as the middle and bottom trays. Confirm that both halves are securely connected. Place the assembled top tray onto the middle-level supports. Loading Recommendations Distribute kits across both sides of each level rather than concentrating all weight in one area. Make sure each tray is resting on its intended supports before adding the next level. Confirm that kits are securely in place Close the lid slowly the first time to check for interference. Do not force the case closed. The case should close easily and still have the ability to be turned upside down without kits coming out of their slots. Use the integrated handles when removing a tray. Support both sides when lifting a connected full-width tray containing kits. REMOVE ALL FOAM THAT COMES IN THE CASE. The inserts are not designed to work with the included foam padding Required Item Harbor Freight Apache 2800 Weatherproof Protective Case Once again, remove the factory foam before installing the tray system. Storage Note This system is intended for organization and physical protection only. It is not sterile, medical-grade, temperature controlled, or validated for storing any particular substance. The Apache case may help slow brief temperature changes because of its thicker shell and enclosed construction, but it should not be treated as active insulation.
