Vortex Cannon Growing up, one of the funniest things to mess around with was an airzooka, so I figured it was time to make one you could print yourself. Just pull it back and let it fly to launch satisfying vortex rings across the room. And if you really want to catch someone off guard... let's just say it pairs suspiciously well with a tiny spritz of fart spray from a safe distance. 😄 It's easy to print, simple to assemble, and guaranteed to get a few laughs. Happy printing! VORTEX CANNON Assembly Guide Before You Begin You'll Need: All printed parts 3 plastic shopping bags (or 1 standard kitchen trash bag) 2 rubber bands (cut into straight strips) STEP 1 – Lay Out the Parts Lay out all printed parts and verify that nothing is missing before beginning assembly. STEP 2 – Prepare the Rubber Bands Cut two rubber bands so they become straight elastic strips. STEP 3 – Install the Elastic Bands Place the center retention clamp in position. Tie one elastic strip to each pair of opposing interior mounting tabs while routing both bands through the center retention clamp. Pull the bands tight before tying the knots. STEP 4 – Verify Band Installation The elastic bands should: Be centered across the opening Pass through the center retention clamp Have equal tension on both sides STEP 5 – Install the Bags Place three shopping bags (or one trash bag) over the rear opening of the cannon. Leave enough material hanging over the edge to be captured by the retention ring. STEP 6 – Install the Retention Ring Important: Install the ring from underneath and slide it upward toward the top of the cannon. Make sure the tapered side of the ring faces upward , toward the widest opening of the cannon. Continue sliding the ring upward until it rests just below the top lip. Tip: Do not trim the excess bag material until assembly is complete. STEP 7 – Lock the Bags in Place Push the center of the bags inward until they reach the installed elastic bands. While holding the bags inward, press the retention ring upward until it snaps securely into place. The bags should now be tightly clamped around the entire opening. STEP 8 – Install the Rear Plate Position the rear plate with the four locating pins over the center of the bags. Push the pins through the bags and into the center retention clamp until fully seated. This securely locks the bags in place. STEP 9 – Install the Threaded Stud Thread the small threaded stud into the center of the rear plate. Tighten until snug. Do not overtighten. STEP 10 – Install the Handle Slide the handle onto the mounting bracket located on the outside of the cannon. Align the holes in the handle with the mounting bracket. STEP 11 – Install the Locking Pin Insert the small straight locking pin through the aligned holes in the handle and mounting bracket. Push the pin in completely until it is fully seated. STEP 12 – Finished Assembly Just trim off the extra bag ends and your Vortex Cannon is now ready to use. Grip the handle, pull it straight back, and release to launch a powerful vortex of air. Tips Three shopping bags produce the best diaphragm. A kitchen trash bag also works well. Replace the bags if they become torn or stretched. Keep the elastic bands evenly tensioned for the strongest vortex. Membership

Clicky Bread – Croissant Fidget Toy A golden little croissant with a satisfying clicky press! 🥐 Clicky Bread – Croissant is a cute fidget toy inspired by the classic croissant. The croissant sits on a white paper liner and a tiny wooden cutting board, creating a warm bakery-style display scene. Press the croissant to activate the hidden MX-style mechanical keyboard switch and enjoy a satisfying click with springy feedback. It works as a relaxing desk toy, a cute bakery-themed decoration, or a small keychain charm. The hole in the cutting board handle can be used to attach a keyring, so no separate keychain version is required. Features Satisfying Clicky Action Press the croissant to enjoy a satisfying clicky fidget experience. The croissant is the main interactive part of the model, while the wooden cutting board base hides the internal switch and supports the clicky mechanism. Classic Croissant Shape The croissant features a rounded curved shape with soft layered details inspired by a classic bakery croissant. The design keeps the main croissant silhouette clear and cute, without making the surface too overly detailed or fragile. Wooden Cutting Board Base Unlike the previous Clicky Bread models that use woven baskets or proofing baskets, this model introduces a tiny wooden cutting board base. The cutting board creates a warm serving scene and gives the model a different display style within the Clicky Bread series. The round hole in the cutting board handle can also be used to attach your own keyring or charm hardware. Paper Liner Detail The white paper liner sits between the croissant and the wooden cutting board. It adds a bakery display feeling, visually separates the golden croissant from the wooden base, and makes the model easier to customize with different color combinations. Desk Toy or Keychain This model can be used in two ways: Desk Toy – place it on your desk and press the croissant whenever you want a small fidget moment. Keychain Charm – attach your own keyring to the hole in the cutting board handle and carry it with you. Both uses are based on the same model. No separate keychain STL is needed. Separate Parts for Easy Color Printing The model is divided into separate printable parts: Croissant Paper Liner Wooden Cutting Board Base Each part can be printed in a different color, so no additional painting is required. A multi-color printer is not necessary. The parts can be printed separately and assembled afterward. Print Profile Options Two print profiles are included. Both profiles create the same final model. The difference is the printing method for the Paper Liner. Standard Print Version This version uses the regular Paper Liner model. Supports are mainly handled by the slicer settings, making it suitable for users who prefer to adjust support settings by themselves. Paper Liner Enhanced Support Version This version includes a pre-designed enhanced support structure for the Paper Liner to help improve printing stability. After printing, the enhanced support structure can be snapped off by hand or carefully trimmed with scissors. The trimmed area will be hidden inside the assembled model, so it does not need to be perfectly smooth. Just make sure not to cut into the actual Paper Liner part. Additional Parts Required One compatible MX-style mechanical keyboard switch is required to create the clicky movement. If you want to use it as a keychain, you will also need your own keyring or suitable keychain hardware. The mechanical switch and keychain hardware are not included with the printable model files. Assembly Install the mechanical keyboard switch into the square hole on the croissant. Insert the paper liner into the slot on the cutting board. Place the croissant onto the cutting board, aligning it with the cross-shaped hole. Press the croissant several times to make sure it moves smoothly and returns properly. If you want to use it as a keychain, attach your own keychain hardware to the hole in the cutting board handle. Printing Notes The croissant, paper liner, and wooden cutting board base are separate parts and can be printed in different colors. Please use the provided print profiles for the recommended orientation and print settings. If your chosen assembly method requires glue, check that all parts fit correctly and make sure the croissant can move freely before applying it. Welcome Back to Clicky Bread This Croissant design adds a new bakery display style to the Clicky Bread series. The previous models used woven baskets, proofing baskets, and square bread baskets. This model introduces a wooden cutting board and paper liner, creating a different warm bakery scene while keeping the same satisfying Clicky Bread interaction. Together, the series continues the main idea behind Clicky Bread: Cute baked goods, warm bakery-themed scenes, and satisfying clicky interaction. Description When I assembled Dummy 13, I found it very inconvenient and frustrating to search through the many parts that were printed all at once. To solve this problem, I created this model. You no longer need to deal with a large number of mixed parts. Each card kit is organized with the part names and the assembly direction clearly marked in order. Simply follow the sequence and assemble the parts step by step. All accessories shown in the picture (e.g., guns, body armor, etc.) are available on my profile. There are many options, so feel free to choose and download whichever ones you like. What's Changed in This Remix One of the biggest challenges when assembling Dummy 13 is failed prints and the confusion caused by the large number of parts. With so many pieces, it's easy to lose track of the assembly order. To solve this, I separated the runners (frames) by body section. For example, the LEG runner contains only the parts needed to assemble the legs, allowing you to complete the entire leg assembly before moving on to the next section. Each runner is also clearly labeled in English (such as LEG , ARM , BODY ) so you can immediately identify which body section the parts belong to. In addition, the layout of the parts on each runner follows the assembly order. Simply start with the part at the top of the runner and work your way down—the parts are arranged in the exact order they should be assembled. ⚠️ Important Do not remove all the parts from the runner before you begin. Instead, detach only the part you need at each step and continue assembling from top to bottom. ⚠️ Printing Recommendations The armor parts can be printed in either PETG or PLA . However, the frame parts should be printed in PETG for the best durability and long-term performance. Print Settings Do not change the layer height from 0.16 mm. Using any layer height other than 0.16 mm is strongly discouraged , as it may cause poor fitment, joint issues, or part failure. Frequently Asked Questions Please follow the assembly guide carefully and take your time. If the runner supports break off easily or looks thinner than expected, this is completely normal. The runner is designed to be easy to remove and its only purpose is to support successful printing. It is not a structural part of the final model. Do not worry about the thickness or strength of the runner — it is intentionally designed this way for easier removal and better print reliability. Each time you add cubes to the playing area, you score points equal to the rows/columns that you create or add to. In QWIRKLE CUBES - Bookcase Edition the tokens have six faces in the same color, with each face having a different one of the six symbols. Players roll cubes, then play the cubes to build color lines and symbol lines to score points. The player with the most points wins! This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the all the QWIRKLE Cubes, 4-Part Board and Player Tokens. To store the parts, first add all the cubes to the box. Then place the boards above the cubes. The Player Tokens are stored at the inner edge of the box beside the boards. INFORMATION & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued, for example, the book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. WORDSTACK Board Game - Bookcase Edition In WORDSTACK Board Game - Bookcase Edition 2 to 4 players build and transform words by placing and stacking letter tiles on a shared 10×10 PlayGrid game board. Every new layer creates fresh scoring opportunities. The player with the highest score when the game ends is the winner. Enjoy building higher, scoring bigger, and creating endless word possibilities in WORDSTACK ! GAME COMPONENTS The WORDSTACK Board Game - Bookcase Edition set includes: • PlayGrid Game Board (4 Corners and Board) • 100 Letter Tiles • 4 Player Pawns and Score Board • Built-in Tile Rack on Game Board • 1 Bookcase Edition Box BOOKCASE EDITION BOX The WORDSTACK Board Game - Bookcase Edition game also includes a Bookcase Edition Box with a slide top. This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the 4-Corner Board Frame, PlayGrid Board, Letter Tiles and Player Pawns. To store the parts, first add the Letter Tiles to the smaller compartment of the box. In pairs, then add the 4 Board Corners and place the Player pawns inside. Place the PlayGrid Board inside the top of the box and slide on the box lid. A small drop of printer oil on the edges of the box lid will help with the slide into the box top. INFORMATION & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued, for example, the book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. IMPORTANT NOTE: I've turned off the prime tower in order to upload the model but turning it on (if it will fit on your plate) will help the quality of your prints. PLAYGRID BOARD ASSEMBLY To assemble the game board, first align the 4 board corners together like a picture frame. Then place the PlayGrid board above the frame and snap down, The board will sit into the special keyhole pegs to hold the whole board assembly together. This project is an original game designed with the concept of the PlayGrid system. The PlayGrid base module was created by @OzarkExpeditions , whose modular platform makes it possible for creators to build entirely new games using the same shared board system. description: Un dolce brachiosauro puzzle 3D facile da montare, educativo e perfetto per stimolare creatività, logica e manualità nei bambini. Questo simpatico dinosauro in stile Montessori è pensato per unire il fascino della stampa 3D al gioco educativo. Il modello è composto da 5 pezzi singoli che si incastrano tra loro in modo semplice e intuitivo. Una volta assemblato, il brachiosauro si sostiene in piedi, diventando sia un piccolo puzzle educativo sia un grazioso elemento decorativo. Il modello è anche scalabile a piacere : puoi aumentare o ridurre le dimensioni in base alle tue esigenze, allo spazio disponibile o al tipo di utilizzo. In grande diventa più scenografico, in piccolo più compatto e veloce da stampare. Puoi inoltre regolare il riempimento/infill per adattare robustezza e peso dei pezzi: con un infill più alto i pezzi risultano più resistenti; con un infill più basso la stampa è più veloce e leggera. A dimensioni standard, il modello è progettato per una stampa rapida , indicativamente in meno di 80 minuti , a seconda della stampante, del materiale, della velocità di stampa, dell’altezza layer e delle impostazioni utilizzate. Consigliato in PLA , anche con piatto texturizzato , per ottenere una finitura più pulita, piacevole al tatto e con un aspetto più professionale. description: ASSEMBLY: The Trammel of Archimedes is a fascinating mechanical fidget that turns a simple rotating motion into a perfectly smooth elliptical path. As you rotate the textured handle, the two sliding joints travel back and forth through the intersecting tracks, guiding the arm around the centre in a mesmerizing continuous motion. This classic mechanism is often called an ellipsograph because a point along the rotating arm traces the shape of an ellipse as it moves. Every clearance was carefully tuned to keep the sliders moving smoothly through the tracks without feeling too loose or easily coming free. The detailed frame, mechanical arm, and textured handle give the model a clean industrial appearance while also making it comfortable and satisfying to operate. Taking less than 68 minutes to print and using under 22 grams of filament , the Trammel of Archimedes is a quick and low-cost print that is perfect for anyone who enjoys mechanical demonstrations, mathematical designs, or satisfying motion fidgets. description: " Know Pain. Feel Pain. Accept Pain. " Bring the leader of the Akatsuki to your collection with this fully articulated 3D printable figure of Pain from Naruto Shippuden . Captured in his iconic, imposing stance, this model is designed for fans and collectors who want to display the power of the Six Paths on their shelf. Key Features: Fully Articulated: Ball-jointed shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees, and ankles allow for a wide range of dynamic poses. The neck and torso also feature articulation for expressive combat stances. Anime-Accurate Design: Sculpted to reflect Pain's tall, lean physique, with attention to his signature orange-red hair, the Rinnegan eyes, and the iconic Akatsuki cloak with its red clouds . Compact Scale: Stands at approximately 14-15 cm tall when assembled—matching the scale of other figures in this series and similar to the official S.H.Figuarts release . Includes One Set of Hands: Comes with one set of hands (open palms/fists). Additional hand options can be printed from the Dummy 13 base model at 1.5x scale. Snap-Fit Assembly: Parts connect with integrated pins and sockets. Please note: Due to the high detail and tight tolerances of this remix, some parts may have a very snug fit. ⚠️ IMPORTANT: A CHALLENGING BUILD ⚠️ This is not a beginner-friendly model. It is a complex remix designed for experienced makers who enjoy a challenge. Please be prepared for the following: Difficult Fit: The Akatsuki cloak and clothing details are designed to fit closely over the base frame. Expect a tight, sometimes frustrating fit. Be patient and persistent. Reprints are Likely: Some parts, especially joint pins and connection points, may need to be reprinted to achieve the perfect fit. Do not be discouraged if your first attempt is not perfect. Multiple Test Fits: You will need to test-fit parts multiple times, sanding or heating connections slightly to get everything to work together smoothly. High Detail: The model features fine details (hair, facial features, cloak folds) that require careful printing and handling. Printing Notes: Supports Required: Due to overhanging parts (especially the hair and the Akatsuki cloak), supports will be needed for a successful print. Enable supports in your slicer. Recommended Layer Height: 0.12mm – 0.16mm for the best detail on the face, hair, and cloak. Recommended Material: PLA or PETG. For the frame/skeleton, PETG is recommended for maximum strength and flexibility. Infill: 15–20% for body parts; 100% for small joint pins if printing them separately. Assembly: Warm the receiving holes slightly with a hair dryer if joints feel too tight. Move each joint carefully after assembly to break in the articulation. Do not force parts —if something doesn't fit, reprint or carefully sand the offending area. What's Included in the Download: Complete STL set for the articulated figure (including Akatsuki cloak details) One set of hands (open palms/fists) Scale: ~14-15 cm (5.5-6 inches) tall when assembled. This size is optimized for detail and joint mobility. While you can scale the model, note that scaling down may reduce joint mobility and make the tight fits even worse. The official S.H.Figuarts version is approximately 15.5 cm, so this matches well . Post-Painting Friendly: The model is not split into color zones, so it prints as a single-color model—perfect for painting Pain's distinctive orange-red hair, the black Akatsuki cloak with red clouds, and his pale skin with your own custom finishes. Alternatively, a multi-color printer can be used to achieve an impressive, paint-free result. Disclaimer: This is a fan-made artistic tribute. description: Use a small amount of lubricant oil in the bearings for a smoother experience and a longer spin time. Lubricant oil tubes are included with all Bambu Labs printers. This bearing gear spinner combines two interlocking herringbone gears , each spinning smoothly on its own internal roller bearing system . Using a bearing instead of a standard print-in-place joint is unusual for a fidget like this, but it makes the spin dramatically smoother than a regular pin joint ever could. The gear teeth mesh together so spinning one wheel drives the other , letting you flick either side and watch the motion transfer between them. Each bearing hub is a scaled-down version of my previous viral bearing fidget , shrunk down and re-tuned so the rollers still spin freely and smoothly at the smaller size. A separate connecting handle rests on top, spinning freely around both bearing hubs and giving you a third way to interact with the mechanism. This fidget is entirely print-in-place , meaning it comes off the build plate already assembled and ready to spin with no additional hardware or post processing . The bold gear teeth and dual-bearing design give it a satisfying mechanical look , while the wide, chunky handle offers a comfortable grip for one-handed spinning . description: 🏹 The Five-Shot Q-Tip Shooter: It keeps getting better You know and love the original Q-tip shooter, and have tried the tri-shot as well. But why settle for one shot when you can unleash five shots at once? With the Five-shot Q-tip shooter, you can load in five one-sided Q-tips and launch them simultaneously. It is the ultimate upgrade for office wars, target practice, or fidgeting at your desk. Note: This model improves on past revisions by having an upgraded trigger mechanism that is more resistant to breaking, as well as more power in the compliant mechanism. However, this means that the trigger is harder to pull back and load, so please be mindful of your technique. Why You’ll Love This Print 100% Print-in-Place: No assembly, no screws, and no extra hardware required. Just pop it off the build plate and start shooting! Zero Supports Needed: Designed from the ground up to print cleanly without any annoying support cleanup. Compliant Mechanism: It uses the natural flexibility of 3D-printed plastic to create its spring tension. No rubber bands needed! Fast & Low Filament: Prints in under an hour and 12 minutes and uses only 45 grams of filament—perfect for burning through those leftover ends of spool rolls. Printing Recommendations To get the best spring tension and durability, use these settings: Material: BAMBU PETG HF (This is the only filament that I have tested extensively, so it is the only one I recommend for the profile. I am sure that high-quality basic PLA would work well, but I can't guarantee the best results.) Infill: 15%-20% (Gyroid or Grid recommended). Walls/Perimeters: 4 walls for extra strength in the flexible bow arms and trigger mechanism. Layer Height: 0.2mm works beautifully for a quick and clean print. How to Load & Fire Prep your ammo: Take three standard Q-tips/cotton swabs and snip off one of the cotton ends (leaving a stick with a single cotton bud). Load: Slide the bare stick ends into the five front barrels. Push them in until they gently rest against the pusher mechanism. Draw & Fire: Hold the grip, pull back the flexible bow arms, click it into the trigger lock, aim, and squeeze the trigger to unleash the ultimate barrage! IMPORTANT: Read Before Printing! This model relies heavily on material properties, so I strongly suggest using Bambu PETG HF for this print . Gravity Shift ist eine neue, dreidimensionale Weiterentwicklung des beliebten Spielklassikers „Vier Gewinnt“, speziell entwickelt für das PlayGrid-System. Die Spieler werfen ihre Spielsteine in das vertikale Spielbrett und versuchen, eine Reihe aus vier eigenen Steinen zu bilden. Doch im Gegensatz zum klassischen Vorbild bleibt das Spielfeld nicht immer gleich: Mit dem mitgelieferten Deckel kann das gesamte Spielfeld während des Spiels verschlossen und anschließend um 180° gedreht werden. Dadurch verändert sich die Richtung der Schwerkraft und alle Spielsteine fallen an neue Positionen. Eine scheinbar sichere Strategie kann sich innerhalb eines Augenblicks auflösen – oder plötzlich zum Sieg führen. Da die räumliche Anordnung der Spielsteine mit zunehmender Spieldauer immer komplexer wird, besitzt Gravity Shift eine besondere Siegregel: Wenn ein Spieler glaubt, vier Steine in einer Reihe zu haben, erklärt er sofort seinen Sieg. Anschließend wird das Spielfeld gemeinsam kontrolliert. Ist die Behauptung korrekt, gewinnt dieser Spieler. Ist die Behauptung falsch, gewinnt sofort der Gegner. Diese Regel sorgt für zusätzliche Spannung, Aufmerksamkeit und taktische Entscheidungen. Gravity Shift nutzt die Modularität des PlayGrid-Systems auf kreative Weise und erschafft ein Spielerlebnis, das mit einem klassischen Spielbrett kaum möglich wäre. Spielregeln Ziel des Spiels Bilde eine Reihe aus vier eigenen Spielsteinen. Die Reihe darf verlaufen: Horizontal Vertikal Diagonal Spielaufbau Das Spielbrett auf eine ebene Fläche stellen. Jeder Spieler wählt eine Farbe. Der Startspieler wird zufällig bestimmt. Spielablauf Der Startspieler beginnt. In seinem Zug: Wähle eine Spalte. Wirf einen Spielstein in die Spalte. Der Stein fällt bis zum nächstmöglichen freien Platz. Danach ist der nächste Spieler an der Reihe. Gravity-Shift-Regel Vor dem eigenen Zug darf ein Spieler das Spielfeld drehen: Deckel aufsetzen. Spielfeld verschließen. Das gesamte Spielbrett um 180° drehen. Deckel entfernen. Durch die veränderte Schwerkraft fallen alle Spielsteine auf ihre neuen Positionen. Dadurch entstehen völlig neue Spielsituationen und Strategien. Siegregel Sobald ein Spieler glaubt, vier eigene Steine in einer Reihe zu haben, ruft er: „Gewonnen!“ Das Spiel wird sofort unterbrochen. Anschließend überprüfen alle Spieler gemeinsam das Spielfeld. HEXADOR Board Game - Bookcase Edition HEXADOR Board Game - Bookcase Edition is a 2 to 6 player game of Sabotage and Strategic Hexagonal Path-Building. Players begin on their home side and guide their pawn across the 4-part hexagon board to the opposite home edge before any other player while other players block their path with Zig-Zag Walls. The first player to move their pawn onto the opposite home edge wins the game. GAME COMPONENTS The HEXADOR Board Game - Bookcase Edition set includes: • 1 Hexagonal game board (4 interlocking sections) • 6 Colored Pawns (Red, Blue, Pink, Yellow, Purple, Orange) • 36 Zig-Zag Walls (6 walls in each player color) • 1 Bookcase Edition Box BOOKCASE EDITION BOX The HEXADOR Board Game - Bookcase Edition game also includes a Bookcase Edition Box with a slide top. This bookcase edition box can be stored on a shelf with your other matching bookcase edition games. The box includes storage areas for the 4-Part Board, Zig-Zag Walls and Player Pawns. To store the parts, first add all the Zig-Zag Walls and Player Pawns to the box. Then place the boards in the large space with two of the boards upside-down. INFORMATION & ASSEMBLY All parts were printed with PLA filament, matt or flat colored PLA filaments work best for bookcase edition games. I use a textured plate for adhesion. Some parts will need to be superglued, for example, the book spine is glued to the square cornered side of the bookcase box. Also the colored hexagon inserts are glued onto the playing board. NOTE: Lay out the boards first in order to match up the colored half pieces. A small drop of printer oil on the edges of the box lid will help with the slide into the box top. IMPORTANT NOTE: I've turned off the prime tower in order to upload the model but turning it on (if it will fit on your plate) will help the quality of your prints. A collection of seven compact magnetic sliders, each with its own texture and sensory intensity. I created this set in part for the @Pipin.World BONBON Capsules Design Contest . The variety of textures makes each one a fun little surprise to discover from a gachapon capsule, and printing the full set lets you find the one that suits you best! Seven Textures Classic : Smooth and simple, with only the embossed icon on the slider. Spiky : The most intense option, with pronounced points that are especially satisfying to press and run your fingers across. Geometric : Similar to Spiky, but less intense and more rounded, with a structured repeating pattern that still provides plenty of tactile variation. Industrial : A subtle diamond plate texture with a gentler sensory effect. Knitted : A detailed woven pattern with a comfortable medium level of texture. Dots : A playful medium-intensity texture that's surprisingly nice to rub along the sides. This one is my personal favorite. Fuzzy Skin : A soft, understated texture for anyone who prefers something more subtle. The set is designed to cover a wide range of preferences. Spiky sits at the most intense end, Geometric offers a similar experience in a more rounded form, Dots and Knitted land around the middle, and Industrial and Fuzzy Skin offer a more subtle touch. Classic is there for anyone who prefers a smooth surface. Magnetic Snap Each slider uses four 6x3mm magnets. Three are placed inside the base, while one is enclosed inside the moving piece. The center magnet repels the moving magnet, helping the slider snap toward either end with a satisfying magnetic response. Printing and Assembly Each slider requires: 4 x 6x3mm magnets Superglue Follow the included diagram and these steps carefully to make sure the magnets have the correct polarity: Prepare the magnets. Hold the four magnets as a stack and mark the exposed top face of the first magnet. Separate them without flipping. Slide the marked magnet sideways off the stack. Mark the newly exposed top face, then slide that magnet off the same way. Repeat until all four magnets have been separated. All four marked faces now have the same polarity. Insert the slider magnet at the first pause. Add a small drop of superglue to the magnet hole in the slider, then insert one magnet with the marked face pointing up. The slider prints face-down, so the unmarked face will point toward the build plate. Insert the outer base magnets at the second pause. Add a small drop of superglue to each outer magnet hole, then insert both magnets with their marked faces pointing up. Insert the center base magnet. Add a small drop of superglue to the center hole, then insert the remaining magnet with its marked face pointing down. This opposite orientation makes the center magnet repel the slider while the two outer magnets attract it. Let the glue hold the magnets in place. Make sure every magnet is seated fully inside its hole before continuing the print. Keep an eye on them for the first few layers after the pause, since the nozzle can pull up a magnet that isn't secured properly. Check the slider orientation before assembly. The slider must be vertical when you snap it into the rails. The top is square, so use the shape on the bottom to confirm its direction. Don't try to insert it sideways, rotated 90 degrees from the correct position. Snap the slider into the rails. Press it in carefully while keeping it straight. If it doesn't go in with reasonable pressure, stop and check its orientation instead of forcing it, as this may damage the rails. Troubleshooting Depending on the filament, the rails where the slider snaps into place may deform slightly during assembly. I've found this is more likely with softer materials, including certain spools of matte PLA. If the slider doesn't travel all the way to either end, a section of the rail probably bent inward while the slider was being pressed into place. Carefully inspect the full path and either trim the deformed plastic or gently straighten it by prying it back into position with a craft knife. Remove or adjust only as much material as necessary. The slider may also feel stiff at first even when nothing is visibly blocking it. Once you've confirmed that it can travel fully to both ends, slide it back and forth several times. This will usually straighten out minor deformation and make the movement smoother. For an even smoother feel, you can brush a small amount of lubricant onto the rail surfaces. Only do this after the slider already travels freely to both ends without lubricant. Print one texture or collect all seven and discover your favorite!

The Triwizard Cup Labyrinth A strategic board game inspired by the legendary Third Task of the Triwizard Tournament "The champions were to enter the maze and reach the Triwizard Cup. The first to touch it would win the Tournament." — Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire , J.K. Rowling, Chapter 31, The Third Task The Triwizard Cup Labyrinth is a strategy board game inspired by the iconic maze from Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire . It recreates the atmosphere of the famous Third Task while introducing original gameplay mechanics designed for players of all ages. Just like the champions in the Tournament, every player must find a path through an ever-changing maze, overcome unexpected dangers, and race to reach the Triwizard Cup before anyone else. Every decision matters, and every turn can completely change the outcome of the game. Although inspired by the Wizarding World's most famous maze, this is an original fan-made board game that combines tactical thinking, player interaction, and a touch of unpredictability. Assembly The game has been designed to be easy to assemble. The main game board consists of two parts that must be glued together before the first game. Once assembled, the board becomes a sturdy playing surface ready for countless adventures. All other components are ready to use immediately. Gameplay The game is inspired by the award-winning board game Quoridor , designed by Mirko Marchesi and published by Gigamic, while introducing several original mechanics that create a completely different experience. Compared to Quoridor, this version features: a significantly larger game board; 15 hedge walls per player instead of the traditional wall count; special dice spaces that trigger magical events; temporary Fire Walls that can completely block passages; the unpredictable power of the Triwizard Cup itself. The result is a game that rewards strategy while embracing the chaotic nature of magic. Objective Your goal is simple: Be the first champion to reach the Triwizard Cup. To claim victory, your pawn must move onto the Cup's space and physically replace the Cup by picking it up. However, in true wizarding fashion, appearances can be deceiving. The Triwizard Cup is a Portkey , and reaching it may not always end your journey the way you expect. Setup Each player begins in one corner of the maze. Every player receives 15 Labyrinth Wall pieces , which can be used throughout the game to reshape the maze and slow down opponents. The youngest player takes the first turn. Taking a Turn During your turn, you must choose one of the following actions: Move your pawn one space horizontally or vertically. Place one Labyrinth Wall anywhere on the board. Diagonal movement is never allowed. Whenever placing a wall, one important rule must always be respected: Every player must always have at least one possible route to the Cup. Walls may slow opponents, but they can never trap them permanently. Dice Spaces Certain orange spaces on the board activate the Magic Die. Whenever a player lands on one of these spaces, they immediately roll the die and resolve the corresponding magical event. These effects can dramatically alter the game, rewarding clever positioning as much as luck. The Magic Die The Sphinx's Riddle Move back two spaces toward your starting corner . Usually a setback—but depending on the maze's current layout, it may unexpectedly become an advantage. Skull The darkest result. Lose your next turn. Maze Mist Exchange your pawn with any other player's pawn. This effect is usually beneficial, but clever opponents may leave you in a much worse position than before. Fire Wall Place one temporary Fire Wall anywhere on the board. Unlike regular maze walls, a Fire Wall may completely block every available route, temporarily trapping players. The Fire Wall remains in play for two complete turns , after which it is removed. Acromantula A giant magical spider attacks. Discard one unused Labyrinth Wall from your personal supply. With fewer walls available, planning ahead becomes even more important. The Cup's Favor Magic smiles upon you. Immediately move one additional space during your current turn. Strategy Victory rarely belongs to the fastest player. Players must constantly balance offense and defense: Build walls to delay your rivals. Preserve enough walls for the final stretch. Decide whether triggering the Magic Die is worth the risk. Adapt to an ever-changing maze where every turn can rewrite the best path. No two games are ever the same. A Magical Race The Triwizard Cup Labyrinth combines strategic planning, tactical positioning, and unpredictable magical events into a fast-paced competition inspired by one of the most memorable challenges in the Harry Potter series. Every wall changes the maze. Every die roll changes the story. And only one champion will claim the Cup. Good luck… and beware of Portkeys.

Dual-Circle Rotating Puzzle Challenge yourself with this unique dual-circle rotating puzzle ! The objective is simple: rotate the two circles to move the pieces until they reach their required positions. Although intuitive and easy to learn, finding the solution can be surprisingly challenging, making it a fun puzzle for all ages. No supports required Great desk toy and brain teaser pieces are in the recommended orientation in both the stl and 3mf 3MF files already contain the correct quantities on each build plate. Assembly Assembly is simple and straightforward. Simply clip the two halves of one colour of the centres together; then slide all edges and corners (including the previously assembled centre of one colour) into the black frame/rail. Next, you are left with the last 2 halves of the other centre piece, just place one on the bottom and clip the other half from the top. Once assembled, mix the pieces by rotating the circles, then try to return every piece to its original position.

Work the oil in by rolling the wheels for a few seconds to eliminate friction and achieve maximum spin speed. Step 2: Add Wheel Grip Tape Cut four thin strips of duct tape to match the width of your printed wheels and wrap them around each wheel it is fine if some of the tape over laps. This adds essential traction to prevent the wheels from not rolling. description: 这是出自逆转裁判5的证物打火机。成步堂和王泥喜在对其进行调查时发现改证物实为一把手枪。 变形前 变形后 我认为如果把这个证物做成模型的话，展示性和可玩性会比较好，而且外观就是一个普通的的打火机，不会让人产生怀疑（？）。所以我就以一个标准zippo打火机为尺寸基准进行建模（当然实际大小还是会有小出入的）。 不幸的是，在试图实现枪的发射bb弹功能时，模型的设计一度因为击发结构过大塞不进枪体而停滞。 然后在makerworld上搜索时发现了这个模型： https://makerworld.com.cn/zh/models/2654907-shou-qiang-yao-chi-kou-v2-gong-neng-xing-fa-she-qi#profileId-3067963 这个模型在如此小的体积内实现了上膛和扳机工作，我在实际打印了一个之后也发现里面的核心机构恰好能够塞进打火机里。于是我按照该机构的运作方式对打火机枪进行建模和改进，最终的打火机枪可以实现一下功能： ——可滑出的外壳作为枪把手； ——另一部分枪壳用于上膛； ——可折叠的扳机以实现在打火机状态下的隐蔽。 下面是拼装说明。 注意！虽然组装的模型允许使用圆珠笔弹簧，但像上面那种中间有密集匝的弹簧是不适用的！！！ 在这两片激发扳机之间涂上胶水，将它们贴在一起如下。 找到这个扳机零件并准备一节耗材丝。 将耗材丝穿过两个零件。如果孔不够大可用剪刀尖扩孔。 这样就完成了折叠扳机的组装。 同样的，将扳机孔和枪主体孔对准后插入耗材丝连接。 擦轮的连接同上。 准备一条0.5*5*20~25mm的弹簧放进枪管里。 然后将击发条沿楔形口朝扳机方向的方式插入枪管。 将小壳沿滑道滑进枪主体。 像这个方孔里塞一根0.5*5*20~25mm的弹簧。 将这个零件安到方孔里，注意凸点的朝向是弹簧。可用小工具将弹簧压缩到一定程度后顺势装进去。必要时使用胶水。 将这跟插销从上面的小孔插进去并压实。 都装好后就是这样的。 通过倾斜连接件使其卡入导轨。 将这两个零件链接起来。 以倾斜的方式卡入。

This model brings the full Mastermind board game into a compact, fully 3D‑printable form. The complete game measures 235 × 140 × 30 mm . 🔧 Construction The game uses a sliding system — the pin storage box slides into the main board . This keeps everything secure, portable, and neatly organized. 🎨 Printing & graphics The board is designed for bed‑printed graphics (ideally two‑color). For single‑color printing , an emboss version of the graphics is included. You can apply Fuzzy skin on the upper rim of the game pins for better grip. The lower part of each pin (the part inserted into the board) should remain smooth . ⚠ Important – box locking pins The locking pins that keep the sliding box closed are 1.5 mm tall . They are intentionally designed larger , so each user can adjust the opening force to their preference. At the original height, the box requires a lot of force to open — not ideal. I recommend lightly sanding the pins — I reduced them to about 0.9 mm . You can also trim them using a slicer modifier . This adjustment significantly improves usability. 🎯 Pin counts Game pins (colors) 160 pieces total 20 pieces for each of 8 colors Information pins (black/white) 50 pieces total 25 pieces for each of 2 colors 🎲 Mastermind rules Mastermind is a logic game for two players. 🔢 Number of positions This version includes 5 positions for the secret code, offering a more challenging game. Players may start with easier variants: 4 positions – classic difficulty 3 positions – fast and simple You can also use fewer colors to simplify the game 🎯 Goal Guess the secret color code created by the opponent. 🧩 Gameplay One player creates a secret combination of colored pins. The opponent places a guess in each row. The guess is evaluated using information pins: Black pin = correct color in the correct position White pin = correct color in the wrong position The guessing continues until the code is cracked or all rows are used. 🏆 Winning The winner is the player who guesses the code in the fewest attempts .

description: 🕷️ Descrizione del Modello Il soggetto è Iron Spider (Spider-Man con la tuta creata da Tony Stark), raffigurato in una posa museale dinamica. Dettagli del costume: Il modello mostra la celebre Iron Spider Suit caratterizzata da linee d'oro metallizzato che delimitano le sezioni rosse e blu notte/metallizzate, oltre al grande logo del ragno stilizzato sul petto. Zampe meccaniche (Iron Legs): Dalla schiena si estendono 4 bracci meccanici articolati finemente dettagliati con finitura dorata e inserti scuri. Base espositiva: Il personaggio poggia su una base tematica che riproduce una roccia incastonata in una struttura tecnologica circolare, arricchita dal logo AVENGERS in rilievo sul fronte. 🎨 Preparazione alla Verniciatura (Stampa FDM) Stampare un modello ricco di dettagli come questo con una stampante a filamento (FDM, es. PLA o PETG) richiede una buona fase di post-produzione per nascondere le "layer lines" (i layer di stampa): 1. Rimozione Supporti e Pulizia Rimuovi con cura tutti i supporti di stampa usando tronchesine e pinzette, prestando molta attenzione alle zampe meccaniche e ai dettagli più sottili. Pulisci eventuali sbavature o fili rimanenti con un bisturi da modellismo ( cutter ). 2. Carteggiatura (Levigatura) Passa la superficie del modello con carta vetrata per uniformare le linee di livello. Parti con una grana più grossa (es. 240 ) per le parti più ruvide e sali gradualmente (es. 400 -> 600 ) per levigare. Usare la carta leggermente bagnata ( carteggiatura ad acqua ) evita che la plastica si surriscaldi e si sciolga. 3. Stuccatura (Filling) Se rimangono fessure o linee visibili, applica dello stucco spray riempitivo (primer riempitivo per carrozzeria) oppure uno stucco acrilico monocomponente sui punti critici. Una volta asciutto, carteggia nuovamente con grana sottile ( 600 - 800 ) fino a rendere la superficie liscia al tatto. 4. Primo e Fondo (Primer) Applica 1 o 2 mani di Primer acrilico (in bomboletta o ad aerografo). Un primer grigio chiaro o nero è ideale: Primer Nero: Ottimo se vuoi dare profondità e usare colori metallizzati per le zampe e la tuta. Primer Grigio: Ottimo per una resa fedele di rossi e blu brillanti. Dopo questi passaggi, il tuo modello sarà perfetto, liscio e pronto per essere dipinto ad aerografo o a pennello!

Sie bestehen aus zwei Hauptkomponenten: einem Ei mit einem grimmigen Totenschädel-Motiv und einem kunstvoll verzierten Ständer. Modellmerkmale: Ei mit Totenschädel-Design: Das Ei ist das zentrale Element des Modells und zeigt einen bedrohlichen Totenschädel, der aus der Oberfläche zu brechen scheint. Die Struktur des Eies wirkt rissig und zerklüftet, was dem Modell eine antike, fast verfallene Optik verleiht. Die Augenhöhlen des Schädels sind tief und ausdrucksstark gestaltet, was dem Modell eine intensive, fast lebendige Präsenz verleiht. Verzierter Ständer: Der Ständer ist reich verziert mit Totenschädeln und organischen, verschlungenen Mustern, die an Wurzeln oder Tentakel erinnern. Diese Details verleihen dem Modell eine gotische und leicht unheimliche Ästhetik. Die Basis ist stabil und kunstvoll gearbeitet, um das Ei sicher zu halten und gleichzeitig optisch zu unterstützen. Farbgebung und Material: Das erste Bild zeigt ein farbig gedrucktes Modell mit kontrastreichen Farben: ein schwarzes Kapuzenmotiv umgibt den weißen Schädel mit leuchtend roten Augen, während der Ständer in einem giftigen Grün gehalten ist. Das zweite Bild zeigt eine monochrome Version in Steinoptik, die durch Licht und Schatten eine dramatische Wirkung erzielt. Druckqualität und Details: Die Modelle sind hochauflösend gedruckt, was sich in der feinen Ausarbeitung der Schädelzähne, der Risse im Ei und der filigranen Muster am Ständer zeigt. Die Texturen sind realistisch und verleihen dem Modell eine beeindruckende Tiefe und Komplexität. Einsatzmöglichkeiten: Diese 3D-gedruckten Modelle eignen sich hervorragend als dekorative Sammlerstücke, für Fantasy- oder Horror-Themen, als besondere Geschenkobjekte oder als Eyecatcher in einer Vitrine. Sie zeigen die Möglichkeiten moderner 3D-Drucktechnologie, komplexe und künstlerisch anspruchsvolle Designs in physische Objekte umzusetzen.

description: Always there when you need it. Never in the way when you don't. Like other filament clip giants before me, I decided to throw my hat into the ring. Meet The Wingman . Every spool deserves one. The Wingman securely parks your filament when it's not in use, then quietly stays out of the way while you print. No snags. No rubbing. No surprises. Just a simple clip that's there when you need it and invisible when you don't. (On a side note, if you need something to cut PTFE tubes that's precise, safe, and seriously satisfying, you won't want to miss out on my Bowden Puck Pro !) Why Yet Another Filament Clip? Because I kept trying the "good" ones and finding little things that annoyed me. Some snagged filament. Some didn't stay attached very well. Some required threading way more filament than seemed necessary. Some were so aggressively optimized to save filament that they forgot they actually needed to print successfully. None of these were deal breakers, but together they convinced me to make my own. So I did. Why The Wingman? Curves in all the right places Some clips have sharp edges, straight walls, or little ridges that can catch filament as it moves around the spool. The Wingman was designed with smooth, rounded surfaces wherever filament might encounter it, because nobody wants a multi-hour print to fail because of a 1-cent piece of plastic. Secure enough to forget about Some clips rely on a single spool hole. Others barely fit. The Wingman uses two mounting points and confidently snaps into place with a satisfying click, staying exactly where you put it. Quick filament parking Some clips are designed to capture a long length of filament before they're satisfied. Why? The Wingman only needs a very short section of filament for a secure hold, making loading and unloading quick and painless. Optimized for actual printing Some designs appear to be competing in a least amount of filament contest. Unfortunately, saving 0.05 grams doesn't help much if the part fails halfway through printing. The Wingman was designed to print reliably first. Once that was achieved, material was trimmed away until only what was needed remained. Features Works with the AMS Lite (with or without top mount), AMS HT, AMS, and AMS 2 Pro Secure dual-pin design snaps firmly into place No pliers, tools, or colorful language required Designed to remain attached during printing and drying Specifically optimized for Bambu spools Gently angled filament path for a secure hold and easy insertion Integrated guide line helps with filament insertion while adding a subtle finishing touch Only 0.56g per clip Important Notes Bambu Studio may report open edges. This warning can safely be ignored and does not affect printing or functionality. Print with a filament intended for functional parts. PLA Matte and other brittle materials may not survive repeated use. To remove a clip, simply push the pegs back through the spool holes using any small object. Depending on filament shrinkage, the filament opening may initially fit tightly. If needed, run a short piece of filament through the opening a few times before use. This is most noticeable with abrasive filaments such as PLA Glow. If using a filament dryer, print The Wingman using a material capable of handling the temperatures you intend to use. Instructions Print as many Wingmen as your spools deserve, keeping the supplied orientation unchanged for best results. Align the pegs with the spool holes and push until they snap securely into place. Feel strangely satisfied. Let the guide line do the aiming, then push the filament into place. Consider adding a second Wingman to the same spool. Future You will appreciate it. The best Wingman knows when to stay out of the way. description: One print. Twelve failure checks. Every card tells you what to inspect, what the answer means, and the three settings to change next. Now fits the A1 mini. Most calibration prints tell you that something is wrong. Print Doctor tells you what it means and what to do next — the diagnosis is printed right on the part, so you never have to go looking it up. ⚠️ Bambu Studio users: set Wall generator to Arachne. Quality → Wall generator → Arachne . Bambu's stock profiles use "classic", which can only lay a bead where a shape is at least one full extrusion wide (0.42 mm on a 0.4 nozzle). The horizontal strokes in the lettering are thinner than that, so classic drops them and the labels print as disconnected dashes. Arachne fixes it completely. OrcaSlicer already defaults to Arachne. The bundled print profile has it preset. What's new in v2 It fits your printer now. v1 was 204 × 180 mm, which meant A1 mini owners could not print it at all. v2 ships in three layouts: one full 239 × 179 mm sheet for 256 × 256 plates, plus Sheet A and Sheet B at 139 × 158 mm each, which fit a 180 × 180 plate with room to spare. Twelve tests, not ten. Three new cards: Overhang angle — four fins leaning at a labelled 30°, 45°, 55° and 65° off vertical. Find the first one whose underside breaks up: that is your printer's real overhang limit, and the number you should put in your support threshold. Clearance & fit — three print-in-place rings around capped posts at 0.15, 0.25 and 0.35 mm radial clearance. Try to spin each one. The tightest ring that still turns is the clearance you can trust in your own designs. Dimensions — a 18.00 mm square tube and a Ø14.00 mm round tube, both with a two-line wall. Measure the outside, the inside and the wall thickness with calipers to separate a flow error from an XY-compensation error. It adapts to your nozzle. Every gap, rib, wall and slot is derived from your nozzle diameter, so the tests still discriminate on a 0.6 mm or 0.2 mm nozzle instead of being tuned only for 0.4 mm. Better as a keepsake. Every card carries its number and a 4.5 mm hole, so once you snap the sheet apart the twelve cards go straight onto a binder ring and live next to the printer as a flip-through reference deck. The breakaway tabs are thinner than v1's and snap cleanly instead of tearing. Sharper geometry. The Z-seam cup is now genuinely round. In v1 it was a 48-sided polygon, and those facet lines could be mistaken for the seam artifacts the card is supposed to reveal. The cat-shaped Print Doctor nameplate, the mushroom cooling test and the elephant-foot paw all survive the rebuild. The twelve tests # Card What you do What it tells you 01 Under-extrusion Look for gaps in the single-line frame and three ribs Flow, clog, or temperature too low 02 Over-extrusion Find the smallest labelled slot still open How much excess flow is closing your gaps 03 Pressure advance Look at the ten hard corners Bulging after turns, thinning before them 04 Stringing Count the strands between four spires Retraction, temperature, wet filament 05 Weak bridging Feel the underside of the 10, 18 and 26 mm spans Longest span your cooling can hold 06 Overhang angle Find the first fin that breaks up Your real overhang limit in degrees 07 Poor cooling Look at the droop on three mushroom caps Whether the layer below is setting in time 08 Z-seam quality Look down the seam line of a smooth cup Zits, gaps, inconsistent layer starts 09 Elephant foot Look at the base flare of the paw First-layer squish and Z offset 10 Layer adhesion Bend the 0.80, 1.20 and 1.60 mm blades Whether layers split or the plastic yields 11 Clearance & fit Spin the three rings The tightest clearance you can design to 12 Dimensions Measure with calipers Flow error vs XY-compensation error The paw on card 09 prints directly on the build plate through a window in the card, so the first layer is never hidden by a card floor underneath it. Which file do I print? Your printer Print this Bambu A1 / P1S / P1P / X1C, Prusa MK4, Ender 3 (220+) print_doctor_v2_full.stl — one sheet, all 12 cards Bambu A1 mini, or any 180 × 180 plate print_doctor_v2_mini_A_cards_1-6.stl then ..._mini_B_cards_7-12.stl How to use it Slice with the profile you actually want to diagnose — not a specially tuned calibration profile. The point is to test what you print with every day. Supports off . The unsupported features are the test. Brim off if you can. A brim hides elephant foot. Print flat, exactly as supplied. Work through the cards. Each raised LOOK / FEEL / COUNT / BEND / SPIN / MEASURE line tells you what to do with that specimen. Use the three printed adjustments as your shortlist. Change one setting at a time and reprint just the card you are chasing. Snap the sheet apart, put the twelve cards on a binder ring, keep them by the printer. The printed suggestions are starting points, not laws. Material condition, hardware wear, motion settings and slicer behaviour can all produce similar-looking symptoms. Recommended print settings Material: PLA for the first diagnostic print Nozzle: 0.4 mm (the model is parametric if you run something else) Layer height: 0.20 mm — this matters, the print-in-place rings on card 11 are designed around a 0.2 mm air gap Walls: 2 Infill: 15 % Supports: Off Brim: Off where possible Orientation: Flat, as supplied Model dimensions File Footprint Max height Full sheet 239.0 × 178.7 mm 21.4 mm Mini Sheet A 138.9 × 158.2 mm 21.4 mm Mini Sheet B 138.9 × 158.2 mm 19.2 mm One connected, manifold print in every case, with optional breakaway cards. The three rings on card 11 print loose by design — that is the test. Parametric The OpenSCAD source is included and is set up for the MakerWorld Parametric Model Maker. Adjustable: sheet layout, nozzle diameter, layer height, label style (raised or flush inlay), part split for multi-colour, breakaway tab thickness, and the binder-ring hole.

model_name: Poo Chute & Dumpster For All A Series
description: *** Update *** Upon request, I have made it so you are now able to print this Poop Chute and Dumpster for the A1 and A1 Mini printers. I added a new Clip to the existing Chute. You now just need to select the correct plate that matches your printer and you on your way. I also added a wider version of the dumpster so it pushes out the dumpster walls so they do not hit the extruder head assembly. You can choose which ever you like best. If you pick the appropriate chute and clip the extruder should be clear. There is the original chute which is longer but I got a few comments stating that the chute will hit the dumpster, which it would if you placed the dumpster walls under the chute, I would suggest not to do this. It would be like placing your cup of coffee under the extruder assembly or print bar, you wouldn't do that right? So funny story. I love printing things. Therefore I have a lot of plastic waste from poop to supports etc…. A while ago my husband says “your going to need a dumpster for all that plastic”. Then my neighbor noticed the several bags of plastic “poop” I have and said the exact thing. And only when my nephew comes over and says the same thing once again I thought to myself, I need to make a little dumpster to catch all the poop my printer makes. I pictured the Home Alone 2 movie where the house Kevin rigs up has a chute outside the window going into a dumpster. So that's where the idea for project came from. There are tons of “poop” bins and baskets for the other printers but I wanted to make one for my new Bambu Lab A2L printer. She's a beast. Very detailed and prints well. I love it. It does shake the house though being a large sized bed slinger. I have been printing on silent mode to calm it down in most cases. This took me a week to create. A little longer than usual but I needed to get the tolerances perfect. My main goal was to make it reliable and easy to print. That was the challenge. I tried several ways to get the chute to print as one piece but it never worked out. So clip or bracket that connects to the printer is separate and has to be glued to the chute. I did make a connection socket so the two fit together perfectly so all is needed is a drop of cyanoacrylate glue (Super Glue) or something similar on each edge of the connection opening and hold it in place for the appropriate time (depending on your glue). I have printed 19 sets of the chute and bracket and glued them together successfully with no problem. Supports were absolutely necessary to accomplish my goal. I tried to keep the settings simple but tweaked the settings like the top and bottom Z distance, speed etc… to get dumpster and chute to come out clean. Just be sure to keep my settings. You can add to them if you please but it wont be necessary as you can tell by my photos. I have had several people that don't have a printer me to print them one just because they wanted the cute little bin. I have even been changing the sizes per their requests. The dumpster itself is scalable and you can make a smaller or larger one depending on your needs. I am sure it will have many uses. Thank you ahead of time and please enjoy. Have a nice day.

TPU Direct Guide for AMS Printing TPU through long PTFE paths can increase friction and make flexible filaments more difficult to feed consistently. This simple guide creates a much straighter filament path from the spool to the printer, helping TPU feed more smoothly while keeping the AMS lid completely closed. The guide simply clips onto the AMS and uses a short piece of standard 1.75 mm filament as the rotating axle. Once assembled, the roller spins freely, reducing drag and allowing the filament to move with minimal resistance. Features: -Designed specifically for TPU printing -Straighter filament path -Smooth rotating guide -AMS lid closes normally -Quick snap-on installation -No screws or hardware required -Compatible with any 1.75 mm filament used as the axle -Printable in PLA, PETG, ABS, ASA or any rigid material Assembly: Print all parts. Insert a short piece of 1.75 mm filament through the roller. Trim or melt the ends slightly to lock everything in place. Clip the guide onto the AMS. Load your TPU spool and start printing. The assembly takes less than a minute. If you regularly print flexible materials, this small accessory can noticeably improve filament feeding while keeping the setup clean and compact.

model_name: True Spring Filament Clip ⧸ Tangle Free Storage
description: A filament clip that solves the three most common problems of traditional filament clips. Plastic Fatigue Most filament clips rely on a printed flex geometry to generate clamping force. Repeated use and elevated drying temperatures gradually reduce the clamping force as the plastic permanently deforms. True Spring Solution The clamping force is generated by a real steel compression spring. The printed parts only guide the movement. No Plastic Fatigue. Constant tension. Filament Stress Many filament clips bend the filament sharply by securing it through spool holes or around the spool rim. Brittle materials may break after long term storage. True Spring Solution The filament is secured close to the spool core with a large bending radius, minimizing unnecessary stress while keeping the filament securely retained. Tangle Risk Some clips secure the filament directly to the wound filament. This can increase the risk of accidental tangles when the spool is handled carelessly. True Spring Solution The filament is retained independently of the wound filament. Nothing is attached to the filament winding itself. Hardware The clip uses two inexpensive compression springs. You can either use a compatible spring from the BOM or simply try the spring from an old ballpoint pen. Many common pen springs fit perfectly. No screws. No glue. No tools. Everything simply snaps together. Printer Tolerance Test Every printer and every filament behaves slightly differently. Since this model relies on precisely fitting moving parts, I strongly recommend printing the Printer Tolerance Test first. The test consists of one plunger and six labeled test sockets with clearances of 0.05 mm , 0.10 mm , 0.15 mm , 0.20 mm , 0.25 mm and 0.30 mm . The correct fit should move smoothly with minimal friction while having as little play as possible. Don't feel like running the calibration? Simply print Print Plate 1 (0.15 mm clearance) . It provides a good fit for most printers and materials. Temperature Testing Successfully tested after 24 hours of continuous filament drying: PETG - 45 °C ASA - 65 °C ASA - 80 °C PC - 85 °C For comparison, I tested a popular Flexi Filament Clip under identical print settings, using the same material and identical drying conditions. After 24 hours at the respective drying temperatures, the flex geometry had permanently deformed and the remaining clamping force was no longer sufficient for reliable reuse. If you have ever dried filament while using this type of clip, you probably know exactly what I mean. Recommended Materials PETG works perfectly for everyday use. For frequent filament drying or elevated temperatures I recommend ASA or PC . Assembly Printed parts and two compression springs. Insert the filament clamps. Insert the springs. Insert the Double Plunger and press firmly. Finished, enjoy.

description: Purge Pipes - Modular Purge Chute System Purge Pipes is a modular, twist-lock pipe system designed to route purge waste exactly where you want it. Whether you're directing waste into a bin, around obstacles, or building a more complex routing system, Purge Pipes makes it easy to create a clean, customizable setup. Compatible with: Bambu Lab X1 Series Bambu Lab P1 Series Bambu Lab X2 Series Bambu Lab P2 Series Bambu Lab H2 Series Features Modular twist-lock connection system Secure, tool-free assembly Expandable with additional pipe sections and fittings Reverse-twist components available for easier installation Designed specifically for routing printer purge waste Print Material Recommendations Purge Pipes can be printed in PLA for most applications. However, if you frequently print with a heated chamber , or regularly print materials such as PETG, ABS, ASA, or other high-temperature filaments , printing Purge Pipes in PETG or ABS is recommended for improved heat resistance and long-term durability. Installation The purge chute mounts to the printer using two BT3×10 screws (preferred). These provide a secure attachment point for the entire Purge Pipes system. Reverse-Twist Parts Standard sections lock together with a simple twist. For installations that include a Y fitting , one branch should use a reverse-twist connector. Why? If both the purge chute and the Y fitting are already fixed in place, a standard connector cannot be rotated into both ends simultaneously. A reverse-twist section solves this by allowing the final connection to lock without needing either end to move. This makes assembly much easier and keeps the entire system fully modular. Build Your Own System Mix and match straight sections, elbows, Y fittings, reverse-twist sections, and future accessories to create a purge routing system that fits your workspace. Whether you're simply extending the chute into a nearby container or building a more elaborate routing network, Purge Pipes is designed to grow with your setup. Happy printing! model_name: P2S X2D - BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier ArUco Marker
description: Successful detection. Every time. No compromises. This model is part of my ongoing BIQU Build Plate Accessories collection. Each model is conceived, printed, and endurance-tested on my own machines, refined through dozens of iterations to match the printer’s true mechanical behavior. Precision isn't assumed here, it’s verified layer by layer. Explore the full collection: BIQU Build Plate Accessories Follow me if you like my work, that kind of appreciation really dries my filament. Likes and boosts feed the Maker World algorithm and keep the new models coming v2 (Dev) Notes During my testing with the newer BIQU FrostBite build plates without the honeycomb handle, I made some interesting observations about the X2D's ArUco detection. The marker was reliably detected between 5 mm and 14 mm in size. Positioning along the Y axis had virtually no influence, as long as the marker remained between the printer door and the printable area. Along the X axis, the center of the marker could be placed anywhere between approximately 35 mm and 135 mm from the left edge of the build plate. These findings differ from my early experiments when the X2D was first released. Back then, the marker seemed to require very precise positioning. Based on my current testing, the detection system appears to be significantly more tolerant than it used to be. Testing on the Glacier plates with the honeycomb handle revealed something different. The honeycomb pattern can interfere with reliable detection, especially when using smaller markers. Based on these findings, I redesigned the marker for v2 (dev). It now uses a 35 % larger ArUco marker and is positioned to provide a cleaner visual background for the camera while remaining well inside the measured detection range. If you're experiencing detection issues, I'd really appreciate it if you could try v2 (dev) and let me know whether it improves reliability on your printer. Back To The Model Tested Compatibility, Fitting And Detection Checked Blue BIQU Panda CryoGrip Pro Glacier Build Plate for Bambu X2D/X1/P1/P2/A1 (256mm*256mm) Purple, Green, Pink, Yellow and Blue BIQU Panda CryoGrip Pro Build Plate for Bambu Lab X1C/P1S/A1 (256mm*256mm) Mechanically Incompatible (No Honeycomp Handle) Matte Orange and Blue BIQU Panda CryoGrip Pro FrostBite Build Plate for Bambu X2D/X1/P1/P2/A1 (256mm*256mm) The BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier is an outstanding build plate for ASA, but there is one annoying drawback: the printer cannot reliably detect it, and the supplied adhesive ArUco stickers are, frankly, a joke. This model puts an end to that. Two print profiles. “Smooth PEI Plate / High Temp Plate” as suggested by BIQU. “Cool Plate Super Tack” as requested by the community. Developed specifically for the BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier on the Bambu Lab P2S and X2D, it provides a precisely aligned ArUco marker that delivers reliable build plate recognition every time. The integrated clips engage directly with the plate's honeycomb pattern, ensuring perfect alignment and a secure mechanical fit. For additional retention, a small strip of 3M 9080 LED tape can be applied underneath the mount. The design has been tested in both PETG and ASA. For science, I even printed the ArUco marker itself in PLA and used it on an ASA print with a chamber temperature of 65 °C. Surprisingly, it held up for several weeks. PETG is an excellent long term choice, while ASA is the ultimate install it once and forget about it solution. No more failed recognition. No more crooked stickers. Just perfect alignment and reliable detection, every single time.

description: Successful detection. Every time. No compromises. This version is designed exclusively for the Bambu Lab P2S and X2D. This model is part of my ongoing BIQU Build Plate Accessories collection. Each model is conceived, printed, and endurance-tested on my own machines, refined through dozens of iterations to match the printer’s true mechanical behavior. Precision isn't assumed here, it’s verified layer by layer. Explore the full collection: BIQU Build Plate Accessories Follow me if you like my work, that kind of appreciation really dries my filament. Likes and boosts feed the Maker World algorithm and keep the new models coming Tested Compatibility, Fitting And Detection Checked Blue BIQU CryoGrip Pro Glacier Build Plate for Bambu X2D/X1/P1/P2/A1 (256mm*256mm) Matte Orange BIQU CryoGrip Pro FrostBite Build Plate for Bambu X2D/X1/P1/P2/A1 (256mm*256mm) Should Work But Unable To Check Myself Because I Don't Have the Build Plates Blue BIQU CryoGrip Pro FrostBite Build Plate for Bambu X2D/X1/P1/P2/A1 (256mm*256mm) Purple, Green, Pink, Yellow and Blue BIQU CryoGrip Pro Build Plate for Bambu Lab X1C/P1S/A1 (256mm*256mm) BIQU SSS Super Spring Steel Build Plate for Bambu A1/P1/X1 (257mm*257mm) BIQU Designer Series Dual-textured Build Plate for Bambu X2D/X1/P1/A1 (256mm*256mm) BIQU Double-sided (PEI/PEO/PET) Build Plate for Bambu X2D/X1C/P1S/P1P/A1 (257mm*257mm) Remarkably Forgiving During my testing with the newer BIQU FrostBite build plates without the honeycomb handle, I made some interesting observations about the X2D's ArUco detection. The marker was reliably detected between 5 mm and 14 mm in size. Positioning along the Y axis had virtually no influence, as long as the marker remained between the printer door and the printable area. Along the X axis, the center of the marker could be placed anywhere between approximately 35 mm and 135 mm from the left edge of the build plate. These findings differ from my early experiments when the X2D was first released. Back then, the marker seemed to require very precise positioning. Based on my current testing, the detection system appears to be significantly more tolerant than it used to be. Just slap the marker in the general direction of the original code and you are fine. The Model The BIQU build plates are excellent, but there is one frustrating drawback. Some ship without an ArUco marker, others include the wrong code, and some come with stickers that simply do not work reliably. This model puts an end to that. Developed specifically for the BIQU build plates, with or without the honeycomb handle, on the Bambu Lab P2S and X2D, this magnetic marker provides precise alignment and reliable build plate recognition every time. The marker is held securely in place by seven 5 × 1 mm magnets (see BOM). The design has been tested in both PETG and ASA. PETG is an excellent long term choice, while ASA is the ultimate install it once and forget about it solution. Transparency Notice Some of the BIQU build plates used for testing were provided by BIQU free of charge. No payment was received, and BIQU had no influence over the design, testing, measurements, or the content of this model page. All opinions and test results are entirely my own.

description: DISCLAIMERS This is a fairly invasive modification. It requires drilling eight 3 mm holes into the acrylic top cover and replacing two of the factory screws on the side of the machine with longer ones. If you are not comfortable making these modifications, I recommend not attempting this. I do not take responsibility for any damage that occurs during the installation or use of this model. If I encounter any issues myself or someone reports any, I will try to release an updated version with a fix or, if that is not possible, I will remove the model to prevent further problems. Please watch the video to see the installation process and the finished result. Somebody will most likely come up with a more elegant or more secure solution in the future. I simply wanted to give this idea a try. I do not recommend printing these parts in PLA or PETG. In the video I used PLA only because I was prototyping. I later replaced every part with PA612-CF. A rigid, temperature-resistant filament is highly recommended. You will need several M3 screws in different lengths. The design is fairly forgiving in some areas, so multiple lengths can work. Below I have listed the sizes I used, along with alternative recommendations based on my testing. I also recommend keeping the parts in their supplied/uploaded print orientation for printing. They were arranged specifically to maximize strength by avoiding weak layer line orientations. All of the strength settings have been tested my be. I do not recommend reducing the amount of walls, top/bottom layers or infill percentage. Increasing is fine. Different infill pattern should also be fine. The model consists of: A - 2 hinge assemblies (2 parts each) B - 2 backplates C - 2 side reinforcements D - 1 middle reinforcement Only minimal supports are required. The holes are intentionally designed with very tight tolerances. In most cases you will need to use the screws themselves to thread the holes slightly during assembly. This is intentional to eliminate unnecessary play. If your printer struggles with dimensional accuracy, you can carefully open the holes up using a 3 mm drill bit. Step 1 Assemble the hinges. Refer to the photos for the correct orientation. The two hinge halves fit together tightly. Each hinge requires: 1 × M3x40 mm screw 1 × M3 nut The screw direction does not matter as long as it passes completely through the hinge and is secured with the nut. Step 2 Remove the factory screws from the toolhead communication assembly. Insert the assembled hinges by pushing the locating pins into the holes where the factory screws were removed. Make sure the pins are fully seated. You may need to twist or wiggle the hinge slightly while pushing it into place. If the pins are excessively tight, lightly sand or shave them until they fit. Secure each hinge with a screw, but do not fully tighten them yet. On my printer, an M3x40 mm screw was almost a perfect fit if you want it to sit flush from the inside (see the video, XXXX timestamp). I personally used M3x45 mm screws and secured them with a nut on the inside. Step 3 Place the top cover back on the printer and make sure it sits straight, flush, and pushed as far toward the hinges as possible. Flip the hinges upward so they sit flush against the cover. Install the mirrored side reinforcements onto the hinges. Each reinforcement only fits on one side. With the reinforcements installed, you can rotate the hinges slightly left or right to fine-tune their position. If the hinges move too freely, lightly tighten the screws from Step 2. The goal is for the side reinforcements to sit perfectly flush against the walls and corners of the top cover. Repeat on the opposite side. Once you are satisfied with the alignment, use the eight mounting holes in the hinges to mark the drilling locations on the acrylic cover. Take your time during this step. This is the point of no return. Up until now, every modification has been completely reversible. After marking, use the square backplate (B, Pictured below) to confirm markings are aligned properly. Huge thanks to @UncleJessy for testing and this tip! Step 4 Remove the top cover and place it on your work surface. Using a 3 mm drill bit, drill all eight marked holes. Make sure your drill is sharp and drill very slowly to avoid cracking the cover. After drilling, remove all burrs and debris. Step 5 Install the screws into the backplates. Top holes: M3x20 mm Bottom holes: M3x10 mm for flush fit. Longer screws will work but reduce the opening angle. The 12 mm screws will protrude slightly and slightly reduce the maximum opening angle of the lid. If you want the cover to open a little farther, use M3x10 mm screws instead. Longer screws can also be used if you prefer a smaller opening angle. There is some room for personal preference here. Insert the screws through the acrylic from the inside until the backplate sits completely flush against the inside wall of the cover. Repeat for the opposite side. Step 6 Remove the hinge assemblies from the printer (see Step 2). Slide the hinges onto the screws protruding from the backplates. Because of the tight tolerances, you may need to rotate each screw gradually with a screwdriver instead of simply pushing the hinge into place. Step 7 Secure the lower four screws (two per hinge) with nuts. Install both side reinforcements, then place the middle reinforcement across the top. Secure the remaining four screws with nuts and tighten everything firmly. Step 8 Flip the hinges outward and reinstall the entire assembly onto the printer. Guide the two locating pins back into the holes from Step 2. Having a second person helping makes this step much easier. Once both pins are fully seated, close the cover and reinstall the side screws from Step 2. Tighten everything completely. Installation is now complete. A few things to keep in mind When closing the cover, you may occasionally need to wiggle it slightly so the two locating pins slide back into the frame correctly. If everything was aligned properly during Step 3, the cover should sit just as flush as it did before the modification. Do not slam the cover open or closed. Do not place objects on the open cover in the opened state. I have no idea how durable the acrylic will be over time. It is not particularly thick, and additional weight or force could cause it to crack. I also do not recommend leaving the cover open on the hinges for extended periods. Open it only when needed. Think carefully before deciding whether this modification is right for you. Finally, I cannot guarantee that every current or future Creator 5 will be manufactured identically. Small design changes may occur without notice, so fitment could vary between machines.
