model_name: BC250 Case MKUU+ (FSP, Apevia, Metalfish PSU)
description: This is a remixed model originally created by the very talented morph91 . Original model link: https://makerworld.com/en/models/2749412-bc-250-gaming-pc-case-mk-ultra-uno . I'm naming this model the MK Ultra Uno Plus : ) Case Highlights: Can be printed in only 3 plates with less than 600g of filament Tool-less design (no screws required) Fits the FSP500-30AS, Apevia ITX flex, and Metalfish flex PSUs Customizable front plates Ability to fit 40 & 50 mm fans on rear Internal clips to attach both halves of case together securely & internal psu lock to securely hold psu in place without external latch Heatsink mod (stick on heatsinks) to help improve thermals Important Considerations: There are two different versions of the fan shroud. One is the exact same as the original, the other is a modified version that allows active airflow to flow to stick on heatsinks that I personally made for my build. You can reference the assembly instructions for photos. Please make sure you only print the plate relevant for your build! Both the apevia and metalfish variants of the back case contain one less internal clip/latch due to space constraints. So these variants may be slightly less rigid when the two case halves are put together The internal psu lock was created specfically for the FSP500-30AS variant. Unfortunately, it will not fit the apevia or metalfish variants. If someone prints either version, I'm more than happy to create a working psu lock for these versions. I just need accurate measurements and someone to test any prototypes. If you're interested then leave a comment/DM me : ) Why not dual fan version? Check this out: https://www.reddit.com/r/BC250Gaming/comments/1uog9wo/bc250_single_vs_dual_fan_with_arctic_p12_pro_vs/ If anyone ends up printing the apevia or metalfish variants, please let me know if anything needs to be adjusted (besides the internal psu lock)! I used morph91 's measurements for the metalfish variant and also lolheyaj 's measurements for the apevia variant, since I do not personally own either of those psus. Also, as a temporary solution for the internal psu lock issue - you could probably use glue to keep the psu secure in the case as a temporary measure. Expected Thermals: Thermals may vary slightly, given differences in thermal paste and depending whether you use the stick on heatsinks like I did. Also depending on 24CU vs 40CU, fan curves, overclock, undervolts, etc. For reference here's my configuration: GPU: 40CU 2000MHz @940mV (+16CU and +500 MHz from stock) CPU: 3800MHz @1060mV (+300MHz from stock) And here are some max temps from a couple games @1080p: Furmark 1080p, 40CUs at stock 1500MHz and 725mV undervolt only hits a max temp of 68C after a couple minutes of running. With no undervolt, I hit 76C. My Part List: BC250 PSU (fsp500-30as, apevia itx flex, or metalfish flex) https://a.co/d/0gOMs9rW black petg https://a.co/d/04eTZ6sm for the two brown pla's from this bundle for my fake wood texture front panels makerworld.com/en/models/2527214-bc-250-scooper fin scooper to straighten fins https://a.co/d/0hZ28ifs for 12mm latching button (you may need a wire stripper, wire crimper, and dupont connectors if you copy me 1:1) https://a.co/d/0jdT5jNV arctic p12 pro pst (has great static pressure for a 120mm fan, with a high airflow max) https://a.co/d/0iLAR7Ty arctic mx-4 thermal paste (ptm7950 is recommended over normal paste, you'd probably see a couple degrees cooler temps with it. I just happened to have some of this on hand) (optional) https://a.co/d/063cMg66 noctua NF-A4x20 (optional) https://a.co/d/038s6cPO stick on heatsink (120x120x20mm) (optional) https://a.co/d/066uYDJ8 rubber anti vibration screws used to mount noctua 40mm fan. You can just use the screws that come with the fan instead, but I just happened to have some of these already Print Instructions: Print the main case components in PETG, and dry filament for 8 hours before printing (reduces stringing). You can print in other filaments, but make sure the glass transition temperature is 80C or higher! PLA is not recommended. Also, make sure to print only one of the fan shroud plates. For more information read the important considerations at the top. If you want to make your front panel have the fake wood texture like mine, then use this as a modifier: https://makerworld.com/en/models/1492898-wood-grain-modifier-add-wood-grain-to-any-models?from=search#profileId-1560821 . You can print both the front panels in PLA. I recommend using a 0.2mm nozzle if you're doing the wood texture like I did. If you are downloading the model to modify or use with a different slicer (and not bambu studio), then make sure to paint a straight line seam on the bottom part of back half of the case. This helps reduce VFAs: Assembly Instructions: Take off the IO shield and the small bracket next to cmos battery Use the fin scooper to straighten the fins underneath where the fan shroud is gonna go. After straightening the fins, use an air duster to make sure any debris is blown off. Also if you haven't already, repaste the chip! Attach fan (recommend arctic p12 pro pst) with pins to fan shroud. Then attach fan shroud to pcb. Make sure the two small latches are pushed as far up as possible (in pic below you can see the one latch is in the corner of the pcb). Optionally here, if you have the stick on heatsinks (120x40x20mm), you can stick them right next to the fan slit. Doing this mod helped my ingame temps by 3-7C. VERY IMPORTANT NOTE: If you do not have/don't plan to use stick on heatsinks print the plate with the original fan shroud instead! Put PSU into back half of case: Add psu lock on left side (currently only compatible for fsp500-30as - currently looking for measurements to make metalfish and apevia versions!): Mount any 40mm fans now (both screws or rubber mounts work): Slide bc250 on alu backplate onto the back half of case. Plug in exhaust fan to the Y splitter of main fan. Plug in the 8 pin power cable: (optional) Place any lower custom front panels on now before you install your 12mm button (This step is for FSP500-30AS psu, idk what pins to short for apevia/metalfish psus but you can probably find out on reddit or the bc250 discord) Plug in latching button to PS_ON and GND. I crimped the wires into two male dupont connectors and put them in a 2pin housing. I slightly have to bend the metal pins to fit into the psu which creates enough friction where the pins don't fall out. There's probably a better solution for this… (I'm currently working on an atx style clip that'll slot in my dupont conector right into it) Attach front half of case, and slide until both halves attach together. Enjoy!

model_name: Ultimate Exhaust Muffler System For X2D/P2S*
description: INTRODUCTION: This is my incredibly over-engineered take on an exhaust fan muffler for anyone tired of the constant buzz from the rear fan on the X2D or P2S. Most designs are a trade-off between airflow and noise reduction. But I decided that wasn't good enough for me. I needed to reduce exhaust fan noise by more than 10 decibels while preserving a large amount of airflow . Now, 4 days later, I've devised a system that can do it in style. FEATURES: 18 dB noise reduction. Interference fit assembly, no glue required! Easy to install and remove ; refer to GIF. Engine-inspired design. Decorative supports that also serve as effective air-cooling fins during high-temperature exhaust. Single-baffle muffler, reducing noise while preserving airflow . Screenshot from OnShape Included. Exhaust pipe can be placed under or to the left depending on personal preference. PRINTING/ASSEMBLY: Layer height: 0.16 mm recommended due to overhangs Infill: 15% Gyroid Material: No restrictions. My example is printed in PLA Basic, and I expect no issues. Changing the orientation of the Exhaust Pipe while slicing WILL CAUSE A FAILURE. It must remain vertical during printing due to the muffler's internal structure. Press the Exhaust Pipe into the slots on the Air Deflector while pushing an Exhaust Clip into the groove on the Exhaust Pipe, then pinch the Exhaust Clip to ensure that it has been fully seated. Lastly, install the Deflector Backplate. Post-processing will be required; make sure to use a sharp craft blade, like an X-Acto knife , while removing supports due to tight tolerances. If the Exhaust Pipe is not fitting in the slots on the Air Deflector, check for remaining supports; even one layer prevents assembly. Ensure that your machine is well calibrated before printing due to complex overhangs and tight tolerances . Also clean the build plate before printing the Exhaust Pipe due to a risk of it shifting during the print . TEST RESULTS I ran multiple tests to prove the design's functionality. Measuring at the exhaust exit, an uncovered exhaust fan can produce 80 decibels ; after installing the muffler, exhaust noise was lowered to 62 decibels. From 7 ft away, uncovered is 57, and muffled is 49. At most, this produces an 18 decibel reduction. It might not sound like much, but try it for yourself. I guarantee it's night and day. I also ran a flow test to see how quickly the fan alone could cool the chamber from 45 to 35 degrees Celsius. Without the muffler, this process took 9 minutes and 16 seconds. With the muffler, it took 9 minutes and 38 seconds. This isn't a direct airflow measurement, but it provides a practical comparison of cooling performance. If you have ideas for additional tests, I'd love to hear them in the comments

Spool Weight has a 2nd Inner cap so you dont have to worry about your weights falling out when moving to new spools ✔ Easy to print and install. Why I Made It I designed this system because my cardboard spools were constantly falling off the AMS rollers , especially as they became lighter. After dealing with countless failed prints, I decided to create a solution that keeps every spool where it belongs and improves feeding reliability. The Full kit includes: 2× Outer Spool Guides 2× Center Spool Guides 4× Refillable Spool Weight Whether you're printing with cardboard spools, plastic spools, or almost-empty rolls , the AMS Reliability Kit helps your AMS feed filament more consistently and lets you finish every last gram of filament with confidence. Assembly Instructions Outer Spool Guides The thin, flat section of each Outer Spool Guide slides between the inner black AMS tray and the outer transparent shell. The guides are intentionally not designed to fit rigidly. This prevents unnecessary pressure that could damage or warp the AMS tray or outer shell. A small amount of movement is normal. Inner Spool Guides The Inner Spool Guides have cutouts along the bottom that pressure-fit over the original short dividers built into the AMS tray. Press each guide down only far enough to hold it securely. Do not press the guides all the way down against the spool rollers. Contact with the rollers may prevent them from rotating properly. After installation, spin the rollers by hand to confirm that they move freely. Spool Weight Fill the Spool Weight Body with a suitable dense material. I recommend using 9 mm steel ball bearings , such as these ball bearings on Amazon . Other options include: Steel nuts, washers, or small sockets Fishing weights Other compact metal objects Do not use batteries , as damaged or aging batteries can leak, corrode, or create a safety hazard. Once the body is filled, thread in the Spool Weight Seal to secure the weights inside. Do not overfill the body, the seal must seat completely into the threads. You can confirm that the seal is fully seated by installing the Spool Cap . If the cap does not sit completely against the body, remove some weight and reinstall the seal. Once the seal is installed, the outer cap can be easily removed whenever you need to transfer the weight to another spool without the weights falling out. Funnel Saver In the .3MF File I have included the “AMS 2 Pro Funnel Saver Guides” from YelTrik Designs Refer to this Model for intructions and use case. They have complemented my AMS Reliabilty Setup well. Feedback and Modification Requests Have an idea for an improvement or need a modified version? Feel free to leave a comment with any requests, questions, or concerns about the AMS Reliability Kit !

model_name: Snapmaker U1 + Sunlu Filadryer S4 Feeder Adapter
description: Humidity, my worst enemy… Snapmaker sent me the U1, and unfortunately, I'm not able to get good prints with printers that have open-air spools (because of the humidity at my location). So I looked for the best way to deal with it, and none of the projects I found were good enough. The closest one used a Sunlu Filadryer S4, so that was my baseline to start this project: Snapmaker u1 + Sunlu Fliladryer S4 Setup Compact setup Air-tight (at least as much as the original S4) It has the feeders as close as possible to the spools → Easier loading and unloading This is a DIY project, so you will need some tools and materials: M3 x 6 Screws, 4 of them with nuts and washers 2 x PTFE connectors. The ones that allow the 4 mm PTFE tube to pass through Drills (3.5 mm for the screws, and one for the size of your PTFE connectors) Extra PTFE tubes (4 mm OD, 2.5 mm ID) to replace the ones that go from the original feeder location to the back of the printer. Feeder extension cable. This might be the trickiest. They can be found as GH1.25 or JST GH1.25. Be sure they are 15-pin and male-female configuration. The length depends on your setup; measure both sides from the feeder's original location to the back of the Sunlu S4. I recommend 50 cm. I'll leave some links in the comments. I don't have measurements of the process, because I did it on the go and wasn't planning to upload it anywhere. But I have some pictures taken from the video I recorded: Depending on your setup, you would want to place the S4 on the right or the left of the U1. Therefore, you need to install the feeders on the side of the S4 that faces the back (as shown in the pictures above). You need to measure the distance between the feeder inputs, and drill the holes in the S4 to install the PTFE connectors. Then, assemble the feeders in the printed holder, and place it with the holes aligned to the filament input. Mark the Holder holes, and drill the 3.5 mm holes for the screw assembly. Assemble it, place the numbers from the inside, and then the funnels (optional, but recommended) Then, place the U1 and S4 in the final position, measure, cut, and install the PTFE tubes from the printer to the feeder. Don't make them too short or they might bend; leave some extra for them to wiggle around with smooth curves. That's about it. As I said, I made it on the go, so I'm not sure if I'm forgetting something 😂

description: The YAPR™ (pronounced "YAP-er") — Yet Another Purge Receptacle Featuring BinLock™ push-button locking technology Not being completely satisfied with the first purge bin I ever printed, I set out to design (overengineer?) my own after getting the A2L. I wanted a purge bin that looked like it belonged on the printer , stayed exactly where I put it, and came off with a simple button press—without magnets, awkward removal angles, or extra hardware. I was tired of: Awkwardly angling or shifting the purge bin to remove it every time I emptied it (and sometimes spilling purge in the process) Constantly nudging the bin back against the printer because it would slowly vibrate away after a print or two Small pieces of purged filament finding their way between the bin and the printer Liners that frequently broke or cracked and needed to be reprinted The YAPR is a push-button A2L purge (or poop!) bin that locks securely in place, prints mostly in place, and requires no magnets or extra hardware . Designed to be the last purge bin you'll ever need to print. Features Easily attaches and detaches using exclusive BinLock™ push-button technology—no bin gymnastics required Securely locks in place and won't slowly vibrate away from the printer Matching side contour helps prevent stray filament from falling between the bin and the printer Contoured to match the printer's lines for a clean, OEM-inspired appearance Prints mostly in place with only a small amount of support beneath the button Available in three sizes: Slim (100mm wide — best for tight spaces), Standard (125mm wide — the daily driver), and Wide (150mm wide — ideal for heavy AMS printing and lower maintenance) Optional liner fully protects the bottom of the bin (unlike many liners with fully cut-out patterns) while also helping reduce purge rattling Won't block your printer's ventilation ports Angled bottom makes it easy to grab those last stubborn pieces of purge Assembly Notes This is specifically designed for the A2L only. For the easiest assembly, assemble within two hours of printing. The BinLock™ mechanism is intentionally designed with a tight initial fit and has a short break-in period. It will become noticeably smoother with use. If the button doesn't move smoothly after pressing it several times, grasp it with pliers and work it in and out a few times. The additional travel and force help speed up the break-in process. Instructions Choose your preferred size, print the bin , peg , and peg cover , then remove the small amount of support beneath the button. If using the optional liner, print the matching size in PETG (or PLA if you primarily print PETG). Press the BinLock™ button (located on the bottom right of the bin) several times to begin the break-in process (The first press requires a fair amount of force, so using two thumbs while bracing the bin against a countertop or table is recommended.) Hold the BinLock™ button down and rub a crayon over the small internal slide (see the second to last model photo for the exact location). While this may seem like an unusual step, it is important for smooth operation of the BinLock™ mechanism. The next few assembly steps are a little tricky—but thankfully, you only need to do them once. Turn the peg cover upside down with its tallest side facing you. Insert the peg upside down so the shortest side of the peg's triangular base faces to the right. The angle of the peg should *not* match the angle of the peg cover. Please see the last model photo for up close pictures. Without disturbing the peg, and with the longest side of the peg cover facing you , insert the peg and cover together into the bin until the cover snaps into place. Turning the bin upside down during this step usually makes assembly easier, and engaging the snap-fit may require a firm push. With the bin upright, press the BinLock™ button several more times. You should notice the peg moving slightly with each press as the mechanism continues to break in. If the button mechanism isn't working correctly, the peg may not be fully seated. Grip the peg firmly with pliers, pull it straight out with steady force (the peg and cover will come out together), then repeat the installation process. Connect to printer Hold the BinLock™ button. Slide the bin fully against the rear frame and side of the printer. Release the button to lock the bin in place. Disconnect from printer Hold the BinLock™ button. Pull the bin straight toward you. Print one. Lock it in. Forget about it.

description: X2D Auxiliary Fan Duct The Bambu Lab X2D auxiliary fans can direct a significant amount of cool air across the left and right edge of the build plate. For materials such as PLA, and particularly PETG, this concentrated airflow may contribute to uneven cooling, edge lifting, corner warping or reduced first-layer adhesion on some models. These deflectors redirect the auxiliary fan airflow upward and away from the print bed, helping prevent the fans from blowing directly across the edges of the print while still allowing air to circulate inside the chamber. Why I designed these I began experiencing prints lifting primarily along the edges closest to the auxiliary fans, which indicated that the concentrated airflow across the front of the build plate was contributing to uneven cooling. Although auxiliary-fan values can be adjusted within the filament and process profiles, the commanded settings do not always appear to remain in effect during printing. In some situations, the printer’s internal control logic applies its own auxiliary-fan behaviour and overrides the values defined in the slicer. This means the fan may continue operating at a higher speed than expected, even after the cooling profile has been adjusted. Because the underlying firmware-controlled behaviour is not currently exposed as a separate user-adjustable setting, it can be difficult to reliably prevent direct airflow from reaching the front edge of the print bed. These deflectors provide a mechanical solution by changing the direction of the airflow itself. Rather than attempting to reduce or disable the fan electronically, they redirect the output upward and away from the build surface while still allowing air to circulate within the chamber. Key features Redirects auxiliary fan airflow upward and away from the build plate Helps reduce concentrated cooling along the edges of the print area May help reduce edge lifting and corner warping Maintains airflow inside the printer rather than completely blocking the fans Installs without permanent modification to the printer Can be easily removed when not required Designed as separate left- and right-hand deflectors Compatibility These deflectors have currently only been tested on the Bambu Lab X2D. Should fit P2S right side Aux Fan They are designed specifically around the X2D auxiliary fan outlets and surrounding clearances. Compatibility with other Bambu Lab printers has not been confirmed. Installation Fit each deflector over its corresponding auxiliary fan outlet, ensuring it is fully seated and secure. The outlet should face upward and inward, redirecting the airflow away from the surface of the build plate. After installation: Check that both deflectors are securely fitted. Confirm that neither deflector contacts the build plate, toolhead or any moving component. Manually move the toolhead throughout the complete build area. Run the printer’s normal homing or movement checks before beginning a print. Do not begin printing until full toolhead and build-plate clearance has been confirmed. Print settings The included print profile is the profile I used successfully for these parts. Recommended starting settings: Layer height: 0.16 mm Walls/perimeters: 3 Supports: Not required Brim: Painted on edges only to prevent lifting Orientation: Print in the supplied orientation The parts should be allowed to cool before removal from the build plate to avoid distortion. Material PLA is suitable for testing and general use. PETG, ABS or ASA may provide improved temperature resistance for long-term use inside the enclosed printer, particularly when printing materials that require elevated chamber temperatures. Important notes These deflectors change the direction of the auxiliary fan airflow. They do not provide electronic control over fan speed. Cooling requirements vary depending on: Filament type Model geometry Print speed Chamber temperature Bed temperature Auxiliary fan speed These parts are intended as a practical airflow-management accessory, not as a guaranteed fix for every adhesion or warping issue. Bed cleanliness, first-layer calibration, filament condition and suitable temperature settings should still be checked.

description: This is a simple magnet fit tolerance test kit for common round magnets used in 3D printed projects. Instead of guessing the perfect hole size for your magnets, print the test strip that matches the magnets you have, press your magnets into the different holes, and choose the fit that works best for your printer, slicer settings, filament, and material. The kit includes separate test pieces for: 3×2 mm magnets 4×2 mm magnets 5×2 mm magnets 6×2 mm magnets 8×2 mm magnets 10×2 mm magnets Each size is a separate part, so you do not need to print the whole kit. Just print the strip for the magnet size you actually have. Each strip includes multiple hole diameters around the nominal magnet size, with the tolerance clearly labelled above each hole. For example, the 6×2 mm strip tests hole sizes from 5.95 mm to 6.25 mm. The magnet pockets are designed for 2 mm thick magnets. The back of each pocket is intentionally thin so the magnet can be pushed back out after testing. Why use this? Magnet fit can vary a lot depending on: Printer calibration Filament type Material shrinkage Nozzle size Slicer settings Hole compensation settings Whether you want a press fit, loose fit, or glue-in fit For best results, print the test strip in the same material you plan to use for your final project. For example, if your finished part will be PETG, print the test strip in PETG. If your final part will be ABS, print the test strip in ABS. PTFE Clips Helps prevent PTFE tubes from rubbing against the top glass These lightweight PTFE tube clips are designed to help keep the tubing from wearing on the upper glass panel on enclosed Bambu Lab printers. They have been tested on the Bambu Lab X2D and are designed for standard 4 mm PTFE tubing , so they may also fit other compatible Bambu Lab models. Why I designed them As the toolhead moves around the printer, the PTFE tubes naturally twist, bend and change position. Some tube-management solutions hold multiple tubes tightly together to create a neater appearance. While this may look tidy, it can also introduce unnecessary tension, stress or twisting into the tubing as the toolhead travels. These clips are designed to support each tube individually. This helps reduce wear on the PTFE tubes from the top glass while still allowing the tubes to move as designed. Key features Helps prevent PTFE wear from rubbing on the top glass Designed for standard 4 mm PTFE tubing Tested on the Bambu Lab X2D Allows each tube to move independently Applies only light tension to the tubing Lightweight and low profile Quick snap-on installation No tools or printer modifications required Small and fast to print How many should I use? I currently use four clips , which provides good support and separation. More clips can be installed if additional support is required, but avoid using so many that the tubing becomes stiff or restricted. Recommended print settings These were successfully printed using: Layer height: 0.16 mm Walls/perimeters: 3 Bed temperature: 60°C Part cooling fan: 0% for the first 2 - 3 layers, then a maximum of 25% Brim: Not required Supports: Not required Keeping the cooling fan low helps prevent these small parts from cooling too quickly, warping or lifting from the build plate. Material recommendations PLA is suitable for normal use where the heated chamber is not being used. For printers operating with a heated chamber, use a more temperature-resistant material such as: PETG ABS ASA Another suitable heat-resistant filament PLA may soften or deform when exposed to elevated chamber temperatures for extended periods. Installation Carefully snap each clip over a PTFE tube. Position the clips along the tubing where support is required. Move the toolhead through its full range of travel. Check that each tube can still bend and move freely. Reposition or remove clips if any tension or restriction is present. Important notes These clips are intended to gently guide the PTFE tubes, not lock them rigidly in place. After installation, confirm that: The tubes still move freely The clips do not contact the cable chain The tubing is not stretched, kinked or twisted The toolhead can reach the full build area The clips remain clear of all moving components Compatibility Tested on: Bambu Lab X2D Tube size: 4 mm PTFE Other models may be compatible but have not yet been tested Support the design

model_name: Tilted Low-Profile TPU Assistant Mount (X2D / P2S)
description: Staffa Compatta, Inclinata e Ribassata per TPU Assistant (Compatibile con Bambu Lab X2D / P2S) Ho progettato questa staffa per la mia X2D (essendo al 100% compatibile anche con il modello P2S ) con un obiettivo principale: migliorare radicalmente l'orientamento dei tasti del TPU Assistant per renderli finalmente visibili dal davanti, ottimizzare la direzione del tubo in PTFE verso l'AMS HT ed eliminare una volta per tutte la necessità di scollegare i tubetti durante l'uso quotidiano o l'essiccazione. Le caratteristiche principali di questo design: Gestione lineare del tubo (Nessun bisogno di scollegare nulla): Molti progetti online richiedono di scollegare il tubo in PTFE dall'AMS HT quando il TPU Assistant non è in uso, ad esempio per inserire il tappo di sigillo e avviare la funzione di essiccazione dell'Hub. Questo spesso comporta il dover riporre il tubetto rimosso per non perderlo. Con questa configurazione, grazie alla distanza ridotta e all'allineamento, non è mai necessario scollegare il tubo . Il condotto rimane stabilmente al suo posto e sigillato, semplificando i passaggi: basta spingere il filamento dall'AMS HT direttamente nel TPU Assistant e si è pronti a stampare. Inclinazione ed Ergonomia dei Tasti: La staffa è posizionata più in basso e inclina il TPU Assistant verso lo sguardo di chi si trova davanti alla stampante. In questo modo la pulsantiera e i LED di stato sono facilmente visibili e comodi da raggiungere direttamente dal fronte. Geometria del percorso posteriore e specifiche tubi: Essendo una staffa ribassata, la distanza geometrica verso l'ingresso della stampante aumenta leggermente rispetto alla configurazione standard, richiedendo un percorso totale fisso di 200 mm . Nota per la community: Bambu Lab raccomanda solitamente 160 mm, ma non c'è assolutamente da preoccuparsi per il caricamento . Il sistema del TPU Assistant è infatti progettato per funzionare ufficialmente anche sulla H2D , che è una stampante molto più grande della X2D e ha un percorso interno del filamento nativamente molto più lungo. Visto che il sistema gestisce quel tragitto maggiore senza problemi, i 4 cm esterni in più introdotti su questo setup vengono digeriti dall'estrusore in totale sicurezza. Per installare il sistema avete due opzioni precise: Setup Diretto: Vi servirà uno spezzone di tubo in PTFE tagliato esattamente a 200 mm . Con Adattatore 4-in-1: Se utilizzate un connettore 4-in-1 come il mio (lungo circa 6 cm), dovrete compensare la misura tagliando il tubetto in PTFE a 140 mm (140 mm + 60 mm = 200 mm). Design Essenziale: La struttura è pensata per essere il più compatta e leggera possibile, riducendo la quantità di filamento necessaria e i tempi di stampa. 🔄 IMPORTANTE: Calibrazione post-installazione Come raccomandato dalle linee guida ufficiali Bambu Lab, dopo aver installato la nuova staffa e posizionato il tubo da 200 mm (o 140 mm con adattatore), è fondamentale lanciare la calibrazione del modulo . Questa procedura serve a far leggere al sistema la nuova lunghezza del percorso, misurando l'attrito per calibrare al millesimo la forza della spinta automatica. 👉 Potete seguire la procedura ufficiale passo-passo a questo link della Wiki Bambu Lab: Guida alla Calibrazione del TPU Assistant . 🛠️ Note di Stampa e Tolleranze Materiale di Test: Il progetto è stato sviluppato, stampato e testato in PETG . Nota sulle tolleranze: L'asola di incastro per il TPU Assistant è calibrata in modo preciso sul PETG. Se decidete di stamparlo in PLA o ABS/ASA, tenete conto che il diverso ritiro termico dei materiali potrebbe influire leggermente sulla tolleranza dell'incastro (potrebbe risultare impercettibilmente più stretto o largo). Per Inatallazione sono necessarie due viti ST 3x12 avanzate dal kit di assemblaggio del TPU Assistant Spero questa soluzione vi è utile!

description: Willkommen zur DryDisc! Da mich die bisherigen Lösungen auf dem Markt nicht überzeugt haben, habe ich diese schmale Trockenmittel-Rolle (21mm) für den Creality Space Pi x4(l) Filament-Trockner von Grund auf selbst designt. Das Ziel war eine unauffällige, extrem robuste und professionelle Lösung, die sich nahtlos zwischen breiteren Filamentrollen einfügt. Einmal installiert, bietet diese Rolle ein Leben lang puren Nutzen. Das Silica-Gel wird beim Trocknen des Filaments im Gerät automatisch mitgetrocknet. Features Ultra-Schmal (21 mm): Nimmt kaum Platz weg und passt problemlos zwischen Standard- und breite Filamentrollen. Optimiert für 2-5 mm Silica-Gel: Die Gitteröffnungen sind exakt so dimensioniert, dass Trockenmittel-Kügelchen in dieser Größe sicher in der Rolle bleiben und gleichzeitig maximal umströmt werden. Wartungsfrei & Robust: Einmal befüllen, ins Gerät stellen und vergessen. Saubere Optik: Alle Schrauben und Muttern sind leicht versenkt für ein professionelles Finish. Druck- & Materialempfehlung Wichtig zur Materialwahl: Beim trocknen mit 75°C , ist normales PETG hier weich geworden! Ich empfehle dringend den Druck in PET, ABS, ASA oder PC , um eine ausreichende Formstabilität bei dieser Hitze zu gewährleisten. Sollte mit weniger Temperatur getrocknet werden, kann PETG funktionieren. Nach dem Druck das Bauteil auf der Platte auskühlen lassen, um Spannungen zu vermeiden. (nicht heiß von der Platte lösen) Benötigte Hardware Pro Rolle werden benötigt: 13x M3 x 18 mm Schrauben 13x M3 Muttern Montage-Hinweise Das Design ist mit sehr engen Toleranzen für die M3-Muttern entworfen. Das ist pure Absicht: Die Muttern sitzen extrem stramm, damit sie bei der Montage nicht herausfallen. Muttern einpressen: Falls sich die Muttern schwer einsetzen lassen, nimm eine M3-Schraube zur Hilfe. Führe die Mutter durch leichtes Hin- und Herbewegen unter etwas Druck in die Aussparung ein. Achte dabei unbedingt darauf, dass das Gegenstück absolut lagerichtig aufgesetzt ist. Solte Silica beim Befüllen in die Schraubenlöcher fallen, diese mit einem dünnen Gegenstand von der anderen Seite wieder hochbefördern. Das Modell wurde mit PET CF auf einem Bambulab A1 gedruckt.

This test lays out 21 bridges on one plate — 3 print speeds (10 / 20 / 30 mm/s) across 7 bridge flow ratios (1.0–1.6) — so you can find the combination that gives flat, fully-fused strands with no sag. Uses only ~7 g of filament, so it's cheap to run as often as you calibrate your filaments. How to use: Print it, flip it over, and read the underside of each bridge. The cleanest, flattest strands mark your ideal bridge flow ratio for that speed. Set those values in your slicer and enjoy clean bridges. Printed on a Bambu Lab P1S. No supports, no brim needed. How to read the results: Flip the plate and look at the underside of each bridge: Best: strands are flat, straight, evenly spaced, and fully fused — no sag, no gaps. Too little flow / too fast: strands sag, droop, or break mid-span. Too much flow: strands bulge, blob, or fuse into a rough mass. Settings to modify in slicer Quality > Advanced > Bridge Flow Speed > Other Layers Speed > Bridge Feedback and comments are welcome, I have much to learn still! description: An honest, straightforward utility tool for Bambu Lab A1 series owners. This tool doesn't magically yank the tube out on its own, but it solves the main pain point: pressing down on the small black PTFE release collets near the extruder. Instead of digging your fingernails in or straining your fingers in a tight space, this tool lets you apply comfortable, even pressure across the entire collet ring. 🛠 How to Use & Troubleshooting Stuck Tubes Standard Removal: Place the tool over the black PTFE collet, press down firmly to disengage the collet teeth, and gently pull the PTFE tube out with your other hand. If the tube is stuck (Twist Technique): Don't just pull it straight up. Push the PTFE tube slightly downward , twist it , and then use the tool to depress the collet while pulling the tube out. For stubborn / heavily jammed tubes: Take a pair of needle-nose pliers and gently squeeze the PTFE tube from all sides right near its base (just above the fitting) to break friction and fix any deformation. Push the tube down and twist it again. Use this 3D-printed tool to hold the black collet down, and smoothly slide the tube out.

description: Print ABS, ASA or nylon on your X2D? Let's deal with that huge purge opening as a thermal leak . It allows heat to escape, messing with your chamber temperature, and also allows VOCs and odors to vent around your filter and into the air unfiltered. Please read print recommendations below I think I remember well I got inspired by P2S/X2D Sealed Poop Chute for Chamber Exhaust Kit by Idea Lab . But I needed something compatible with Exhaust Fan Hose Adapter for X2D by sbstn , couldn't find anything so designed it myself. The point is simple – make it airtight, easy to mount, and out of the way of the exhaust hose. Key Features: Keeps warm inside to prevent warping during prints of filaments sensitive to chamber temperature. Keeps VOCs and odor inside preventing leaks of it, at least through the poop exit (of a printer). Print recommendations: X2D with Bambu filament and auto calibration should print it without any supports. But enable if you don't really want to worry about it. Do not remove brim if you are not sure your print bed has insane adhesion. Print this chute with heat resistant filaments if you actulally plan to print with warm/hot chamber (e.g.during ASA prints): 1) erick974 said that this chute, if made of PLA, can deform when printing stuff made of ASA for example. 2) RaniDrama said made of PETG deformed and fell out during long ASA print. So if your chamber is actually getting hot, please print at least with PETG, but preferably with other materials with higher heat resistance.

description: PETG Supportless Perfect Overhang Print Profile This is a print profile setting designed for supportless PETG printing with perfect overhangs, tested on a propeller model. Key features include: 1. Outer/Inner Wall Speed Reduced to 50/60 mm/s Slower printing speeds prevent under-extrusion and stringing. 2. Disable Overhang Speed Slowdown Disable slowdown for overhangs above 45°. This prevents the nozzle from dwelling too long in one spot, which causes heat buildup and sagging. 3. Enable Prime Tower (Wipe Tower) Allows extra layer cooling time and reduces filament blobs/droppings on the model. 4. Lower Layer Height to 0.12 mm A lower layer height provides better support for steep overhang angles. 5. Increase Outer/Inner Wall Line Width to 0.6 mm Enhances the structural support and stability of inner and outer walls. 6. Increase Part Cooling Accelerates model cooling to avoid high-temperature sagging and deformation. 7. Open the Top Lid, Keep the Front Door Closed Keep the top glass lid open for heat dissipation, but close the front door to prevent model warping. 8.Disable precision wall to improve the support between inner and outer wall. If you experience sagging like in the image below, please improve overall printer ventilation, turn on the AC, or print at night. However, do NOT change the heatbed temperature to avoid warping. Tested on: Bambu Lab P1S

description: This is a dedicated mount that uses the A1 mini's Z-axis cover to attach the BMCU 370C to the right side of the printer. Most existing mounts position the BMCU behind the printer, feeding the PTFE tube from the rear toward the front. However, if your setup has limited rear clearance, this can create an excessively tight bend in the PTFE tube. To solve this problem, this mount routes the filament from the right side of the printer toward the left, allowing the PTFE tube to follow a smoother, more natural curve even in tight spaces. After testing several designs, I found that positioning the filament path at approximately a 45° angle while placing the BMCU slightly farther from the printer provided the best tube routing. The main model is based on this design. The Long 45° Version is the main model. Three additional optional versions are also included: Short 45° Version 30° Version Straight Version Feel free to choose the version you like best. Installation Notes Before installing this mount, remove the spacer secured to the printer's Z-axis cover with three screws. The original three screws are reused to secure this mount in place. No additional hardware is required.

description: 6" Modular Window Exhaust System Description This is the 6-inch version of my modular window exhaust system. The window pass-throughs are now fully stackable , allowing you to customize the layout to fit your application. For example, you can install: 4" pass-through on the bottom with one or more 6" pass-throughs above 6" pass-through on the bottom with additional 4" or 6" sections above This modular design allows you to configure the system for 3D printer exhaust, laser engravers, portable A/C units, or other ventilation needs while adapting to a wide range of window heights. ⚠️ Before You Get Started Parametric models can currently only be generated through the Bambu Handy app or MakerWorld. Bambu Studio does not currently support generating parametric models. If you generate and print directly from the Handy app, it will use your current default print profile , not the print settings recommended for this project. Before starting a print, verify that your default profile includes the appropriate settings for the selected part, including: Support generation (when required) Wall count Infill Layer height Any other project-specific settings For best results, either update your default print profile to match the recommended settings in this project or print through MakerWorld/Bambu Studio after generating the parametric model. ⚠️ Safety Information Do not operate a portable A/C and a 3D printer or laser exhaust through the same window opening unless the airflow is properly isolated. If both systems must share a window, install blast gates to prevent contaminated air, smoke, fumes, or odors from flowing back into the room. For maximum safety and performance, use separate windows whenever possible. This project is intended for venting air only. Always follow the manufacturer's safety recommendations for your printer, laser, and ventilation equipment. Compatible Accessories Links to additional accessories for the 4" system are provided below. Parametric Tubing Generator Magnet & Mounting System 4" Exhaust Pipe Y Splitter with Blast Gates AC Infinity 6" to 4" Reducer Magnet Mounting System Multiple magnet pocket sizes are included to compensate for manufacturing tolerances. Available pocket sizes: 10.00 mm 10.05 mm 10.10 mm A test print is included in the print profiles for checking magnet fit before printing the final parts. Magnet Options Primary: 10 × 6 mm magnets Alternative: Stack two 10 × 3 mm magnets The 10 × 6 mm magnets were selected to provide sufficient holding force so attachments remain securely connected during normal operation. Airflow Improvements & Laser Compatibility This redesign has been optimized for 4-inch and 6-inch ducting systems , including transfer fans such as AC Infinity units. Improvements ✔️ Fixed outlet replaced with a removable blast gate ✔️ Blast gate allows the system to be completely closed when not in use ✔️ Larger outlet opening with a gradual internal taper for improved airflow ✔️ Larger exterior screen ✔️ Reduced material usage on non-structural parts Only the bottom window mount is printed with increased wall count and infill to support the mounting hardware. All remaining components use reduced settings to minimize print time and filament usage without sacrificing functionality. Recommended Print Settings 4 wall loops 15–20% Gyroid infill Organic Tree Supports enabled 0.20 mm layer height Support Z-gap: 0.265 mm (recommended for easier support removal) Compatible Equipment With the airflow improvements, this version is suitable for: Bambu Lab H-Series printers equipped with laser modules xTool laser engravers Portable A/C systems using 6-inch intake and exhaust hoses in the same window assembly ⚠️ Important The original computer-fan version was designed only for standard 3D printer exhaust and is not suitable for laser applications due to its limited airflow. A link to the original version is provided if that better fits your needs. LINK Installation The system may be installed either vertically or horizontally , just like the original design. All components are now fully parametric , allowing dimensions to be customized as needed. Compatibility The new components are generally not compatible with the original design unless the overall widths are identical. The 6-inch components are not compatible with the previous design because the larger duct size required an increased overall width. Assembly Recommendations Print the window hole sections first , then perform a test fit in your window. After verifying the fit, determine how many filler sections are required. Included components: Transition pieces Filler sections Top cap Depending on your window height, you may only need a transition section and a top cap. ⚠️ Tight Fit by Design The dovetail joints are intentionally designed to fit tightly. This minimizes air, smoke, and odor leakage through the seams. If assembly or disassembly is difficult: Apply a light coat of lithium grease to the dovetails. Do not force the parts together, as excessive force may damage printed components. If a looser fit is preferred, the dovetail clearance can be adjusted directly in the parametric model before printing. model_name: Modular AMS Riser for H2 Series Printers
description: An open-frame, highly configurable AMS riser designed around standard 2020 aluminum extrusions. Built for flexibility, expansion, and minimal material waste without requiring complete reprints when modifying your setup. KEY FEATURES Configurable & Expandable: Utilizes 2020 aluminum extrusions to allow custom attachments and easy adjustments as your setup evolves. Open & Lightweight: Minimizes filament usage and print times while maintaining structural rigidity. Forgiving Tolerances: Main frame pieces are separated from the interlocking connectors. If tolerances differ due to filament or slicer settings, only small connector pieces need quick reprinting—saving time and material. Reversible Assembly: Friction-fit tapered draft joints hold the frame together snugly without glue, allowing full disassembly if needed. Preserves all original factory (OEM) functions of the top glass lid (removable with lid closed sensor actuator). HARDWARE REQUIREMENTS Main Riser: 4x Corner Frame Sections + 4x Interlocking Keys Secure Brackets: 4x Printer Cabinet Retainer Clips AMS Mounts: 8x AMS Corner Retainers (4x Left, 4x Right) Threaded Inserts: 4x M4 Heat Set Threaded Inserts Magnet: 1x Small Magnet (4mm diameter x 1.75mm thick) 2020 Aluminum Extrusions: 8x 2020 end caps 2x Frame Side Rails (Cut to 475mm minus the thickness of your end caps) 2x AMS Support Rails (Cut to 760mm) Fasteners & Hardware: M4x8mm Socket Head Cap Screws (SHCS) M4 2020 T-Nuts 2020 90-Degree Corner Brackets Compression Spring (for Lid Sensor Switch) Optional: 2020 End Caps ASSEMBLY GUIDE Step 1: Assemble the Riser Frame Install Threaded Inserts: Heat-set one M4 threaded insert into the provided hole on each of the four main riser pieces (refer to diagrams for placement). Join the Frame: Lay out the four main riser pieces upside down on a smooth, flat surface. Insert the interlocking keys and cabinet retainer devices. Note: The interlocking components feature a slight draft taper to draw the joints tight as they seat. Make sure they are oriented correctly before pressing them together. No adhesive is required. Step 2: Attach Side Extrusions Mount the two 475mm side extrusions to the left and right sides of the main riser frame using the M4x8mm SHCS and M4 T-nuts through the pre-drilled countersunk holes. Step 3: Install AMS Crossbar Extrusions Mount the two 760mm extrusions across the frame using 2020 90-degree corner brackets. Rear Rail: Align flush with the riser assembly and tighten securely. Front Rail: Install loosely for now—you will adjust its position when seating the AMS units. Step 4: Fit AMS Units and Corner Retainers Install the 8 AMS corner retainers onto the support rails (pay attention to Left vs. Right orientation): Secure the four outer corner retainers first, ensuring they are square to one another. Attach the four inner corner retainers loosely so they can slide. Place an AMS unit onto its outer retainers, lower it into the inner retainers, and adjust until the unit rests flat without rocking. Carefully lift the AMS unit straight up and tighten the inner retainers. Repeat for the second AMS unit, then fully tighten the front crossbar rail. Step 5: Mount to Printer Remove the glass lid from the printer and set the riser frame into the top cavity. Engage the four retainer brackets so their fingers grip under the printer cabinet rim for a secure fit. Step 6: Assemble Lid Sensor Switch Install Magnet: Glue a small magnet (4mm diameter x 1.75mm thick) into the cavity on the end of the pushbutton shaft (refer to diagram). Assemble Pushbutton: Drop the two-part pushbutton assembly into the front-left hole of the riser: Place the spring inside the outer barrel. Insert the pushbutton stem, ensuring it glides smoothly. (If making a custom spring, wrap spring wire around an appropriate diameter mandrel until you achieve desired tension and bounce). Step 7: Final Set Up Reinstall the top glass lid onto the newly installed riser assembly, place your AMS units into the corner retainers, and run your lines.

description: Flow Rate Calibration Cube | Micrometer Dieser einwandige, oben offene Kalibrierungswürfel dient zur präzisen Einstellung der Flussrate beziehungsweise des Flow Ratio eines Filaments. Die tatsächliche Wandstärke wird an mehreren Stellen mit einer Bügelmessschraube oder einem präzisen Mikrometer gemessen. Aus dem Mittelwert aller Messungen lässt sich anschließend der korrigierte Flussratenwert für das verwendete Filamentprofil berechnen. Der Würfel benötigt nur wenig Material, ist schnell gedruckt und eignet sich ideal zur Feinabstimmung neuer oder bereits vorhandener Filamentprofile. Benötigte Hilfsmittel Bügelmessschraube oder präzises Mikrometer Bambu Studio oder ein kompatibler Slicer Das zu kalibrierende Filament Aktueller Flussratenwert des Filamentprofils Eingestellte Linienbreite der Außenwand Durchführung 1. Würfel drucken Drucke den Würfel mit genau dem Filamentprofil, das kalibriert werden soll. Verändere für den anschließenden Kontrolltest möglichst keine anderen Einstellungen wie Temperatur, Geschwindigkeit oder Linienbreite. Lasse das Modell nach dem Druck vollständig abkühlen. 2. Wandstärke messen Miss jede der vier Würfelseiten an mehreren Stellen: mindestens 3 Messungen pro Seite empfohlen sind 5 Messungen pro Seite bei 5 Messungen pro Seite entstehen insgesamt 20 Messwerte Miss möglichst mittig auf den geraden Wandflächen. Vermeide dabei: die Ecken des Würfels die Z-Naht den oberen Rand die ersten Schichten sichtbar unregelmäßige Stellen Verwende bei jeder Messung einen gleichmäßigen und möglichst geringen Messdruck. Mittelwert berechnen Addiere alle gemessenen Wandstärken und teile die Summe durch die Anzahl der Messungen: Mittelwert = Summe aller Messwerte ÷ Anzahl der Messwerte Je mehr saubere Messungen verwendet werden, desto zuverlässiger ist das Ergebnis. Zielwert bestimmen Der Zielwert entspricht der in Bambu Studio eingestellten Linienbreite der Außenwand . Du findest den Wert unter: Qualität → Breite der Linien → Außenwand Beispiel: Außenwand-Linienbreite: 0,42 mm Wichtig: Verwende als Zielwert nicht automatisch den Düsendurchmesser, sondern immer die tatsächlich eingestellte Linienbreite der Außenwand. Aktuellen Flussratenwert ermitteln Öffne das verwendete Filamentprofil und notiere den dort eingestellten aktuellen Wert für die: Flussrate / Flow Ratio Beispiel: Bisheriger Flow Ratio: 0,988 Neuen Flow Ratio berechnen Verwende folgende Formel: Neuer Flow Ratio = Zielwert × bisheriger Flow Ratio ÷ gemessener Mittelwert Beispielrechnung Zielwert: 0,42 mm Bisheriger Flow Ratio: 0,988 Gemessener Mittelwert: 0,421 mm Rechnung: 0,42 × 0,988 ÷ 0,421 = 0,985653 Gerundet ergibt sich ein neuer Flow Ratio von: 0,986 Trage den neuen Wert anschließend in das Filamentprofil ein. Drucke den Würfel danach erneut und kontrolliere die Wandstärke mit einer weiteren Messung. Falls erforderlich, kann die Berechnung wiederholt werden. Excel-Formel Die Berechnung kann auch direkt in Excel oder einer anderen Tabellenkalkulation durchgeführt werden: =Zielwert*Bisheriger_Wert/Mittelwert Beispiel mit Zellbezügen: =I13*I6/D6 Dabei steht: I13 für den bisherigen Flow-Ratio-Wert I6 für den Zielwert D6 für den Mittelwert aller Messungen Ergebnis interpretieren Gemessene Wand ist dicker als der Zielwert: Der Flow Ratio wird reduziert. Gemessene Wand ist dünner als der Zielwert: Der Flow Ratio wird erhöht. Mittelwert entspricht dem Zielwert: Die Flussrate ist bereits passend eingestellt. Hinweise Die Kalibrierung sollte für jedes Filamentprofil separat durchgeführt werden. Hersteller, Material, Farbe, Drucktemperatur und weitere Einstellungen können das Ergebnis beeinflussen. Dieser Würfel dient ausschließlich zur Kalibrierung der Flussrate beziehungsweise des Flow Ratio . Er ist nicht für die Einstellung von Flow Dynamics, Pressure Advance oder K-Wert vorgesehen. Für reproduzierbare Ergebnisse sollten alle Messungen mit derselben Bügelmessschraube und mit möglichst gleichmäßigem Messdruck durchgeführt werden. Druckprofil Einwandiger, oben offener Kalibrierungswürfel Keine Stützstrukturen erforderlich Geringer Materialverbrauch Kurze Druckzeit Ideal für wiederholte Kontrollmessungen Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch können abhängig von Drucker, Filament und verwendeten Einstellungen abweichen.

description: Update: For those who are having a tough time printing this in ASA, you can print it in ABS, which could be just as challenging but in my experience requires less prep work than ASA. If printed in ABS, drying temps should be limited to 70-75c. Another option is prinintg this in PETG, but drying temps should be limited to 60-65c with longer drying times. Another option may be using HT PLA (may not handle the load in hot environments ) or HT PLA Plus (promises better load performance under heat) from Polymaker. I have not tested these HT PLA filaments so I cannot provide any other guidance. Hello! I’m excited to introduce my desiccant drying system specifically designed for the Creality Space Pi x4 filament dryer. I dedicated a lot of time and effort to developing this model, going through numerous iterations until I reached this version. After experimenting with a model I found in MakerWorld and encountering several issues, I decided to create my own. My goal was to design a strong, modular system that ensures unobstructed airflow. I also wanted something at incorporated a pour spout without taking up a lot of space or using a lot of filament. This filament drying system is stackable, robust, and easy to use. It’s large enough to accommodate two boxes and a frame on each side of the Space Pi x4. It measures 1500mm by 150mm by 60mm, features 2mm holes and a pour spout in one of the corners. Each box can hold a maximum of 500 grams of desiccant, but I recommend not exceeding 300 grams to expedite drying times and prevent overloading the frame. I successfully dried approximately 400 grams (200 grams per side) of wet desiccant in about 6 hours at 85 degrees Celsius, which is significantly faster compared to other solutions. Please note that to achieve the optimal drying temperature of 85 degrees Celsius, I highly recommend printing this model in ASA filament. I’ve shared my personal settings in the profile I published, which is in ASA. For faster prints, I used a .6mm nozzle, but if you prioritize quality, you can print it with a .4mm nozzle. Make sure to adjust the print settings accordingly. Turn off all cooling, lower the volumetric flow to 12 cubic millimeters per second, heat up the chamber to 65 degrees Celsius, and heat the build plate to 100 degrees Celsius. If you don’t have a heated chamber, heat soak it for at least 30 minutes before printing to minimize the risk of warping. Additionally, ensure that you use a textured PEI plate or an engineering plate. Wash it with soap and warm water, and apply a glue stick. ASA emits toxic fumes so use air filters and a proper mask when printing with ASA. Your health is too important to risk it! description: Top right side spool holder with PFTE tube connection for P1S/P2S/X2D. My setup consists of a single P1S with an AMS2 pro. I was tired of how, when I was drying filament in my AMS I couldn't easily print. (I know there is a side mount and I could change some PFTE tubes on the back, and maybe also add a PFTE tube splitter - but that is not easy fix…) I found some top side mounts, which worked fine for me. However, I noticed that the sudden movements of the tool head could cause a big pull in the filament, which could cause it to unroll a bit. The sudden pulls are also not ideal when printing in TPU. So I designed a version where you can connect a PFTE tube from the tool head to the spool holder. This eliminates any sudden pulls in the filament (I know it might give more resistance in the PFTE tube when printing in TPU). It has worked flawless when I want to print in PLA and PETG when my AMS is busy drying other filament. See attached video. Instructions Cut a piece of PFTE tube at 35 cm (or more conveniently, the width of the opening in the top after removing the glass plate). 2. Add one end of the PFTE tube to the holder from underneath. 3. Push the PFTE tube through the holder until it is flush with the surface 4. Attach the holder to the right side by pushing it down from the left side. It should be place roughly in the middle. 6. Push the holder down for a more secure fit 7. Take off the front of the tool head and take out the existing PFTE tube 8. Insert the PFTE tube from the holder 9. Put the front cover of the tool head back ín place 10. Put on a roll of filament on the holder and Insert it into the PFTE tube . Push the filament all the way though the PFTE tube until it can't go any further . On your printer or from the software, load the filament from the external spool and you are now ready to print :-)

description: ## Bumblebee Security Camera Housing – Tapo TC71 Compatible Bring the ultimate Autobot protector to your desk or shelf! This custom-designed, Bumblebee-inspired security camera housing is built specifically to fit the **Tapo TC71** camera. ### The Story Behind the Model This is my **first-ever 3D model**! After seeing an inspiring video online, I decided to take on the challenge. I used AI to generate the initial concept image, converted it into a 3D model, and then heavily modified and engineered the design from scratch to make sure it fits the Tapo TC71 perfectly. I poured a lot of energy, time, and hours of trial and error into this project. As a beginner, I learned so much along the way (and used quite a bit of filament to get it just right!). I would be incredibly happy to hear your feedback, advice, or suggestions—good or bad—to help me improve for my next designs! --- ### Key Features * **Perfect Fit:** Tailored specifically for the Tapo TC71 camera. * **Super Stable Base:** Designed with a heavy, massive torso and legs to ensure your camera stands rock-solid on your desk without tipping over. * **Lightweight Helmet:** The helmet section is optimized to be light and perfectly sized so it doesn't strain the camera rotation. * **Two Versions Included:** Choose between the **Pin-Joint Assembly** version or the **Fixed** version. --- ### Print Settings & Assembly Tips My test models (shown in the photos) were successfully printed with the following setups: * **Yellow Version:** Printed on a **Bambu Lab A1** using the **0.24mm Draft** profile. * **Gold Version:** Printed on a **Bambu X2D** using a **Standard Layout / Settings**. To save you some headaches, here are my highly recommended tips based on my test prints: * **The Golden Rule for the First Layer:** I highly recommend starting your print at **50% speed** until the first layer is perfectly laid down and has solid bed adhesion. Once the ground is good, you can safely bump the speed back up. * **A Warning on Multi-Color Printing (AMS/AMS Lite):** I strongly advise **against** printing this model in multiple colors directly from the slicer. I tested printing just a single leg in 2 colors, and the filament waste (purge) was equivalent to the weight of an entire extra leg! It is much more efficient and cost-effective to print it in a single color and post-process/paint it afterward (which is exactly what I did with my painted version!). * **If you choose the Pin-Joint Version:** * Scale the legs up by **1mm or 1.5mm on the X, Y, and Z axes** in your slicer. * Give the pins a quick, light sanding before assembly. This will make them fit smoothly. If they go in too tight, you risk breaking the pins when trying to disassemble them. * **If you want a hassle-free print (Fixed Version):** * Print the **Fixed version**. It takes a little longer to print, but you won't need to scale anything or worry about joint tolerances. Everything is pre-sized and ready to go! --- ### Feedback is Welcome! Since I am just starting my 3D design journey, please feel free to leave a comment, post your makes, or give me a Boost if you like my work! Your support and advice mean the world to me.

And install the new rear panel before you can install the External Exhaust Fan upgrade. Instructions installing the rear panel are here . This model is divided into 3 parts: the Base Module, Fan Module, and Output Stage (Hose Adapter/Fan Grille). This partitioning allows easy modification of any component without needing to reprint the other components. For example, the Hose Adapter can be easily replaced to support different hose sizes. Let me know in the comments the Inner Diameter (ID) of the particular hose that you need. Assembly Base Assembly The first step is to assemble the Fan Vent Base. The two types of clips (as shown in Figure 1) are inserted into the Fan Vent Base (Low Profile Fan Vent P2S V4.stl) in the positions indicated in Figure 2. Figure 1: Low Profile Fan Vent Clips Be sure to orientate all the clips to point in the same direction, as indicated by the green arrow in Figure 2. Then insert the BT2x5 self-tapping screws, provided with the Bambu kit, from the opposite side (see the green arrows in Figure 12) and secure the Clips with the screws. Figure 2: Base Clip Attachment Finally apply the pre-cut black Foam Tape provided with the Bambu Kit to the Base. Confirm the correct position before pasting to avoid errors. Ensure the foam is aligned with the edge, and paste the four strips of top foam one by one as shown in Figure 2. If you have an X2D and can't peel the tape of the factory fan cover, search for "1mm foam tape" on Amazon, they offer many options. If available, insert the External Exhaust Air Filter as shown below. Fan Module The next step is to assemble the Fan Module. Latches Each Latch consists of two parts: Body and Latch. First install the Latch Body part (Figure 3) on the fan Module connector, then insert two BT2x5 self-tapping screws as indicated by the green arrows and tighten them on the both sides to attach it to the Latch Body. Note: The screws act as shafts. Do not over-tighten them, otherwise the Latch will not work smoothly. Figure 3: Latch Body Installation Next install the Latch Latch part (Figure 4) on the fan Module connector, then insert two BT2x5 self-tapping screws as indicated by the green arrows and tighten them on the both sides to attach it to the Latch Body. Figure 4: Latch Body Installation Now use the same process to attach the Latch components on the opposite of the Fan Module for the Base, and on the top and bottom of the Fan Module for the Hose Adapter, as shown in Figure 5. Figure 5: Hose Adapter Latches Fan Installation Before continuing remove any leftover support material from around the inside of the Connector Holes (Figure 6) and the ‘top’ inside surface of the PCB case (as indicated by the blue arrow in Figure 6). And ensure that PCB connectors fit through the holes, and the PCB fits snugly against the top surface of the PCB case. Route the fan cable through the Fan Cable Hole as shown in Figure 6 and Figure 8. Figure 6: PCB Case Then press the fan into the Fan Module with the orientation shown in Figure 7, while pulling on the fan cable. Note that the gasket that wraps around the fan is facing out. Also the airflow direction arrow on the side of the fan must be facing out as well. The surface of the fan should be flush with the surface of the fan module. Figure 7: Fan Orientation PCB Installation Connect the Fan Cable to the PCB then fit the connectors into the connector holes (Figure 6) and rotate the PCB so that it flat against the bottom of the PCB case. Finally use a BT2x5 self-tapping screw to secure the PCB to the Fan Module. Only one screw is necessary, because the left side of the PCB is held in place by its connectors. Figure 8: PCB Installation Now press the PCB Cover into the PCB Case. Make sure that the Connector Baffles (as shown in Figure 9) are over the connectors. Also make sure that there is no left over support material in the slots that the cover will clip into, otherwise it will not seat tightly. Only print the Plate associated with the option that you choose! For all 3 options, you will need to press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Hose Adapter Module so that it seats as show in Figure 10a. Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Hose Adapter. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 10a: Hose Adapter Fan Grill Similar to the Hose Adapter (Figure 10a), press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Fan Grille so that it seats as show in Figure 10b. Note: There may be some elephant foot around the outside edge of the gasket, scrape it if necessary to allow the gasket to be pressed into the Fan Grille. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 10b: Fan Grille Right Angle Hose Adapters Similar to the Hose Adapter (Figure 10a), press the Hose Adapter Gasket into the Right Angle Hose Adapter so that it seats as show in Figure 10a. Also, one end of the gasket is chamfered on both edges. The chamfered edges should be facing out when inserted. The Gasket is printed with the chamfered edges facing up. Figure 10b: 3.75inch and 75mm Right Angle Hose Adapters The Right Angle Hose Adapters can be attached with the hose facing up, down, forward, or backwards. Figure 10c - Installed Right Angle Hose 75mm Adapter, facing up The Low Profile Fan Vent P2S X2D Rt Angle Hose Adapters Vx.3MF file includes two versions of the 3.75 inch and 75mm adapters: One with normal Tree supports and the other using tree supports and PETG as an interface layer. Tired of ironing that comes out blobby, dragged, or just plain ugly? So was I. Most ironing calibration tests wastes filament printing giant plates covered in embossed numbers you only need to read once. This one lets you skip that entirely and just read the image in the documentation. Each square on the plate is set to a different combination of ironing flow percentage and ironing line spacing . Print it, find the square with the cleanest top surface, and plug those exact values into your slicer. Done. What's included: Ironing Test (No Numbers) .3mf — the clean version. How to use it: Print either .3mf (the no-numbers version if you want to save material). Find the square with the smoothest, cleanest top surface for your filament and printer. Match that square to the mapping image to get its ironing flow % and line-spacing values. Drop those values into your slicer's ironing settings — and enjoy ironing that just works, every time. Notes: Saved from Bambu Lab Studio as .3mf, but the settings transfer to any slicer with ironing controls (Orca, etc.). No supports needed. description: Hello everyone! I'm excited to present my first collaboration model. description: This is a fully custom window‑mounted vent system I designed for my Bambu H2C printer. My goals were simple: Airtight Secure Permanent installation Fast magnetic connection/disconnection of the exhaust hose Weatherproof cover for when the printer isn’t running I wasn’t satisfied with the existing MakerWorld options, and my window is only 521 mm wide , so I built something specifically for my setup — but I’m sharing the Fusion file, STEP file, and laser‑cut gasket files so you can adapt it to your own window if it’s similar. This design is meant for small windows, but the parametric model makes it possible to adjust dimensions if your window differs. Features 🔒 Airtight & Secure The duct and window frame use 2 mm EVA foam gaskets , recessed 1 mm into the mating surfaces for a tight seal. With magnets pulling the duct into place, the connection feels solid and leak‑free. 🧲 Magnetic Quick‑Connect The system uses 10 mm × 2 mm neodymium round magnets : 10 magnets in the window frame 10 magnets in the duct Optional: 10 magnets in the weather cover This lets you instantly attach the exhaust hose when printing, and swap it for the weather cover when not. 🌧️ Weatherproof Cover The optional cover seals the opening when the duct is removed. I printed mine in PETG, but any outdoor‑friendly filament works. 🪟 Permanent Window Fixture The window frame stays installed permanently. The two halves connect with a tight dovetail joint . I intentionally used small tolerances for a high‑quality feel — sanding the edges slightly helps if the fit is too snug. 🧰 Customizable CAD Files Included: Fusion 360 file with editable parameters STEP file for use in any CAD program .lac laser file for cutting EVA gaskets Printable gasket groove outlines if cutting by hand If your window is wider than ~520 mm, you may need to split the extension piece — Bambu Studio makes this easy with built in tools. 🧪 Material Recommendations ASA‑CF (my choice): weather‑resistant, rigid, great for outdoor use PETG : perfectly fine for most users Any other weather resistant material that has some temperature resistance (ABS, PET-CF, etc.) Parts & Materials Printed Parts Window Frame (2 pieces, dovetail connection) Duct Outside Vent Weather Cover (optional) Gasket inserts (optional if cutting by hand) Hardware 30 ea. - 10 mm × 2 mm neodymium magnets EVA foam sheets , minimum 9" × 12" , 2 mm thick Glue for gaskets (contact cement or similar adhesive works best, super glue not recommended as it's likely too rigid) Tools Bambu H2C laser module (optional, could cut gaskets by hand) Sandpaper (for dovetail tuning) Utility knife if cutting gaskets manually Assembly Notes Ensure magnet polarity is consistent across all parts. Install magnets on the duct and optional weather cover are opposite polarity of magents in the window frame so they attract and don't oppose. Test-fit the dovetail before final installation — light sanding may be needed. Laser Cutting Notes (H2C 10W) For 2 mm EVA foam gaskets, these settings work extremely well: Power: 35% Speed: 6 Air assistant: On Pass: 1 Cut Offset: 0.00 This produces crisp edges with minimal melt. Who This Is For This design is not universal — it was built specifically for my window dimensions and style. But if your window is similar, or you’re comfortable modifying CAD files, this can get you most of the way to a perfect custom vent. If your window is very different, you may still find the duct, magnet system, and gasket approach useful as a starting point. Feel free to download my files as a starting point for your project. IMPORTANT: Before committing to a full print, I strongly recommend slicing off a small test segment of the window frame to verify the fit in your window. In your slicer, cut a short 3–5 inch section from the model (left‑to‑right, as it sits in the frame) and print that first. This quick test ensures the final part will fit properly before you invest time and material into the full print. Included Files Fusion 360 file (with parameters) STEP file STL files for all parts .lac laser file for EVA gaskets Printable gasket outlines Assembly instructions (text) Final Thoughts This vent has been rock‑solid for me — airtight, secure, and incredibly convenient. I can leave the window fixture installed permanently, snap the duct on magnetically whenever I print, and seal it with the weather cover when I’m done. If you adapt it to your own window, I’d love to see your remix.

description: This modified top-mount AMS 2 Pro flipper moves the AMS 55mm further forward, allowing it to raise fully when the H2D is positioned close to a wall. It was designed for setups such as mine where there is not much clearance behind the printer (about 85mm in my case from the wall to the back of the printer), where the original flipper would cause the AMS lid to hit the wall before it could be raised enough. You will need the Original H2 AMS Flipper long arms for this: https://makerworld.com/en/models/1815860-h2-simple-ams-flipper The brackets are a direct replacement for the two small AMS 2 Pro mounting brackets from the print above, so there is no need to reprint the larger arms that attach to the back of the printer. The modification also includes a front handle to make lifting the AMS easier. The handle is secured from below using one of the original AMS transport screws 3x16mm, so no additional hardware is required. Assemble by sliding the folding arm upper bracket onto the dovetail joint of the handle, you can use a bit of filament to secure it, but as it fits from the bottom it won't come off anyway so not really needed, just for extra peace of mind. The arm uses gopro style pronged fitment, just slide this on and push through the securing pin, it should sit flush so give it a firm press, this is tapered at the end so should secure well. The folding support arm holds the flipper securely in the raised position once lifted. Also as the AMS does not tilt all the way back with this mod, the printer can continue printing while it is raised because the filament spools remain securely seated on the rollers. There is a stopper on the long arm so it won't flip forward so be aware and don't force it to fold out front, it fold back neatly out the way, there is a bit of friction at first, but over time it should loosen so the foot/arm will fall into place when you flip the AMS. The Arm will work with the glass in place or not, so you can use this when you need access to the top while printing such as when using TPU to feed directly in from the top without having to remove the AMS unit. description: First-Layer-Flussraten-Kalibrierungstest Finde mit einem schnellen und materialsparenden Test die optimale Flussrate für die erste Schicht deines Filaments und Druckprofils. Diese Kalibrierungsplatte enthält 16 einzelne Testflächen, die jeweils mit einer unterschiedlichen Flussrate für die erste Schicht von 0,85 bis 1,15 gedruckt werden. Nach dem Druck kannst du die Oberflächen direkt miteinander vergleichen und den Wert auswählen, der die gleichmäßigste und vollständig geschlossene erste Schicht erzeugt. Warum dieser Test sinnvoll ist Eine falsch eingestellte Flussrate der ersten Schicht kann zu folgenden Problemen führen: sichtbare Lücken zwischen den Drucklinien schwache Haftung der ersten Schicht raue oder überfüllte Oberflächen erhöhte Rillen durch zu viel Material ungleichmäßige Unterseiten Mit diesem Test kannst du mehrere Werte in nur einem Druck vergleichen, anstatt jeden Wert einzeln testen zu müssen. Enthaltene Flussraten Obere Reihe: 1,08 · 1,10 · 1,12 · 1,15 Zweite Reihe: 1,00 · 1,02 · 1,04 · 1,06 Dritte Reihe: 0,92 · 0,94 · 0,96 · 0,98 Untere Reihe: 0,85 · 0,87 · 0,89 · 0,90 Nutze das beigefügte Referenzbild, um den jeweiligen Wert der einzelnen Testfläche eindeutig zuzuordnen. So wertest du den Test aus Drucke die enthaltene 3MF-Datei, ohne die individuellen Objekteinstellungen zu verändern. Löse die Testflächen vorsichtig vom Druckbett. Vergleiche die Oberflächen aller Testflächen. Halte die einzelnen Teststücke gegen eine helle Lichtquelle. Wähle den Wert, bei dem die Drucklinien vollständig miteinander verbunden sind und die Oberfläche gleichzeitig glatt und gleichmäßig aussieht. Flussrate zu niedrig sichtbare Lücken zwischen den Linien Licht scheint deutlich durch schwache oder leicht trennbare Oberfläche Flussrate zu hoch raue oder wellige Oberfläche erhöhte Rillen zu viel Material zwischen den Linien Optimales Ergebnis Drucklinien sind vollständig miteinander verbunden glatte und gleichmäßige Oberfläche keine deutlichen Lücken oder übermäßigen Rillen Übernimm den ermittelten Wert anschließend als Flussrate der ersten Schicht in dasselbe Filament- und Druckprofil, das du für den Test verwendet hast. Wichtiger Hinweis Dies ist ein Test für die Flussrate der ersten Schicht und kein Z-Offset- oder Druckbett-Nivellierungstest. Für zuverlässige Ergebnisse solltest du dieselben Einstellungen verwenden wie bei deinen späteren Drucken: Filament Düse Druckplatte Temperatur Filamentprofil Druckerprofil Effiziente Kalibrierung 16 Werte in einem Druck etwa 23 Minuten Druckzeit etwa 6,02 g Filament keine Stützstrukturen erforderlich keine Montage erforderlich Druckzeit und Materialverbrauch können je nach Drucker, Filament und verwendeten Einstellungen leicht abweichen. Wenn dir dieser Kalibrierungstest geholfen hat, freue ich mich sehr über eine Bewertung, einen Make oder einen Boost.
