Required AMS Lite Components This project is a modification of the original AMS Lite and therefore requires either a complete AMS Lite to disassemble or the corresponding replacement parts purchased separately. The main components required are: AMS Lite motherboard AMS Lite feeder motors AMS Lite power/data cable Filament Funnel Units and their original hardware Replacement parts can be purchased directly from the Bambu Lab store. Before buying individual components, it is recommended to compare their total cost with the price of a complete AMS Lite, as the actual savings depend on your country, currency, availability, and current promotions. Two-Motor Configuration The Pocket Edition can also be assembled using only two motors , installed in the two center positions while leaving the two outer positions of the M-Block empty. This configuration reduces the number of components required when four filament channels are not needed. Depending on current prices, however, purchasing individual spare parts is not always less expensive than buying a complete AMS Lite. Bill of Materials – Additional Hardware The following hardware is required in addition to the parts recovered from the original AMS Lite. Standard Version 6 × M3×16 screws Top Mount In addition to the Standard Version: 3 × M3×20 screws Wall Mount In addition to the Standard Version: 16 × M3×8 screws Suitable wall screws and anchors for your mounting surface IKEA SKÅDIS Mount In addition to the Standard Version: 16 × M3×8 screws Dimensions Approximate dimensions of the Pocket Edition: Width: 165 mm Depth: 75 mm Height: 140 mm When installed using either the Wall Mount or IKEA SKÅDIS Mount , the Pocket Edition extends approximately 125 mm from the mounting surface, depending on the selected configuration and PTFE tube routing. For the Top Mount , simply add the Pocket Edition height above the printer to determine the total required clearance. PTFE Tube Routing The PTFE tubes can be routed: Directly from the front. From the rear. Along either side of the Pocket Edition with a smooth bend. The design is intentionally flexible, allowing each user to adapt the tube routing to their own printer layout and spool placement. Important Information Keep the PTFE tubes between the Pocket Edition and the printer as short as reasonably possible while avoiding tight bends or kinks. Excessively long PTFE tubes increase friction during filament loading and unloading. Over time, this may place additional stress on the feeder motors and could eventually lead to loading errors. The AMS Lite is designed as an affordable filament management system and therefore uses relatively small motors. The Pocket Edition has been thoroughly tested and operates reliably, but minimizing PTFE tube length is one of the best ways to ensure consistent performance. The tubes should not be so short that they create sharp bends, nor so long that unnecessary friction is introduced. The ideal configuration is the one that allows the filament to travel with the least possible resistance. Looking for a More Complete Solution? AMS Lite Pocket Edition was designed with compactness, flexibility, and versatility as its primary goals. If you're looking for a more advanced and fully modular solution—including integrated spool holders, roller systems, and multiple configuration options—you may also be interested in my AMS Lite 4.0 project. It offers a more comprehensive approach while maintaining full compatibility with the original AMS Lite electronics. Need Help? If you still need help or have any questions, feel free to send me a private message . It allows me to manage requests more efficiently and provide more accurate support for each individual case. This is a Remix of Bambu Labs PTFE guide that was released alongside the Filament track switch. After months of usage, I started to notice some of the design flaws and things that I did not like. I downloaded the step files Bambu Lab provided in their original listing and proceeded to make my changes. The changes I made are: Reduced the PTFE guide's overall footprint to simplify it, reduce the use of filament and make it more widely compatible with AMS stacking solutions. Widened the sides of the guide to make room for the use of piece of 25mm x 10mm double sided tape (I used the Gorilla Invisible Hold Mounting Tape). Slightly increased the thickness of the guide to increase strength and rigidity, and ensure correct alignment with the AMS, AMS 2 Pro, AMS HT. Strengthened the tabs that hold the tube by increasing its thickness by .25mm. While this seems very minimal, it is very effective at preventing the tube from dropping down over time. An unexpected benefit from my changes is that you can place the guide exactly where the PTFE tube wants to be. Installations instruction: Cut a 10mm by 25mm piece of double sided tape and place them on the tabs that face the AMS, AMS 2 PRO, and AMS HT. Place the tube into the base. Remove the plastic/paper lining from the tape. Remove the PTFE tube from the AMS. Slide the PTFE tube into the guide tube. Slide the PTFE tube into the AMS. Use the PTFE tube to help you install the guide and ensure proper alignment. Aim for having the AMS and AMS 2 PRO release button to be right in the center of the guide. For the AMS HT, ensure air vent is in center of the guide. Please refer to the photos provided which are for an AMS 2 PRO and AMS HT. Press the base firmly against the AMS, AMS 2 PRO, and AMS HT. I have tested this and have had no issues. As long as you use a good quality tape, you should not have any issues. This model is designed as a parametric OpenSCAD / MakerWorld Customizer file. You can adjust the bar diameter, clamp tolerance, block size, bolt spacing, nut pockets and corner radius directly in the MakerWorld customizer. Key Features Fully customizable bar diameter Designed for navigation bars, GPS bars and handlebar-style mounting points Bar runs through the short side of the block Two-piece clamp design: front and back part Both parts are placed print-ready with the groove facing upward M4 bolt holes Optional M4 hex nut pockets in the back part Rounded corners Adjustable clamp undersize for a tighter or looser fit Suitable for common adventure motorcycle navigation bars Common Diameter Examples Recommended starting values: BMW / adventure GPS bar: Bar_Diameter = 12.0 Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 Hardware M4 Bolt 25mm M4 nyloc nuts Some BMW navigation bars: Bar_Diameter = 16.0 Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 Hardware M4 Bolt 30mm M4 nyloc nuts Always measure your own bar with calipers before printing. Small differences matter for clamp fit. Important Assembly Note Both parts are shown in print orientation with the bar groove facing upward. For assembly: Place the back part against the navigation bar. Flip the front part over. Put the front part over the bar. Insert the M4 bolts. Tighten gradually and evenly. The two half-round grooves will clamp around the bar. Parameters Main customizer parameters: Bar_Diameter Nominal diameter of your motorcycle navigation bar. Bar_Offset_X Moves the bar groove left or right from the center of the block. This is useful when the navigation bar needs to sit slightly off-center. Default value: 0.0 mm Range: -10 mm to +10 mm Clamp_Undersize Reduces the actual groove diameter for a tighter clamp. Example: Bar_Diameter = 12.0 and Clamp_Undersize = 0.30 creates an effective 11.7 mm clamp . Block_Length Overall length of the clamp block. Block_Width Overall width of the clamp block. Half_Thickness Thickness of each half. Set to 0 for automatic thickness. Corner_Radius Controls the rounded corners. Bolt Parameters Bolt_Size Selects the bolt size used for the clamp. Options: M3, M4, M5 The model automatically adjusts the bolt hole diameter and nut pocket size based on this setting. Bolt_Clearance Adds extra clearance to the selected bolt diameter. Example : Bolt_Size = M4 Bolt_Clearance = 0.5 This creates a 4.5 mm bolt hole. Increase this value if your printer makes holes too tight. Manual_Hole_Diameter Manual override for the bolt hole diameter. Set this value to 0 to use automatic hole sizing based on Bolt_Size and Bolt_Clearance. Use this only if you want full manual control over the hole diameter. Hole_Spacing_X Horizontal spacing between the left and right bolt holes. Measured center-to-center. Hole_Spacing_Y Vertical spacing between the upper and lower bolt holes. Measured center-to-center. Back Nut Pocket Parameters Nut_Pockets Enables or disables hexagonal nut pockets in the back part. Options : true Adds hex nut pockets to the back part. false Creates normal through-holes only. Nut_Pocket_Clearance Adds extra clearance to the automatic nut pocket size. Increase this value if your nuts are too tight. Decrease this value if your nuts are too loose. Manual_Nut_Flat_To_Flat Manual override for the hex nut pocket size. Measured flat-to-flat. Set this value to 0 to use automatic sizing based on Bolt_Size and Nut_Pocket_Clearance. Manual_Nut_Depth Manual override for the hex nut pocket depth. Set this value to 0 to use automatic depth based on Bolt_Size. Increase this value if your nuts sit proud of the surface. Advanced Parameters Preview_Cutaway Creates a cutaway preview to inspect the internal groove and holes. Options: false Normal printable model. true Cutaway preview mode. Use false before exporting for printing. Facet_Count Controls the smoothness of circular features such as the bar groove, bolt holes and nut pockets. Options : 32, 48, 64, 96, 128 Recommended value : 96 Higher values create smoother curves but may generate larger files. Print Settings Recommended material: PETG ASA ABS PETG-CF Suggested settings: 4–6 walls/perimeters 40–60% infill 0.2 mm layer height Print both parts with the groove facing upward Use supports only if your slicer requires them for the nut pockets For motorcycle use, avoid PLA because heat and sunlight can deform the part. I created this project out of pure frustration. I was very dissatisfied with the performance of the original wheels on my robotic lawnmower – I tested both the standard version and the one supposedly designed for "heavy terrain." The result was always the same: the robot constantly dug in, stalled, and damaged the lawn. I decided to design my own solution. The machine finally drives without any problems, doesn't dig into the ground, and maneuvers smoothly throughout the garden. Key design features: Optimized spike design: The shape, length, and spacing of the spikes have been designed to prevent the robot from digging in. The design provides excellent traction while allowing the machine to turn smoothly without tearing up the turf. Rearview of the original weight: This is a very important detail – the inside of the wheel has been modeled to easily accommodate the original weight. This allows the robot to maintain a proper center of gravity and ground pressure. Dedicated cover: A flat cover encloses the inside of the wheel, protecting the weight and hub from the accumulation of dirt, mud, and grass clippings. Mounts to the wheel bolt, and a removal key is included. Removal key: A simple but extremely useful T-shaped key is included. It fits perfectly into the slots in the cover, allowing for easy and safe removal when cleaning or servicing is needed. Printing instructions: Material: I highly recommend PETG. The wheels are used outdoors and are exposed to moisture, impact, and sunlight. PETG provides the necessary flexibility and durability that regular PLA might struggle with over time. The tags — the real difference Most swatch holders give you slots and nothing else. Once you pass ~30 swatches, slots alone stop being enough: you can't tell where PLA ends and PETG begins, and you have no way to flag a colour you've run out of. The included tags slot into the same rails as the swatches and act as dividers and labels . Four are included ready to print: PLA PETG Multicolor Out of Stock The text is a raised emboss, so a simple filament change at the top layer gives you a two-colour tag with no AMS and no multi-material setup — yellow on black, red on black, whatever reads best on your bench. If your swatches feel too tight, a 0.02–0.04 mm bump in X-Y contour compensation (negative) usually fixes it without reprinting at a different size. The bodies print fine at 0.28 mm draft layers if you want speed, but the tag lettering looks much cleaner at 0.2 mm or 0.16 mm. For the tags: insert a filament change / colour change at the first layer of the raised text (around 0.8–1.0 mm from the top of the tag) to get the two-tone look shown in the photos. description: Automatisches, passives Entlüftungsventil für den SUNLU AMS Heater. Während der Heizlüfter läuft, öffnen der Luftstrom und der geringe Überdruck im Gehäuse das Ventil automatisch. Viel Spaß beim Nachbauen! Feedback und Verbesserungsvorschläge sind jederzeit willkommen.

EXTERNAL ACTIVATED CARBON FILTER Rev.0 FEATURES: Compact dimensions (208 x 86 mm , H 310+XX) , to be placed behind the printer. Usable area of the carbon chamber is 94 cm2 , max height of the carbon / top synthetic wool 10 cm . Air can be extracted from the printer via the “Magnetic AIR extractor” or through fittings that you can build or buy , as long as they are suitable for corrugated tubing with an outer diameter of 40mm (standard). Here you can also find an angle fitting for the Kobra S1 Max riser , which I downloaded online. The filtered air can be released outside the printer , or routed back inside the printer using other fittings. If the airflow is too strong, you can use just one fan, but remember to close the outlet of the fan that is not being used with resistant tape. ADVANTAGES: The activated carbon is distributed horizontally , occupying the entire surface of the grid , REGARDLESS of the amount of carbon you want to use , NO empty corners are left without carbon . With a height of 3.5 cm you get approximately 200g of activated carbon. The dirty air coming from below and moving upwards , passes through the entire surface of the activated carbon. The layer of synthetic wool placed under the activated carbon (optional) serves to prevent carbon dust from falling onto the fans (when they are off). The layer of synthetic wool placed above the activated carbon (optional) serves to prevent activated carbon dust from exiting the filter into the printer chamber or the surrounding environment. Maintenance is super simple , just remove the 4 rubber bands , remove the carbon chamber and replace it. CAUTION: Regarding the use of the magnetic air extractor, always check whether the grid you see on your printer is an air exhaust from the inside to the outside (so you can use the extractor) or a cooling intake (so you cannot use the extractor). PLEASE CHECK YOUR PRINTER'S FUNCTIONS CAREFULLY BEFORE MAKING THIS MODIFICATION / ADDING THIS DEVICE. I AM NOT RESPONSIBLE FOR ANY DAMAGE CAUSED BY THIS DEVICE. Airflow Capsule Kompakter Silikat-Behälter für Filamentrollen, Dryboxen und luftdichte Lagerlösungen. Kurzbeschreibung Die Airflow Capsule ist ein wiederverwendbarer Behälter für 2–5 mm Silikatkugeln zur Feuchtekontrolle bei der Filamentlagerung. Die Bauform ist so ausgelegt, dass die Capsule in den Kern vieler Filamentrollen passt und damit vorhandenen Leerraum nutzt , statt zusätzlichen Platz in Beutel, Box oder Lagerbehälter zu belegen. Durch die offene Geometrie mit seitlichen Schrägstrukturen, perforierter Innenstruktur und zusätzlichen Bodenöffnungen kann die Luftfeuchtigkeit im geschlossenen Lagerraum wirksam an das Trockenmittel gelangen. Gleichzeitig bleiben die Silikatkugeln sicher im Behälter. Vorteile Für 2–5 mm Silikatkugeln geeignet 1 mm Sieböffnungen halten die Kugeln sicher zurück Kompakte Bauform für den Einsatz in vielen Filamentrollenkernen Kein zusätzlicher Platzbedarf in vielen Lager-Setups Wiederverwendbar und leicht nachfüllbar Drehverschluss mit Gewinde für sicheres Öffnen und Schließen Saubere Alternative zu losen Silikatbeuteln oder losem Granulat Geeignet für Dryboxen, luftdichte Beutel und Lagerboxen Warum die Airflow Capsule sinnvoll ist Filamente reagieren je nach Material mehr oder weniger stark auf Luftfeuchtigkeit. Eine trockene Lagerumgebung hilft dabei, Feuchteaufnahme zu reduzieren und die Materialeigenschaften länger stabil zu halten. Die Airflow Capsule unterstützt das, indem sie das Trockenmittel dort platziert, wo es praktisch und platzsparend eingesetzt werden kann: direkt im Kern der Filamentrolle . Das Produkt ist nicht einfach nur ein geschlossener Behälter mit Löchern. Die Geometrie ist darauf ausgelegt, einen guten Feuchteausgleich zwischen Umgebungsluft und Silikat zu ermöglichen. Deckel und Verschluss Die Airflow Capsule wird über einen Drehverschluss mit Gewinde geschlossen. Der Deckel wird aufgesetzt und durch Drehen sicher verriegelt. Dadurch sitzt er fest auf dem Behälter und kann sich im normalen Einsatz nicht unbeabsichtigt lösen. Vorteile des Gewinde-Drehverschlusses: sicherer Halt im geschlossenen Zustand einfaches Öffnen zum Nachfüllen oder Wechseln des Silikats saubere und wiederverwendbare Lösung ohne loses Einstecken besser kontrollierbares Schließen als bei reinen Steckverbindungen Der Verschluss ist damit auf praktische Wiederverwendung ausgelegt: sicher im Betrieb, aber jederzeit wieder lösbar . Physikalisches Prinzip Silica Gel arbeitet über Adsorption . Wassermoleküle werden an der großen inneren Oberfläche des Trockenmittels gebunden. Entscheidend ist deshalb nicht nur die Menge des Silikats, sondern auch, wie gut die Luftfeuchtigkeit das Material erreichen kann. In einer geschlossenen Box oder einem Beutel gibt es in der Regel keinen starken Luftstrom. Die Feuchteverteilung erfolgt daher vor allem durch: Diffusion geringe natürliche Mikro-Konvektion langsamen Feuchteausgleich im gesamten eingeschlossenen Volumen Genau hier ist eine offene Behälterstruktur sinnvoll. Die seitlichen Schrägöffnungen, die durchlässige Innenstruktur und die zusätzlichen Öffnungen im Boden vergrößern die Kontaktfläche zwischen Umgebungsluft und Trockenmittel. Das beschleunigt nicht im Sinne eines Ventilators den Luftstrom, aber es erleichtert den Feuchteausgleich , weil die Luftfeuchtigkeit von mehreren Seiten an das Silikat gelangen kann. Warum die schräge Struktur sinnvoll ist Die schräg angeordneten Öffnungen erzeugen in einem stehenden Luftvolumen keinen gerichteten Windkanal . Das wäre physikalisch übertrieben. Sie haben trotzdem einen realen Nutzen: mehr freiliegende Austauschfläche weniger abgeschirmte Bereiche bessere Erreichbarkeit des Trockenmittels von mehreren Seiten stabile Außenstruktur trotz offener Bauweise guter Kompromiss aus Luftzugang und mechanischer Stabilität Die Wirkung entsteht also nicht durch „Luft wird aktiv hineingezogen“, sondern durch eine offene, günstig zugängliche Geometrie , die Diffusion und Feuchteausgleich unterstützt. Technische Daten Außendurchmesser: 54 mm Höhe: 36,8 mm Außenwand: 2 mm Innenwand: 2 mm Lochdurchmesser Sieb Deckel: 1,5 mm Lochdurchmesser Boden/Gehäuse: 1,3 mm Lochabstand Seitenbereich: 2,844 mm Lochabstand Boden: 3 mm Geeignete Füllung: 2–5 mm Silikatkugeln Verschlussart: Drehverschluss mit Gewinde Eignung für Silikatkugeln 2–5 mm Die 1,5-mm-Öffnungen sind deutlich kleiner als die verwendeten Silikatkugeln mit 2–5 mm Durchmesser. Dadurch bleiben die Kugeln sicher im Behälter, während Luftfeuchtigkeit weiterhin an das Trockenmittel gelangen kann. Das macht die Capsule geeignet für: Silikatkugeln wiederverwendbare Trockenmittelgranulate in passender Körnung Filamentlagerung in geschlossenen Systemen Geschätzte Füllmenge Je nach tatsächlicher Innengeometrie liegt die realistische Füllmenge bei ungefähr: ca. 30–40 g Silikatkugeln Diese Angabe ist als praxisnahe Bandbreite zu verstehen, da Boden, Deckel, Gewinde und Innenkontur die exakte nutzbare Füllmenge beeinflussen. Was diese Menge bringt Silica Gel kann je nach Typ und Umgebungsbedingungen typischerweise etwa 20–35 % seines Eigengewichts an Wasser aufnehmen. Bei einer Füllmenge von ca. 30–40 g Silikat ergibt sich damit eine praxisnahe Wasseraufnahme von ungefähr: ca. 6–10 g Wasser im typischen Einsatzbereich Für einen geschlossenen Lagerraum einer einzelnen Filamentrolle ist das relevant, weil nicht nur die eingeschlossene Luftfeuchtigkeit abgefangen wird, sondern auch Feuchte, die beim Öffnen eingetragen wird oder langsam in das System eindringt. Abschätzung zur Wirkdauer und Feuchtereduktion Die folgenden Angaben sind keine garantierten Messwerte, sondern technisch und praxisnah abgeschätzte Richtwerte unter typischen Einsatzbedingungen. Sie gelten für einen gut geschlossenen Lagerbehälter, eine Füllmenge von ca. 30–40 g Silikat und den Fall, dass der Behälter nicht ständig geöffnet wird. Unter diesen Annahmen ist typischerweise zu erwarten: eine spürbare Reduktion der Luftfeuchtigkeit innerhalb einiger Stunden ein deutlicher Effekt nach etwa 12–24 Stunden eine Stabilisierung des Lagerklimas meist nach ca. 1–3 Tagen Die voraussichtliche Wirkdauer einer Füllung liegt je nach Einsatzbedingungen grob im Bereich von: mehreren Wochen bei normalem Gebrauch bis zu einigen Monaten in einem sehr dichten System mit seltenem Öffnen ca. 2–4 Monate in einem sehr dichten, kleinen Lagerraum unter günstigen Bedingungen teils auch länger, es hängt auch mit der Restfeuchte im Filament oder Undichtigkeiten ab. Diese Werte dienen ausschließlich der Orientierung. Die tatsächliche Wirkung hängt unter anderem ab von der Dichtheit des Behälters, der Umgebungsluftfeuchtigkeit, der Häufigkeit des Öffnens, dem Feuchtezustand des Filaments sowie von Menge, Qualität und Zustand des verwendeten Silikats. Wichtig für die Einordnung Bereits stark feuchtes Filament wird durch die Capsule nicht schnell „trocken gebacken“ . Die Stärke des Systems liegt vor allem darin: Feuchtigkeit im Lagerraum zu senken den Zustand trockener oder vorgetrockneter Filamente zu halten Feuchteeintrag nach dem Öffnen wieder abzufangen Lagerbedingungen langfristig zu stabilisieren Nutzen bei einer 1-kg-Filamentrolle Die Airflow Capsule ist besonders sinnvoll für die Lagerung einzelner Rollen in: Vakuumbeuteln luftdichten Beuteln Dryboxen geschlossenen Kunststoffboxen Gerade bei einer 1-kg-Rolle ist der Rollenkern meist ungenutzter Raum. Die Capsule nutzt diesen Bereich sinnvoll, ohne den Lagerplatz für die Rolle selbst zu verschlechtern. Das bringt in der Praxis: kein loses Trockenmittel im Behälter keine zusätzliche Stellfläche saubere Positionierung nahe an der Rolle einfache Wiederverwendung Geeignete Filamente Besonders sinnvoll für Lagerung von: PLA PETG ABS ASA Ebenso nützlich bei feuchteempfindlicheren Materialien wie: TPU PA / Nylon PC Wichtig: Die Airflow Capsule ist eine passive Lösung zur Lagerung und Feuchtestabilisierung . Bei bereits stark durchfeuchtetem Filament ersetzt sie kein aktives Trocknen im Filamenttrockner oder Ofen. Typische Einsatzbereiche Filamentlagerung im Spulenkern Drybox-Systeme Vakuumbeutel Aufbewahrungsboxen mit Dichtung Langzeitlagerung einzelner Spulen Fazit Die Airflow Capsule ist eine kompakte und durchdachte Lösung zur Aufnahme von Silikatkugeln für die Filamentlagerung. Die Konstruktion kombiniert: sichere Rückhaltung der Kugeln gute Zugänglichkeit für Luftfeuchtigkeit zusätzliche Austauschfläche auch über den Boden sicher verschließbaren Deckel mit Gewinde-Drehverschluss platzsparende Integration in viele Filamentrollen saubere und wiederverwendbare Handhabung Dadurch ist sie eine praktische Alternative zu losen Silikatbeuteln und eine besonders effiziente Lösung für alle, die vorhandenen Leerraum im Rollenkern sinnvoll nutzen möchten.

description: The SnapMaker U1's SpoolBox design by CC3DProjects is beautiful, but one of the biggest problems for any filament spool holder for the SnapMaker U1 is the loss of the RFID filament detection feature. The SnapMaker U1's RFID detection requires the tags to be as close to the side panels as possible. For best results, the RFID tag should touch the side panel. Requirements You must have purchased the SpoolBox by CC3DProjects already paxx12 firmware must be installed on the SnapMaker U1 to allow detection of custom RFID tags To enable OpenSpool NTAG215 RFID tags, load in your browser http:// /firmware-config Snapmaker Components > Filament Detection > OpenRFID (force generic vendor) This allows NTAG215 to be detected by Orca Slicer, even for unrecognised brands I cannot share the SpoolBox base plates, as you need to purchase them separately. Instructions (IMPORTANT) Load the CC3DProjects SpoolBox 3MF Adding negative part from STL. Export the negative object in the last plate as an STL file Open SpoolBox 3MF Select the base plate Right-click “Add negative part” “Load” Select the SpoolBox Mount Negative.stl file Position it as shown in the pictures. Reference positions (mm)/rotations below. You don't need them to be so precise; these are just what I have in my slicer. Snapmaker Spool Box LH Plate 1 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: 7.88, 37.09, 56.16 Rotation (absolute): -180, -90, 180 Snapmaker Spool Box LH Plate 2 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: 12, 62.33, -7.83 Rotation (absolute): -180, -180, 138.35 Snapmaker Spool Box RH Plate 1 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: -12.45, 61.69, -7.88 Rotation (absolute): 0, 0, 41.45 Snapmaker Spool Box RH Plate 2 Size: 32, 56.2, 24.2 Object coordinates: -50.68, 44.55, -7.88 Rotation (absolute): 0, 0, 0 For each cutout, create a support-enforcer cube with the same size, position and rotation. As the SpoolBox 3MF defaults to manual supports, you need support enforcers on the cutout. Select the base plate Right-click “Add support enforcer” “Cube” Resize and reposition the cube over the negative object. After you slice, make sure that the supports appear under the flaps. Printing the RFID teardrop wrappers Open the SpoolBox-RFID-Wrapper 3MF Edit the text objects to customise your labels Remember to use the actual filament you want as your base colour, and black or white as the text colour. Purchasing NTAG215 discs Discs must be 25mm in diameter Search your local online shops, or at AliExpress. There are many listings. Here's one: https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005012682271345.html Writing to your RFID discs No app needed; write to your RFID discs here: https://printtag-web.pages.dev/ Push the RFID disc into the RFID teardrop wrapper Loading filament Slide the RFID into the cutout pockets before loading filament, as shown in pictures. The white RFID disc must be facing the printer. Load filament as normal

description: Stop buying disposable vacuum bags! This is a reusable, easy-to-empty 3D printed dust bin designed specifically for the iRobot Roomba Combo Essential series (405, 505, Y0110, Y0140 Auto-Empty Dock). Instead of replacing the bag every time, you reuse the rubber gasket and filter fabric from one donor OEM bag, making your vacuum station eco-friendly and cost-effective! 🛠️ Important MakerWorld / Print Details Compatible Models: iRobot Roomba Combo Essential (405 / 505) & Auto-Empty Dock. Supports: Needed for overhangs/bridges on the main box body. Hardware Required: 1x Used OEM disposable bag (as a donor for the rubber gasket and filter membrane). CA Glue (Super Glue / Kropelka). A small piece of 1.75mm filament (used as hinge pin). 📋 Step-by-Step Assembly Instructions Clean the Prints: Remove all print supports from the printed box and components. Salvage the Rubber Gasket: Tear open the paper/cardboard mounting plate from your old disposable bag and carefully extract the rubber sealing gasket. Trace the Shape: Place the 3D printed box onto the fabric of the old dust bag and trace its outline onto the bag. Cut the Filter: Cut out the filter membrane along the traced line, leaving a slight excess around the edges. Install the Gasket: Glue the salvaged rubber gasket onto the top section of the printed box (the part that slides into the Roomba station). Glue Lower Body: Glue the lower part of the box towards the alignment line marked on the printed body. Insert Moving Element: Insert the moving flap into the top section (also marked with an alignment line), then glue the upper and lower body sections together. Invert: Turn the box upside down. Align Grids & Hinges: Fit the hinge combs to the grid (check the 3D model if "L" and "R" markings aren't clear on your print). Important: The side with the handle must be aligned with the "L" hinge comb and the "L" mark on the box. Create Hinge Pin: Slide a piece of 1.75mm 3D printing filament (acting as the hinge pin) from the handle side (L) — it will go in easily. Trim it with extra length so you can pull it out later if needed. On the "R" side, it will fit very tight at first (it will wear in over time). Position Filter: Place the cut filter fabric over the opening on the box. Attach Hinge Grid: Align the grid with hinges to the box following the "L" and "R" markings. Once fitted, glue the "L" side first, then the "R" side. Alignment lines on the box guide the hinge placement. Keep the grid firmly held in place so everything fits and moves smoothly. Chamfer Insertion Edge: Chamfer/bevel the edges of the part that slides into the Roomba dock as needed for a smooth fit. Ready to Use! You now have a reusable, emptyable dust bin for your Roomba station! ⚠️ Important Notes & Tips Filter Sealing Tip: Make sure the filter cut from the old bag is tucked thoroughly into the slanted grooves between the grid and the box. This guarantees a proper dust-tight seal. Volume Constraint: Do NOT attempt to scale up or make a bigger box. A larger box decreases vacuum suction pressure, preventing the station from emptying the robot properly! First Run Check: Check for any dust leaks around the filter during the first few cycles until you get comfortable mounting it correctly. Disclaimer: I am not responsible for any damage to your Roomba if assembled incorrectly. Use at your own risk. Video Guide: A detailed video instruction guide will be uploaded soon! Feel free to leave a comment if you have questions or feedback. 💡 Final Notes & Tips: Filament Choice: I printed mine using PLA Nylon. However, I highly recommend using PETG or a strong, high-quality PLA for the best durability and flexibility. Check the Photos: Please take a close look at the uploaded photos—they contain additional visual tips and guidance on how to assemble everything correctly! Video Shorts: Check out the two shorts below for a quick preview. Note that they feature the earlier prototype of this bin; the current version fixes all the initial design flaws and has been working flawlessly for over a month now!

A horizontal DIY SUP trolley. The black printed version is the latest, although some photos and the video was made with V1(red). It makes the SUP transport much easier than carrying. I designed the black V2 version so the strap holes are facing the edges of the SUP rather then being parallel. It makes feeding the strap through much easier therefore securing the SUP is better. It uses a 28mm wood dowel, the size is customizable to fit different sized SUPs. The wheels I got here are 20cm in size, other hardware used are 2 bolts which are 8mm in dia, 2 big and 4 medium washers and 4 nuts to secure the wheel. The dowel is attached to the wheel assembly by “D shape locking pins” - M6x55mm The round wheel shaft is required onto the bolts so the wheel runs freely when tightened. Installation is very simple: insert the bolts with a slightly bigger washer into the printed “leg” add a washer on the other side of the bolt (reinforce the 3d printed part) twist on the wheel shaft onto the bolt add the wheel add another washer secure it with locking nuts drill a straight hole into the dowel, insert it into the wheel assembly and put the D shape locking pins on it (it is required so each side is locked together) All parts available either DIY shops and on Amazon (D locking pins) I use this trolley when I have to park far from launch point, and on the water I can put the disassembled part under the bungee cords on the back.

description: Эти антивибрационные ножки уменьшают передачу движений от Bambu Lab A1 на стол. Каждая опора состоит из двух одинаковых напечатанных частей и одного стального шарика подшипника диаметром 7-10 мм . Шарик помещается между вогнутыми поверхностями, позволяя принтеру слегка двигаться вместо того, чтобы передавать все инерционные силы на стол. Чашки имеют эллиптический профиль: они допускают небольшие движения вблизи центра и обеспечивают возрастающее сопротивление по мере увеличения смещения. Некоторое покачивание принтера во время быстрых движений является нормальным и является частью принципа работы. Необходимые детали Для одного Bambu Lab A1: напечатайте прилагаемую модель 12-18 раз ; используйте 6-9 стальных шарика подшипника диаметром 7-10 мм . используйте два куска фанеры толщиной 10мм или больше. 300х400мм для Bambu Lab A1. Для других моделей размеры могут быть другими. Верхняя и нижняя части идентичны, поэтому включена только одна модель. Печать Протестированная версия была напечатана из PLA , но могут быть использованы и другие филаменты. Печатайте детали вертикально, стоя на плоской боковой грани . Такая ориентация обеспечивает более гладкие вогнутые поверхности чашек и позволяет стальному шарику свободнее двигаться. Рекомендуемые настройки: высота слоя: 0.20 mm; 3 стенки; заполнение 100%; без поддержек. Сборка Приклейте половину распечатанных деталей на один кусок фанеры и вторую половину на другой кусок так, чтобы при совмещении чашки деталей совпадали друг с другом (добавил версию модели с отверстиями под винт для прикручивания деталей). Поместите шарики диаметром 7-10 мм в чашки. Накройте второй идентичной частью. Осторожно установите принтер на собранную платформу. Выполните калибровку принтера после установки.

After talking to a few people on reddit i can to realize that the aux fan is connected to the fresh air intake fan and can not be ran independently of that fan. the problem is if you want to filtrate your chamber, you have to run the aux fan, which can be a problem for materials that like less cooling during print. coincidently those materials are also the worst if not filtered properly. printed mine in petg with .2 layer height with default tree supports in the orientation shown, and it took about 35 mins. cranked the aux fan up to 75% to test after popping it in and can confirm that it successfully pushes the air down away from the print bed and towards the filter, which after filtering it pushes it back up through the aux fan creating a circulation effect within the chamber. Should just pop right in the aux fan output and hold. Make sure when popping it into the fan outlet, that the legs are positioned so that they are surrounding the first peg on the grill (PROPER ORIENTATION IS SHOWN IN THE PICTURES FOR THE ITEM), if you put all the feet on both sides of the first peg it may break one of the legs and leave a gap on one side of the fan open. ANNOUNCEMENT Version 2 is finally available. With slimmer design, improved hinge mechanism, and built in pins, the assembly is much simpler, and the model is fully parametric . I invite you to test your printing skills and show me the smallest working version you can create! Model link in this post: https://makerworld.com/community/post/1832304 Have fun! Assembly Demonstration Maker’s Note I’m a hobby modeler, and I'm trying to enter MakerWorld contests with designs that push me beyond my limits. This is my biggest project so far, and it took many weekends of modeling, printing, testing, breaking parts, and going back to the drawing board. (I have an ever increasing pile of failed prototypes) My long-term goal is to create a free, easy-to-print and easy-to-assemble parametric generator that lets anyone generate a set of toy fingers fitted to their own hand. I do have a slight tendency toward maximalism, so I’m not ready to publish the fully customizable version until I’ve confirmed that it works reliably across a wide range of finger sizes, but in the meantime, I wanted to see how people react to the idea and whether it is worth putting the extra work into the generator. Please try the current version with an open mind, and feel free to leave constructive feedback. I’ll do my best to incorporate the feedback into the customizable version. Background I first came across this type of finger extension in this Adam Savage video. It immediately looked like something that would be incredibly fun to build and wear… Then I looked at the price tag :D (after spending so much time on this, I fully understand the pricing. Gary's fingers are truly a work of art both aesthetically and mechanically) That sent me down the rabbit hole of researching how I could make my own. While looking through existing projects and mechanisms, I found the work of Dragonator , whose notes were invaluable during the development process. A big shoutout to him. Seeing his amazing model, I’m sure he is one of the few who understand both the pain of designing a mechanism like this and the joy of finally putting it on for the first time and feeling the fingers move with your hand. Design Considerations I’ll demonstrate the main design decisions with pictures below, but these were the areas I focused on most: Cylindrical, adaptive geometry The mechanism is built around mostly cylindrical finger sections. This makes a final design I find aesthetic. I believe most similar finger have an adaptable base section that goes around the fingers, and the rest of the mechanism is interchangeable. I wanted the whole finger to be driven by parameters. Low-profile control shaft movement One thing I struggled a lot with is how to keep the controller shaft as low to the body as possible both at the two end states, and during the movement. With a few tradeoffs, I think I well achieved both. Easy assembly This was the thing I feared the most. In the commercial version, there is obviously no assembly required, it is put together beautifully with additional hardware. I tried different ways of connecting parts, and after multiple failures came up with a snap-in design, which I'm truly proud of. Clean seam lines I wanted the finger to have a clean, cylindrical look when it's straight. However cylinders generally have problems with seam lines. I intentionally placed a straight groove at the bottom of the parts, so you wont need to paint seam lines yourself, you can just hit print and know the lines will look acceptable. The support tradeoff This is the price I decided to pay. Many things in my design are supported, and while many I could have eliminated, I decided the one-time price of removing the supports is well covered by the gains I got in aesthetics and assembly. How the Mechanism Works The finger sections are linked together so that movement from your real finger is transferred through the control shafts to the extended segments. «SCYTHEON MK.IV HYBRID» Cyberpunk mantis blade «Hey, choom! Well, what do you say, time to put a little more "cyber" into this punk? I got just the thing for you — some shiny, brand-new military-grade chrome. Just make sure to upgrade your ICE and keep those damn netrunners off your back, hermano. So, what's it gonna be... time to become a legend, no?» 1. Concept Few pieces of sci-fi equipment are as iconic as the cybernetic mantis blade. This project is inspired by that legendary concept while deliberately avoiding a direct reproduction of any specific design. Instead of replicating an existing prop, the focus was placed on engineering, functionality, and manufacturability. Every component was designed from the ground up to create a fully mechanical model that is both visually convincing and practical to build. The result is a 100% 3D-printable, fully functional mechanism that requires no additional hardware — no screws, springs, magnets, pins, or glue. Every moving part is printed and assembled into a working extendable blade mechanism. Rather than being just a static display piece, this model was created as an engineering project that demonstrates what can be achieved using modern desktop 3D printing while capturing the unmistakable aesthetic of the cyberpunk genre. 3. Description Overview The model consists of a forearm bracer, decorative hydraulic cylinders, a three-link extension mechanism, an extendable claw blade, and a manual drive handle. The complete project consists of 78 printed parts, plus two dedicated assembly wrenches used during construction. The wrenches are assembly tool only and are not part of the finished model. Despite the term "blade" being used, the model does not incorporate an actual sharpened blade. All exposed edges are intentionally blunt, with a minimum chamfer of 1.5 mm, making the finished model suitable as a cosplay prop or display piece rather than a cutting tool. To operate the mechanism, place the bracer around your forearm and secure the two halves using the integrated locking clips. Pull the drive handle downward to deploy the linkage and extend the blade. Pull the handle upward to fully retract the blade and fold the mechanism back into its compact position. The mechanism is fully mechanical and operates reliably in any orientation, whether held horizontally, vertically, or upside down. With the exception of several screws and the internal gears used in the blade extension mechanism, the design is fully symmetrical and can be assembled for either the left or the right arm. Dimensions Deployed: 800 × 196 × 124 mm Folded: 350 × 130 × 124 mm The articulated linkage extends to an overall length of 600 mm, measured from the first folding pivot to the end of the claw blade. 4. Printing Material Compatibility This product is designed to be printed entirely from PETG. Main Print Settings Layer height: 0.2 mm Nozzle: 0.4 mm Perimeters: 3 Top solid layers: 1.2 mm Bottom solid layers: 1.2 mm Infill: 40% Supports: Tree supports Printing Recommendations For the best results, it is strongly recommended to use the supplied print profile without modifications. 5. Assembly A comprehensive, fully illustrated step-by-step assembly manual is included. Every assembly step is explained in detail, making the build process straightforward despite the model's sophisticated mechanical design.

The wider it is, the easier to press in the pin, but also the less resistance to keep it in the hole. CLEARANCE The distance between parts. (e.g. if the gear is 5mm wide, and the clearance is 0.4mm, then the gear-space will be 5.4mm wide) HOLE_CLEARANCE How much bigger should the pin-holes be than the pins. (e.g. if the pin's diameter is 2mm, and the clearance is 0.2mm, then the pin-hole has a diameter of 2.2mm) SUPPORT_CLEARANCE The distance between the support and the part it supports. If it is too small, the support will fuse with the part, and not break off easily, if it is too large, the support will not help the part, and the part will sag. Maker’s Note I’m a hobby modeler, and I'm trying to enter MakerWorld contests with designs that push me beyond my limits. This is my biggest project so far, and it took many weekends of modeling, printing, testing, breaking parts, and going back to the drawing board. (I have an ever increasing pile of failed prototypes) My long-term goal was to create a free, easy-to-print and easy-to-assemble parametric generator that lets anyone generate a set of toy fingers fitted to their own hand, and as promised, here it is! (perhaps you have found this model through my first prototype ) Background I first came across this type of finger extension in this Adam Savage video. It immediately looked like something that would be incredibly fun to build and wear… Then I looked at the price tag :D (after spending so much time on this, I fully understand the pricing. Gary's fingers are truly a work of art both aesthetically and mechanically) That sent me down the rabbit hole of researching how I could make my own. While looking through existing projects and mechanisms, I found the work of Dragonator , whose notes were invaluable during the development process. A big shoutout to him. Seeing his amazing model, I’m sure he is one of the few who understand both the pain of designing a mechanism like this and the joy of finally putting it on for the first time and feeling the fingers move with your hand. I have already shared my prototype on MakerWorld, and now sharing the fully parametric version. Design Considerations Thin Frame I've got some constructive feedback on the first attempt's cylindrical design. In this version, I kept the mechanism profile as low as possible, to allow you to create decorative skins around it to your liking. (Let me know in the comments if you want cutters or examples, but most parts are simple rectangles) Easy to Replace Parts The parts are designed to be easy to replace and change. (e.g. different fingertip designs) Parametric Dimensions In order to best fit all finger sizes and preferences, I allow users to change a wide range of parameters through MakerWorld's Parametric Model Maker. Not only the finger sleeve, but the whole model is driven through parameters, including the gears. Low Profile Shaft One thing I struggled a lot with is how to keep the controller shaft as low to the body as possible both at the two end states, and during the movement. With a few tradeoffs, I think I well achieved both. Easy Assembly While I believe my snap-in mechanism was elegant and simple, it still took time and preparation to use filament hinges. In this version, I simplified assembly even further, so all hinges are already printed into the model. You just print and assemble. Designed Support I built support into the model itself. (depending on your printer accuracy, they might fuse. in this case you have the ability to individually remove the problematic support pieces and replace them with auto generated support) How the Mechanism Works The finger sections are linked together so that movement from your real finger is transferred through the control shafts to the extended segments. The animation below shows the movement more clearly than I could explain it in text. FAQ Q: Your model is so amazing, can I give you multiple boosts? A: Yes, you can. Thanks. Final Note If you happened to have a failed print, please don't be mad. If it makes you feel a little better, I burnt through this many failed prototypes, to be able to create a good generator for you :)

description: Master Sword in Bloom – Korok Forest Pedestal ⚔️🌸 This is my take on the Master Sword resting in Korok Forest after the Great Calamity. Zelda left the sword under the protection of the Great Deku Tree, trusting that Link would eventually return to reclaim it. I imagined it sitting there untouched for the next hundred years, with vines and flowers inspired by the Silent Princess slowly growing around the blade as the forest reclaimed its resting place. It is not meant to recreate one exact scene from the game. It is more of a “what might it have looked like?” version of the Master Sword just before the hero finally returned. 🔹 Model Details ✔ Master Sword surrounded by sculpted vines and flowers ✔ Silent Princess inspired flower details ✔ Raised Hylian crest on the front of the pedestal ✔ Sword and pedestal print as separate sections ✔ Alignment connector included for assembly ✔ Works well as a single color print or painting project ✔ Sized for a desk, shelf, or gaming display 🔧 Printing Notes The flowers, vines, crossguard, and smaller details benefit from a lower layer height. The included profile uses: ✓ 0.08 mm layer height ✓ 0.4 mm nozzle ✓ Supports already configured ✓ Separate sword and pedestal sections ✓ Alignment connector between both pieces The upper sword section contains several small overhangs and detailed areas, so support removal should be done carefully. Flush cutters and a small pair of pliers can help around the vines and flowers. Slower outer-wall speeds can improve the visible surface finish, especially around the blade, crossguard, flowers, and raised crest. Matte PLA works especially well because it helps the sculpted details stand out without creating strong reflections. description: Description A modular cyberpunk / sci-fi gauntlet armor kit designed to turn a simple glove into a futuristic wearable cosplay prop. The model includes separate armor plates for the fingers, thumb, knuckles, back of the hand and wrist area. The pieces are printed separately and then glued onto a real glove. I used a fleece glove, but the parts can be attached to many types of fabric gloves depending on surface, flexibility and glue compatibility. I also included a raw full-glove reference file with all parts placed together, so you can see where each element is intended to go before assembly. This file is mainly for placement reference; for printing, use the separated armor parts / print profile. Sizing / Scaling This gauntlet was designed for my hand size: 20 cm from the wrist crease to the tip of the middle finger . To resize it for your hand, measure the same distance on your own hand and use this formula: Scale (%) = Your hand length / 20 cm × 100 Examples: 18 cm hand → 18 / 20 × 100 = 90% 19 cm hand → 19 / 20 × 100 = 95% 21 cm hand → 21 / 20 × 100 = 105% 22 cm hand → 22 / 20 × 100 = 110% Apply the same scale to all armor parts so the proportions stay consistent. Hand width, finger thickness and glove stretch can vary, so I recommend printing one or two finger plates first and testing the placement before printing the full set. Assembly Print the separate armor plates. Place the parts on the glove and check the full layout before gluing. Start with the larger hand and wrist pieces, then continue with the fingers and thumb. Glue the parts onto the glove one by one. I used hot glue for assembly. Be careful: hot glue can pass through thin fabric and burn your hand. I recommend wearing a second glove underneath the glove you are working on while positioning and pressing the parts. Test each part placement before gluing permanently. Printing Notes The included print profile has support settings tuned for easy removal. The model does use supports, but in my test print they came off cleanly and without much effort. Approximate material use from my print: Total material: around 120 g Supports: around 40 g The model was created as a wearable prop, so the armor plates are separated to make assembly easier and to allow the glove to remain flexible. Included Files Print profile with tuned support settings Full-glove raw reference file showing the intended placement of the parts Disclaimer This is a cosplay / costume / decorative prop , not protective equipment. It is not intended for impact protection, work safety, sports protection, self-defense or real combat use. The print profile was created and tested on a well-calibrated printer with a clean build plate and properly tuned filament settings. Results may vary depending on printer calibration, bed adhesion, filament condition, support settings and general machine setup. I cannot guarantee identical results on uncalibrated printers, dirty build plates, wet filament or poorly tuned extrusion/adhesion.

model_name: Dragon Spine Armor - Deployable Scale Mechanism
description: Dragon Spine Armor is a wearable articulated back mechanism inspired by dragon scales, vertebrae and fantasy armor design. The armor is built from modular backbone segments that follow the shape of the back . Each scale module is connected to a cable-driven slider system : when the pull rings are pulled, the scales lift and open like a mechanical dragon spine. The scales return to their closed position using elastic bands. The design is fully mechanical — no motors, electronics or screws are required. It uses print-in-place hinges, printed pins, slider plates, strings, return elastics and adjustable TPU neck and waist straps. This project is designed as a wearable cosplay/fantasy armor piece and as a mechanical 3D printing challenge. The modular structure makes the backpiece flexible enough to move with the body while still keeping a strong visual dragon-spine silhouette. For assembly, please follow the included assembly guide carefully , especially the string routing and tension adjustment steps. Equal string tension is important so that all scales open evenly. Required non-printed parts: - String/thread - Return elastic bands Print profiles: - Main armor parts: PLA - Neck and waist straps: TPU, printed separately This is a decorative cosplay accessory and not protective safety equipment.

Geralt’s steel sword from The Witcher game series, designed for slaying humans. The silver sword consists of a total of 14 3D-printed parts. Like the other swords from my production, this sword is assembled using an M5 threaded rod that runs through the entire length of the sword. Everything is fully concealed and not visible anywhere. Thanks to the use of the threaded rod, the sword is very sturdy, suitable even for fencing, and will not break. All parts of the sword are connected by an M5 threaded rod with a length of 1000mm , which runs through the center of all components. M5 lock nuts are installed at both ends of the threaded rod. One M5 nut is located in the Blade_4 part, and the other in the Pommel part. Start screwing the threaded rod into the Blade_1 part until the end of the rod is 974 mm from the bottom of the Blade_1 part . Then slide the remaining parts onto the threaded rod according to the assembly drawing. The nut in the Blade_1 and Pommel parts are embedded during printing. To insert the nut, a pause is created in the print profile, allowing the nut to be placed into the 3D print. Blade_1 and Pommel are printed on a separate build plate in order to minimize potential losses in case the nut insertion into the 3D print is unsuccessful. For the first time on this sword, an improved anti-rotation system has been used to prevent the blade sections from twisting relative to each other. The alignment pins are now integrated directly into the printed parts, so there is no need to print and insert them separately. Enjoy the print, and I hope you like Geralt the Witcher’s silver sword. Insert the dart into the barrel, seat it with the ramrod, cock the lock, aim, and fire. The entire loading and firing sequence is designed to resemble the operation of a historical flintlock while using a completely different internal propulsion system. The model features a compact folding design. Both the stock and the front assembly lock securely in their folded and deployed positions, allowing the blaster to be stored or transported in a much smaller package while remaining ready for use within seconds. Designed primarily for PETG printing, the model is almost entirely 3D printed. No metal springs, screws, glue, filament retaining pins, or other additional hardware are required. The only non-printed components are the elastic bands used for propulsion and mechanism operation. In addition to the original HEX 13 mm dart version, the project also includes a separate conversion profile for standard 0.5-inch foam darts. description: Want a replica of a US WW1 grenade? This is the original "pineapple" grenade from WW1 that was the predecessor to the Mk2 grenade we all know from WW2. This grenade has a spoon handle that flies off when you pull the pin, just like the real thing would. Background: Introduced in 1917, the US Mk1 Grenade was the first fragmentation hand grenade developed by the United States for use in World War I. It was notoriously complicated to operate in the field, often requiring the user to manually ignite the fuse before throwing. Due to soldiers struggling to arm it under pressure, the Mk 1 grenade was quickly recalled and replaced by the improved Mk 2 grenade fuze in 1918 (which this model depicts). Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. It is designed to work with the Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring (linked lower on the page). If you use a pen spring, you can usually cut it in half and get two springs. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu filaments used Basic Bronze Dark gray filaments are also period appropriate Silk+ Silver Assembly takes seconds Metal Spring Version 1. Insert the peg into the topper while its upside down. 2. description: Want a life-size replica of the Laser Guided APKWS Rocket used by the US, Ukraine, NATO, and many other militaries? This is around ~6ft / ~2m long and can be assembled in seconds just by screwing the printed parts together, no glue is required. It comes with moving fold-out fins for extra realism. You can also print optional wall mounts to place it on the wall. It is designed to use as little filament as possible while still being strong and sturdy. Note: this new model is completely interchangable with my other Hydra rocket models (the screw-together version, not the peg assembly version). So you can print any parts from this model and combine it with other hydra rockets you've printed. Bambu filaments used Warhead at the top Basic Yellow Silk+ Titan Gray Overture Silk Copper ( Amazon link ) Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Rocket Body Basic Light Gray A white filament would work as well Silk+ Red Silk+ Silver (for the mid-body fins) Polymaker Metallic Silver ( Amazon link ) Basic Silver would work great too Engine Metal Iridium Gold Silk+ Gold would work too Assembly is super easy The parts simply screw together, so if you make a mistake you can just unscrew and re-screw in seconds, no problems. Make sure you don't over tighten – they are quite strong, but all plastic screws can eventually break under enough pressure – you should be able to screw them until they feel snug. 1. Screw the main body together, which includes 4 longer white/gray segments, one shorter red segment, and one short white/gray segment. 2. Then take each of the silver fins and connect all 4 to a base by sliding them together. It may take a little bit of forcer, pushing down on a table can help. 3. Now the assembled fins and clip them into the tall gray section. They should snap in easily if you line it up right. If you can't get the fins to snap in, try a different (probably lower) angle. 4. Next begin screwing on the other parts one by one to the far right end (the end with the red strip). 5. Then, assemble the warhead portion at the tip with the pegs provided like you see below and screw it onto the top of the rocket. 6. Lastly, begin connecting the rocket motor by connecting the top threaded piece to the bottom piece with the two long pegs provided. 7. Then the final step is to attach the fins to the rocket motor – the will snap into place with little force. Note that they must be facing clockwise , not counter clockwise. If you insert them counter clockwise you will find that they don't fold all the way.

The WW2 Bazooka was a shoulder-fired, rocket-propelled anti-tank weapon that gave infantry soldiers the unprecedented ability to destroy armored vehicles . It fired a high-explosive, shaped-charge warhead from a reusable steel tube, relying on venting gases out the back to eliminate dangerous recoil. Named after a novelty musical instrument due to its odd tubular shape, it became one of the most iconic "tools of victory" for the Allied forces. tags: halo|halo energy sword|elite|elite energy sword|arbiter|master chief|halo cosplay|energy sword
description: Ever wanted a life-sized Halo energy sword? Me too! I was surprised that I couldn't find a print for this, so I made one myself. Coming in at just over a metre long, this is a faithful replica of the iconic Halo weapon. It looks great printed in either translucent blue or clear PETG, with light channels down the middle of each blade and compartments on both blades for electronics (batteries - sized for 18650 cells, control boards etc). Everything is designed to key together to allow for easy printing and assembly. This print takes up 5 full plates on my P2S and took a few days to print, with around 1.5kg of blade material. Each plate is as packed as it can reasonably be. It can of course be printed on smaller printers like the A1 and can be scaled down appropriately to suit this. Key assembly steps: Print and attach hilt sections together. I printed these in a grey PLA+, then stuck them together with CA glue. The fit is tight and may need a bit of force. There is a channel down the inside of the hilt to route wires for lights or switches. Optional - sand, prime, paint hilt. I painted with a base of black acrylic and then steel / silver acrylic on top, then sanded paint down in places to give a weathered look. Print blade base parts and attach to hilt. The fit between the hilt and blade base is a bit looser than any of the other joins, as this gives a bit more tolerance for any accumulated accuracy errors throughout the print. The intended attachment method is to use an M8 nut / insert / T-nuts heat-set into the handle, and an M8*40mm bolt through the blade into this nut / insert. You could however just use a suitable epoxy to bond the two parts well. Either way, this should be a secure connection once properly glued / torqued down. Attach blade pieces to blade base, finishing up with the optional reinforcing bar (secured using M3 heat inserts and M3*10mm bolts into the blade sections). You could use a suitable glue to attach these together, though the keyed fit is pretty tight. Optional finishing steps. I used a UV-set clear resin to fill the join lines between sections and make things look a bit more continuous. This certainly isn't a magic fix as it is obviously still printed in pieces, but it does help! You can then install electronics if desired. I found LED rope or LED-strips worked well (ideally with high density RGB COBs. If they're too far apart you get a less diffuse effect). description: Spartan/Trojan War Hound Dog Helmet – Fully Articulated Bring the glory of the ancient world to your furry companion! This isn’t just a costume piece; it’s a high-detail, 3D-printable tribute to the legendary warriors of Troy and Sparta, specifically designed to fit the unique anatomy of a dog. Whether it’s for a photoshoot, a convention, or just to show the neighborhood who the real "Alpha" is, this helmet is the ultimate accessory for your four-legged warrior. 🏛️ History of the Model The design is inspired by the Corinthian-style helmets used by ancient Greek hoplites and later stylized in Trojan lore. Historically, these helmets were symbols of strength, protection, and status. I wanted to translate that intimidating, majestic silhouette into something comfortable and wearable for pets. The intricate swirls and Celtic-inspired patterns on the cheek guards add a "mythical" flair, bridging the gap between historical accuracy and high-fantasy cosplay. ⚙️ Functional Design & Assembly This model is unique because it features fully functional articulated cheek guards (flaps) . The Hinge System: Unlike static models, this helmet uses custom-designed hinges. You will need to print the included hinge pins separately. Assembly: Once printed, align the cheek guards with the main helmet body and slide the 3D-printed pins through the knuckles. This allows the flaps to swing outward, making it much easier to put on and take off your dog while ensuring a comfortable fit against their jawline. Durability: The crest is reinforced to handle the "zoomies," but it remains lightweight enough for medium to large breeds to wear comfortably. 📏 Sizing and Fitting Your Warrior Because every "Good Boy" is a different size, scaling is critical. Measurement: To get the perfect fit, I highly recommend using my Cosplay Calipers Measuring Tool . Measure the width of your dog's head between the ears and the length from the brow to the back of the skull. Scaling & Orientation: If you need to scale this up for a Great Dane or down for a Terrier, or if you need to slice it to fit a smaller print bed, check out my comprehensive guide: How to Size, Scale, Cut, Pin, and Orient Armor in Bambu Studio . 🛠️ Printing Tips Filament: Looks incredible in Silk Silver PLA or "Antique Gold." Support: Tree supports are recommended for the internal dome and the hinge knuckles. 🔄 Remix Potential & Alternate Uses This model is a fantastic base for further creativity! Cat Version: Scale down to roughly 40-50% for a "Battle Cat" aesthetic. Fan made design Liberator carbine from Helldivers 2 Its pretty much all there with the exception of the pouch. Not quite good enough yet to get that part done properly. *Edit 7/19/26: Wall mount print profile has been added. Fully assembled it is almost 24 inches long. Features: Working picatinny rail with attachments. Sights can be quick swapped with each other or a scope if you go with 8x2 magnets. 2 different threaded muzzle options 2 sight options 1 scope option 1 under barrel “flashlight / laser combo” (2 parts held together with magnets) 1 under barrel grip Most parts are separated out for easy color printing. I'll provide an AMS profile for some of the main parts & accessories if you want to go that route. (Grip, main sight, flashlight attachment & buttstock) Assembly: *Assembly is pretty straight forward but there are a lot of pieces. See images for the renders that show where everything goes. Yellow parts in the images are all the connecting / guide pins. You will want to assemble the 3 main sections first. Front, Mid, rear using the larger connecting pins. *Be sure to remember to put in the barrel insert into the mid section prior to any gluing (if you are doing that). Slide rear top (as I call it *on plate 4) into the mid section using connecting pin. Little holes on the top need to be towards the rear of the gun. Buttstock will hold the main rear and top rear sections together with connecting pins. Buttstock covers - There are small alignment holes for pins on the rear top. Add in pins to rear top (may be tight). Place covers onto pins. They only go on one way, see images for reference. Buttstock straps - These should fit snuggle into the openings on the covers. I'd start by inserting the strap on the right side of the gun fist, then push the left side up and in. Straps may need some filing. Mine fit in nice and required no gluing. Magazine connects to the bottom of the rear section using connecting pins. Magazine end cap and loop need to be glued on. Grips & trigger guard - There is an indent in the grip and the upper grip where the trigger guard sits. Due to the design you need to assemble these at the same time. Put 2 pins in the upper grip place it flat side down (in not already attached to mid section). Hold flat side of trigger guard in the grip with one hand while pushing the grip onto the pins guide the angle side of the trigger guard into the indent on the upper grip. Seems difficult when typing it out but its easy. Do test a test fit before gluing anything. I filled my trigger guard down a bit to get perfect fit before gluing. Top picatinny rail is held in my the screw pins. I added the screw pin down into the rails first, then aligned the pins above the holes & pushed them all the way into the main body of the gun. Mine were snug and required no glue. Bottom and side picatinny rails are all the same size & go in as descried above. Cover plates - These are glued on after everything is assembled. Under barrel plates hide some of the seam lines. Top 2 for the bolt area are aesthetic. If you want to use the top 2 be sure to glue them in before you glue in the bolt pin. Slide picatinny mount onto the rails. Add in magnets, make sure you get polarity right on the accessories for easy swapping. There are pins to secure the mount to the rails. Slide the pin in and place on the cap on the other side. You can glue them if you like, I chose not to since the mounts were snug on the rails for me. *Only 2 mounts are in the profile. Print more if you need them. Notes: Most larger flat pieces have 3 walls and 10% infill. I've also slowed the outer / inner wall speeds down to 60-80mm/s to try and negate seeing lines. Smaller items have brims and .16 layer heights to keep the details. Supports are enabled on individual objects where needed. Magazine & magazine end cap have a ton of triangles so you will see that warning. Simplify them at your own risk. Screw pins - I printed them facing up because I didn't want texture to show. Feel free to rotate them 180 if you have smooth plate. Magnets: if you use them for all accessories you will need 16 or 20 8x2 magnets. Be sure to get your polarity correct for easy swapping. If not using magnets you can print our 8mmx4mm plugs. I'm probably missing something but will update notes as needed. CLICK HERE FOR MORE HELLDIVERS SWAG o7

Hey everyone! A life size model of the iconic WW1 shotgun, the Winchester model 1897. This does not fire or technically cycle, but it does have a simple moveable pump action mechanism. Each plate has been separated to individual parts, such as the receiver, barrels, foregrip, stock, etc. Of course some of the larger parts (like the stock and heatshield) had to be split and have dowels that are printed with them. These dowels aren't meant to hold the model together alone, they more act as guides to make sure everything is straight, so make sure to use glue as well!!!!! :) In order for the foregrip to slide on the mag tube, you may need to do a bit of sanding post printing, but it shouldn't be too bad. I apologize for the inconvenience, getting tolerances right with these kind of things can be difficult! Assembly is easy as pie. Start by gluing the 2 tubes halves together. After this insert the longer tube (barrel) into the top hole of the receiver, then insert the bottom one as well. Make sure the flared end of the second tube is AWAY from the receiver (this is what the heat shield will later rest on/touch). Add the assembled stock to the other end (make sure to join the two stock sides in the correct orientation). Afte this simply slide on the assembled heat shield and the foregrip to the bottom tube! If you have any questions feel free to ask. Assembly shouldn't be too hard :), I will likely post assembly pics soon as I am going to print another. If this model does well, I will also add a bayonet for it!

Want a replica of the frag grenade from game PUBG (Player Unknown Battleground)? This grenade even has a spring-loaded handle that flies off when you pull the pin. The PUBG frag grenade is similar to the real-life M67 grenade, however, there are some distinct differences in its rounded shape and differences with the fuze that this model reflects. Spring options (for flying handle) Metal Spring (recommended) – if you have a metal spring, even a pen spring will usually work, then print the metal spring profile. Bambu Store's 0.5x7x12mm spring is what this model is designed to work with. Pen springs work as well though, many different types have been tested and work fine. You can often cut pen springs in half and get two grenade springs since this model only needs a 12mm long spring and pen springs tend to be about 24mm. Plastic Spring – if you don't have a metal spring, but still want the handle to fly off, then print the plastic spring profile. If the spring eventually wears out, just print a new one and pop it in. Don't leave the spring under tension when not using it as it will wear out much faster. Avoid Matte and Silk filament for the spring itself, Basic and Metal work better. No Flying Handle - if you don't want the handle to fly off and just want a grenade model, simply print either version and don't put in a spring. Bambu filaments used Silk+ Silver Matte Yellow Polymaker Army Green ( Amazon link ) Matte Dark Green works too Metal Spring Version Assembly 1. Use the two pegs to connect the two halves of the grenade together. 2. Flip the silver top upside down and insert the peg. Make sure the peg is sticking out of the top, if not rotate 90 degrees. 3. Insert your spring into the silver top next, just like you did with the peg. 4. Screw the silver top onto the grenade – keeping the silver top upside down makes this easier (so spring doesn't fall out while screwing it on). That's it – now you can attach the spoon handle, put in the pin, and use it – enjoy! Plastic Spring Version Assembly 1. Use the two pegs to connect the two halves of the grenade together. 2. Flip the silver top upside down and insert the spring. Make sure the spring's peg is sticking out of the top, if not rotate 90 degrees. 3. Screw the silver top onto the grenade – keeping the silver top upside down makes this easier (so spring doesn't fall out while screwing it on). That's it – now you can attach the spoon handle, put in the pin, and use it – enjoy!

I tested some of the prints on my Bambu P2S and they printed fine. I used tree supports on the starting textured plate to test the prints. I would recommend a smooth plate since most of the head pieces print on one of the hammer faces so smooth will look better. I transferred all the settings I used in Cura into the .3mf, but did slow down the print settings for the P2S with silk. My version of the Sickle, with a squishy trigger and moving battery latch. EXCLUSIVE FOR BAMBU SOFTWARE! (read the description to see why) This is a passion project that I considered not uploading for this reason alone, but I ultimately reconsidered tonight and decided to do so, because the only other options as for making this prop are either limited in nature or simply have too steep of a price tag for me, which is why I also decided to ensure this stays free forever. A lot of work and many, many sleepless nights went into making it possible. READ ME! It looks difficult to assemble but it's really not. I have named each and every single part as for what it is and where it goes, plus arranged the plates in such a way to be as straight-forward as possible. If you ever feel stuck (although I doubt it), read the name each object has and refer to the blown up view in the pics as the set of instructions. I recommend printing this out of PET-G or higher-strength materials. Use PLA at your own risk but I'd advise you to steer clear of it! Remember to add the tubes and the foil (look for a mylar blanket) to make it 1:1 as in-game! For the trigger, I designed it around the spring off a pen. Seriously; don't bother. Go grab the cheapest pen from a store and you got the spring; cut it short with some pliers if it's too compressed in there. Trust it; I designed it with that in mind. As for the magazine release/ battery latch, simply super glue 4 4x2 magnets. The set opening limit is purely mechanical; I measured it to fit perfectly and match the in-game opening angle, so don't force it or you'll break something. As for closing, slap it back and it'll stay in place no matter how you handle it. I've pulled it straight from the game files and I have done my outmost best to maintain the accuracy. I did everything I could in Blender and MeshMixer, but I ultimately had to do much of the fixing, cutting and putting together directly in slicer due to the impossibility of some parts. With that said, some negatives I put in there are MANDATORY for the build to work. I cannot guarantee it will work on any software other than Bambu Slicer, but you can download and check. DO NOT ATTEMPT to print it without the negative parts added to each piece of the prop. Also, DO NOT attempt to modify any of the structural parts. I have taken the time to make sure everything aligns absolutely flawlessly in the slicer. However! As you can see from my photos, I was a bit too hasty with the glue and some parts didn't seal shut while I assembled mine. description: A fully 3d printed Single-shot Cap-powered BB pistol! Fully 3d printed springs. Has 10 bodies to print, can fit on an a1 build plate at minimum. Semi-auto hammer and trigger system though it is single shot. hammer action works well. The larger spring is the hammer spring, simply slot into the holes in the hammer and the main body. The smaller spring is the Trigger spring, do the same. The two main halves of the pistol snap together, may need a spot of glue on the joints. To use, get a standard 8-shot ring cap, then cut off an individual cap using a utility knife, being careful with fingers. Break the barrel (shown in images) by pressing the barrel release latch (shown in images as well) on the left hand side of the pistol body, then lift the barrel, tilting it upwards from the end near the hammer. Load the singular cap into the recess at the end of the barrel, making sure it sits snug. To lock the barrel, manually push the barrel release latch now protruding from the right hand side back into its original position. this can be fiddly ads the hole is quite precise. This is a muzzle loader-so from the muzzle, cut out a small square of tissue. Place it on the muzzle and get a standard 6mm BB. place the BB on top of the tissue wad and using a blunt skewer, ram the BB and the wad into the barrel until you feel it stop (do not ram too hard as the cap holder will snap). Then you are ready to fire! To reset the trigger, pull the hammer back manually and hold it, then let go of the trigger and it should spring back into place. You can pull it gently to help with this. *DISCLAIMER* I am not at fault for misuse of this toy causing damage to living beings and surroundings. Be responsible with this toy-never point at any living being , fire with Adult supervision and at a fixed target. Consider wearing Eye pro if necessary. Remember, this is a TOY ONLY and should be used extremely sensibly only in the right conditions.
