To that end I designed it around these little magnet operated light up warning lights: https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0CMTJQRYX . The lights have a reed sensor in them that when the magnet is on the back they don't do anything but when you remove the magnet they light up. And the pattern is similar to the actual grav charge, close enough without needing expensive electronics or wiring anything. The back of the holder has some indents of 15mm magnets. Glue some magnets to the back and that will be strong enough to keep the light off. When you pull the grav charge off the holder the reed switch turns the unit on and the lights start to flash then after about 10 seconds go to the circular pattern. I added magnets on the bottom of the grav charges themselves also so you can still stick it to something like in the show but without affecting the light. Place it back on the holder and it turns back off. I went with these lights because they also turn themselves off after a couple minutes so they won't kill the battery if you leave them out. Print Details I printed the body and holder in Bambu ABS - Silver. The body has scarf seam turned on in its object settings which leaves less of a seam on the outside but does sometime affect the color slightly in that spot. If you are going to paint them leave scarf seam on, if you are going to leave them as is you may want to turn that off so the color is more consistent but the seam will be more noticeable. The cover is Bambu PETG Translucent Clear that I then used a red Sharpie oil based paint pen on because I couldn't find a good clear red filament. The combination ended up looking really good so that's what I would recommend or even possibly just a red marker. For printing the cover I have the speeds set to 20mm/s and a custom Bambu Transparent PETG setting that turns off cooling. It's the only way to get a mostly clear lens but you can of course use standard settings, the lens just might not be as clear and the LEDs won't be as distinguishable. Or you can buy a after market clear lens sized for about 28mm. I tried to optimize the print so no supports are required and the 2 x 4 magnets on the bottom should be press fit although I'd add a dab of glue behind them. The holder for the light also is press fit but you can also glue that in to be more secure. Since the lights turn themselves off the batteries should last for years so personally I glued them in.

description: This one is for Squidward who relentlessly pushed for me to make the model, and then was so grateful when I got started! I hope you enjoy it! I designed this mask a bit different from my others and I am happy with the outcome. Essentially, I incorporated the mesh eyes directly into the mask so they don't need to be added or printed separately. If you would prefer to print it all in one color (to save time and money), you should be able to easily paint the mesh portion black with some black acrylic paint. I also experimented with how the horns are printed and attached to the head to make them more integrated into the design and also to avoid needing supports on them. My first version was a bit to tight to fit on my head, but it fit on everyone else's in my home. In this version I tweaked the hole size for the head and flattened the bottom of the print a bit to improve printability and eliminate some of the supports. I believe this should fit any head pretty easily now. One under appreciated part of my work is figuring out how to get a model absolutely maximize the space of a p1s sized printer. In this case of this print, lots of adjustments were made to get it just right. For this hobby (designing and 3d printing models) I certainly go through phases. After filling up all the wall space in a room with Hollow Knight masks, I prioritized new areas. This was a nice break from my current phase which has been pond fountains, I think I have one more of those left in me before switching again. I am experimenting with designing a toy for kids during long car rides, I am excited about it and hope to share it soon!

After a longer wait than I hoped, the supported version of my unexpectedly popular flamberge print is ready!! This was the first ever success that I had with taking a large video game sword and making a good, 3D printed version of it. I identified some problems with the original design and I have added some very minor details to the model and added a channel for a 4ft/1.22m long, 5/16"/.794cm diameter fiberglass rod through about 3/4 of the length of the prop sword. The sword is 5.6ft/1.71m long when fully assembled. In the U.S. I have found that the easiest access to rods like this is by purchasing driveway markers from a hardware store like Home Depot or Lowe's. To assemble, start with the end of the hilt, add your rod, and start stacking the pieces from there. If a piece doesn't slide easily over the rod and overlapping section of the piece below it, there's a good chance that it needs to be rotated 180 degrees. IMPORTANT FOR ASSEMBLY: Please do NOT print this version if you can't find a supporting rod - the rod doesn't leave space for meaningful printed structure (keying blades only) and the blade will snap with ease if assembled without support. Also note that the last 1.6ft/.5m of length are unsupported in the interest of balance and weight reduction - this means that hitting something with more than gentle force will likely snap the end of the blade. description: Inspired by Homer's Iliad , this full-size modular spear is my own interpretation of Achilles' legendary weapon. Rather than recreating a movie or game prop, I wanted to design a display piece that captures the spirit of ancient Greek mythology while remaining practical to print and assemble on a standard FDM printer. Every decorative section tells part of Achilles' story through carefully chosen artwork: Greek key borders inspired by classical architecture Olive branches representing Greece A Corinthian helmet surrounded by laurel branches, symbolizing Achilles as a victorious warrior Mount Pelion with ash leaves, referencing the legendary origin of Achilles' spear The Greek inscription ΑΧΙΛΛΕΥΣ engraved into the shaft Realistic wood grain running throughout the spear The completed spear measures approximately 200 cm in length and is designed around a 150 cm wooden broomstick handle , creating a lightweight yet incredibly strong display piece. Modular Design This model has been designed to suit different building styles. For maximum strength and durability, I recommend using a 150 cm wooden broomstick handle as the internal core. This creates a rigid finished spear while keeping the printed parts lightweight. However, the spear can also be assembled without the wooden core if you prefer a fully 3D printed version. For builders wanting additional reinforcement, the spearhead and butt spike have also been designed to accept: Four 10 mm × 40 mm wooden dowels Two 40 mm screws (8 mm head) These reinforcement methods are completely optional . They are included for builders who want extra strength, but the model can also be assembled without them depending on your intended use. Please note: Wooden broomstick handles and wooden dowels can vary slightly in diameter depending on the manufacturer. You may need to lightly sand the broomstick handle or dowels to achieve the perfect fit. Test fit all parts before applying glue. Colour Options This model has been designed to give makers complete creative freedom. Option 1 – Paint Your Own Print everything in a single colour and paint the model yourself to achieve realistic wood, bronze and twine effects. Option 2 – Multi-Colour Printing If you own a printer with an AMS or another multi-material system, the decorative details can be printed in multiple colours straight from the printer, allowing you to create your own unique version without painting. Whether painted by hand or printed in multiple colours, every maker can create their own interpretation of Achilles' legendary spear. Print Settings Material PETG Layer Height 0.16 mm Walls 3 Nozzle 0.4 mm Supports Only where required Additional Materials 1 × 150 cm wooden broomstick handle (approximately 30 mm diameter) 4 × Wooden dowels (10 mm × 40 mm) 2 × Screws (40 mm long with an 8 mm head) Super glue or epoxy Twine for both grip sections Assembly Instructions Test fit all printed parts onto the wooden broomstick handle before gluing. If required, lightly sand the broomstick handle or wooden dowels to achieve a smooth fit. Assemble the spearhead: Screw the spearhead socket onto the broomstick handle. Insert the two 10 × 40 mm wooden dowels. Apply glue and slide the spearhead into place. Install the first grip section (the decorative brass-style rings are already part of this printed piece). Install the Achilles shaft section, ensuring the ΑΧΙΛΛΕΥΣ inscription faces the correct direction so it can be read when the spear is standing upright. Install the remaining decorative shaft sections in any order you prefer. Install the second grip section. Assemble the butt spike: Screw the butt spike socket onto the broomstick handle. Insert the remaining two 10 × 40 mm wooden dowels. Apply glue and attach the butt spike. Wrap both grip sections with twine. Lightly pass a flame from a lighter over the twine to remove any loose fibers and give the grips a cleaner, more authentic finish. Take care not to scorch the printed parts. Features Approximately 2 meters long when assembled Modular construction Designed for standard 250 × 250 mm FDM printers Optional wooden core for maximum strength Optional dowel and screw reinforcement Detailed engraved artwork inspired by Homer's Iliad Beginner-friendly assembly Easy to transport and store thanks to the modular design Suitable for display, collections and cosplay Painting Suggestions Wood Dark brown base coat Medium brown dry brush Light tan highlights Metal Aged bronze or brass Black wash for weathering Light metallic dry brushing on edges Grips Leave the twine natural for a rustic appearance Or apply a light brown wash for an aged look Designer's Note Rather than recreating an existing film or game prop, this spear is an original interpretation inspired by Homer's Iliad . Every engraved section was chosen to represent part of Achilles' legend—from the ash wood of Mount Pelion to the Greek inscription of his name—creating a display piece that tells a story while remaining practical for everyday 3D printing. Whether you choose to paint it by hand or print it in multiple colours using an AMS, I hope you enjoy building it as much as I enjoyed designing it. If you make one, I'd love to see your finished version!

description: Hey there! :) My sis is playing an orc character in a recent DnD campaign, and she asked me: Could you make something I can wear as an Orc? And I was like: 👁👄👁💡 Yep, anyways, that's how I ended up here :D 🎲 My goal for this mask was to make it as light and airy as possible. The mouth of the mask is closed, so instead I made sure the nostrils are wide open and added a **Sword Tear** both to look cool and to create an extra point of ventilation. This mask is also lighter and more flexible than my other mask designs, and is only like 34 gr? So you can feel more comfortable wearing it! 🎲 Sizing: The size I'm wearing here has a width of 15 cm, and it's a bit loose for me. This mask is quite flexible, so I think the same size could also fit people bigger than me. In case of doubt, you can scale the mask up or down by a centimeter. Don't forget to apply the same uniform percentage scaling to the fang components too. Remember that the design tolerances will change after scaling, and you may need to use glue at the interfaces between components or shave down the connecting parts of the fangs a little. 🎲 Print Notes: 3 Walls, 0.2 mm layers, 0% sparse infill Enable the supports, but block them from being generated in the middle of the mask, in the nose and lip area. (It's already done for the print profile) Give the mask a lot of outer brims: 10 mm or so. Important: This is a super speed-sensitive print! Bring your speed down to under 90 mm/s for all walls, first-layer speed, and first-layer infill speed. I recommend printing at around 60 mm/s. Increase the support generation threshold for fangs to 60 degrees to provide them more structure and stability during printing. Clean the parts thoroughly before wearing, and secure the fangs in place with a little glue. That's all, I hope you enjoy it and send me your pics wearing it in the comments! :) Happy printing! ✨🥂 Check out my Cosplay, Fairs & Events Fashion collection for more wearable cool props like this!

description: Wearable Iron Man MK2 helmet , fully optimized for printing on all 3D printers, including the A1 Mini. Stop wasting your time and start printing this masterpiece! The model dimensions are designed based on what I consider the international standard: Budwin's Sizing Head No. 3 , whom I deeply thank for making it available and making everyone's life easier. Main Features & Smart Cutting No Harsh Cuts: The cuts follow the helmet's design lines, making the joints invisible from the outside for a clean look. No Circling: Dividing the model into pieces eliminates the "stair-stepping" effect on the dome typical of single-piece prints, ensuring a smooth surface with no sanding needed. Easy Printing: Splitting the project reduces individual print session times and the risk of failures, making it accessible to anyone with any printer. Multi-Color Without AMS: The black and gold parts are separated from the main body, allowing you to print them directly with the correct color filament even without an automatic material system. Improved Ergonomics and Fit: The back section has been modified for a complete design, the ears have been hollowed out to increase width, and the eyes are perforated to ensure visibility. Custom Display Stand: you can use this fantastic stand custom-made for this helmet to display it at its best. Disclaimer: Some of the images shown have been modified using AI. 💡 Printing Tip You can use the default settings, but for the best results, I highly recommend making a small temperature adjustment. The flawless finish you see in my photos is actually due to printing the materials at lower temperatures than the defaults that are set automatically. I printed in Bambu PLA Basic at 205°C instead of 220°C. ⚙️Magnetic Mechanics (No Electronics!) By following the video instructions and watching the uploaded GIFs, you can achieve a fully functional mechanical opening without the need for complex circuits. The GIFs are from my other MK3 project, but the assembly process is identical. Magnetic Back: The first GIF shows you how to implement a magnetic closure that improves fit when wearing the helmet. On plate number 9, you will find the clips for 8x2 magnets needed to close the back of the mask. Magnetic Faceplate: The second GIF shows you how to implement magnets that allow the mask to open and lock onto the upper section. High-quality magnets are recommended for a stronger hold. On plates number 10 and 11, you will find the clips for 8x2 magnets needed for this purpose. Hidden Magnet Clips: The front and back clips have a different design. The front ones are specifically engineered to completely hide the magnets from view; however, they require a stronger magnet grip, so feel free to use the clips from plate 9 for both purposes. However, you still need Plate 10 because it has the taller clips used to keep the faceplate open! Maximum Freedom: By separating the magnet holders from the main structure of the helmet, the final choice is up to you: you can use this magnetic system, implement your own motorized electronic mechanisms, or simply weld all the pieces together. 🔨Assembly Guide The pieces must be joined after printing. Among the uploaded photos, you will also find a visual diagram explaining how to pair them. You can use glue, but for the best results, a permanent bond, and high mechanical resistance, I recommend using a soldering iron or a 3D pen to carefully melt and weld the joints from the inside . I welded the entire helmet myself without any problems, as you can see for yourself from the photos of the finished project! Pro-tip: I recommend starting by joining the top and back-top pieces. Since they are the largest parts, they are the trickiest, join them by gently pressing the two parts together to ensure there is no gap. All of this makes this mask a masterpiece! Happy printing! - GB

Berserk: Dragon Slayer I created this model for my Advanced Manufacturing class where our final project required us to incorporate something we learned during the semester. I decided to combine 3D printing with carbon fiber skinning to create a functional, lightweight version of Guts' iconic Dragon Slayer . When designing this model, my main goals were strength, functionality, and minimizing material usage . Many of the Dragon Slayer models I've seen on here require an incredible amount of filament ( ~6kg ). By designing the sword around a structural core, I was able to reduce the total filament usage to roughly 2.5kg while still creating a sword sturdy enough to swing around. The model is designed to fit a 256mm³ build volume and is hollow throughout most of the blade. The center of the sword is designed to accept a 1-inch PVC pipe approximately 75 inches long , providing the primary structural support and preventing the blade from flexing during use. A few things to note: The tip of the blade is intentionally infilled for added durability. I included two versions of the base section : A hollow version to minimize filament usage and overall weight. An infilled version for those who prefer a heavier, more realistic feel. The hilt and chain are printed as a single piece . A modifier is included that automatically increases this section to 6 walls and 99% infill , since I consider these to be the most critical structural parts of the build. Recommended Print Settings These are the PLA settings I personally used: 3 walls 3% Gyroid infill Support for the hilt, chain, and tip only. These settings produced rigid parts that became significantly stronger after being reinforced with carbon fiber. If you don't plan on carbon fiber skinning the sword, I'd recommend printing with: 4 walls 6% Gyroid infill for some extra strength. Assembly To bond the pieces together, I used JB Weld Plastic Bonder , which is compatible with thermoplastics, carbon fiber composites, coated metals, and several other materials. After assembly, I filled all of the seams with wood filler before beginning the epoxy process. At the time of uploading this model, I'm currently applying the final layers of epoxy. After that, I'll sand everything smooth and paint the finished sword. I've been documenting the entire build process, so keep an eye out for a YouTube video showing the complete build from printing to the finished prop! If you end up printing one, I'd love to see your results. If you notice any fitment issues or have suggestions for improvements, please leave a comment and I'll do my best to update the model as quickly as possible. Happy printing!

description: Description A sci-fi exoskin glove armor made from individual 3D printed modules embedded into a thin tulle/mesh layer during printing. The result is a flexible sheet of armor-like modules that stays aligned thanks to the tulle layer, making the final placement on the glove much easier than positioning each piece separately. After printing, the excess tulle is trimmed away, leaving the modules connected only where needed. This version uses a strong red and black color combination , giving the glove a high-tech, cybernetic, almost biomechanical look. How it works The modules are printed with a pause after the first layer. During the pause, a piece of tulle/mesh is placed over the print and fixed to the build plate. Printing then continues, embedding the tulle into the printed parts. In my test print, the tulle was positioned using magnets. It can also be positioned with masking tape, as long as the tape does not cover an important part of the print area or the prime tower. After removing the print from the build plate, the excess tulle was cut away with scissors. Assembly The printed mesh-backed armor sections are attached to a fabric glove. For this prototype, I used gel superglue to attach the printed modules to the glove. The tulle helps keep the modules aligned during placement, so the assembly process is much easier and cleaner than gluing every small module one by one. Recommended assembly steps: Print the armor modules with the tulle/mesh embedded. Remove the part from the build plate. Trim the excess tulle around the printed modules. Test the placement on the glove before gluing. Apply gel superglue carefully to the back of the modules. Press the armor section onto the glove and let it cure fully. Printing notes This project uses a planned pause during printing in order to insert the tulle/mesh. Important: use a thin tulle/mesh fabric make sure it lies flat on the build plate fix it with magnets or masking tape keep the tape/magnets away from the print area do not cover the prime tower if using multiple colors make sure the tulle does not wrinkle before resuming the print The model was printed in red and black , but other high-contrast color combinations can work very well too. Sizing / Scaling This glove was designed for my hand size: 20 cm from the wrist crease to the tip of the middle finger . To resize it for your hand, measure the same distance on your own hand and use this formula: Scale (%) = Your hand length / 20 cm × 100 Examples: 18 cm hand → 18 / 20 × 100 = 90% 19 cm hand → 19 / 20 × 100 = 95% 21 cm hand → 21 / 20 × 100 = 105% 22 cm hand → 22 / 20 × 100 = 110% Apply the same scale to all armor so the proportions stay consistent. Hand width, finger thickness and glove stretch can vary, so I recommend printing one or two finger plates first and testing the placement before printing the full set. Notes This is a decorative/cosplay glove project, not protective equipment. The final look depends a lot on the glove used, the glue, the flexibility of the fabric, and how carefully the tulle is trimmed and positioned. Disclaimer This model and print profile were created and tested on a calibrated printer with a clean build plate and properly tuned filament settings. Results may vary depending on printer calibration, filament condition, bed adhesion, material, cooling, pause timing, tulle thickness, glue type, and assembly method. I cannot guarantee identical results on uncalibrated printers, dirty plates, wet filament, or poorly tuned extrusion/adhesion.

description: A Project Hail Mary inspired glove. This is the “Weaver”, which is based of of Rocky's 3d printer thingies that he uses to make the little figurines and chains seen in the movie. My design is based of of scenes from the movie, as well as clips from Adam Savage's “How Rocky's Models Were Made for Project Hail Mary” Youtube video. Link . This design takes small details and brings that to life, giving you a wearable glove/gauntlet that closely matches those seen in the movies and videos. The design includes a variety of nozzle designs, as well as replaceable and detatchable “material sticks”. The cables seen in the images use raw pieces of filament. The filament used in the images are made from TPU, allowing for comforatble articulation and flexibility. Assembly: The design is built around the “wrist mount” stl file, which you should resize accordingly to fit your wrist. The “anglers” stl files are slid into the two ear shaped slots, in which the “material sticks” are inserted into the slots. The connection between the wrist mount and anglers are designed to be loose, so you can use glue if you want to keep it in place easily. On the other end of the anglers are holes designed for you to put your filament pieces. Cut two lengths of 1.75mm filament, and slot it into the holes. On the “top nozzle” stl, there is also a hole meant for the other side of the filament to slide into. On the top nozzle, there is a slot meant for either the "finger clamp" or “alt finger clamp”. The connection between these two pieces is designed to be a friction fit, so no glue is needed. On the finger clamp pieces, there are also two slots meant for “finger rings”. For each finger clamp, you should use one small finger ring on the tip and one regular finger ring on the back. For the thumb piece, it is assembled the same as a finger clamp and finger ring, with the only exception being using the thumb ring and only needing one. Refer to the renders and images if you need help. Sorry for the bad photos by the way, I had to use my left hand because my right hand had the model on it.

description: Therian Bone Prop – Hueso Ergonómico para Therian Si alguna vez has intentado sujetar un hueso en la boca durante un rato, seguramente habrás notado que la mandíbula termina fatigándose. Mantener la boca demasiado abierta durante mucho tiempo resulta incómodo y puede ejercer una presión innecesaria sobre la articulación temporomandibular. Con esa idea nació este proyecto. Este hueso incorpora un soporte ergonómico interior , diseñado para adaptarse a la forma de la dentadura humana. En lugar de sujetar el hueso únicamente con la fuerza de la mandíbula, el apoyo distribuye la presión de forma mucho más uniforme, permitiendo llevarlo de una manera más cómoda y estable. ¿Cómo está fabricado? El modelo se imprime en dos mitades , lo que permite obtener un acabado limpio sin necesidad de soportes. Una vez impresas ambas piezas, se unen mediante: Tetones de alineación incluidos en el diseño. Resina epoxi bicomponente (recomendada para obtener la máxima resistencia). Este sistema facilita el montaje y garantiza una unión sólida y perfectamente alineada. Características ✔ Diseño ergonómico para mayor comodidad. ✔ Reduce la apertura necesaria de la mandíbula. ✔ Soporte adaptado a la dentadura humana. ✔ Impresión FDM sin soportes. ✔ Montaje sencillo mediante epoxi bicomponente. ✔ Optimizado para boquilla de 0,4 mm. Material recomendado Recomiendo imprimir este modelo en PETG . Además de ser más resistente que el PLA frente a golpes y deformaciones, el PETG ofrece una ligera flexibilidad que hace que el apoyo resulte más cómodo durante el uso. Otra ventaja importante es que el PETG es un material ampliamente utilizado en aplicaciones relacionadas con el contacto con alimentos. Existen numerosos filamentos de PETG con certificación para uso alimentario , aunque esta característica depende siempre del fabricante y del filamento empleado. En cualquier caso, si el hueso va a utilizarse de forma habitual, recomiendo imprimirlo con un PETG de buena calidad , ya que proporciona una excelente combinación de resistencia, durabilidad y comodidad. Para unir las piezas recomiendo utilizar resina epoxi de dos componentes. Recomendación ✅ Material recomendado: PETG. ✅ Boquilla: 0,4 mm. ✅ Altura de capa: 0,20 mm. ✅ Unir las dos mitades con resina epoxi bicomponente. description: 一、模型设计概述 本模型基于《我的世界》游戏内二维像素剑造型进行3D重构。区别于仅做平面拉伸的同类模型，该设计利用高低落差的阶梯式结构，塑造出三维立体的体素浮雕质感。在无需多色打印的条件下，依然可通过光影呈现丰富的层次感。 剑柄部分针对握持的人体工学进行了重新设计。参考游戏内官方3D化逻辑，将原二维扁平剑柄进行90度旋转并合并重组，消除冗余块面，使握把具备真实的立体体积和圆润的握持手感。剑柄底部设计有贯穿的镂空结构，可穿入挂绳，用于悬挂或作为背包挂饰。 二、打印与组装参数 文件拆分 ：剑身与剑柄已完成分体处理，默认分布在1-2两盘，可分开独立打印。 公差与组装 ：经多重精度测试，公差控制精准。装配预期为无胶水拼装（摩擦力卡合结构），无需额外使用粘合剂。 打印设置测试 ：内部已进行多组打印参数实测，以保障最佳打印质量。 三、耗材适配与操作提示 多色与单色适配 ：模型未预设固定配色，任何基础色彩耗材均可直接打印。纯色打印即可凸显像素浮雕质感；若配备多色打印系统（如AMS），或具备后期手涂上色能力，由于全模型皆为方块构造，表面涂装和分色操作非常简便，可根据游戏原作色彩自行调配。 耗材翘边预警 ：模型默认未在剑身部分添加辅助裙边（Brim）。若使用PETG或ABS等收缩率较高的材料，打印时 必须 在切片软件中手动开启裙边功能，否则极易发生翘边；若使用PLA材料，则无需额外处理。 打印尺寸限制 ：针对A1 mini 等较小打印平台的机器，无法直接打印原比例尺寸模型，可通过切片软件等比缩小后输出缩小版本。 四、文件开源与兼容性说明 本模型同步提供 STEP 格式开源文件，可在网页端下载。用户可将其导入任意CAD软件中进行结构修改，用于创作个人二次开发版本。 注意 ：此STEP文件暂无法在 Bambu Studio 切片软件中直接打开。如需在常见切片软件中预览和打印，请直接下载模型提供的 STL 格式文件。

model_name: Spider-Man PS4 Web Shooter with TPU Strap Remix
description: I wanted to make web shooters for a halloween costume, but I couldn't find any with TPU straps, so I Peter Parkered it and modified one myself. It's parametric so you can adjust to your wrist size, just put in the circumference of your wrist. To find the circumference of your wrist, simply use a string or cord of some kind and wrap it around your wrist, marking where it crosses over on both sides. Then lay it straight and measure the length between the markings. My wrists are quite small at 15cm around, so you will almost definitely need to increase the value for yours. I did not create the web shooters, I simply designed the strap and the cutout slots in the web shooters. I also thickened them around the middle so that the nozzles do not dig in to the wrists. Print profiles contain only the web shooters, not the TPU straps. *YOU MUST USE THE WEB VERSION OF MAKERWORLD OR THE BAMBU HANDY APP TO CUSTOMIZE, BAMBU STUDIO WILL NOT WORK* Printing the TPU straps is a bit tricky (as is with any TPU print, at least for me), try playing around with the orientation but keeping the long thin side touching the build plate (I hope that makes sense). Of course, make sure to use a glue interface layer on the build plate before printing. They slide in from the bottom, and look quite similar to the fitbit straps Peter uses in the game. I printed the web shooters with a 0.2mm nozzle using the settings in the print profile. I still have to paint mine, and I will add new pictures once I have. wow i suck at taking pictures

description: 参考高达中HG吉姆手枪设计的一个小玩具，按真人比例设计，可以当做玩具，也可以当做cos道具。 下图是与HG吉姆的对比，吉姆手枪背大家戏称为水枪。 吉姆的小帮手，一般被称为喷枪。吉姆在人印象里挺弱的一部分原因就是这把短小的手枪一样的主武器。其实本身cap部分和元祖步枪差不多，但是从节省成本考虑最终将收束部分阉割，枪头其实和步枪也差不太多，但是枪管也短了很多，进一步节省体积和成本。由于收束效果太差，所以并不推荐远距离使用，使用效果更像“霰弹枪”，但即便如此依然可以在近距离一发打穿扎古正面装甲。单发耗能并不多，所以弹数相比元祖步枪而言反而更多，应该有十几发，有种说法喷枪有一个速射模式，在此状态下可以较低出力发射“夺命十二连发”，在粒子储能罐耗尽后可以挂在机体充电口上缓慢回复。由于散布和射速的关系，喷枪的命中率其实还挺高，在联邦的物量战术下，成群结队的吉姆和铁球搭档为联邦的最终胜利立下汗马功劳。

当然我们也上传了3D打印的连接件，直插设计，对插时候稍紧（可能需要小锤辅助），可以作为 临时替代 。 PETG和PLA密度相比如下（相同体积零件， PETG 会更重一点 点，大约重 2%‑3%），建议用PETG打印 PLA 1.24‑1.25 1.24 Bambu Lab PETG 1.27‑1.29 1.27 Bambu Lab 比如同一个蝴蝶刀模型，同样填充率，PETG 打印成品 重量会比 视觉双重提示，形成肌肉记忆。当然，用在本模型上装饰作用大于实际作用，但也可以为之后用真正金属款打下基础。 多多练习，相信你一定可以 也能转出个像样的“开合花”动作，刀身在空中划过的弧线，和游戏里角色耍刀的镜头几乎重合，那瞬间的代入感，直接把游戏里的热血劲儿给拽到了现实里。 小贴士 蝴蝶刀 （Balisong）是一种非典型折刀，其结构包括刀柄、旋转机构、刀刃与锁定机构四个部分。由于其小巧便携、易于隐藏的特点，它也常被用于自卫或作为时尚饰品。 蝴蝶刀的英文名字起源于菲律宾巴坦加斯的一个小镇叫Balisung，这个镇子以生产蝴蝶刀而闻名。从英文的表面的意思看，bali是指裂开，sung 是指动物的角，综合起来动物裂开的角，就好像是刀，而早期蝴蝶刀的刀柄也是由来自动物的角进行雕刻而成的。 二战后，随着菲律宾移民（菲律宾曾为美国殖民地）将蝴蝶刀带入美国，该刀具凭借其允许做出的独特甩刀动作与低廉的价格，迅速在青年群体特别是飞车党中流行，成为街头文化符号。然而，因飞车党犯罪频发，蝴蝶刀逐渐被视为非法行为的象征。20世纪60年代初，美国政府迫于舆论压力，将蝴蝶刀等视作弹簧刀具加以严格限制，禁止其生产、进口与过境，致使其一度淡出公众视野。直至1970年，蝴蝶刀从联邦“非法弹簧折刀”名单中移除，随着法规放宽，重新在美国流行起来。 现代蝴蝶刀大致可以按照单刃、双刃，直柄、弯柄进行分类。从结构上来说，蝴蝶刀主要有两种类型，分别是铆钉结构和螺丝结构。蝴蝶刀结构新颖精巧，与常见口袋型折叠刀有明显区别。其设计无需刀鞘，刀柄可旋转组合成坚固手柄，同时兼具收纳功能，闭合时长度减半，便于安全携带。该刀具作为对传统折刀的改进，支持单手开合，这一特点成为其重要标志，并衍生出多种炫酷操作手法，使其频繁出现于影视作品之中。 第一次知道蝴蝶刀、想上手练习，就是来自三角洲影锋 。 重要安全提醒（必须注意） 我国管制刀具法规： 开刃蝴蝶刀属于管制刀具，严禁私自购买、携带、上街 ； 想要练习只能选择 无刃、圆角训练款（练习刃） ，仅适合居家把玩，外出携带依旧存在风险；不要因为游戏热度盲目入手，分清管制刀具与训练玩具。 简单总结 CSGO 种下蝴蝶刀的游戏圈子基础； 《三角洲行动》借着手游巨大流量，完成了蝴蝶刀在国内泛年轻群体的破圈，掀起新一轮练习、收藏训练蝴蝶刀的风潮。

Description A replica of the Apollo Lunar Module's Contact Light — the indicator that illuminated on the LM control panel when the probes extending from the landing gear touched the lunar surface, alerting the crew it was time to shut down the descent engine (famously seen during the Apollo 11 landing). This build reproduces the look of the original indicator while hiding a modern electronics core inside, allowing it to be switched on/off through Home Assistant. Power comes from a single hidden USB-C female jack in the "plug" housing: 5V feeds the D1 Mini directly, while a step-up module generates 12V for the AD16-30DS lamp. The lamp's negative wire is routed to a D1 Mini GPIO, which is pulled LOW to light it up. Components AD16-30DS indicator lamp (12V) Wemos D1 Mini USB-C female jack 5V→12V DC-DC step-up module 4x M3.5 flat-head slotted screws 2x 3.5mm Phillips-head screws Wiring USB-C 5V/GND → D1 Mini 5V/GND (direct) USB-C 5V/GND → step-up IN, output trimmed to 12V Step-up OUT+ → AD16-30DS + AD16-30DS - → D1 Mini GPIO (LOW = light on, HIGH/input = off) Common GND between USB-C, step-up, and D1 Mini D1 Mini flashed with ESPHome/Tasmota → integrated into Home Assistant
